name: 2025 Jingle Bell Run - Bellingham, WA
description:
Get ready for this year’s Jingle Bell Run, the original festive race for charity brought to you by the Arthritis Foundation. Wear your favorite holiday gear, and let's jingle all the way toward a cure!

Whether you're running, walking, or strolling, bring your friends, family, and coworkers along for the ride. Together, we're spreading joy and making strides towards a brighter future — saying "YES" to life, despite arthritis.

Don't miss out on this special occasion to make a real difference while celebrating four decades of impact with the Jingle Bell Run. Let's lace up, hit the pavement, and jingle our way toward victory over arthritis!

name: 2025 Seattle Ghost Marathon, Half & 50K
description:
November 29, 2025, will be the 40th running of the Seattle Ghost Marathon.  It started in 1985 when the Seattle Marathon changed courses and moved from Saturday to Sunday of Thanksgiving weekend.

The course is a very flat and fast certified Boston Marathon qualifier.  The marathon is comprised of two 13.1-mile loops run on streets and sidewalks along scenic Lake Washington in Seattle, WA.

The race start/finish is at the Ferdinand St Boat Launch (47.557338, -122.262188) 5018 Lake Washington Blvd. S, Seattle, WA 98118.  It runs south with a clockwise loop of scenic Seward Park and back north to the start/finish area.  It continues north along Lake Washington through Leschi.  The north turnaround is just past the Madrona Drive intersection (47.613496, -122.281265) then you run south back to the start/finish.  There are aid stations every 3.1 miles on each loop.

The race is managed and supported by two non-profit groups.  NW Ultras has been the driving force behind the event since 2004 and Green Lake Crew has supported the event since 2013.  It is limited to 450 total participants regardless of which event they run.  

Packet pickup is on race day.

No dogs are strollers are permitted on the course due to the sidewalk sections.

See more details on www.nwultras.com

name: 2026 Get Outside 5k Fun Run
description:
Join us for a community-wide "Get Outside" 5k Fun Run, Saturday, January 24th at 9:30AM- we'll be at the Port of Skagit Trails!

With special thanks to Skagit Runners, this family-friendly event benefits the Boys & Girls Clubs of Skagit County, helping provide vital out-of-school programs and summer club scholarships for local youth while promoting healthy lifestyles!

The trail is gravel packed terrain with slight inclines and descents within a wooded landscape and airport.  Some areas of the trail narrow in and some may have softer ground, so be prepared to navigate the elevation and terrain as you support the Clubs!

Runner check-in opens at 8 AM (grab a treat or beverage from True North Bakery to fuel your run)

Race is chip timed.

Everyone is invited to come move with us and celebrate the day together!

Bring your family, rally your friends, and let's make this winter race one to remember while impacting your local youth with greater opportunities this summer!

All proceeds directly benefit Boys & Girls Clubs of Skagit County, a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit EIN: 91-1670669.  

Learn more about the Boys & Girls Clubs of Skagit County here: https://skagitclubs.org/. 

We are looking forward to this day full of movement, laughter, and community spirit with you!  See you at the starting line!

name: 24 Hours of Riverside
description: The 24 Hours of Riverside is a 24 Hour Mountain Bike Race taking place Memorial Day Weekend 2025 at Riverside State Park in Spokane WA.  But there's so much more!  It will be a weekend of riding and camping and fun that you will never forget!  Race starts at High Noon on Saturday.  There will be food and beverage options on-site at different times throughout weekend. Camping on-site as well.  And don't forget the Kid's Bike Parade Saturday Night!  So much fun in 24 hours, you'll be sad it's only 24 hours!

name: 3rd Annual Turkey Trot
description:
Join us for our 3rd annual Turkey Trot benefitting Country Roads Animal Sanctuary and Willapa Harbor Health Foundation.  Registration is $25 and includes snacks and a drink from Wild Pines Coffee plus a event t-shirt. 


Country Roads Animal Sanctuary is a dedicated refuge for animals in need, providing rescue, rehabilitation, and lifelong care to creatures of all kinds. Based on the belief that every animal deserves love, respect, and a safe environment, the sanctuary serves as both a haven for rescued animals and a hub for community education and engagement.

 

 

From neglected farm animals to abandoned household pets, the sanctuary is committed to giving each resident a second chance at life. Animals receive quality veterinary care, proper nutrition, and enrichment, ensuring their physical and emotional well-being. For those who can be rehomed, the organization works tirelessly to place them in loving, forever homes.

 

Core Values:

• Compassion: Putting the well-being of animals first in everything we do.

• Community: Building connections and fostering education to inspire kindness and responsible animal care.

• Stewardship: Maintaining high standards of care for the animals, land, and resources entrusted to us.

 

Country Roads Animal Sanctuary also offers educational programs to raise awareness about animal welfare, sustainable farming, and the importance of ethical treatment of all living beings. The organization thrives on community support, with volunteers, donors, and advocates playing a vital role in its success.

Whether you’re looking to adopt, volunteer, or donate, Country Roads Animal Sanctuary invites you to join their mission to make the world a better place for animals, one life at a time.

name: 5K Run, Walk, & Roll
description:
Back by popular demand! Join us for ASAPC’s 3rd Annual Community 5K: “Run, Walk, Roll” to help bring awareness to Early Support for Infants and Toddlers! 

WHO CAN PARTICIPATE? The ASAPC Community 5K, Run, Walk, & Roll Early Support for Infants and Toddlers Awareness Event is an event for ALL families in Pierce County and the surrounding areas! 

WHEN: Saturday, May 10th, 2025

WHERE: Bradley Lake Park, 531 31st Avenue SE, Puyallup WA 98374

WHY: The purpose of this event is to raise the importance of Early Support Services for infants and toddlers. A Step Ahead in Pierce County (ASAPC) has been committed to supporting families of infants and toddlers of all abilities by enhancing their development and relationships both at home and in their community. We aim to empower families with children from birth to age three who have developmental delays or are at risk for delays by equipping them with resources, service coordination, caregiver support, transition information, and therapeutic and/or educational services. 

Our vision is a community that embraces and integrates children of all abilities and treasures the unique gifts each child possesses.

name: 8th Annual Maple Valley Turkey Trot: Thanksgiving Day 5K
description:
Join us for the 8th Annual Maple Valley Turkey Trot 5K presented benefiting the Maple Valley Food Bank! Register by end of day November 1 to guarantee your race day t-shirt. Sign ups after November 1 do not guarantee a shirt.
___

The Maple Valley Turkey Trot is a FUN walk or trot Thanksgiving morning through Lake Wilderness Park organized with the intention of coming together as a community during the Thanksgiving holiday to help those in need.

Children in strollers are not required to register (but will not receive shirts). All proceeds raised will go to fund Maple Valley Food Bank Programs as we enter into our organization's busiest season. All ages are welcome! We encourage Thanksgiving costumes & accessories!
___

Thank you to all of our sponsors, for making this great community event possible!

 

PRESENTING SPONSOR

TBD

 

GOLD LEVEL SPONSORS

TBD

 

SILVER LEVEL SPONSORS

TBD

 

BRONZE LEVEL SPONSORS

TBD

Interested in Sponsoring the Turkey Trot? Email carl@maplevalleyfoodbank.org

___

Advanced Packet Pickup
TBD!

Day-Of Schedule
- Packet pick-up will begin at 7:30 AM on race day. Come early to grab coffee and snacks, and take photos in our photo booth (and with our giant turkey)! There's plenty to do and we'll have music keep up the energy!
- The race will begin at the Beach House at Lake Wilderness Park promptly at 9:00.
- Race route: https://www.mapmyrun.com/routes/view/6296717431

Parking
Please utilize the lower parking lots at the Lake Wilderness Lodge, nearest the arboretum, or the park parking lots specifically. Upper lots near the lodge will be closed off for safety on the route.

Chip Timing
This event will NOT be timed. A fun-run in its fullest form!

Strollers, Dogs, Bikes, and Water
We encourage the use of jogging strollers along the route of this family-friendly 5K. However, out of consideration for other participants, dogs will not be allowed on the course (with the exception of service dogs). For the safety and convenience of all participants, bikes are NOT permitted, as this is a fairly narrow out and back course. We will have water stations near the beach house before and after the race.

Accessibility
Please note that, while generally flat, this race course may not be suitable for all abilities, as the terrain is both paved and gravel. There is a slight incline to access the Green to Cedar River Trail from the arboretum. We will have volunteers stationed at these points to assist on an as-needed basis.

___
Race Contact Info
If you have any additional questions about this race, please contact Jon Cantalini at info@maplevalleyfoodbank.org 

Tickets are non-transferable and non-refundable.

name: A Merry Christmas Run 5K/10K/13.1 SEATTLE
description:
🎅 🎄  Join the Christmas Run! 🎄 🎅

Jingle All the Way: A Merry Christmas Run!" is a delightful Holiday run that reminds us of the true essence of Christmas – spreading love, giving selflessly, and cherishing the joy of togetherness with family, friends, and even strangers, all while getting a run in before the Christmas festivities! 

 

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal!

name: Alexander's Hope Valentine's Day Dash
description:
The Alexander's Hope Valentine's Day Dash 5k run/walk is back for the 7th year! 

Dogs & strollers are both welcome at the race! Our race will start & finish at Downtown Bellevue Park & run along the streets of Bellevue!

All funds raised will go to support the local 501(c)(3) nonprofit - Alexander's Hope which advocates for organ donation awareness and helps fund local, lifesaving youth heart screenings.

name: Anacortes Santa Run
description:
Every runner receives a full Santa Suit for the run!   Yes, that's right. EVERYONE will run in a Santa Suit. 

Join other runners all dressed as Santa and run a 5k in beautiful Anacortes WA.

Family Discount!!! Register 3 or more runners on same account and save $5.00 per runner!!!!

December 6, 2025 9am Start

 

Pick Up Bibs and Santa Suits in Anacortes:

Dec 4 and 5 from 5-7pm at the Anacortes Rockfish Grill beer garden!! Enjoy the happy hour from 3-6. Rockfish Address is 320 Commercial Ave, Anacortes WA 98221 (beer garden is the tent behind the restaurant)

 

Race Day Pick up ($3) is for out of the area runners. (You can pick up your Bib and Santa suit from 7-8am day of race.) If you can make the pick up on the 4th and 5th, we'd love it.

 

Every registration will help fund the Anacortes High School Cross Country Team!!!


5k Run of Santas in Anacortes WA. 

  • Group start-with Christmas Carols
  • Cookies, Coffee, Hot Cocoa and treats
  • timed
  • finishers medal
  • Prize!!!!- 1 Gallon of delicious Eggnog for first male and female across the finish line
  • Beat the Elves. Compete against two elves (Anacortes High School XC runners) staring 5 minutes after you. Every elf beating Santa gets a sticker. 

The Course is a beautiful flat 5k around Cap Sante Marina.

name: Auburn Turkey Trot 5K
description:
Join us at Sunset Park in Lakeland Hills, Auburn on Thanksgiving morning for a family-friendly 5K run/walk!  The race will begin and end at the park and follow a nearly flat route through the heart of Lakeland Hills.  The Auburn Turkey Trot is a FUN walk, run, or TROT, organized with the intention of coming together as a Community during the Thanksgiving Holiday to support students and families through the programming of the Auburn Public Schools Foundation.   We encourage Thanksgiving costumes & accessories! We look forward to kicking off the Holiday Season with you ALL!

Pre-schoolers & Strollers are welcome and do not need to register!  

Dogs are not allowed on the course due to insurance constraints!

Chip Timing - This event will not be timed!  It is a FUN-RUN in its fullest form.  

You can find parking at the Chase or Haggen near Sunset Park. Race will start promptly at 9am!

The route is two loops from Sunset Park, to Lakeland hills Elementary and back up to Sunset Park via Lakeland Hills way. 

HAGGEN AFTER PARTY: Upon completion of your walk or run, please gather at the Haggen PUB for donuts, prize drawings, and team awards!  Must be present to win! Thank you, Haggen Food and Pharmacy, for hosting APSF Turkey Trotters!

name: Bainbridge Island Parks & Trails Foundation Trillium Trail Run
description:
Bainbridge Island's beloved spring running event is back!

Join Bainbridge Island Parks & Trails Foundation in running or walking a 10K or 5K on a scenic wooded course from Battle Point Park, along the Forest to Sky Trail, and looping among the towering firs of the Grand Forest. An early Kids Fun Run course is within Battle Point Park.

Run for the Trails

Trillium Trail Run will launch the Foundation’s “Trails Connect Bainbridge Island” campaign, to build four new signature trails around the island: the Lost Valley Trail, nexus of the east-west, cross-island trail route from Winslow to Gazzam Lake; Sunny Hill to Nutes Pond Trail; and the Waypoint Woods gateway trail. All race proceeds benefit trail development. 
Race packets, including timing chip-integrated bib, will be distributed the morning of the event.

name: Beat the Blerch
description:
Beat The Blerch is a 5K, 10K, half, and full marathon created by The Oatmeal and inspired by this comic about running.

Our Carnation, Washington race will take place in a quaint little town located about 35 minutes outside of Seattle. 

It begins at King County’s Tolt MacDonald Park, and it’s a beautiful flat, out-and-back course that winds its way through evergreen, mossy forests along the Snoqualmie valley trail. Near the starting line of the race are strawberry farms and pumpkin patches, which offer guided tours in case you’re still up for a bit of walking after the race.

name: Big Hurt
description:
The Big Hurt is a multi-sport race that includes four legs and participants can race solo in Iron Division or as a relay team. Big Hurt is unique in that all transitions are at the same location, making for an all-day party atmosphere. Even better, the transition is located on the beautiful waterfront in downtown Port Angeles. Race legs include:

* A 15-mile mountain bike that takes place in the foothills above Port Angeles (10-mile mountain bike, 5 miles on road downhill to downtown Port Angeles race hub for transition to kayak leg)
* A 2.6-mile kayak in Port Angeles Harbor
* A 30-mile road bike that goes west out of Port Angeles and crosses the Elwha River and visits Freshwater Bay, as well as the lower parts of Kelly Ridge on Dan Kelly and Eden Valley Roads.
* A 10K Run, out and back on the Olympic Discovery Trail along the waterfront

Full Big Hurt info here. 

Please make note of our very specific KAYAK REQUIREMENTS - click here to review. Also note that we will NO LONGER ALLOW PADDLEBOARD in the kayak leg. Also note that you cannot pick up your kayak until 3pm - please plan your day accordingly. From 3-4pm you can hand carry your kayak out to wherever you have parked in the downtown area. Starting at 4pm you can drive into the drop off/pick up lot to pick up your kayak.

BRAND NEW!! THE BIG HURT PODCAST. Our very own cast of characters – the Big Hurt Committee – discussing what you will find on the courses, and giving you all sorts of race information and tips.

Listen on:  Spotify    Apple    Amazon

Team Division Categories: Regular (3-4 team members), Masters (3-4 team members all age 50+), Tandem (2 team members), Company Team (no more than 1 member that does not work for the company), and High School (high school students age 15 and up - can include one adult team member). 

The prices of the event are:

Iron Divison:

  • Early bird through December 31: $85
  • January 1 - August 31: $95
  • Sept 1 - Sept 25: $105

Teams:

  • Early bird through December 31: $60 (High School $30)
  • January 1 - April 30: $69 (High School $35)
  • May 1 - August 31: $75 (High School $40)
  • September 1 - Sept 25: $85 (High School $45)

name: Big River Race
description:
Come join us for the Third Annual Year of the Big River Race!

 

 Saturday, May 30th, 2026 for a Half Marathon, 10k, 5k & FREE Fun 1 Mile. Run along one of Eastern Washington's biggest landmarks, the Columbia River. Enjoy a scenic route on paved riverfront trail. This race offers you four different options; a distance for everyone in the family, group of friends or coworkers.
 
The course will be flat & fast! Perfect for your first time to achieve one of these distances or set a new personal goal. The race will start & end at beautiful Chiawana Park (west end of the park) in Pasco, Washington. Chiawana is a Native word for “Big River”.

 
The Columbia River has provided this region's culture and economy for thousands of years. It is the largest river in the Pacific Northwest. The river forms in the Rocky Mountains of British Columbia, Canada and flows through Washington. This Big River irrigates more than 6,000,000 acres of agricultural land. Agriculture is huge part of our community and is possible because of this valuable water source.
 
The race course will have fun, themed aid-stations, cheer squads & music along the way. You run the miles, we bring the entertainment and support! We believe your achievements should be celebrated. Invite all the friends and family to come watch you cross the finish line! Chiawana Park as beautiful shade trees, a big grassy park and a gorgeous view of the river. After the race sit, relax and enjoy some post race treats.
 


Our race values come from the meaning: Chiawana
•compassion • creativity • reliability • generosity • loyalty

name: Birch Bay Road Race
description:
Run along the beautiful shores of Birch Bay at the Birch Bay Road Race! You’ll spot eagles and herons as you run or walk along our USATF certified courses. Birch Bay is a seaside village close to the Canadian border, just two hours from Seattle and an hour and a half from Vancouver, BC. Stay at Semiahmoo Resort and make a weekend out of it! Running groups and teams are invited to sign up for the Club Challenge. Walkers are welcome.

Race Website: https://orcarunning.com/birchbay/

Interested in signing up for more than one Orca Running race? Check out the Orca Running/Evergreen Trails Bundle options. Find out more here!

description:
Raise the Bar Events is excited to present the 2025 Black Diamond Olympic Tri, Olympic Aquabike, Sprint Tri & Olympic and Sprint Relays
 
Triathletes will swim in picture perfect Deep Lake at Nolte State Park followed by rolling, elevation-friendly bike & run courses winding through the sleepy communities of Ravensdale, Selleck, and the farmlands of Enumclaw.

 

All participants will receive a medal, race tee, and a hot meal! Podium finishers will receive pint glasses. 
 
Raise the Bar has managed a team of multisport athletes since 2004. Out of that group emerged a knowledgeable and energetic event staff who bring their passion and racing experience to event production.  In addition to them, our team of 200+  athletes race and volunteer in great numbers - giving RTB events a community-friendly vibe and excellent execution. Come race with us!

name: BRRC 43rd St. Paddy’s Five Miler
description:
Come and race, ye lads and lasses! The 2026 BRRC 43rd St. Paddy's 5 Miler will be a jig of a time.  By popular demand, the St. Paddy's 5 Miler is back again at Spokane Community College on March 8, 2026. The same out & back route as last year 2025. This is an official qualifying race for 2nd SEEDING at BLOOMSDAY 2026.  Qualifying times: Women 37:00 and Men 31:00. At 10:30 am there will be a FREE  "Lucky Leprechaun Jig" for kids 6 years old and under. All runners in the Leprechaun Jig will receive a Ribbon.  At 11:00 am there will be an Awards ceremony; Overall Male & Female, Masters (40+) Top Male & Female. Top 3 Male & Female in age groups 0-10,11-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70-79, 80+.  At 11:15 am there will be prize drawings including a $250 cash prize plus other prizes. MUST be present to WIN!

Normal Registration:

  • $35 registration with unisex shirt through February 20th ($3 extra for 2XL & 3XL)
  • $20 for run only with no shirt option
  • $20 after February 20th with NO Shirt option, must be received by March 6th or at SCC on Race Day
  • $30 Day of Race Registration NO SHIRT
  • All Mail-in entries must be received by February 20th to receive a shirt or March 6th with no shirt

Leprechaun Jig Registration:

  • Event is free for the Lucky Leprechaun Jig for those 6 years old and younger
  • Youth shirts can be ordered separately for $13 through February 20th
  • All Mail-in entries must be received by February 20th to receive a shirt or March 6th with no shirt

Packet Pickup

  • Saturday, March 7, 2026 from 10-2:00 PM at MUV Fitness, 14927 E. Sprague
  • Sunday, March 8th, 2026 day of race, at 8:00 am at SCC. 

The Start

  • Rest rooms provided in the gymnasium building
  • The race will offer a gun start at 9:00 am. 
  • Kids, 6 years and under, can run the Lucky Leprechaun Jig (approx. 50 meters) that will start at 10:30 am.

The Finish

  • There will be water at the finish line and at the turn around
  • Top Male and Female, Top Masters (40+) Male and Female awards
  • Top 3 in Age Groups Male & Female: 0-10, 11-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70-79, 80+
  • Stay around for $250 Cash Prize plus other drawings at 11:15 am. Must be present to WIN!

name: BRRC Thanksgiving Turkey Trot
description:
Happy Thanksgiving 2025

Continue the Spirit and Tradition of the BRRC Family Friendly Thanksgiving Fun Run/Walk by participating in the Annual BRRC Turkey Trot on Thanksgiving Day at Manito Park Duck Pond (https://my.spokanecity.org/parks/major/manito/).  We want to continue the tradition of the giving season. 

There is no entry fee to participate in the Turkey Trot.  Registration process is only for donations with all donations going to 2nd Harvest Food Bank in Spokane. 

There will be prize Drawing at 10:00 AM that morning.

Cash donations are accepted on Run Sign Up.  Sign-on to the website ( https://runsignup.com/Race/WA/Spokane/BRRCAnnualTurkeyTrot ), click on DONATION and complete the information.  Cash donations or food donations to the 2ND Harvest Food Bank will be accepted at the event on Thanksgiving morning.  The food bank has seven times the buying power than we do. (A$5.00 donation will buy $35.00 worth of food). 

We are Thankful for You and Your Family this Holiday season, so don’t delay, join BRRC and all your friends.  In addition to registering and donating on line, you can also register for this year's BRRC Turkey Trot in-person at Manito Park.  Carpooling is strongly advised due to limited parking at Manito Park.  Arrive early to sign the waiver prior to the event.  For the safety of the participants, please have your dogs on a leash.

name: BRRC's Recycle Fun Run 2026
description:
The four-mile run benefits the BRRC volunteer program.  Please bring your gently used shoes and clothing for donation to high school athletes in the area. Fish Lake Trail Head: The trailhead is near Government Way and Sunset Hwy.  Take I-90 to Exit 279 for US-195 S toward Colfax/Pullman. Continue on 195 for 0.3 miles, then turn right onto W. 16th Avenue, which turns into S. Lindeke St. Continue on Lindeke until you see the parking lot on the right, about another 0.5 miles. Trailhead is near Government Way and Sunset Hwy.  Parking is limited, so please car-pool. 

From the Spokane trailhead, the route follows a mild uphill grade. The bridge crosses over the I-90 Freeway. On your left, trees separate you from US 195 for a couple miles and then from Cheney Spokane Road, which loosely parallels the trail. Half-mile markers guide you through the dry uplands of Eastern Washington. The trail follows a piece of corridor of the Oregon–Washington Railroad & Navigation Company (a division of the Union Pacific Railroad) through the Latah Valley, formerly Hangman Valley. At Marshall Canyon, take in railroad history as you travel beside active rail lines through the area known by rail fans as "The Tunnel."

name: Cascade Express Marathon & Half Marathon
description:
A Premier Boston Qualifying Course in the Pacific Northwest!

WITH JUST UNDER 1500' OF DOWNHILL, THERE'S NO BOSTON TIME PENALTY!!

This course is a premier Boston Qualifying Course, with a high BQ rate! Enjoy 26.2 miles of flat and then scenic downhill with a gorgeous view of the Cascade Mountains as you glide down the gravel trail on this point-to-point course. This is the ONLY marathon course that features jaw-dropping views as you run along Keechelus Lake. With just under 1500’ of gradual net downhill, we assure you that you will “find your super fast” on the way to a speedy time, PR, or BQ!

The Cascade Express Half is one of the fastest half-marathon courses in the country! Enjoy 13.1 miles of scenic downhill with a gorgeous view of the Cascade Mountains as you glide down the gravel trail on this point-to-point course. This is the ONLY  half-marathon course that features a run through the famous 2.4-mile Snoqualmie Tunnel. With 800’ of gradual net downhill, we assure you that you will “find your super fast” on the way to a speedy time or a PR!

Enjoy your finish with a custom medal, a tech shirt, and a drop bag.

Marathon is a Boston Qualifier USATF 
Half Marathon is also certified

name: Chilly Chili 5K, Team Awards and Chili Competition
description:
Bloomsday Road Runners Club's (BRRC) is proud to announce the return of the BRRC Chilly Chili 5K. The BRRC Chilly Chili 5k will be held at the Spokane County Moran Prairie Grange in 2026. Whether you run, walk or take refuge in the Grange, we will reward you for your efforts by hosting a Chili Competition, an Awards Ceremony and Music.  As BRRC has always done, we will have a gun start with a chip timed finish. The starting line will be in the parking lot of the Moran Prairie Grange, turning right onto 61st Ave heading west. Then turn left at S. Freya St. heading South to 65th Ave where you will turn right heading West on 65th until you get to get to S. Regal Rd at which time you will turn Left heading South.  You will run down a hill and then back up a hill to the turn around at the top of the hill where there will be a water station, make the turn around and run the same course back to the finish at the Grange.  In the Grange you will have the comfort of a heated facility, Chili and hot/cold drinks during the awards presentation.

Registration:

  • $25 General online Race Registration, includes Chili Cook-Off Competition, Awards and Music.   $30 Day of Race Registration, includes Chili Cook-Off Competition, Awards and Music.
  • $0 Runner's Party online Event Registration for Chilly Feed and Competition, Awards and Music. BYOB Drinks. (Run not included with this registration).

Packet Pick-Up:

  • Saturday, January 24, 2026 12:30 to 1:45 pm at Moran Prairie Grange

The Start:

  • Starting line will be in the parking lot of the Moran Prairie Grange

The Finish:

  • Overall awards for the 5k race will be given to 1st place Male and Female
  • Top 3 in Age Groups Male & Female: 0-7, 8-12, 13-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70-79, 80+
  • Cross Country Team awards and 5K Race results will be announced 
  • Stay around for the Running Team's Chili Cook-Off, Awards Ceremony and Music. There will be Running Team Chili Cook-off awards 1-4 place.  Delicious Cinnamon Rolls and Hot Drinks will be provided along with the Chili.

name: Cinco De Mayo Run 5K/10K/13.1 SEATTLE
description:
🌶️🏃‍♂️ Run Against All Odds: Cinco de Mayo Run! 🌟

This Cinco de Mayo, challenge yourself and celebrate resilience, community, and culture with the Cinco de Mayo Run Against All Odds! Whether you’re running for fun or for fitness, this event is all about pushing limits and embracing the spirit of overcoming obstacles—just like the holiday itself! 

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack

name: Cirque Series - Crystal Mountain, WA
description:
Join us at Cirque Series at Crystal Mountain.  7.9 miles featuring 2,614' ft vert.

Prizes
Prizes will be distributed at the end of each race and for the overall series winners. There are three categories in which the prizes will be given out: Sport, Expert and Pro.  Prizes for each race are as follows:

Pro 
1st place - $1000 cash each race
2nd place - $250 cash each race
3rd place - $150 cash each race

Expert 
1st - $400 in Gear each race
2nd - $250 in Gear each race
3rd - $150 in Gear each race

Sport 
1st - $300 in Gear each race
2nd - $200 in Gear each race
3rd - $100 in Gear each race

Grom Award - youngest competitor will be recognized.

OG Award - wisest competitor will be recognized.

Lexie Award - the "unofficial MVP" of the race will be recognized.

Middle of the Pack Award - the person that finished exactly middle will be recognized.

Overall 2026 Season Winner + Points
The racers with the most points at the end of all races will be declared the overall 2025 winner.  The top 20 racers of each event will obtain points. The following is the per stage breakdown as a function of place:

1 - 50pt    6 - 30pt    11 - 20pt 16 - 10pt 
2 - 40pt    7 - 28pt    12 - 18pt 17 - 8pt
3 - 36pt    8 - 26pt    13 - 16pt 18 - 6pt
4 - 34pt    9 - 24pt    14 - 14pt 19 - 4pt
5 - 32pt    10 - 22pt    15 - 12pt 20 - 2pt

PRIZE MONEY 2026 OVERALL SEASON STANDINGS   **Men's & Women's
PRO
PEAK FREAK Belt Buckle - Overall 2026 season
PEAK FREAK Belt Buckle - Overall 2026 season
PEAK FREAK Belt Buckle - Overall 2026 season

EXPERT
1ST - PEAK FREAK Belt Buckle - Overall 2026 season 
2ND- PEAK FREAK Belt Buckle - Overall 2026 season 
3RD- PEAK FREAK Belt Buckle - Overall 2026 season

SPORT
1ST - PEAK FREAK Belt Buckle - Overall 2026 season 
2ND- PEAK FREAK Belt Buckle - Overall 2026 season 
3RD- PEAK FREAK Belt Buckle - Overall 2026 season

**Everyone that runs six 2026 Cirque Series races will receive a Cirque Series 2026 PEAK FREAK belt buckle. 

Registration
We are capping the race at 700 entries, we encourage to sign up right away.

LODGING - LOGE Alta Crystal is located 15 minutes down the road from the mountain. Heated pool, hot tub, & free shuttle service. LOGE Alta Crystal is more than a place to stay, it's basecamp for adventure & connection. Inspired by the surf, climbing, & camping culture of the 70s, & the laid-back energy of a road trip with friends. BOOK (15% auto-applied): LOGE ALTA CRYSTAL

Looking to stay right at the base of the mountain, all Cirque Series participants are invited to stay at LOGE’s sister property Crystal Mountain Hotels, offering comfort and convenience, just 5 minute walk to the mountain and onsite food options. Crystal Mountain Hotels BOOK (15% auto-applied): CRYSTAL MT. HOTELS

Bibs / Timing Chips
Cirque Series will utilize Competitive timing to time the event with a disposable chip placed on the back of your bib. Please do not fold, crush or remove the chip from the bib. You may dispose of the chip/bib after the race is over.

Rules / Guidelines
Please help us preserve the beauty of our mountains and assist in maintaining an enjoyable, safe event for everyone involved.

Please respect private property near the trails. Do not trespass.
No littering: Participants are encouraged to carry water and food during the event.
Please dispose of all waste and recyclables in the proper containers.
Please be respectful of all Forest Service officials.
Do not impede another runner.
Leave no trace: Pack-in pack-out.

We will provide SKRATCH hydration at aid stations & finish line.

julian@cirqueseries.com

name: Climb for The Cure 2026
description:
Climb for the Cure is a timed Gravel race to the summit of Mt. Spokane.

The race aims to raise money and awareness about the life-changing work being conducted at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

Race Details
Start: Big Barn Brewery
Summit Mt. Spokane
Ends: Big Barn Brewery
‍
Whole New Routes: View Here

Race Day: June 14st, 2026
Start Times: 7:00 AM - 9:00 AM
Race is on: rain or shine
‍
Official chip-timed race.
‍A Routes Recommended for:
‍A Route: Intermediate - Intermediate to Expert MTB/Gravel ride.
B Route: Moderate to Intermediate riders
E-Bike is open class

 

*ATTN: Corporate Cup or Teams: riders must have a minimum of four (4) racers, and the team captain must register for the Corporate Cup Route to invite other team members. Teams can be any size beyond the minimum four, but the fastest four combined finish times win the Corporate Cup in 2025.

name: Coffee Lovers and Chocolate Lovers 5K & 10K
description:
Join us for a one-of-a-kind Pacific Northwest experience where we bring together two of life’s greatest pleasures — coffee and chocolate! On Sunday, January 18, 2026, lace up and take in the scenic beauty of the Sumner Link Trail with fellow runners and walkers.

After your miles, treat yourself to the perfect pairing — freshly brewed coffee from our friends at Keurig Dr Pepper and handcrafted chocolate delights from Puyallup Chocolates. It’s the perfect blend of movement, flavor, and community — a truly sweet celebration you won’t want to miss!

name: Coffee Lovers Run 5K/10K/13.1 SEATTLE
description:
☕️For all the Coffee Lovers, this run is for you!

You’ll love the shirt we send you. Set a goal, bring a friend, and join this super fun 5K/10K/13.1 Half-Marathon!

 

Overview:

Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.

This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)
Yes, but please note that it takes time for us to ship your shirt. Your shirt will likely arrive after the run. You can wear any shirt you find appropriate to run the race! 
 
Wave Times: (Email Us Your Desired Wave Time: info@thebestraces.com)
(Waves filled on a First Come, First Serve Basis)
Wave A: 7:30AM
Wave B: 8:00AM
Wave C: 8:30AM
Late runners can run upon arrival (Please note our coordinators stay 3 hours after the first wave)
Are there any other Questions we missed?
https://www.thebestraces.com/faq/
Virtual Run Option:
- Our Virtual Run uniquely offers a Training Pack with Digital Tools to support your run. 
Virtual runs can be done any time and place of your choosing using any tracking device (optional). After you finish, you can submit your results to info@thebestraces.com to receive your medal! 
Race Bundle:
Sign-up for more races and get a discount! 

Sponsorships & Promoting your Business:

If you're looking to become a sponsor, we'd love showcase your business!
https://www.thebestraces.com/events
 

Team Glo Volunteers:

If you're interested in helping put on runs for the Community and helping people achieve their goals, we invite you to join our team of volunteers, fill out the form here: https://www.thebestraces.com/volunteer-form/
 

Be part of the Journey!

Our Charity Initiatives. Find out more @ www.thebestracesjourney.com
Keep running. Every mile you log after the race, we'll donate $1 to one of the charities we work with! (Note that Fundraising is Optional)

name: Couve Clover Run
description:
RUN, GIVE BACK & PARTY on Vancouver’s Waterfront!
Join us for the 12th Annual Couve Clover Run and celebrate in your festive green while running or walking 3, 7 or 10 miles along an extremely fast and scenic course to support local charities! We will make you earn your post-event party, but it will be off the charts hosted by Why Racing Events and other downtown Vancouver Pubs & Breweries.

We believe this is one of the prettiest courses in the Northwest! We’ve designed the 3 miles, Lucky 7 miles and 10-mile courses to take you through some of the most scenic areas of Vancouver and it really highlights our wonderful community including historic Officer’s Row, Fort Vancouver, the Columbian Riverfront, and more. The course is mostly flat with a couple of short hills.

name: Donut Dash 5k
description:
Dash for your donut at the Donut Dash 5K and 1K fun run for kids.

A fast and flat course around Capitol Lake and out and back along Deschutes Parkway.

Race starts and finishes at Heritage Park in Olympia, WA.

 

Be sure to register early to guarantee your spot. The race is limited to 400 participants and we sold out in 2025!

5K

Saturday, March 14, 2026 at Fleet Feet from 2 to 4 pm. 3405 Capitol Blvd SE, Olympia, WA 98501

name: Dugan's Run
description:
Dugan's Run is a long standing fun run hosted by Dugan's Pizza in Ocean Shores since 1985, in which a portion of the course is on the beach of Ocean Shores and we have a race for everyone! Check in to pick up race numbers, and T-Shirts Saturday, March 21st 2:00pm - 5:00pm and race day morning Sunday, March 22nd from 8:00am - 9:30am. Races start with the Kid's Dash at 10:00am, followed by the Youth Mile, then 5K, and awards ceremony will be held at Dugan's Pizza after the races conclude. 

This event is all about having a good time and enjoying friends, family, running is not required! Your 4-legged leashed walking/running companion is welcome to join in.  

ONLINE Registration: 12/01/2025 - 03/20/2026 
IN PERSON Registration and bib pick-up held at Dugan's Pizza: Sat 03/21/2026 (2:00pm-5:00pm) & Sun 03/22/2026 (8:00am-9:30am) 

*PLEASE ENSURE PARTICIPANTS ARE REGISTERED IN THE RACE FOR THEIR AGE GROUP*

  • KID'S DASH (10 & UNDER)
    • FREE Registration

name: FORGE
description:
FORGE Backyard Ultra

  • Run a 4.167-mile loop every hour on the hour for 12 hours
  • Complete all 12 loops and you'll have run 50 miles
  • Miss the start or don’t finish in time? Your FORGE is over.

Everyone is celebrated but we will have winners: Male and Female 1. fastest total time & 2. final loop winner

Space is limited. Secure your spot today.

Date: June 6, 2026

Location: Trails and dirt roads south of Swinomish Casino, Skagit County, WA

Start Time: 7:00 AM

All Runners will receive:

  • FORGE running hat
  • FORGE hoodie
  • FORGEd custom medal(finisher prize)
  • Day of race food and snacks, Tailwind Nutrition Endurance Fuel.
  •  
FORGE is a race built around a unique and growing format known as the "backyard ultra." Unlike traditional races where runners aim for a set distance or time, backyard ultras follow a simple but demanding structure: runners complete a 4.167-mile loop every hour, on the hour. Whatever time remains after finishing a lap becomes their rest period before starting again at the top of the next hour. This continues until the event reaches its predetermined duration—in FORGE’s case, 12 hours.
The format is gaining popularity worldwide because it removes the pressure of speed and replaces it with a test of endurance, pacing, and mental toughness. Fast runners and steady runners line up together every hour. Everyone starts at the same time, and the race unfolds differently for each participant. Some will aim for a personal-best distance, while others will push to complete all 12 laps.
One of the most unique aspects of this style of racing is the community it creates. The time between laps—when runners gather, recover, and prepare for the next start—becomes a shared experience. Conversations happen. Encouragement is exchanged. Whether you’re completing your first backyard-style event or chasing a new personal milestone, you’re not doing it alone.

 

At its core, FORGE is about stepping into a challenge and discovering what you’re capable of. There’s no finish line waiting for you at a set distance—just another lap, another opportunity to push forward. It’s an event designed to be hard, but also to be welcoming, rewarding, and deeply memorable.

name: Fort Steilacoom Resolution Series
description:
EVENT CALENDAR

January 10, 2026 – 5K and 10K 
February 7, 2026 – 5K, 10K, 15K 
March 7, 2026 – 5K, 10K, 20K

 

PRE-REGISTRATION: Available through Weds prior to Event

Individual Events:  5K - $30, All Other Distances -  $35
Age Group Discount (19 and under): 5K - $10, all other distances - $15

Series Bundles:

Participants may bundle their registration as a 5K series (5K-5K-5K) - $75, 10K Series (10K-10K-10K) - $90, or a Progression Series (10K-15K-20K) - $90,   Participants can also receive a $10 discount when bundling 3 individual events.  This allows you to design your own series at a discounted rate from individual entries. 
Purchase peace of mind with Event Insurance available at checkout through a third-party entity.  This entitles you to a full refund of your pre-registration costs for 18 covered reasons including injury, illness, weather, mechanical breakdowns, layoffs etc...
 

DAY OF RACE REGISTRATION: Available starting 1 hour prior

5K - $38 
All Other Distances - $43
19 and under: $15 for 5K, $20 for all other distances
Series bundle registration also available on Jan 4 from 8-9AM starting at $90 for the 5K Series and $105 for the longer series.
 

AGE GROUPS

0-14, 15-19, 20-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65-69, 70-74, 75-79, 80-85, 85-90, 90-94
 

PARKING AND PACKET PICKUP

Plenty of parking is available on site within the park. Signage will direct participants to parking and packet pickup.  
 

COURSE DESCRIPTION

All events utilize a flat and fast 5K loop within Fort Steilacoom Park.  The course is 95% paved with 5% packed trail.  Participants will have access to our aid station (water, electrolytes and restrooms) at the conclusion of each 5K loop.  Participants of the 10K, 15K, and 20K events will repeat the 5K loop.  Each mile will be clearly marked on the 5K loop.  Course map can be found here. 
 

RACE DAY SCHEDULE 

08:00 — Packet Pickup & Day of Race Registration open
08:55 — Registration and Packet Pickup Ends 
09:00 — Combined event start 
 

RESULTS

All events are chip-timed by Peak Performance Timing, and results will be available to finishers at our results kiosk and published to our RunSignup Results page.  
 

PHOTOS

All events will be photographed.   Event Photos are expected to be uploaded to our website by Sunday 6PM and can be downloaded for free. 
 

AWARDS

Each participant who completes 2 or more of our events will receive a custom finishers medal. Medals will be available to pick-up after you complete your second event.
Age group ribbons for each event will be awarded to top 3 in each age group. These will be available at our results kiosk near the finish line.
Overall awards will be provided to men’s and women’s winners in each distance.
 

FACILITIES

Restrooms will be available near the start, and at the conclusion of each 5k loop.  Our finish line will include numerous refreshments
 

ADVERSE WEATHER

This is a winter race series, and we are frequently confronted with cold, rain, wind and snow.  In the rare event that inclement weather forces a cancellation or postponement of the event, participants will receive an email by 7AM.  We will also make every effort to update our website and other social media resources. 
 

REGISTRATION DETAILS

Registrants are welcome to switch events on race day (for example 10K to 5K).   This can be done at packet pickup.
 
Dogs (and other leashed animals) are NOT allowed on our course.  Thank you!
Strollers are allowed. 
 

CONTACT INFORMATION

Darrin Hatcher/darrinhatcher.fsrc@gmail.com/253-720-0168

name: Frosty Moss Relay
description:
Welcome to the Green Season on the Olympic Peninsula of Washington State
Towering evergreens. Endless moss and ferns. Miles of waterfront. Snowcapped mountains. Need a cure for gray-season blues? Frosty Moss has you covered.

Pavement + Trail Runners Unite
From the Sol Duc River to Sequim Bay, the 80-mile Frosty Moss course follows the paved Olympic Discovery Trail and the singletrack Adventure Route. The 30-mile Mini Moss course begins at Ediz Hook in Port Angeles and end at Sequim Bay.

Celebrate After the Race
As if your day wasn’t epic enough, 7 Cedars Resort is ready to help you celebrate. They will host hot food, cold drinks, awards and fun after the race.

FROSTY MOSS RELAY
80 Miles – 15 Legs – Teams of 2-5
Relay legs are a mix of distances (3-11 mi) on paved or single-track trail ** Check out the Frosty Moss legs here
Wave starts 6-9 am

MINI MOSS RELAY
30 Miles - 8 Legs - Teams of 2-4 
Relay legs are a mix of distances (3-5 mi) on paved trail ** Check out the Mini Moss legs here
Wave starts 1-2 pm

FROSTY MOSS 50k (MINI MOSS SOLO)
Same route and greatness as Mini Moss, but solo! 
Start time 1pm, time cap 8.5 hours (9:30 p.m.)

REGISTRATION. Registration closes March 12, 2026 at 8:00 p.m..  

Frosty Moss: Teams of 2, 3, 4, or 5; $95 per person. Limited to 60 teams. Teams of 2-3 will be grouped for timing / awards. Teams of 4-5 will be grouped together for timing / awards. (price increase to $110 starting February 1)
Mini Moss: Teams of 2, 3, or 4; $75 per person. Limited to 45 teams.  (price increase to $85 starting February 1) 
Mini Moss 50K: $85 (price increase to $90 starting February 1) 

WHAT’S INCLUDED

In addition to an epic outdoor experience in the far northwest corner, all runners receive…

  • Swag bag of Frosty Moss Relay goodies and other surprises.
  • Comprehensive event guide, maps, course marking, and on-course race support.
  • Taco Bar and awards at the after-party at Jamestown S’Klallam Tribe’s 7 Cedars Resort.  No-host bar.
  • Bragging rights for getting after it all day on the Olympic Peninsula in winter!

WHO
You & your best running buddies—any mix of age, gender & ability, as long as your team can average a 12-minute pace or faster. Load up your team van with food, drinks, extra layers, tunes, and a fun competitive spirit. Captains, sign up and create your team, then start inviting your team members to sign up!

THE FROSTY MOSS EXPERIENCE

Frosty Mossers trace the Olympic Discovery Trail (paved multiuse path) & Adventure Route (singletrack trail) from west to east, beginning at the Camp Creek Trailhead along the Sol Duc River and finishing in Blyn at Sequim Bay. Mini Mossers follow the Olympic Discovery Trail from Ediz Hook in Port Angeles to Blyn at Sequim Bay.

You will be asked to enter the average pace of your team (minutes / mile). Be as accurate as possible. Do NOT pad your time because you are worried about making the cutoffs. If you run faster than your average pace and beat the exchange zone volunteers, you will be held and made to wait. You do not have anything to gain by padding your average pace! If your team members change over time and you need to adjust your average team pace, you can do so. 

You are welcome to use our FROSTY MOSS AVERAGE TEAM PACE CALCULATOR or MINI MOSS AVERAGE TEAM PACE CALCULATOR to help you. Please read the instructions on it first.

The team captain and 50K solo runners must attend the check-in/orientation at 7 Cedars Resort on Friday evening, March 14th. Your team can come with you, but only the team captain is required. Captains bring your Team Roster and your required night running gear.

Make sure to book your room(s) at 7 Cedars Resort - you can walk to your room right from the after party! They are offering a special rate of $169 King or Double Queen for us. To book, call the reservation agents at (360) 683-7777 Extension 1 and use the booking code FROSTY. Click here to book online. 

See the full website at: Frosty Moss Relay

To sign up - TEAM CAPTAINS -

  1. Sign up and Create your Group (Team Name)
  2. Choose your estimated average team pace (be as accurate as possible - if you register "conservative" and you end up running faster than your estimate, you will cause the race major issues in that volunteers may not be at exchanges yet. If this happens, you will not be allowed to exchange and you will have to wait for the volunteers to arrive before you can exchange and continue along the course. 
  3. SET UP A PASSWORD for your team, to prevent the general public from signing up onto your team.
  4. Let your team members know the Group/Team Name to sign up under as well as the Average Team Pace that you have chosen (they must choose the same) *you can change team members until a day and a half before the race.
  5. Plan your team theme - do it up! Costumes, care decorations, anything and everything! There will be prizes for the best Team Theme! 
  6. Follow us on social media to get race updates, including fun things like our hashtag contest with big prizes!

Refund Policy: There are no refunds for participant-initiated cancellations and no deferrals to next year. Transfers to another athlete are allowed. To transfer, follow these instructions. Transfers can be made until three days before the race. During the registration process, you will have the chance to purchase refund insurance (unavailable for Canadian racers - rules of the insurance company and not us or RunSignUp), which will allow a full refund if you are unable to attend the event due to several covered reasons including accident, illness and family emergency. Full insurance info, terms, and conditions HERE.  

If we are forced to cancel the race for any reason, participants will receive a free transfer to the following year, or an 80% refund.

name: Girlfriends Run
description:
THE GIRLFRIENDS AND PINK BRIGADE HAVE RAISED OVER $900,000 OVER THE LAST 18 YEARS!
The 20th Annual Girlfriends Run offers a Half Marathon, 10K & 6K designed specifically for women to get together to do something good for themselves and to help support a very important women’s cause.

We started this event to honor and support one of our BFFs, Joleen Skarberg, who was diagnosed with Breast Cancer and continues to run it every year with her daughters, sisters, nieces, cousins and girlfriends! Watch for her – she’ll be wearing #1!

About half the gals run, half walk and many do a combination of running and walking. It doesn’t matter how you get to the finish line, as long as you get there!

The 20th Annual Girlfriends Run offers a Half Marathon, 10K & 6K designed specifically for women to get together to do something good for themselves and to help support a very important women’s cause.

We started this event to honor and support one of our BFFs, Joleen Skarberg, who was diagnosed with Breast Cancer and continues to run it every year with her daughters, sisters, nieces, cousins and girlfriends! Watch for her – she’ll be wearing #1!

About half the gals run, half walk and many do a combination of running and walking. It doesn’t matter how you get to the finish line, as long as you get there!

name: Girlfriends Triathlon & Fitness Festival
description:
GIRLFRIEND, YES, YOU CAN CROSS THE FINISH LINE!

This 28th Annual Girlfriends All-Women’s Triathlon & Fitness Festival at a beautiful venue along the Columbia River offers something for everyone so rally your girlfriends, train together and then cross the finish line with your best girls!

It is one of the most scenic areas with views of the Columbia River, Mt. Hood, Mt. St. Helens and Vancouver Lake. The course is flat and fast with a down-current swim close to the shore so perfect for a 1st time Triathlon or Multisport event! Kids Triathlon and a Sunset 5K/10K are scheduled Friday night and Co-Ed events on Saturday so make a whole weekend of it for the whole family.

PARKING IS INCLUDED IN REGISTATION FEES.

name: Give NCW Turkey Trot
description:
Give NCW Turkey Trot is a great way to start your holiday season! The event features timed 5K and 10K races and an untimed, free run for kids. The 5K and 10K races are held on the Apple Capital Loop Trail along the Wenatchee riverfront. The Kids Race is held on a short course near the grounds of Pybus Public Market. Strollers and leashed dogs are permitted.

This family friendly event kicks off the annual Give NCW online giving campaign hosted by the Community Foundation of NCW.  Special thanks to Presenting Sponsor, Wenatchee Valley Medical Group and Gold Sponsors, Cordell Neher & Co. and Cashmere Valley Bank. Thanks to their sponsorship, every dollar from registration fees goes to support Give NCW. This giving campaign starts Thanksgiving Day and runs through Dec. 31 and supports over 75 nonprofit organizations in NCW. Race proceeds will be shared among the nonprofit organizations that participate in the campaign.

The “Best Dressed Individual” will receive a $500 Giving Card that can be redeemed to support nonprofits on Give NCW, and the “Best Dressed Group” will receive a $1,000 Giving Card. 

Planning to bring your dog? Enter your canine companion during the registration process and for an extra $5 donation, your pup will receive a Turkey Trot bandana (if it is among the first 150 to register) and a chance to win a Gift Basket from our friends at Firehouse Pet Shop!  

Location: The two races start and finish on the trail behind Pybus Public Market. The Kids Race is held in the boat launch parking lot behind Pybus Public Market.

Start times: 9:00am kids race; 9:15am 10K; and 9:30am 5K. 

Youth who are 12 years and younger can run untimed for free in the 5K, with a paid adult. Do not register them unless they want to be officially timed and qualify for the commemorative socks.

Packet pickup at Pybus Market: Wednesday, Nov 26th from 2:00pm-8:00pm or Thursday (race day), Nov 27 7:00am-8:45am. There will be NO DAY OF REGISTRATION

Swag: The first 750 paid registrants will receive a pair of commemorative Turkey Trot socks.

Aid stations: There are two aid stations - one at the 5k turnaround and one at the 10k turnaround with water and Gatorade. Porta potties are located at the start/finish, but not along the course. Note that the restrooms inside Pybus Market will not be open.

Course map: See below

Website: https://cfncw.org/turkeytrot

Email: melissa@cfncw.org.

name: GOAT Run
description:
* 50K * Marathon * Half Marathon *

The Great Olympic Adventure Trail Run (GOAT Run) is a trail 50K, marathon & half marathon that traverses Kelly Ridge between the Olympic National Park and the Strait of Juan de Fuca in Washington State.

The route follows the single track Adventure Trail for the majority of the course, plus some unpaved forest road mixed in, and less than a mile on pavement. The finish line is in Olympic National Park at the deep, glacially carved Lake Crescent. Famous for its turquoise blue waters of exceptional clarity, the lake is the perfect place to end the race.

The course reaches a maximum elevation of 1,619 feet, with a cumulative elevation gain of 1500 ft for the half, 3500 ft for the marathon, and 3700 ft for the 50K. Challenging? Absolutely! This is a difficult course. But it’s worth it! *(note: half course is long, about 14 mi)

What’s included?

In addition to an epic outdoor experience in the far northwest corner, all runners receive a professional well-organized event, a well-marked course, food and snacks at water stations along the course, a piece of custom race swag, free shuttle to start, chip timing, after-party at Log Cabin Resort including heavy snacks and water / electrolyte. Bring cash or card with you, as we will have a beer / cider garden at the finish line!

Where to stay

Olympic Lodge in Port Angeles is offering a special 25% off discount for GOAT Runners.
Booking link here. 
Or phone direct at 360-452-2993 and use booking code GOAT to receive the same discounted pricing.

GOAT Run is Cupless

Unnecessary waste and trash is something we are working to eliminate from our events. As an organization dedicated to maintaining a clean race and doing our part to keep our trails clean, starting in 2024 we will be going cupless. This means we are eliminating the use of disposable cups at our races. Runners will carry their own hydration vessels, weather it be a backpack, water bottle, or a compressible cup such at the HydraPak speed cup.

Giving Back

This race is a friendly, community-based event, and a portion of race proceeds is donated to the Peninsula Trails Coalition and the Peninsula Chapter of the Back Country Horsemen of Washington, in appreciation for their countless hours of trail construction and maintenance on the North Olympic Peninsula.

Refund Policy
  • 50% refund available until August 15, NO REFUNDS AFTER THIS DATE
  • No deferrals to next year
  • Transfers are allowed until 3 days before the race. Transfer instructions.
  • You will have the choice during the registration process to buy cancellation insurance (unavailable for Canadian racers – rules of the insurance company and not us or RunSignUp). With the insurance, you will get a full refund in certain circumstances including including accident, illness and family emergency, even after the August 15th date. Click here for more info and FAQ about the RegShield insurance.
  • If we are forced to cancel for any reason, runners will get a free transfer to the next year, or an 80% refund

Full information on our website.

Giving Back

This race is a friendly, community-based event, and a portion of race proceeds is donated to the Peninsula Trails Coalition and the Peninsula Chapter of the Back Country Horsemen of Washington, in appreciation for their countless hours of trail construction and maintenance on the North Olympic Peninsula.

Refund Policy
  • 50% refund available until August 15, NO REFUNDS AFTER THIS DATE
  • No deferrals to next year
  • Transfers are allowed until 3 days before the race. Transfer instructions.
  • You will have the choice during the registration process to buy cancellation insurance (unavailable for Canadian racers – rules of the insurance company and not us or RunSignUp). With the insurance, you will get a full refund in certain circumstances including including accident, illness and family emergency, even after the August 15th date. Click here for more info and FAQ about the RegShield insurance.
  • If we are forced to cancel for any reason, runners will get a free transfer to the next year, or an 80% refund

Full information on our website.

name: Guardian Angel Color Run
description:
Join us for the Guardian Angel Color Run on Saturday, May 17th!

 

Celebrating 11 years, our Guardian Angel Scholarship Program offers a unique opportunity to serve our St. Nicholas community and invest in our students’ futures by creating Saints and Scholars. The program provides tuition assistance to local families who wish to make Catholic education a priority in their lives.

 

The run is open to the public as well as St. Nicholas students, families and parents. Join us for a family friendly 5k run/walk along the Cushman Trail featuring color stations along the course and a color blast at our start line. Each participant will receive a t-shirt designed by a St. Nicholas student, a color packet and lots of fun!

 

Once you've finished the race stick around for music, cupcakes and light refreshments!

name: Heroes Walk 5K & Community Resource Fair
description:
CHECK IN BEGINS AT 9:00 AM 


Empowering Communities and Fortifying Families to End Veteran Suicide and Strengthen our Heroes to Lead their Communities.

HONOR HEROES - FORTIFY FAMILIES - CELEBRATE FREEDOM

Walk in support of veterans to choose LIFE. The enemy did not have victory in war, and will not win in the day to day battle for our veteran’s lives. Together we can end veteran suicide and fortify families after service. Live life abundantly with a community that hears, sees and recognizes the sacrifices of our HEROES. Family and supporters of our veterans are encouraged to join. Let’s gather in a big way to show the love and support of our veterans and the USA. 

The circle of return from military service to civilian life is a personal and community process. Join a community wide celebration and resources fair as we help veterans and families make the journey back home after service. 

Schedule: 

9 AM Registration Opens and Community Resource Fair

10 AM Opening Ceremonies 

11:00 AM Walk Commences on paths through Riverfront Park.
Those walking with kids are welcome to bring scooters, wagons, bikes or strollers to make your time easier with little ones. 

12 PM Victory Celebration at the Finish Line

1 PM Closing Ceremony and Resource Fair Closes


Heroes Walk brings awareness, solutions, and builds a connected community to end veteran suicide and homelessness by providing resources for wrap around care for the whole veteran and their family or support system. The content and event day will be mindful of the multigenerational crowd. 

Organizations desiring to join the resource community fair or sponsor the event, please email info@heroeshomestead.org.  Services for adults, children, veterans and spouses (including Gold Star families), as well as basic life needs and life enhancement and more are welcome to join.

Shirts will be $20

name: I love the 90s 5k
description:
I love the 90s 5k! 🏃🏽‍♀️ 🏃🏽 

Get ready to groove and run down memory lane at the I Love the 90s 5K, where you can lace up your sneakers & jam to classic 90s tunes!

Join us for the I Love the 90s 5k! Lace up your sneakers and get ready to groove to the best hits of the 90s while running through beautiful Green Lake Park in Seattle, WA. This in-person event is a blast from the past, celebrating all things 90s. Whether you're a fan of grunge, pop, or hip-hop, this 5k is for you! Dress up in your favorite 90s attire and relive the nostalgia with fellow participants. The course will take you around the scenic Green Lake, providing a picturesque backdrop for your run. So grab your friends, put on your Walkman, and let's make some memories together at the I Love the 90s 5k!

name: Jack & Jill Downhill Marathon, Half Marathon Washington
description:
We are in the World's top 25 fastest courses! https://www.halfmarathons.net/fastest-marathons/

Jack & Jill's Downhill Marathon is a fast, gentle downhill course on one of Washington's most scenic trails. North Bend, WA, is located just 31 miles east of Seattle. After you pass through the Snoqualmie Tunnel, you can enjoy the next 23 miles down a gradual 2000-foot net drop down the Cascade to Palouse Trail on a hard-packed, shaded dirt/gravel road. "YES," you can use your finish time to qualify for Boston or chalk up a new PR. Either way, this 26.2-mile journey is breathtakingly beautiful and sure to be a favorite.

"The finish line was awesome! They announce your name and let you know if you qualified for Boston. The crowd was amazing at the finish. And yes, I rang that PR bell with Pride! Would I run this marathon again? Absolutely!" - Annie
"This was an incredibly well organized race and package pickup"
"I was super impressed with how you all organized this race. The aid stations were so well stocked and in creative locations."  - Marilee
"Best finish line ever!" - Nicole
"Thanks for another fun event! See you again soon." - Marilee

🚐 SHUTTLE BUS INFO

Marathon: No shuttle to the start. You are responsible for your own transportation.
Half Marathon: Shuttle buses will take runners to the trailhead. From there, it’s a scenic 1-mile walk to the start.
No parking at the half marathon start, trailhead, or finish line.
Return shuttles are provided to take all runners back to their original parking locations after the race.
 
⏱️ Rolling Start

Start is staggered by pace groups with ~1 minute between waves.
All runners will be on course within a few minutes.
Line up according to pace to reduce congestion—faster runners should not have to weave around.
Half Marathoners: Don’t be late! A late start means walking uphill while others are racing downhill. Not fun.
 
👟 Shoes & Tunnel Gear

Road shoes are perfect. Trail shoes are not necessary.
Some runners use gaiters to prevent kicking up rocks, but that’s personal preference.
Marathon runners MUST carry a light for the tunnel.

Use the tear tag on your bib to mark your light and drop it in the bucket at the tunnel exit.
 
💧 Aid Stations

Located every ~2.5 miles.
Stocked with water, Gatorade, and GU gels at select stations.
 
🚫 Bib Rules

Do NOT run with someone else’s bib. This creates safety, emergency contact, and result issues.
We take this seriously—please respect the race, your fellow runners, and our volunteers.
 
🎽 Packet Pickup

Location: Snoqualmie Running Company

📍 38843 SE Newton St, Snoqualmie, WA 98065

Friday, July 25 – 11:00 AM to 7:00 PM
Saturday, July 26 – 3:00 PM to 7:00 PM
Race Day Pickup: PRE-PAID and PRE-ARRANGED ONLY for $25 paid by Wednesday of race week. Bibs will be available at the start line. You’ll receive your bib, shirt, and drop bag tag. 

 
🎒 Drop Bags

Bring a reasonable amount.
Secure it tightly and use the provided bib tag for ID.
We’ll transport your drop bag to the finish.
 
❗Refund Policy Reminder

As noted at registration:
No refunds, deferrals, or transfers.
Our only exception is if you volunteer to support the event.

 
Thanks for being part of this amazing community—we can’t wait to see you out there!

name: Jasper Mountain Trail Fest 2026
description:
Jasper Mountain Trail Fest is a fundraising event that benefits Jasper Mountain Reserve, an environmental 501(c)3 non-profit organization to improve and enhance wildlife habitats for rare and endangered flora and fauna native to the Blue Mountains in the Southeast corner of Washington State. Come and enjoy the beautiful natural scenery with the knowledge that your signup funds will benefit the conservation of the reserve.

 

For 2025, we are offering four unique race options:

1) Our classic (fifth annual!) 5-person relay race, 100 km total distance
2) Solo Half marathon, 13.1 miles with 2,570 feet of elevation gain
3) Solo Full marathon, 26.2 miles with 5,140 feet of elevation gain
4) Solo 7k Family Run (4.4 miles) with minimal elevation gain

 

Prices increases are on  April 17, 2025, May 18, 2025, and June 14, 2025. Sign up by May 29th, 2025 to guarantee you receive a race t-shirt and medal! (we have a few extras for late registrants on a first come-first serve basis).Contact info@jaspermountainreserve.org with any questions.

 

All races take place on the following single track trails (click on each for details):

Red Loop (3.3 miles)
Green Loop (4.4 miles)
Black Loop (5.4 miles)

 

Reserve Information and Accommodations

The start and finish line is at 934 Payne Hollow Road, Dayton, WA 99328, which can only be found on Google Maps.

 

Suggested arrival is during daylight the day prior to the race. Suggested departure is the day after the race. There will be an informal welcome reception and short presentation about the race in the Start/Finish area, commencing at 8:00PM on the evening prior to the race.

 

Parking and campsites, close to the start/finish line, is included in the race fee.

Campsites for racers are within Jasper Mountain Reserve. As this is a nature reserve, loud noises, including car engines, power generators, high volume loudspeakers etc. are strictly forbidden. Dogs must be on leash at all times. Camp-fires are only allowed at one designated area (please familiarize yourself with WA State and Columbia County seasonal camp fire restrictions). Bring your own food, water, and (battery) power sources (Jasper Mountain Reserve is off the grid, meaning there is no water or electricity). Portable sanitary facilities will be provided. As there is no garbage and recycling collection service please collect all trash and take it with you when you depart.

 

Accommodation options are also available just a short drive from the race! Choose from hotels and Airbnbs in nearby Dayton (11 miles from the event), Waitsburg (16 miles), or Walla Walla (37 miles).

 

Relay Race Details (Start Time 7:00AM):

Relay teams consist of 5 people sharing one assigned bib with an adjustable belt that can be exchanged between team members. Each racer signs up individually and can choose one of the following options:
1) No Team (the race organizers will assign you to a team)
2) Join an Existing Team
3) Create a New Team

 

All teams start together with the 1st runner of each team running the red loop at the same time. Once completed, the 1st runner passes the bib to the 2nd team member who will complete the green loop. Once completed, the 2nd team member passes the bib to the 3rd team member who will complete the black loop. Once completed, the 3rd team member passes on the bib to the 4th team member who will run the red loop, followed by the 5th team member who will run the green loop, followed by the 1st team member who will run the black loop and so on, until all 5 team members each have completed all three loops. Race timing will provide results for entire teams as well as individual times (splits) on each separate trail loop.

 

All three loops combined are exactly 13.1 miles, the distance of a half marathon. The relay race is expected to take 10-15 hours. Due to the rugged terrain which includes steep downhills, headlamps are mandatory for any runners after 8:00PM.

 

Half Marathon and Full Marathon Details (Start Time 7:00AM)

Calling all Ultra Trail Runners! Our new course is crafted specifically for the adventurous spirit of the ultra trail community. The half marathon is the perfect choice for those eager to test their limits or begin their journey toward ultra distances. For the fearless and bold, the full marathon awaits: 26.2 miles with over 5,000 feet of elevation gain, set against a backdrop of breathtaking natural beauty in the Blue Mountains. This isn't just a race; it’s a chance to immerse yourself in the beautiful landscape of a pristine nature reserve. Get ready to experience the ultimate trail running adventure, you won't be disappointed! All three trail loops within Jasper Mountain Reserve combined are exactly 13.1 miles, the distance of a half marathon, The full marathon will run the combined trail loops twice.

 

7k (4.4 miles) Family Run Details (Start Time 7:15AM)

This exciting new option will be on the beautiful Green Trail, 4.3 miles long with minimal elevation gain. It is ideal for runners who prefer a sprint option, or families with kids to run together, and for participants who prefer to walk.

4) Solo 7k Family Run (4.4 miles) with minimal elevation gain

 

Prices increases are on  April 17, 2025, May 18, 2025, and June 14, 2025. Sign up by May 29th, 2025 to guarantee you receive a race t-shirt and medal! (we have a few extras for late registrants on a first come-first serve basis).Contact info@jaspermountainreserve.org with any questions.

 

All races take place on the following single track trails (click on each for details):

Red Loop (3.3 miles)
Green Loop (4.4 miles)
Black Loop (5.4 miles)

 

Reserve Information and Accommodations

The start and finish line is at 934 Payne Hollow Road, Dayton, WA 99328, which can only be found on Google Maps.

 

Suggested arrival is during daylight the day prior to the race. Suggested departure is the day after the race. There will be an informal welcome reception and short presentation about the race in the Start/Finish area, commencing at 8:00PM on the evening prior to the race.

 

Parking and campsites, close to the start/finish line, is included in the race fee.

Campsites for racers are within Jasper Mountain Reserve. As this is a nature reserve, loud noises, including car engines, power generators, high volume loudspeakers etc. are strictly forbidden. Dogs must be on leash at all times. Camp-fires are only allowed at one designated area (please familiarize yourself with WA State and Columbia County seasonal camp fire restrictions). Bring your own food, water, and (battery) power sources (Jasper Mountain Reserve is off the grid, meaning there is no water or electricity). Portable sanitary facilities will be provided. As there is no garbage and recycling collection service please collect all trash and take it with you when you depart.

 

Accommodation options are also available just a short drive from the race! Choose from hotels and Airbnbs in nearby Dayton (11 miles from the event), Waitsburg (16 miles), or Walla Walla (37 miles).

 

Relay Race Details (Start Time 7:00AM):

Relay teams consist of 5 people sharing one assigned bib with an adjustable belt that can be exchanged between team members. Each racer signs up individually and can choose one of the following options:
1) No Team (the race organizers will assign you to a team)
2) Join an Existing Team
3) Create a New Team

 

All teams start together with the 1st runner of each team running the red loop at the same time. Once completed, the 1st runner passes the bib to the 2nd team member who will complete the green loop. Once completed, the 2nd team member passes the bib to the 3rd team member who will complete the black loop. Once completed, the 3rd team member passes on the bib to the 4th team member who will run the red loop, followed by the 5th team member who will run the green loop, followed by the 1st team member who will run the black loop and so on, until all 5 team members each have completed all three loops. Race timing will provide results for entire teams as well as individual times (splits) on each separate trail loop.

 

All three loops combined are exactly 13.1 miles, the distance of a half marathon. The relay race is expected to take 10-15 hours. Due to the rugged terrain which includes steep downhills, headlamps are mandatory for any runners after 8:00PM.

 

Half Marathon and Full Marathon Details (Start Time 7:00AM)

Calling all Ultra Trail Runners! Our new course is crafted specifically for the adventurous spirit of the ultra trail community. The half marathon is the perfect choice for those eager to test their limits or begin their journey toward ultra distances. For the fearless and bold, the full marathon awaits: 26.2 miles with over 5,000 feet of elevation gain, set against a backdrop of breathtaking natural beauty in the Blue Mountains. This isn't just a race; it’s a chance to immerse yourself in the beautiful landscape of a pristine nature reserve. Get ready to experience the ultimate trail running adventure, you won't be disappointed! All three trail loops within Jasper Mountain Reserve combined are exactly 13.1 miles, the distance of a half marathon, The full marathon will run the combined trail loops twice.

 

7k (4.4 miles) Family Run Details (Start Time 7:15AM)

This exciting new option will be on the beautiful Green Trail, 4.3 miles long with minimal elevation gain. It is ideal for runners who prefer a sprint option, or families with kids to run together, and for participants who prefer to walk.

name: Jasper Mountain Trail Fest 2026
description:

1) Our classic (fifth annual!) 5-person relay race, 100 km total distance
