name: Woodinville July 4th 5K
description:
The "Woodinville July 4th 5K"  and Kids dash is helping to raise money for the Northshore Senior Center and their Northshore Inclusion Program which supports individual with Intellectual Disabilities in the our area.

It's time to celebrate our Independence Day and the coming of summer.  What a great way to start of the family activities of summer and the outdoors with a run or walk along our beautiful Sammamish River Trail.  Whether you are a runner, power walker or casual stroller, this is a great event for you and your family.  We will start things off with a 6 year old and under Kids Dash and then get into the main 5K event.  It will be a great morning!   We will have prizes for the most patriotic costumes.   Best Family, Best Youth and Best Individual.   Come dressed to impress.

So break out the suntan lotion, put on your best beach or "red, white and blue" running attire and join us for a fun filled morning.

name: Woodinville Turkey Trot 5K
description:
The Annual Woodinville Turkey Trot is ready to roll this year!     We are planning of having the Kids Parade again this year led by the Woodinville HS Marching band.  At our Kids Dash the kids 6 and under will run a short course of about 200 yards on the trail and finish under the start/finish arch.   The morning should be a great way to get your Thanksgiving Day off to a great start before that all important turkey dinner.  

This year we will have 2 different events including:

1.      5K at Wilmot Park 

2.      Virtual 5K

3.       Kid's Dash

Our event continues to be hosted by Woodinville Running Company with a portion of the proceeds and 100% of the sponsorship dollars going to the Woodinville HS Boosters Wrestling Team.    Look for the t-shirt reveal soon.  

As for the events

5K at Wilmot Park

The 5K will begin run after we complete the Kids Dash which should be approximately 9:15am.  The course is a flat, fast out and back course on the Sammamish River trail.  Runners will organized by running pace so please seat yourself accordingly.  Your official time won't begin until you've reached the timing mats under the arch.

Virtual 5k

The Virtual 5k is the same as last year and this allows you to pick your own course and run or walk 3.1 miles and then submit your time.  This is a great option for those who want to social distance, but still have a goal to shoot for and get a great running shirt!  This category is not eligible for the age group 

This year’s Turkey Trot is going to be a great event.  We are excited to be Wilmot Park and being together in beautiful downtown Woodinville with friends and family on Thanksgiving morning.  So, let’s have fun, stay safe and be thankful for the many blessings of what went well this year.

name: Woolley Trail Runs
description:
Woolley Trail Runs are a 50k, Marathon, and Half Marathon located in Sedro Woolley Washington. All three runs are out and back with a few road crossings. Participants will heed traffic while crossing all roads, there will be NO crossing guards. As with all NW Ultra events these are meant to be fun runs with limited aid. Any diversion from the trail will be marked as well as all turnaround points. All three courses are out and back on railroad grade gravel path. The course has a slight (unnoticeable) uphill grade on the way out, with of course the same downhill grade on the return. There will be an aid station at each of the turnaround points (6.6 miles, 13.15 miles, 15.7 miles) and mile 4. Plan on carrying water and aid.  This is not a USATF certified course and you can’t qualify for Boston, but it is at least the advertised distance.

COURSE INFORMATION:
The course starts a quarter of a mile west of the trail head off Fruitdale Rd & SR 20. It continues east along the Cascade Trail. For a full map of the Cascade Trail please visit the Skagit County Parks & Recreation’s website here.

DROP BAGS:
Drop bags can be dropped off at the start the morning of the race.  Drop bags will be allowed at all aid stations.  Please mark on your drop bags your bib #, which aid station it goes to (mile marker) and your name.  They will not be returned until after the last runner has left each aid station, or participants may drive out to retrieve their bags.  If participants do not retrieve their drop bags they will be donated, we will not mail them to you.

START TIMES:
The official start time is 9:00 am.  All runners starting at the official time will be eligible for awards. 
The early start time is 8:00.  Runners opting to start early will not be eligible for awards.  Runners starting early are doing so because they expect to finish after the course closure time, if they start at the official time.
Minimum finish times will be given to all early start runners running faster the following times.  If you plan on running faster than these times you need to start at 9:00 am! 
1/2 Marathon – 2:30 minimum time 
Marathon – 5:00 minimum time 
50k – 6:00 minimum time 

DIRECTIONS TO EVENT:
Add your starting point to the following google map to find detailed directions.(Google Map) From Interstate 5 (I-5) take exit #232/Cook Road towards Sedro Woolley.  Drive east on Cook road 4.3 miles and take a left onto North Cascades Highway.  Drive 1.1 miles along North Cascades Highway until you reach Township Street.  Take a right on Township Street and drive 0.2 miles to Polte Road.  Take a left onto Polte Road.  Parking can be found 0.2 miles later at the Central United Methodist Church (1012 Polte Rd, Sedro Woolley, WA) just across the street from the trail head.

name: Yakima Mile
description:
Presented by Home2 Suites and Tru by Hilton - Yakima Airport

7th Annual Yakima Mile -- Saturday, June 7, 2026

The course follows a one-mile, gradual downhill stretch of Yakima Ave. finishing in the shadows of Yakima’s historic Larson Building. Yakima Mile is open to kids, families, dogs, veterans, elite runners, and all those who want to run their fastest mile…. EVER (or walk, or jog... as you like).

The Elite Mile races bring together many of the fastest milers from around the nation in hopes of breaking the Fastest Mile in Washington – yet again  – and taking home some big cash prizes. Sam Prakel currently holds the men's fastest mile in Washington time of 3:50.5 and Nikki Hiltz holds the women's record at 4:20.5.

Competitive races are stacked across the board with cash prizes – the total purse for 2026 is over $60,000. Including $10,000 across the TOP 3 groups by number of finishers. If you are interested in participating in the TRU-ly RAD Group Challenge at this year's Yakima Mile, reach out to hello@yakimamile.org

Youths 18 & under register for free thanks to the generosity of our sponsors Home2 and Tru by Hilton

------

Yakima Mile is much more than a race. We bring our community together for fun and fitness; providing a healthy community event open to everyone, highlighting and celebrating the Yakima Valley on a local and national scale. Hogback Development Company, the producer of Yakima Mile, seeks to work with community leaders, businesses, and individuals to shed light on and better access the invaluable services provided by YWCA to survivors of domestic violence. 

To learn more about the Yakima Mile, heats, prizes, what we do, and why we do it, visit www.yakimamile.org.
And to stay updated with all things Yakima Mile, follow @YAKIMAMILE on Instagram

Run for fun. Run for health. Run for the record. Run to show your community spirit. Run to support survivors of domestic abuse.
YWCA YAKIMA DOMESTIC VIOLENCE LOCAL HOTLINE - 509.248.7796 

 

Registration Cost

Youth (18Y & under): FREE
Adults (19-59): $25
Senior Citizens (60Y+): $12.50

name: Yakima River Canyon Marathon and Half-Marathon
description:
Join us for one of the Pacific Northwest's most scenic Boston Qualifiers. Our marathon and half marathon point to point courses travel through the spectacular Yakima River Canyon on a USATF Certified course along paved Washington State Route 821 between Ellensburg and Selah, WA. 

 

Awards: We will offer overall and age-group awards this year. Awards will be distributed in real time at the finish line -- check for results at nsplit.com/results.  Details below.

 

Cutoff Times: We will enforce cut-off times this year. Those who feel that cannot complete the race comfortably in seven hours are urged to contact the race director and ask for the early start, which is two hours before the 8 a.m. regular start. We offer the early start for those anticipating they will be on the course for six-and-a-half hours or more, and the race director must approve your participation in the early start. Early starters are not eligible for age-group awards, which are handed out in real time at the finish line. Thank you for your understanding.

 

Price Increase: Marathon and Half Marathon prices increase by $10 on after Feb 27. Sign up early! Registration is online only, and there is no in person registration on race day or the day before.

 

Race Deferrals: If you decide to defer your entry to next year, the deadline for informing us is Feb. 27.

 

Half Marathon Limited to 200 Runners: As in past years, entries will be capped at 200 in the half-marathon due to logistics involving bus transportation. At this point, we have no limit on marathon participants.

 

RACE HEADQUARTERS: Selah Civic Center, 216 South First Street, Selah, Washington.

 

Entry Includes: The (Non-Refundable) Entry includes T-shirt, race-day transportation (if needed), finisher medal, and a finisher’s certificate.

 

WEEKEND SCHEDULE

  • FRIDAY, March 27th:
    • Packet pickup for the Marathon and Half-Marathon from 3-8 p.m. at the Selah Civic Center..
  • SATURDAY, March 28th (Race Day):
    • Marathon packet pickup Saturday morning at the Ellensburg Days Inn, near the intersection of Berry Road and Canyon Road from 6-7:45 a.m.
    • Half-Marathon packet pickup Saturday morning at the Selah Civic Center from 6-7:45 a.m.

COURSE RECORDS, MAPS & DESCRIPTIONS:

  • COURSE RECORDS (Marathon & Half Marathon) – Click Here
    MARATHON COURSE INFORMATION & MAPS
    START MAP – Click Here
    COURSE MAP – Click Here
    COURSE PROFILE – Click Here
    FINISH MAP – Click Here

 

MARATHON RACE START 
Use Exit 109 from I-90. Go south past the Buzz Inn and Flying J Truck Plaza. Take the first left onto Berry Road…to the race start headquarters at the Days Inn, 901 Berry Road. The starting line is on Canyon Road .2 mile south of the Berry Road intersection. (see map)  For safety reasons running in the right lane is recommended, but not mandatory.

 

MARATHON COURSE DESCRIPTION: This point-to-point Marathon course is exceptionally scenic as it offers spectacular views of the Yakima River Canyon. It starts on Canyon Road .2 mile south of the Berry Road intersection in Ellensburg, Washington. After two loops, it proceeds directly south to the canyon. There are two major hills and many curves as the course follows the Yakima River downstream on the asphalt surfaced highway. The long downhill just before the finish in rural Selah, Washington, near the canyon’s mouth contributes to the net elevation loss of a few hundred feet as it brings the runners to the Yakima Valley orchard and ranch country.

 

PERSONAL GEAR:
Drop bags to go to the Finish Area may be left at the designated vehicle in front of the Days Inn on race morning before 7:45 a.m. Do not place cash or expensive items in the bags. The bags will be supervised, but we will not be responsible for lost or stolen items.

 

COURSE SUPPORT:
Aid stations will be located every 2-3 miles to provide water, Powerade, and medical aid of band-aids and petroleum jelly. Medical personnel and restrooms will be available throughout the race.

 

RACE FINISH:
Use exit 26 from I-82. Take Highway 821 north about 3 miles. (see map)
There will be bus transportation from the finish area to the Selah Civic Center and to the Best Western Ahtanum Inn.

 

COURSE CLOSURE:
The course will be open for 7 hours. Runners and walkers who have not finished by 3:00 p.m. will be given rides to the finish area. Early starts are allowed only with special permission. Only official and local vehicles are allowed on the race course. Spectators may view the race at the start, finish, and Thrall Road intersection with Canyon Road. There are no accessible intersections in the canyon. No bicycles or baby joggers are allowed on the course.

 

HALF-MARATHON INFORMATION
START MAP – Click Here
COURSE MAP – Click Here
COURSE PROFILE – Click Here
FINISH MAP – Click Here

 

HALF MARATHON RACE START TIME & LOCATION:
The 9:30 a.m. start is at the 13.1 mile marker of the Marathon. All participants will be bused to the start. At 8:00 a.m. three buses will leave the Selah Civic Center, 216 South First Street, Selah, WA and one will leave from the Best Western Ahtanum Inn, 2408 Rudkin Road, Yakima, WA. There will be no early starts.

 

HALF MARATHON COURSE DESCRIPTION: This Half-Marathon course will start at the 13.1-Mile mark of the Marathon Course for a point-to-point. The course is exceptionally scenic as it offers spectacular views of the Yakima River Canyon. The Half Marathon Participants will be bused to the start (no need to reserve bus). Three buses will leave the Civic Center at 8:00 a.m. for the starting area, and one bus will leave the Best Western Ahtanum Inn (2408 Rudkin Road, Yakima) at 8:00 a.m.  SPECIAL NOTE:  NO EARLY START

 

Personal Gear to be taken to the Finish Area: 
Drop bags may be left on a designated bus at the start.

 

Course Closure:
The course will close at 3:00 p.m.

 

BUS SERVICE

  • MARATHON – Buses will leave at 6:00 a.m. from the Selah Civic Center and the Best Western Ahtanum Inn to take participants to the Days Inn gathering area in Ellensburg.
  • HALF MARATHON – Buses will leave at 8:00 a.m. from the Selah Civic Center and the Best Western Ahtanum Inn for the starting line at the 13.1 mile marker of the half marathon.

 
 
AWARDS & DIVISIONS:
Awards will be presented to the top three male and female finishers and to the first three finishers in the age divisions (male & female 19 and under, then five year increments to 85+). Awards will be distributed in real time at the finish line -- check for results at nsplit.com/results. All entrants will receive a T-shirt, and all finishers will receive a finishers medal.

 

LODGING, ACCOMMODATIONS & WEATHER:

YAKIMA, WA:
Best Western Ahtanum Inn, 2408 Rudkin Rd., 1-800-348-9701
*There will be race day bus service from the Best Western Ahtanum Inn to the starting areas and from the finish area
*Marathon Bus - 6:00a.m. Half Marathon Bus - 8:00a.m.

  • ELLENBURG, WA: 
    Days Inn, 901 Berry Road, 1-888-889-9870
    Comfort Inn, 1722 Canyon Road, (509)925-7037
  • OR CONTACT: 
    • Yakima Valley Visitors & Convention Bureau – 1-800-221-0751, (509)575-3010, or yvvcb@visityakima.com 
    • Yakima Chamber of Commerce – (509)248-2021 or http://www.yakima.org 

 

WEATHER

The average low temperature this time of year is 29 degrees and the average high is 56 degrees.

 

ARCHIVED RESULTS

  • CLICK HERE TO VIEW ARCHIVED RESULTS – YEARS 2001 – 2019
  • 2022 – 2024 RACE RESULTS www.nsplit.com/results

THE GREAT RACE AND DEDICATED RACE DIRECTORS - RACE REVIEWS  CLICK HERE TO READ MORE!

  • Email: fpurdy@charter.net
  • Phone:  (509) 961-9769

MARATHON COURSE DESCRIPTION: This point-to-point Marathon course is exceptionally scenic as it offers spectacular views of the Yakima River Canyon. It starts on Canyon Road .2 mile south of the Berry Road intersection in Ellensburg, Washington. After two loops, it proceeds directly south to the canyon. There are two major hills and many curves as the course follows the Yakima River downstream on the asphalt surfaced highway. The long downhill just before the finish in rural Selah, Washington, near the canyon’s mouth contributes to the net elevation loss of a few hundred feet as it brings the runners to the Yakima Valley orchard and ranch country.

 

PERSONAL GEAR:
Drop bags to go to the Finish Area may be left at the designated vehicle in front of the Days Inn on race morning before 7:45 a.m. Do not place cash or expensive items in the bags. The bags will be supervised, but we will not be responsible for lost or stolen items.

 

COURSE SUPPORT:
Aid stations will be located every 2-3 miles to provide water, Powerade, and medical aid of band-aids and petroleum jelly. Medical personnel and restrooms will be available throughout the race.

 

RACE FINISH:
Use exit 26 from I-82. Take Highway 821 north about 3 miles. (see map)
There will be bus transportation from the finish area to the Selah Civic Center and to the Best Western Ahtanum Inn.

 

COURSE CLOSURE:
The course will be open for 7 hours. Runners and walkers who have not finished by 3:00 p.m. will be given rides to the finish area. Early starts are allowed only with special permission. Only official and local vehicles are allowed on the race course. Spectators may view the race at the start, finish, and Thrall Road intersection with Canyon Road. There are no accessible intersections in the canyon. No bicycles or baby joggers are allowed on the course.

name: Yakima River Canyon Marathon and Half-Marathon
description:
Join us for one of the Pacific Northwest's most scenic Boston Qualifiers. Our marathon and half marathon point to point courses travel through the spectacular Yakima River Canyon on a USATF Certified course along paved Washington State Route 821 between Ellensburg and Selah, WA. 

 

Awards: We will offer overall and age-group awards this year. Awards will be distributed in real time at the finish line -- check for results at nsplit.com/results.  Details below.

 

Cutoff Times: We will enforce cut-off times this year. Those who feel that cannot complete the race comfortably in seven hours are urged to contact the race director and ask for the early start, which is two hours before the 8 a.m. regular start. We offer the early start for those anticipating they will be on the course for six-and-a-half hours or more, and the race director must approve your participation in the early start. Early starters are not eligible for age-group awards, which are handed out in real time at the finish line. Thank you for your understanding.

 

Price Increase: Marathon and Half Marathon prices increase by $10 on after Feb 27. Sign up early! Registration is online only, and there is no in person registration on race day or the day before.

 

Race Deferrals: If you decide to defer your entry to next year, the deadline for informing us is Feb. 27.

 

Half Marathon Limited to 200 Runners: As in past years, entries will be capped at 200 in the half-marathon due to logistics involving bus transportation. At this point, we have no limit on marathon participants.

 

RACE HEADQUARTERS: Selah Civic Center, 216 South First Street, Selah, Washington.

 

Entry Includes: The (Non-Refundable) Entry includes T-shirt, race-day transportation (if needed), finisher medal, and a finisher’s certificate.

name: Year-to-Year Run 2025-2026
description:
WALK OR RUN IN THE NEW YEAR!! Cowlitz Valley Runners presents a local favorite, the Year-to-Year Run. Ring in the New Year while you run. Start off that New Year's resolution the right way. We will run the lake loop, i.e., 3.6 miles, beginning at 11:50 PM on 12/31/25.  Register online by 3:00 PM,12/31/25, or in-person between 10:30 and 11:15 PM, Cost is only $15. 

LONG-SLEEVED T-SHIRTS are available for $30.  Order by December 4th to guarantee your shirt and size. Shirts will be available at packet pick-up before the race.  You don't have to participate in the race to buy a shirt!

name: Zintel Canyon 4K
description: This is the 10th Annual run in Zintel Canyon.  It is a 4 km (2.5 mile) run on the scenic Spirit of America Trail in the heart of Kennewick, Washington. The trail includes sections that are paved, gravel, and dirt. Registration is $25 and includes a T-Shirt.  The race is not chip timed, but we will manually record times at the finish and post results.

name: 10th Annual Run 2 Remember
description:
5K RUN/WALK (ALL AGES) and 1/2 MILE KIDS RUN (AGES 6-12)

9:00 AM      MAY 16, 2026   

Salem Riverfront Park

200 Water Street NE, Salem, OR 97301

Participation is open to everyone in the community.  This is our 10th year honoring the men and women who have died in service to our country.  By reaching out to the survivors and family members, we hope to promote a community of support on behalf of those “Never Forgotten.”

name: 13th Annual Ugly Holiday Sweater Run
description:
The 13th Annual Ugly Holiday Sweater Run is a FREE untimed 5K run/walk on Saturday, December 20th at 9 am. This event benefits Ladybug CDH Foundation, so please bring items for families in the NICU (cotton receiving blankets, small stuffed animals, blank journals).  Suggested donation $15.  For more information about the Ladybug CDH Foundation go to http://www.ladybugcdhfoundation.com

Options for a 1 mile race, or do the full 5K or even a 10K as it's an out and back. So run as far as you like! It's a fun run, so run, walk, or skip!

***No packet pick up.. Print a bib at home or just come early on Saturday for the pre-race fun and snacks and grab a RoadID bib! 

Post-race refreshments, RoadRunner Sports Shopping Discount and raffle drawings!

Race starts at 9:00AM.

Raffle and Awards at 9:45AM

Want to volunteer to help or be a sponsor? Email us at Ladybugcdh@gmail.com

name: 19th Annual - 2025 Give n' Gobble Turkey Trot
description:
The Sherwood Turkey Trot tradition continues for its 19th year!

A family discount is available when you register multiple people together. The family discount is only available if all members live in the same household.
To get the family discount, select "Family Package" under Multi-Person Pricing on the 1st registration step

There is also a team discount if you join a team with more than 10 people on it. 

This registration page is for all types of registration: Family, Team, and Individual.

The race will take place at Sherwood Middle School on Thanksgiving morning. 
The 5K Walk starts at 9:00am and the 5K Run and 10K Run starts at 9:05am.

Bib Pick Up and Food Donation Dropoff Times:
There are two bib pick up options:
1) Recommended: Saturday before Thanksgiving (11/22) at Sherwood YMCA
🕓 Time: 12pm to 2pm
📍Address: 
Sherwood Regional Family YMCA
23000 SW Pacific Highway
Sherwood, OR 97140

You must register by end of day Thursday 11/20 to pick up at the Saturday packet pikup

2) Before the event starting at 8am Sherwood Middle School. Make sure to arrive early if you wish to do this option.

At both locations you can bring a bag of nonperishable food (or 3 cans or a box of cereal - or more!) to receive your shirt

If you are a family or team, all of your family or team's bibs will be in one packet. One person should pick up the packet and distribute to the rest of the family or team At the Saturday bib pickup or race, you can bring a bag of nonperishable food (or 3 cans or a box of cereal - or more!) to receive your shirt

If you are registering with a sponsor code, your bib and shirt will only be available on race day in our VIP area.

name: 2026 Bend Beer Run
description:
What’s Included in Your Registration Fee:

  • A scenic, untimed 5K route through Drake Park and downtown Bend, along the beautiful Deschutes River.
  • Four craft beer stops featuring local breweries along the race course.
  • Entry to The Little Woody Festival, where you can enjoy:
    • A Little Woody Tasting Glass
    • Six drink tokens for beer or cider of your choice
    • Live music, games, and barrel-aged brews.
  • Costume contest prizes for the best-dressed participants—grab your friends and get creative!
  • Event bib for the race.

Event Details:

Check-in:

Begins at 11:00 AM at The Commons Café (875 NW Brooks St., Bend, OR).
Pick up your bib and get ready to run!

Race Start:

The race kicks off promptly at 12:00 PM outside The Commons Café.

Course Information:

This untimed 5K is all about the experience—run, walk, or jog while enjoying beer stops and the lively atmosphere.

Finish Line:

The finish brings you directly into The Little Woody Festival, where your post-race celebration begins!


Important Notes:

This is a 21+ event.
Costumes are highly encouraged for a chance to win fun prizes.
Additional details can be found on the race website. 

Location: Start at The Commons, Finish at Deschutes Historical Museum
 
Join the Bend Beer Run for a brew-tiful blend of fitness, fun, and fantastic craft beer!

name: 2026 Conquer the Canyon
description:
Join us June 6, 2026 and get ready to Conquer the Canyon - HALF MARATHON (13.1 miles), 10K, and 5K! And the return of the 5K Doggie Dash!

Cruise through Redmond’s Dry Canyon Trail which boasts stunning high desert geological features and peaceful scenic surroundings. The majority of the Dry Canyon is a nature preserve with steep rocky walls - a tribute to the area’s volcanic past. The course also weaves through Redmond's town center. Catch impressive natural views and traditional city scenes featuring pavilions and historic landmarks.

Choose your distance: 5K, 10K or 1/2 marathon.

Each race is professionally chip-timed by Eclectic Edge Racing and supported by outstanding event staff and medical personnel who are there for you at every turn. Meet friends and family at the post-race party with music, food and drink! Beautiful custom-designed medals await every runner at the finish line.

RACE SCHEDULE

Packet Pickup: Friday, June 5 from 2-6pm at SCP Redmond Hotel (Downtown Redmond). You may also pick up your packet one hour before your race time at the race.

RACE START TIMES

  • Half Marathon - 9am
  • 10K - 9:15am
  • 5K - 9:30am
  • 5K Doggie Dash - 9:33am

Starting line and finish and after party is in Centennial Park in Redmond.

All finishers receive a custom-made medal, food and drink at the after-party!

name: 2026 Happy Girls Bend Run
description:
Calling all Happy Girls!!

The 16th Annual Happy Girls Run series returns to Central Oregon with its first race of the season in Bend, Oregon. Participants of all abilities can choose from the all-women’s Half Marathon, 10K, or 5K races.  

You will be graced with gorgeous scenic views on a mix of trails, groomed paths, and paved surfaces. Cross the finish line and enjoy the post-race party with a fabulous gift bag and a unique Happy Girls medal. Adult beverages and food are provided.

Grab your friends, make a weekend of it, design a team costume, and let's go, girls!

name: 2026 Happy Girls Sisters
description:
Enjoy some bonding time with women of all ages and levels in the appropriately named town of Sisters, Oregon. Choose between the all-women’s trail half marathon featuring single-track in the Deschutes National Forest (on the Peterson Ridge Trail system) with some pretty stellar views or take part in the 5K and 10K road race that winds through scenic downtown Sisters. All races cross the same finish line, welcoming all to enjoy the beautiful FivePine campus under the towering Ponderosa pines.

**Make sure to register early – the half marathon is limited to 500 runners and sells out every year.

name: 2026 Haulin Aspen
description:
Mountain Trail Running Has Never Been Better

One of Oregon’s favorite trail full marathon and half marathon races returns for the 22nd year on Saturday, August 8th, 2026. 

No pavement here. Featuring a full all-trail marathon, a half marathon, and a 6.5-mile course (dubbed the “Half As”), the Haulin’ Aspen features beautiful trails that wind through the Deschutes National Forest, showcasing some epic views. With varying terrain and elevation, the cool wooded pine setting provides a challenging and exciting experience. Enjoy the beautiful single track, steep trails, fast descents, and amazing views starting at an elevation of nearly 5500'. Make it a destination this summer – Bend and the Cascades welcome you!

name: 2026 Hot Cocoa Run
description:
Join us on Sunday, Feb 15 for the return of the Hot Cocoa Run!

⭐️ Race entry includes admission to all three days of WinterFest! ⭐️

 

Early registration will close on Thursday, February 12 at midnight. Any latecomers can sign up on-site on Sunday morning starting at 11 am.

🚨 Check-In Details 🚨
WinterFest entry is included with your registration! All Hot Cocoa Run attendees will receive an emailed WinterFest ticket to your email on file for the run. You will use this ticket to gain entry to WinterFest NOT your registration. Our volunteers at the entry gates can also look up your name if you can not find your WinterFest ticket.

Don't forget to check in! Your QR code will be scanned to get your registration information. Print your QR code or have it available on your phone when you arrive. 

Check-In Options

Packet pickup will be available at
Location: Old Mill District  - SEE COURSE MAP FOR EXACT LOCATION. We will do our best to have signage to direct you to the start area.
Date: Sunday, February 165
Time: 11 am -12 pm

A fun 5K with a full Hot Cocoa bar at the finish with toppings and Crater Lake spirits.

The Hot Cocoa Run will take place during WinterFest 2026 celebrating the magic of winter Feb. 13 - Feb. 15 at the Old Mill in Bend, OR.

This will be an untimed 5K loop on Sunday at noon during the Northwest’s biggest festival. A full hot cocoa bar with all the toppings and Crater Lake spirits, including espresso vodka, await one and all at the finish line. Costumes are encouraged!

name: 2026 Salmon Run
description:
Join us for the 38th annual Salmon Run which returns to Bend, Oregon on April 18, 2026.

Distances include the HALF MARATHON (13.1 miles), 10K, and 5K races. All courses weave along the beautiful Deschutes River on trails and some pavement.

Taking place in the spring, the Salmon Run is one of the first running events of the season and the essential tip-off to the local racing scene in Central Oregon. Traversing beautiful dirt and paved trails amongst junipers and pines, the race course winds through some of the most scenic natural areas in Bend and finishes on the lawn Riverbend Park. Make a weekend of it!

Bring the kids for the Little Fry Run too!

Course Details  

The Salmon Run course takes runners along the beautiful and picturesque Deschutes River.  The half marathon course is 75% paved sidewalks and 25% trail.  The 10K course is 80% paved sidewalks and 20% trail.  The 5K is 65% paved sidewalks and 35% trail.  All courses will be marked with a combination of mile markers and directional arrows.

Finish Line Festivities

Enjoy a post-race party with delicious food and beverages (beer!) and music. We’ve got gift bags and awards for the top three male and female finishers in both open and master’s categories! 1st, 2nd & 3rd place ribbons for top age-group finishers.

Parking for Race Day

There is limited parking at Riverbend Park on race day. We highly recommend carpooling. Parking attendants will direct you as you arrive. Additional parking is available on City streets. 

For full details regarding the Salmon Run, click here.

name: Arrows Challenge
description:
ARROWS CHALLENGE

Welcome to the first-ever Arrows Challenge presented by Portland Bible College! 

This February, we’re inviting our PBC community—alumni, friends, students, faculty, staff, and supporters—to move with purpose. The challenge is simple: log 28 miles in 28 days by walking, running, swimming, riding, or moving throughout the month of February.

For over 50 years, Portland Bible College has been committed to training and developing leaders for the Kingdom of God. As we look ahead with faith and anticipation, we recognize that advancing our mission happens step by step and mile by mile.

Choose Your Impact

As part of the Arrows Challenge, each participant will choose to support one of two fundraising opportunities, both supporting areas that help strengthen the future of PBC:

1. Support the Online Program Upgrades
Support upgrades and improvements to PBC’s Online Program, helping us expand our reach and equip more leaders around the world.
(See the initiative overview here.)

2. Support the Archer's Fund
Support the Archer's Fund, which supports initiatives that directly benefit students, including scholarships and specific projects that improve the students’ experience, including campus upgrades.
(Learn more about the Archer's Fund here.)

All of the funds raised through joining the challenge, and through team and individual fundraisers, will directly support the above initiative of your choice.

Move. Give. Make an Impact.

As you complete your miles, we invite you to prayerfully consider making a donation or encouraging others to give toward your team’s cause. Post about the challenge on social media, invite your friends on a walk, and tell a friend about PBC. Every gift helps advance the mission of Portland Bible College and invests in the next generation of Kingdom leaders.

Join us for this month-long challenge as we strengthen community, build momentum, and move PBC forward together—mile by mile.

name: Bend Marathon and Half
description:
Welcome to the Bend Marathon, Half Marathon, 10k and 5k. With local ownership the 2026 events will be the best mountain town races anywhere. These are spectacularly scenic courses through West Bend emphasizing everything that makes Bend, Oregon great. You'll cruise around neighborhood parks, through ponderosa pine forests, along the mighty Deschutes River, and finish in a beautiful iconic Bend location to a hoppin' afterparty where the music is playing, delicious food is waiting, and you can relax because you just finished your best race ever! Join us for the 11th edition of the Bend Marathon, Half Marathon, 10k and 5k.

name: Best in the West Triathlon Festival
description:
Best in the West Triathlon Festival - Designed by athletes, for athletes!

Nestled in the foothills of the Cascades and fed by the Santiam River, Foster Reservoir offers premier recreation facilities to the outdoor enthusiast and an excellent location for a triathlon festival.

Swim in the beautiful Foster Lake. Miles of low use roads wind through the hills and along the river, providing an exhilarating ride for the cyclist. Following the wooded shoreline, the run course offers relief from the summer sun.

To top off your race experience, we put on an awesome post race party! We put together a HUGE BBQ with local produce just for you! After you fill up on delicious food, top it off with a couple of ice cold beers, ciders or beverages on us, and enjoy the live music and awards ceremony.

With a family friendly atmosphere and races for all ages and abilities, you’ll find yourself hanging around for the whole weekend. A large, well kept campground is the final component of the equation for the ultimate triathlon festival. We hope you will join us!

The Best of the West Triathlon Festival aims to promote health and fitness through a weekend of competitive and fun racing while also providing a healthy living expo where participants, volunteers and spectators will learn how to live healthier happier lives. Our goal is to help bring out the best in you!

www.bestinthewesttriathlon.com

name: Camelback Run
description:
When:
March 1, 2025

Where:
All races will start and finish on or next to the new Phoenix High School track!

See our course maps.

How long:
15k, 5K and Kids' Mile

Why?
This event is a fundraiser to help the Phoenix High School Track and Field team raise money to help pay for meet entry fees, purchase new throwing implements and jumping equipment.

What is the entry fee:
$25 or $20 for club members. As with all SOR events, participants who are 18 and under run free!

Day of race entry fee will be $25.

What is the course like:
15K – This course gives you a chance to run the back roads of Phoenix, take in some amazing sights, and conquer some gnarly hills.

5K – This out-and-back route turns around at the end of Hilsinger road (just before the intersection of Hilsinger and Pioneer).

Kids' Mile - The kids' mile will be run on the track

Where is Packet Pickup:

Bib pick-up and day-of-race registration will be available from 9–10 am on the day of the race. Check-in, start, and finish will all be situated on or near the track.

Awards:

Age division awards are provided by People's Bank. Trophies will be awarded to 1st place age group finishers, medals for 2nd place finishers and ribbons for 3rd place finishers.

*Races are on public roads and trails that ARE NOT closed to cars, pedestrian or cyclist.  Please use caution while on public roadways and paths.

name: Cascade Half Marathon & 10K
description:
The races will be held on Sunday, January 18, 2026. The Half Marathon, 10K, and 2-mile races run on a flat course on country roads, surrounded by scenic farmland. There is water and toilets on the course. There is an early option for those expecting to take longer than 2 1/2 hours to run the Half Marathon. Participation is limited to the first 1,000 registered runners for all three races combined. Day of race registration is an option, cash or check is preferred but we will have an option for credit card.

 

All half & 10k finishers will receive a medal as they finish. Awards will be given to the male and female overall and masters winners in the Half Marathon and 10K, as well as three-deep for age group winners, per 10-year age category. No awards will be given for the 2-mile race. Early starters' results in the Half Marathon will not be considered for overall or age group awards. There will also be many random prize giveaways from our generous sponsors! To become a sponsor, please contact us below.

 

Packet pickup is in the junior high school gym, where race participants can relax, stretch, and stay warm. Families and friends can hang out in the gym, too. We will have a coffee cart on site, courtesy of I-Jive coffee. Since the race starts and finishes right in front of the gym, you can stay inside until the last minute! Afterward, you can celebrate your accomplishments in the school's cafeteria with hot soup, coffee from I-Jive, and freshly baked cookies!

 

Proceeds from the race will benefit Cascade High School's track & field program, as well as provide scholarships to graduating high school seniors from the mid-Willamette Valley who wish to continue their education.

 

**Strollers are allowed on the race course but please give an appropriate amount of space to the other runners. Dogs are not allowed on the race course.

name: Cheadle Lake 5K/10K Fun Run & Walk and 1/2 Mile Kids Obstacle Dash
description:
The 17th annual running of the Cheadle Lake 5K/10K Fun Run/Walk and Kids Obstacle Dash will once again be hosted by Build Lebanon Trails on Saturday, May 2, 2026. The 5K/10K Fun Run and Walk begins at Cheadle Lake Park and follows newly completed paths, north to River Park where it loops back to Cheadle Lake Park. The route surfaces for the Run/Walk are a mix of concrete, asphalt, gravel and dirt paths.

The Kids Obstacle Dash is a 1/2 mile course for kids 10 and under. More than 20 obstacles include the gunny sack race, a balance beam, the pool noodle slalom, and much more.  Adults are welcome to follow their kids and help them out if needed. Free registration for the first 200 kids! Use coupon code DASH

This event supports Build Lebanon Trails (BLT) a non-profit that has been building and maintaining multi-use, free to use, public trails in the Community since 2005. Events start at 9:00 A.M. at Cheadle Lake Park (37919 Weirich Drive, Lebanon.) Day-of Registrations open at 8:30. Kids Dash start is at 9am. 5K & 10K start is at 9:30am. 

If you are interested in helping by sponsoring the event visit BLT's website at buildlebanontrails.com where you will find the list of sponsorship benefits.

name: Coos County Odyssey 2026
description:
View Results Page

 

Travel around Coos County, Oregon in this fourth virtual odyssey that will take you through many unique and interesting locations in the county. This year's event is 253 miles, with 25 milestones to earn badges. As a participant, you can exercise in a number of different ways to earn miles on the virtual platform. Form teams and compete with and motivate your friends and family to start the year off right, achieving your fitness goals, while helping Coos County Families in Need. The Coos County Friends of Public Health (CCFoPH) is hosting this event to raise money for The Nurses’ Purse fund.

 

The Nurses’ Purse is a discretionary fund which can be accessed by public health nurses at Coos Health & Wellness to help families in need with essentials such as food, winter clothing, infant care, and payment of medical bills for the uninsured. The relatively small assistance from this fund can help families overcome what seem to be insurmountable obstacles to their health and wellbeing. 

We Hope you will participate in the challenge! And whether you 'race' or not, we invite you to help Coos County Families by clicking the Donate link.  The Coos County Friends of Public Health (CCFoPH) is a non-profit 501c3 organization.  Your donations are tax deductible, to the extent allowed by law.  

     

 

Links below will take you to information about the Coos Odyssey Challenge

name: Forest Grove Lions Club Run & Walk for Sight and Hearing
description:
All levels of runners and walkers encouraged to participate!!
Registration fees includes a long sleeve tee shirt and personalized bib if registered by 11:59 pm on September 8th. 
Online day of event registration (no cash, no check, electronic payment only)

For more information, visit forestgrovelions.org, or contact Race Director, Sydney, msdaniels@vgmhc.org.

name: Gator Grinder Triathlon
description:
The North Lake Physical Therapy Gator Grinder Triathlon is an excellent introduction for the first-time triathlete, as well as a great early season event for the experienced racer.  All proceeds support the Canby Gators Swim Club.  Thank you for your support.

Swim

500-yard (20 lengths, 10 laps) pool swim in a 6-lane, 25-yard pool, with up to 4 swimmers per lane. There will be volunteer lap counters. Drafting is permitted. The swim will be seeded by 500-yard swim-time submissions. Heat assignments will be e-mailed by the Thursday before the race. name: HAGG Lake Triathlon & Multi-Sports Festival
description:
RACE AT THIS HISTORICAL EVENT AND STUNNING VENUE!

Hagg Lake Triathlon – Rich in Beauty, Rich in Tradition!

Come race at the 45th Anniversary of the Annual Hagg Lake Triathlon & Off-road Endurance Sports Festival, one of the oldest and most gorgeous Triathlon courses in the nation! Now offering an Off-Road Triathlon, Half Marathon Trail Run, 5K Trail Run & Camping!

Olympic & Sprint Triathlon, Duathlon & AquaBike & NEW OFF-ROAD SPRINT TRIATHLON, DUATHLON & AQUABIKE, Half Marathon Trail Run, and 5K TRAIL RUN!

The modern sport of triathlon had its modest beginnings with an event held in Mission Bay in San Diego, CA on September 25, 1974. There were 46 athletes that day. Seven years later, Hagg Lake Triathlon became one of six stops on the Bud Light Triathlon Series Tour drawing about 500 athletes, with Dave Scott coming out on top. Today, as one of the nation’s oldest and longest-running triathlon events, Hagg Lake enters its 38th year and it continues to draw upwards of 700+ athletes. Its popularity is rooted in the rich tradition and the exceptional venue, which is one of the most scenic in the country. The Hagg Lake course offers a true test of this terrific sport with its rolling hills on both the bike and run leg portions of the event. Make the Hagg Lake Triathlon & Off-road Endurance Sports Festival one of your summer stops and compete on the course that has seen many of the greats in the sport of triathlon.

name: HAGG Lake Triathlon & Multi-Sports Festival
description:
RACE AT THIS HISTORICAL EVENT AND STUNNING VENUE!

Hagg Lake Triathlon – Rich in Beauty, Rich in Tradition!

Come race at the 45th Anniversary of the Annual Hagg Lake Triathlon & Off-road Endurance Sports Festival, one of the oldest and most gorgeous Triathlon courses in the nation! Now offering an Off-Road Triathlon, Half Marathon Trail Run, 5K Trail Run & Camping!

Olympic & Sprint Triathlon, Duathlon & AquaBike & NEW OFF-ROAD SPRINT TRIATHLON, DUATHLON & AQUABIKE, Half Marathon Trail Run, and 5K TRAIL RUN!

The modern sport of triathlon had its modest beginnings with an event held in Mission Bay in San Diego, CA on September 25, 1974. There were 46 athletes that day. Seven years later, Hagg Lake Triathlon became one of six stops on the Bud Light Triathlon Series Tour drawing about 500 athletes, with Dave Scott coming out on top. Today, as one of the nation’s oldest and longest-running triathlon events, Hagg Lake enters its 38th year and it continues to draw upwards of 700+ athletes. Its popularity is rooted in the rich tradition and the exceptional venue, which is one of the most scenic in the country. The Hagg Lake course offers a true test of this terrific sport with its rolling hills on both the bike and run leg portions of the event. Make the Hagg Lake Triathlon & Off-road Endurance Sports Festival one of your summer stops and compete on the course that has seen many of the greats in the sport of triathlon.

name: Ho Ho 5k
description:
The triumphant return of a holiday classic.  A festive 5K exuding the holiday spirit! HoHo's and Snoballs (Hostess) to all finishers.  Dress up encouraged and, keeping with tradition, there will be free trees AND THE FRUITCAKE!!  IYKYK!! 

Get in the spirit and bring canned food and jackets/blankets and come out for a great 5K run and walk!  Also collecting cat and dog food for the humane society! Friendly dogs are welcome.  

Late registration and number pick-up will begin at 8 AM race morning.  Bring some warm clothes to change into so you can enjoy the festive post event fun!

name: Hood to Coast Semper Fi & America's Fund Team
description:
Join our Semper Fi & America's Fund Team for the Hood to Coast Relay and help us raise $20,000 for The Fund.

Our team will be comprised of Team Semper Fi (service members who participate in The Fund's Recovery through Sport program) and Community Athletes (Fundraisers). This partnership will be a unique experience for everyone involved!

The Providence Hood To Coast Relay, located in Oregon, is the most popular and largest running and walking relay race in the world, annually drawing participants from over 40 countries. Known as the Mother of All Relays, the event takes 12-member relay teams 199 miles from the iconic top of Mount Hood to the beaches of the Pacific Ocean. The event has sold-out for 30 straight years and on lottery opening day for 23 consecutive years. 

Fundraising minimum $3,000. Your $3,000 fundraising will cover the costs for a member of Team Semper Fi to participate in the Relay.

Registration cost $225.00 per person

  • As you register for the team a personal fundraising page will be created for you. This page can be customized with pictures and your personal message. 
  • Each team member will receive a Semper Fi & America's Fund running shirt.
  • Each team member is responsible for their own travel to and from the event.
  • The Fund will provide vans that will transport the team during the event.
  • The Hood to Coast Relay takes place on Friday, Aug 27nd through Saturday, August 30. Participants need to arrive in Portland no later than Thursday, Aug 27 and stay until Sunday, Aug 30.

name: HOTV Resolution Run
description:

Heart of the Valley Runners is excited to keep the tradition of providing a FREE 5k and 2k run/walk to begin the new year! We hope you'll join us and your neighbors for some community, fun, and motivation, to stay active in 2025. Register online or day of race at Avery Park/Thompson Shelter between 9:00 - 9:45 am. 

Strollers for your wee ones are welcome. No dogs or bikes, please!

description:

Join us for our 7th Annual Hunger Run to help fight food insecurity in Columbia County. 

Starting and ending at the Columbia Pacific Food Bank, the 1-Mile, 5K and 10K run/walk routes will take you through downtown and old town St. Helens. Come early and stick around after your race to check out our info vendors, collect swag, and have a great time. 

Help us hit our goal of 400 participants!! All monies raised stay in our county and support our community partnerships.

name: Jingle Bell 5k Relay
description:
For teams or individuals, this event is a 1k loop, through the Holiday Light Display in Riverfront Park. The loop can be completed as an individual 5 times or bring a team and divide up the 5 loops as a relay. Relay teams will be given glow sticks to hand off to the next person.

Cost: $10 per team (A team is 1 person or more.)

name: Lake Oswego Lake Run
description:
2025 marks the 49th year of the Lake Oswego Lake Run! 

 

For more than 4 decades, runners have gathered in Lake Oswego to tackle the hilly terrain and enjoy the beautiful views. The run has attracted runners of all ages from across the country and is welcoming you to join us this year on Saturday, May 3rd.

 

Beyond a beloved community event and a great way to get out, be active, meet a goal, prepare for a year of races ... Proceeds from the Lake Run support Oregonians in need of stable and affordable housing. By running in the Lake Run, you are doing so much more goodness than just for yourself and the friends/ family you run alongside, you are helping your community. This run is organized by Northwest Housing Alternatives, where we create opportunity through housing and work tirelessly to end homelessness in Clackamas County. Please join us in this endeavor, in this fight for everyone's basic right. Together, we can change lives.

 

Gender Recognition and Inclusion: We believe that everyone has a place in the running community that is respectful, safe, and inclusive. In an effort to support individuals that do not identify as either male or female, we have the categories of non-binary and "Prefer Not to Say." Individuals who select either option will be eligible for the non-binary awards category.

 

FAQ's

name: Longest Night Mile
description:
WHERE:  Phoenix High School Track

WHEN: Sunday, December 21st, 2025

  • 6:15pm- Heat 1  5:45min pace & Under 
  • 6:25pm- Heat 2  5:46 -7min Pace 
  • 6:35pm- Heat 3  7-9min Pace 
  • 6:50pm- Heat 4  9-11min Pace 
  • 7:05pm- Heat 5  11min Pace & Up

COURSE DETAILS:  Four times around the Phoenix High School Track

RACE FEES: Option 1: Bring 2-3+ boxes of dry cereal. YES you read that right! The SOU food bank coordinator expressed to us in 2019 that the students are excited when there is cereal in the food bank because there rarely is and when it is there it doesn't last long. So, we thought it would be a fun treat before Christmas to stuff their pantry full of cereal goodness! We also hosted a can food drive at our Turkey Trot for the SOU food bank and a portion of the proceeds went to them as well so don't worry, we made sure they had other food items. 

Option 2: $13 online or $15 day of (cash or check only) which will also be donated to the SOU Student Food Pantry.

RACE DAY INFO: Registration 5-6pm - Bring $15 or 2-3+ boxes of dry cereal and sign waiver to participate.  

AWARDS:  Ribbons for the top 3 places in all age groups. $100 prize for any male who runs sub 4:00 minutes and any female who runs sub 4:40 minutes.

RESTRICTIONS: Absolutely no roller skaters, bicycles, skateboards, baby joggers, dogs, headphones, or unregistered participants

RACE DIRECTORS: Nathan & Shayla Watt

name: Mac's Run
description:
Hilly and challenging course with breathtaking ocean views. The race is entirely on paved roads.  

For both courses, runners loop through Shore Acres heading out (south), and run straight back on the return (north).

5K Course Map

10K Course Map

Note that students are $5.00.  Please use the coupon code Student2022 to register.  To avoid credit-card fees, you will not be charged at check-out.  Please bring $5.00 (exact change appreciated) to registration!

Starting Oct 1, 2025, all vehicles require a parking pass (cost is per vehicle, not per runner).  Cost of a day pass is $10 for in-state or $12 for out-of-state.  Daily passes are available at a kiosk near registration with a QR code using your phone.  We are working with the parks to see if we can sell them as part of registration, but details have not been worked out yet.  Annual state park passes are $30 for one year and $50 for two years.  They can be purchased at the gift shop at Shore Acres or on-line.  FYI, the price will double to $60 for an annual pass January 1 and they will no longer issue two-year passes, so if you visit our beautiful state parks, it is cheaper to buy now.

name: Miles for Midwives 2026
description:
THANK YOU VOLUNTEERS, SPONSORS AND PARTICIPANTS FOR AN AMAZING 2025 EVENT!

Miles for Midwives 5k walk/run/roll was at 10am on May 16, 2026 at the beautiful Champoeg State Park, located halfway between Oregon City and Salem. This annual event raises awareness about the impact midwives have on improving outcomes in maternal and infant health and supports two professional midwifery organizations, The American College of Nurse-Midwives Oregon Affiliate and Oregon Midwifery Council. Please join us in celebrating the important work Midwives provide to women, pregnant people, and families by stepping out in support!

Support The Cause

Money raised will go directly to improving maternal health care in Oregon.

All proceeds benefit The Oregon Affiliate of the American College of Nurse-Midwives and the Oregon Midwifery Council. 

Center For Hope & Safety

10% of your registration will go directly to The Center for Hope & Safety, which is a 501(c)(3), independent nonprofit offering safe refuge and support to victims and survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking and human trafficking.

You can learn more about this organization via their website HopeAndSafety.org or via their Facebook / Instagram pages. 

Diaper Drive

One in two families cannot afford diapers.
Please bring new cloth or disposable diapers for donation to local nonprofit diaper banks on the day of the event. Donations will be delivered into The National Diaper Bank Network (NDBN), a national nonprofit established in 2011.

For more information on this important topic, see nationaldiaperbanknetwork.org or track the tag #enddiaperneed. 

Registration

Registration is open from Feb 24th until the start of the race on May 15th at 11pm through this event page on RunSignup.com. 

  • Registrations before May 3rd to receive a souvenir T-shirt and a discounted registration price of $48. T-shirt availability is not guaranteed for registrations after May 3rd.
  • Registrations between May 10th through May 16th do not include a T-shirt but remain discounted at $48 and T-shirt availability is not guaranteed. 
  • Registration starting at 5pm on Friday, May 15th, through race day will be $58 and T-shirt availability is not guaranteed. Sign up early!
  • Registration for ages 16 and under is FREE.

name: Milwaukie Mile
description:
Welcome to the second annual Milwaukie Mile! Our goal is to provide a safe and fast course for all members of the community to race their pace and set a new personal best in the mile! The course runs gently downhill along the Trolley Trail, starting at the Park Avenue Max Station and finishing in Milwaukie Bay Park. The race will be held the morning of Saturday July 12th, 2025.

The race is open to runners, walkers, and families with strollers. Dogs are not allowed to accompany runners, walkers, or volunteers. You can spectate with your dog on a leash, but please stand back from the course when doing so for the safety of the participants. 

***Please note - T-shirt size and availability are not guaranteed for registrations after July 4th.***

 

Awards

All registered participants will receive a Milwaukie Mile T-shirt. The top-3 finishers in the following categories will receive a special award:

  • Non-binary
  • Open Women
  • Open Men
  • 18 and under Girls
  • 18 and under Boys

 

Transportation

The race starts only a few steps from the Park Ave Orange Line Max Station. Participants and spectators are encouraged to use public transportation to travel to the race!  If you must drive to the race, auto users are encouraged to park in Downtown Milwaukie or at the Park Ave park and ride garage

 

Donations

A portion of the race proceeds will be donated to the Milwaukie High School Cross Country team. If you want to make a dedicated donation to the team to support their 2025 season, we will gladly pass 100% of your donation on to the team! Any amount given would be greatly appreciated and thank you for your generosity! Please click the Donate tab above to donate directly. 

 

Sponsorship

The Milwaukie Mile is a small community event which would not be possible without the support of generous sponsors. If you would like to support or sponsor the event in any way, please email Milwaukiemile@gmail.com.

 

Zenner's - For 95 years, Zenner's has been perfecting its craft of quality sausages and smoked meats, prepared from the best local ingredients into products that have become Northwest favorites.

Bliss Esthetics - Nestled in Gladstone, Oregon, Bliss Esthetics is your one-stop getaway for self-care.

SaunaGlo - Located in the heart of downtown Milwaukie, SaunaGlo is a community Nordic sauna and cold contrast lounge. Experience how a magical place can inspire, heal and awaken your spirit and the senses.

 

Volunteers

Milwaukie Mile is supported by some amazing volunteers! They help us with event coordination, athlete safety, and logistics. If you would like to volunteer, please reach out!

 

Photos:

Mateo Flores was out on the course capturing all the fun. Photos can be found on a shared google drive linked HERE. These are free for you to download for personal use - we only ask that you honor Mateo’s hard work and give photo credit to Mateo Flores or tag @teotooktheflick when sharing on Instagram. Feel free to also tag @milwaukiemile so we can celebrate with you!

name: Monsters & Mimosas 5K - Diamond Lake
description:
Get ready for a spooky-good time at the Monsters & Mimosas 5K, where Halloween fun meets festive celebration! This spirited run invites ghosts, goblins, and costumed creatures of all kinds to hit the course for a frightfully fantastic fall morning.

Join us at Diamond Lake Resort where all race participants will receive a custom finisher medal, a race-themed shirt, and a refreshing mimosa waiting for them at the finish line—because even monsters deserve a little sparkle after a solid run! We'll have juice and water for those under 21.

We’ll also be recognizing top finishers with awards in the usual five-year age groups starting at 10 & under, giving everyone a chance to show off their speed along with their costumes.

Join us for miles, mimosas, and a whole lot of Halloween magic!

name: Newport Celebration Run
description:
Join the Newport Celebration Run on July 4th!

Celebrate Our 12th Anniversary with a Unique and Scenic Running Experience!

Event Highlights:

🌊 Exclusive Run on NOAA Pier: A rare chance to run on the 1,300+ feet NOAA pier, thanks to NOAA's MOC-P.
🏅 Finisher's Medal: For all half marathon, 10k, and 5k finishers.
🍺 Free Beer: (21 and over) Courtesy of Rogue Brewery.
🎟️ Personalized Custom Bibs
⏱️ Professionally Chip-Timed Races

Course Information:

  • Half Marathon: Challenging course with ~1,500 ft elevation gain, featuring ~5.22 miles of pavement, ~5.28 miles of single-track trails, and ~2.6 miles of paved roads.
  • 10k & 5k: Flat, fast courses perfect for setting a personal record.
  • Kids Run: Fun and exciting race for the little ones!

What you'll get:

✔️ Finisher's Medal for all 1/2 Marathon, 10k & 5k finishers
✔️ Personalized custom bib
✔️ Professionally chip-timed
✔️ Beautiful scenic, flat courses
✔️ (1) Beer (21 and over) Courtesy of Rogue Brewery

Why Run with Us?

  • Support a Great Cause: A portion of every registration supports the Rotary Club of Newport.
  • Run Scenic Routes: Enjoy breathtaking views of the Pacific Ocean, Yaquina Bay, and more.
  • Community Spirit: Join a well-supported, friendly event with a vibrant atmosphere.

name: Newport Resolution Run
description:
Welcome 2026 with a Splash!

Kick off the New Year with the Newport Resolution Run & Polar Bear Plunge—an unforgettable way to embrace 2026! Choose from three exhilarating races:

🏃‍♂️ Half Marathon – A thrilling mix of flat, fast pavement and challenging single-track trails. Start and finish on flat terrain, but prepare for a 10K of trails in between that will test your endurance. The half marathon has a 2:45 cutoff time for full course support, but we’ll be cheering you across the finish line no matter what!

🏃‍♀️ 10K & 5K – Flat, fast, and perfect for setting your New Year’s PR!

The Ultimate Finish Line Experience

The race concludes at the breathtaking Pacific Ocean shoreline. And here’s the twist: 🎉 Celebrate your finish by plunging into the icy Pacific for a Polar Bear Plunge! The plunge is optional, but the memories will last forever. (Prefer to stay dry? That’s okay too!)

Why Join

This event is all about challenging your limits, celebrating the New Year, and embracing the invigorating thrill of the Oregon Coast. With scenic views, fun camaraderie, and an electric atmosphere, it’s the perfect way to start your year!

Registration Policies

💰Refunds:

  • No Refunds. No Expection.
  • Cancel 30+ days before the race to receive a 50% credit toward future Ardor Adventures events.
  • No credit for cancellations made within 30 days of the race.

🔄 Transfers:

  • Transfers are allowed until the December 21, 2024, deadline. A $10 transfer fee applies.

More Information

📅 Race Date: Saturday, January 3, 2026
📍 Location: South Beach State Park, Newport, OR
🌐 Learn More: Event Website

Don’t Miss Out!

The Newport Resolution Run & Plunge is more than a race—it’s a celebration of resilience, adventure, and starting the year with bold goals. Whether you’re running for a personal best, tackling the half marathon trails, or taking the ultimate plunge, this is the event to launch your 2026 with purpose.

✨ Register now and start your year with a splash!

name: Newport Turkey Trot
description:
🦃A Thanksgiving Tradition for Lincoln County Families!

Join us for the 13th Annual Newport Turkey Trot — a festive, family-friendly Thanksgiving morning tradition! Whether you're walking or running, the 5K, 10K, and Kids Fun Run offer something for everyone. Enjoy scenic views of Yaquina Bay, the Hatfield Marine Science Center, and the Pacific Ocean — and start your holiday with fun, fitness, and community.

🎭Costume Contest 
Show up in your best Thanksgiving-themed gear and you could win fun prizes! We love seeing turkeys, pies, pilgrims, and creative flair on the course.

🤝 Giving Back
A portion of every registration supports the Food Share of Lincoln County, helping local families in need during the holiday season.

 

👟Team Registration

Rally your crew and run as a team!

Social Teams: Friends, families, and fun-seekers
Corporate Teams: Represent your workplace with pride
School Teams: Parents, teachers, and students unite!

🏆 The team with the most participants will receive special recognition!

🎽Registration Includes:

  • Finisher's Medal for every participant 🏅
  • Chip-timed results ⏱️
  • A beautiful, flat course with coastal views 🌊
  • Support for a great local cause

Shirts are optional and can be added during registration:

$13 if purchased on or before November 16, 2025.
$20 after November 16, 2025



Race Day Schedule (November 27, 2025):

📦 Packet Pickup

  • Wednesday, November 26: 5:30 PM – 7:00 PM at Arctic Circle Restaurant
  • Thursday, November 27: 7:45 AM at South Beach Marina

🏃‍♂️ Race Start Times

  • 9:00 AM – Kids Fun Run (0.5 mile)
  • 9:20 AM – 5K & 10K Start

name: Oregon Trail Game® 5K
description:
Online registration is now closed. There are 18 race-day registration slots available for the 5K, offered on a first-come, first-served basis.

2025 Results: https://www.hubertiming.com/results/2025OregonTrail

Race prices includes shirt as long as registered before May 1st.

Under new ownership! The Oregon City Schools Foundation is producing the race this year. All proceeds benefit Oregon City Schools.

Based on the classic 1980's computer game, The 8th Annual Oregon Trail® Game is ready for you to make some decisions!

Ford the river or float it? Stop to hunt or keep moving to make it to the Oregon Territory before winter falls? The Oregon Trail® Game has a simple premise—take on the persona of a pioneer in 1848 and get your covered wagon from Missouri to Oregon City without breaking a wagon wheel or losing a relative to dysentery. 

Now the game has been reincarnated in the form of a 5k race. While fans of the classic 80s video game will enjoy this literal stroll down memory lane, even the uninitiated will enjoy the challenge of getting through the race, and staying alive on the metaphorical trail. Grab your pioneer bonnet and get ready to survive the journey! 

In addition to receiving a timed score, runners will also receive a game score at the end, based on the decisions they make throughout the game. 

The Kids Fun Run will start at 9:30am. It'll be divided into two groups. The younger group will run approximately 100 yards. The older group will run approximately 200 yards. The kids fun race is untimed.

COURSE:
The Oregon Trail® Game 5K is a fun yet challenging course through historic Downtown Oregon City.  Get up, get moving, and don't die of a snake bite!


 

Hope to see you out on the trail!

name: ORRC 1200 Club
description:
ORRC’s 1200 Club program is available for current club members to run or walk 1,200 miles in one calendar year (averaging about 100/month, or about 25/week). The purpose is meant to be a challenge and motivational tool running from January 1 through December 31.

Participants who complete 1200 miles in one calendar year (January through December) receive a jacket the first year, and patches to add to the jacket in subsequent years. You must be prepared to track your walking and running miles and report them to the club at the end of each month.

Give yourself a challenge and join the 1200 club! Click here to join ORRC if you're not already a member.

name: ORRC Ralph's Run
description: Formerly the ORRC Y2K Run, now Ralph's Run in honor of longtime ORRC member Ralph Brown, this event moves back to its original premise of a changing distance every year. Starting out in 1986 as the 8.6 in '86, it will now be 20.26K in 2026. You get a new PR every year! It also features a 10K run/walk, a 5K run/walk, and a kid's run.  All events start at 9am and the course closes at noon.  (There is an 8:30 start intended ONLY for 20.26K participants who can’t make the three hour cut-off.)

name: ORRC Turkey Trot at The Zoo
description:
The Non-ORRC Member 5K is SOLD OUT!

You can still register by becoming an ORRC member and registering for the ORRC Member 5K.

To become a member click here: ORRC Membership

The ORRC Turkey Trot at the Oregon Zoo is a multi-generational family event. Runners and walkers of all abilities love the 5K, untimed out-and-back course.  The event starts at The Oregon Zoo by the Forestry Center and the Max station, then goes out toward the International Rose Garden, and finishes inside The Oregon Zoo at the Elephant Plaza. The Tot Trot (children 0- 4 years old) and the Gobble Gallop (for children between 5 and 10 years old) events follow the 5K at the Elephant plaza inside the zoo.

Every entrant in the 5K and kids events receive an awesome beanie hat and chocolate turkey. Event shirts are an optional purchase, but the deadline to request a shirt is November 1st.

PLEASE NOTE: The event is capped for non-ORRC members at 2,300 participants! And there is no day of race registration. Register early to ensure your entry! Last year's event sold out by November 6th!

Approximately $25,000 of registration fees benefit The Oregon Zoo.

name: ORRC Vernonia Marathon,  Half Marathon, and Marathon Relay
description: Picture yourself running a beautiful, tree-lined course along the 21 mile Banks-Vernonia State Trail.  Both events feature a gentle 7-mile, 400-foot downhill into Banks.  Hot soup, baked potatoes and hot showers await all runners and walkers. This Boston Marathon qualifier course, USATF Certified, is point-to-point, with 23 miles closed to vehicular traffic. The half marathon course is also USATF Certified.

name: Owyhee Off-Road Challenge
description: Embark on an unforgettable adventure in the heart of the Owyhee High Desert! Join us in Adrian, Oregon—just 54 miles northwest of Boise, Idaho—for the Owyhee Off-Road Challenge, featuring 55k, Half Marathon, 10k, and 5k distances. Immerse yourself in stunning vistas of the Owyhee and Snake River Valleys, rugged peaks, and wide-open spaces, all while enjoying the warm hospitality of the Adrian community. With the friendliest volunteers west of the Rockies, this event promises not only breathtaking scenery but also a welcoming, small-town vibe. name: OXFORD Classic Community 5k
description:
Welcome to the 34th Annual Oxford Classic! This meet has become one of Central Oregon’s longest-running and most competitive cross country traditions. Each year it brings together teams from across the region for a high-level mid-season competition. For the first time, we are excited to add a Community 5k — open to everyone who wants to be part of the action!

The Oxford Classic will be held at Drake Park in Bend, Oregon. The course follows a loop through the park along the scenic Deschutes River, featuring a mix of grass and paved pathways. It is flat and fast, with wide stretches designed to accommodate pack racing and plenty of areas for spectators to cheer.

name: PDX Triathlon Festival
description:
Join us for the 43nd Annual PDX Triathlon Festival at Blue Lake Regional Park and kick off the summer racing season. The fun begins on Sunday where athletes compete on our scenic, flat and fast course in either the Super Sprint, Sprint or Olympic Distances. NEW: A 5K on Sunday or try our Paddle Triathlon for those of you who would rather kayak or paddle-board! Relay options are great for friends, family & co-workers!

The Annual PDX/Blue Lake Triathlon was started by the Portland Triathlon Association and Frank Goulard, who is still an active, local Masters Triathlete. He participates in many of our events so come on out and meet the legend, the man who started it all for us here locally!

This weekend festival offers an Olympic and Sprint Distance Triathlon, Duathlon & AquaBike, and a Super Sprint course that offers shorter distances for those new to the sport or just going for pure, raw speed. The Super Sprint is also a great event for our Junior Triathletes!

Recognized by NW triathletes as the “must do” event to open the triathlon season, the PDX Triathlon encompasses two full days of racing (Kids races & Sunset 5k on Saturday & Super Sprint, Sprint & Olympic races on Sunday) including a Sports & Fitness Expo. Triathlon Clubs from across the NW gather to launch the MultiSport season.

The bike courses are flat and fast, with the majority occurring on a section of Marine Dr that is closed to all but local traffic. This makes the course one of the safest and fastest in the region.

PARKING IS INCLUDED WITH REGISTRATION COST.

Triathlon Clubs from across the NW gather to launch the MultiSport season.

The bike courses are flat and fast, with the majority occurring on a section of Marine Dr that is closed to all but local traffic. This makes the course one of the safest and fastest in the region.
