name: Portland Bridge Swim
description:
Portland Bridge Swim: Sellwood Bridge to St. Johns Bridge

Sunday July 12, 2026

Ultramarathon-Distance Open Water Event

Hosted by Portland Bridge Swim

 

LOCATION & COURSE:   The course is approximately 11 miles (17 km) on the east side of the Willamette River through downtown Portland, Oregon. The swim will start at Sellwood Riverfront Park (SE 7th Av. & Miller St.) south of the Sellwood Bridge, pass under all 12 of Portland’s bridges on the Willamette River, and finish at Cathedral Park (N. Edison & Pittsburg Av.) west of the St. Johns Bridge. Water temperature is expected to be 66–74 degrees Fahrenheit.


TIDES & START TIME:  High tide on July 12, 2026 is 3:13 am, and low tide is at 12:42 pm. The swim will start at 7:30 am and all swimmers must be out of the water by 3:30 pm.


ELIGIBILITY: This event is open to any swimmer over the age of 18 years old who has completed the eligibility requirements.


ENTRY WEBSITE & REGISTRATION:  To qualify, swimmers must show that they have completed a minimum 5000 m/5500 yd swim faster than 1:40, within 3 years of race day. Only pool swims will be accepted for qualification. Swimmers who cannot complete one mile in open water in 35 minutes should NOT enter. All entries MUST be received by 4:59 pm Pacific time on Sunday, July 5, 2026. Due to organization & safety needs, late or day-of-race entries will not be accepted.


ENTRY LIMITS:  The Portland Bridge Swim is limited to the first 100 entrants. We will maintain a waiting list in case early entrants drop out.


CANCELLATION POLICY:  Swimmers who do not compete, or who do not complete the swim, are not eligible for refunds. If the swim is canceled up to 60 days prior to race day, 50% of entry fees will be refunded. If the swim is canceled less than 60 days prior to race day, no fees will be refunded.


RULES:  

  • SAFETY TOW BUOYS (STBs): All swimmers MUST wear the STB, provided with their swim packets, during their entire portion of the swim. STBs, defined as inflatable buoys tethered to the waist of the swimmer, are permitted in Category I Swimwear events per USMS Rule 303.4.2.E. Swimmers may not use the STBs for flotation assistance.
  • Swimmers must wear the standard latex cap provided in their swim packet. Swimmers must notify race organizers by Friday, July 3, 2026 if the cap cannot be worn. You will need to wear a suitable cap of the color assigned to you for your wave.
  • All drafting is prohibited.  Swimmers must remain 3 meters or more from other swimmers, except when rounding buoys, when overtaking other swimmers when space is not readily available, when unescorted at the start and finish of the swim, and/or when the swimmer's escort craft becomes disabled.  Incidental or accidental incursion into the 3-meter zone of another swimmer shall not be the basis for disqualification.
  • Swimmers may not make deliberate contact with craft, craft operators, and/or physical features on or near the course during the swim.
  • Propulsive devices, such as fins & paddles, and flotation aids, such as pull-buoys, may be allowed at the discretion of the Race Director if an adaptive category is offered for the race. Please contact info@portlandbridgeswim.com before registering if you need to use an adaptive device.
  • Earphones and snorkels are also not allowed. 
  • Motorized watercraft are not permitted as escorts for swimmers. Under no circumstances may a swimmer come in contact with a motorized watercraft. Swimmers who are supported by motorized craft will be disqualified.

QUALIFYING SWIM:  

  • To qualify for individual entry, swimmers must show that they have completed a minimum 5000-meter (5500-yard) swim faster than 1:40, within 3 years of race day.
  • Only pool swims will be accepted for qualification. This qualifying swim does not have to take place in a competition, but registration requires the location of the swim and the signature of an observer. 
  • If you make a mistake in your entry, we will make a good-faith effort to get your correct qualifying swim information. However, swimmers who cannot provide appropriate qualifying time information WILL NOT BE PERMITTED TO SWIM and their entry fee will not be refunded. 

CUT-OFF TIME:  For safety coverage, swimmers on the course who have cleared the Fremont Bridge (approximately 5.5 miles) within 4 hours of race start (note: later waves have less than 4 hours) will be stopped, transported to the race finish, and listed as DNF in the results. Swimmers who have not completed the race within 7 hours of race start will be stopped, transported to the race finish, and listed as DNF in the results.


SAFETY—OUR PRIMARY CONCERN:  Safety boats will monitor the entire course and medical personnel will be on site at the finish. Swimmers are required to have an escort in a non-motorized craft (kayak, stand up paddleboard) in a life vest and equipped with an additional life vest for the swimmer. Each escort will be provided additional mandatory race-specific safety materials. Swimmers MUST wear the brightly-colored swim cap and use the standard tow float provided in their race packet. Swimmers and escorts must follow all announced safety rules without exception.


ESCORTS:  Swimmers are required to have an escort in a non-motorized craft (ie. kayak or paddleboard). Swimmers must provide their own paddler escort and craft. For swimmer safety, motorized watercraft are not permitted to escort swimmers. 


KAYAK RENTALS: A limited number of kayaks, provided by Alder Creek Kayaks, are available for rental as an option at registration.  Kayak rental includes boat, paddle, two life jackets, delivery at the start, and pick-up at the finish. If the escort cannot fit in a standard-size rental kayak, please contact the race organizers to discuss options.


TRANSPORTATION:   A shuttle will be available at the finish to transport swimmers and escorts back to Sellwood Park. With the exception of the rental kayaks above, swimmers are responsible for transporting their kayaks and they may not be taken on the shuttle.


SCHEDULE:  Sunday, July 12, 2026

5:30-7:00 am Check-in at Sellwood Park
6:30 am Pre-race meeting
7:30 am Swim start
11:30 am Individual swimmers who have not reached mile 6 will be stopped & transported to the race finish.
2:00 pm Awards at finish in Cathedral Park
3:30 pm Individual swimmers who have not reached the finish will be stopped & transported to the race finish.

AWARDS:  All finishers will receive a 2026 Portland Bridge Swim medal.  Awards will be presented to overall race winners, and the top 3 finishers in each category. 


RESULTS:  Results will be available after the race, and will be posted at www.portlandbridgeswim.com.  


OREGON SERIES:  Involvement in the Oregon Series TBD.


EVENT WEBSITE:  www.portlandbridgeswim.com


EVENT DIRECTORS:  Daniela Klaz, info@portlandbridgeswim.com

name: Race to Space
description:
Join us for the 5th Annual Race to Space on May 9, 2026, on Linfield University's Wellness Trail. This is a timed race with 12, 8, 6, 3, and 1-hour options, and an alternate 4-loop relay for teams of 2-4 participants. NEW this year is the Bingo Run! For each lap, runners draw a number. Once you have pulled the three numbers that match what appears on your bib, you have finished the race. Choose from 10, 20, or 30-number races, with the option to continue running after your bingo card is filled. 

Base Camp is located at the start/finish of our approximately 1.5-mile loop trail course, located at 57 Keck Drive, McMinnville, OR.  Profits from the event go to charity.

 

Sign up before December 31 to get the best pricing.

 

Find Your Why

Our event provides runners and walkers with many options because people have different goals and fitness levels. Looking for something short just to get moving or to work back from an injury? Try the one-hour Moon Shot or grab friends and run the relay. Training for a half marathon? The three-hour Mission to Mars will give runners lots of time to get in the mileage. Maybe you're preparing for a marathon or longer. The 6-, 8-, and 12-hour options are for you. If running a marathon or ultra has always been on your bucket list, but you're worried about being too slow or not having enough fitness, the 6-, 8-, and 12-hour races provide a great opportunity to fulfill that dream. 

Want to try your luck and something new at the same time? The Bingo Run gives every runner a chance to win, with a bit of luck, by filling their card first. Every time you complete a lap, draw a number. If that number matches one of the bingo numbers on your bib, you mark off that number. Once your bingo card is filled, you're finished! (though we'll probably let you keep going). Awards will be given to those who fill their card the fastest, measured both in time and the number of draws, so there may be multiple winners. If the competitive aspect doesn't matter to you, maybe this event appeals to you for the uncertainty of how far you will have to run to get a bingo. 

Regardless of your why, the beauty of a loop course is that you only need to finish one lap to be a finisher (unless you're in the relay, then your team needs to complete four loops, or if you're in the Bingo Run, then who knows how far you will have to go). If you have your sights set on running the 26.2 miles of a marathon or longer, but you're just not feeling it on race day, you're never more than 3/4 of a mile from the start/finish. Those rebuilding from an injury or testing themselves with a new distance can bail if needed and still be a finisher.

(Scroll down toward the bottom if you want to know our why)

General Information

The various events start at different times to avoid course congestion.

Starting at 7:00 AM:

Abduction Adventure (12-hour race)

Bingo 30

Starting at 8:00 AM:

Moon Shot (1-hour race) 

Journey to Pluto (8-hour race) 

Bingo 20

Starting at 9:30 AM:

Mission to Mars (3-hour race)

Solar Shuffle (6-hour race)

Bingo 10

Starting at 12 PM (noon):

Space Sprint (4-loop relay, 2-4 runners per team)

 

Pricing (through the end of December)

Moon Shot - 1 hr race - $25.00 

Mission to Mars - 3 hr race - $40.00 

Solar Shuffle - 6 hr race - $50.00 

Journey to Pluto - 8 hr race - $60.00 

Abduction Adventure - 12 hr race - $80

Bingo 10 - $40

Bingo 20 - $60

Bingo 30 - $80

Runners in the timed events who also want to compete in Bingo can do so for an additional $10

Space Sprint - 4 loop relay (2-4 per team) - $60.00 per team 

 

What to Expect on Race Day

Plan to arrive at least 30 minutes prior to your scheduled race to pick up your race bib. Parking is just a few feet from packet pickup and the start/finish. 

 

Course Description

Loop course: Our race will be a ~1.5-mile loop course run at Linfield University’s wellness trail. It is a mostly dirt/bark dust trail. The start/finish and aid station will be located just off SE Lever Street on Wildcat Circle (in Google Maps, it is the parking lot to the SE of the Linfield University Nicholson Library). There are areas for runners to set up their own aid stations or chairs along the course, and vehicle access is very close.

What shoes should I wear? The trail is not very technical, with just a few tree roots; road shoes work best in dry conditions. If conditions are wet and muddy, trail shoes might be a better option.

Oregon's May weather can be unpredictable. For two of the first four years of the event, high temperatures topped 85 degrees. We have yet to have any significant rain at the event, but this is Oregon, so mentally prepare for anything.

The aid station will provide water and an electrolyte drink, as well as a variety of sweet and savory snacks. Special requests will be considered, but runners with specific needs or preferences are encouraged to bring their own food and drink to supplement. Runners are encouraged to bring their own reusable cups to help reduce waste. 

 

Volunteer Information

Not looking to run? We are seeking volunteers for our race! Jobs for volunteers include registration and packet pickup, course monitors, aid station, waste management, and set-up/takedown. Volunteers will get swag and our heartfelt thanks.

 

Swag

Top finishers in each race will earn special awards. All participants will receive a pair of high-quality running socks. If we get enough entries by mid-April, shirts will also be provided. We are always working on securing additional swag for our amazing runners and walkers, so stay tuned and be ready to be surprised!

 

Refund policy

Unfortunately, we will not issue any refunds or transfers should you not be able to run on race day. Costs are incurred prior to race day, and profits will be donated to charity, so we cannot make any exceptions to this policy.

Why are we putting on this race?

Most of the crew you will see working the race are students in an Economics of Running class at Linfield University. The class project is to offer an event that encourages students to put their understanding of economic concepts into action. While our primary why is educational, we're happy to provide fitness opportunities, particularly for the running community. If we're fortunate enough to earn a profit on the event, extra monies go to benefit a local charity.

Space Sprint (4-loop relay, 2-4 runners per team)

 

Pricing (through the end of December)

Moon Shot - 1 hr race - $25.00 

Mission to Mars - 3 hr race - $40.00 

Solar Shuffle - 6 hr race - $50.00 

Journey to Pluto - 8 hr race - $60.00 

Abduction Adventure - 12 hr race - $80

Bingo 10 - $40

Bingo 20 - $60

Bingo 30 - $80

Runners in the timed events who also want to compete in Bingo can do so for an additional $10

Space Sprint - 4 loop relay (2-4 per team) - $60.00 per team 

 

What to Expect on Race Day

Plan to arrive at least 30 minutes prior to your scheduled race to pick up your race bib. Parking is just a few feet from packet pickup and the start/finish. 

 

Course Description

Loop course: Our race will be a ~1.5-mile loop course run at Linfield University’s wellness trail. It is a mostly dirt/bark dust trail. The start/finish and aid station will be located just off SE Lever Street on Wildcat Circle (in Google Maps, it is the parking lot to the SE of the Linfield University Nicholson Library). There are areas for runners to set up their own aid stations or chairs along the course, and vehicle access is very close.

What shoes should I wear? The trail is not very technical, with just a few tree roots; road shoes work best in dry conditions. If conditions are wet and muddy, trail shoes might be a better option.

Oregon's May weather can be unpredictable. For two of the first four years of the event, high temperatures topped 85 degrees. We have yet to have any significant rain at the event, but this is Oregon, so mentally prepare for anything.

The aid station will provide water and an electrolyte drink, as well as a variety of sweet and savory snacks. Special requests will be considered, but runners with specific needs or preferences are encouraged to bring their own food and drink to supplement. Runners are encouraged to bring their own reusable cups to help reduce waste. 

 

Volunteer Information

Not looking to run? We are seeking volunteers for our race! Jobs for volunteers include registration and packet pickup, course monitors, aid station, waste management, and set-up/takedown. Volunteers will get swag and our heartfelt thanks.

 

Swag

Top finishers in each race will earn special awards. All participants will receive a pair of high-quality running socks. If we get enough entries by mid-April, shirts will also be provided. We are always working on securing additional swag for our amazing runners and walkers, so stay tuned and be ready to be surprised!

 

Refund policy

Unfortunately, we will not issue any refunds or transfers should you not be able to run on race day. Costs are incurred prior to race day, and profits will be donated to charity, so we cannot make any exceptions to this policy.

Why are we putting on this race?

Most of the crew you will see working the race are students in an Economics of Running class at Linfield University. The class project is to offer an event that encourages students to put their understanding of economic concepts into action. While our primary why is educational, we're happy to provide fitness opportunities, particularly for the running community. If we're fortunate enough to earn a profit on the event, extra monies go to benefit a local charity.

name: Rose City Mile
description:
Rose City Track Club is proud to present the 9th annual Rose City Mile! Our mission is to provide a fun and accessible opportunity for runners of all ages and abilities to test their fitness. Join us on Saturday, June 20 at Franklin High School in southeast Portland for a track meet like no other.

We believe that everyone has a place in the running community that is respectful, safe, and inclusive. On race day we present awards in men's, women's, and non-binary categories. Participants who select either "Non-Binary" or "Prefer Not to Say" during sign up will be eligible for the non-binary awards category.

Online registration closes at midnight on Thursday, June 18.

Runners will have the option of registering for the Rose City Mile the day of the race for $38.50 (inc. $3.50 fee). Same day registration closes 50 minutes before the first heat in each section.

Sponsorship

Rose City Mile would not happen without the generous support of our sponsors. Our event features 300 competitors of all ages, as well as many spectators cheering them on. We have four tiers of sponsorship available. To learn more, please check out our 2025 sponsor packet or email rosecitymile@rosecitytrack.com.

name: Roseburg to Coos Bay Relay
description:
68-mile, 5 person running team or 24-mile, 4 person walking team.  Staggered start depending on predicted finishing time.  The slowest running teams (or those who want to get more value for money) will start at 6AM.  Runners start a the ADAPT parking lot in Roseburg, walkers start in Laverne Park, Coquille.  The race ends at the Coos History Museum (1210 N. Front St., Coos Bay). 

Who says running is a lonely sport?  Grab four friends and start cheering!  

Proceeds benefit Camp Millennium, dedicated to providing outdoor recreation activities to kids with cancer.

name: Run for a Reason 2026 with Two Daughters Foundation
description:
Run for Two Daughters Foundation at the 2026 Eugene Marathon, raise money to cover your registration costs, and support our mission of providing free peer grief support to young adults across the country!


There's no more iconic place to achieve your running accomplishment than in Track Town USA! You can tackle the full 26.2 miles in the marathon, or sign up for the half marathon or 5k! Whatever you choose, you will be in the company of other Two Daughters Foundation team members and enjoy the beautiful scenery of South Eugene and the University of Oregon.


To run for team Two Daughters Foundation, sign up and fundraise for your spot! The fundraising minimums are listed below. Two Daughters Foundation will send you a registration link once you've achieved your fundraising goal. All profits received by Two Daughters Foundation go towards our charity's mission of providing free grief support to young adults in Oregon and beyond that are navigating the serious illness or loss of a parent or parental figure.

**Note: The deadline to meet the fundraising minimum is March 15, 2026**

All Team Members Receive:

  • FREE registration for the race! As soon as your fundraising goal is met, your registration fee is waived for the race of your choice.
  • An official Two Daughters Foundation T-shirt
  • Fundraising platform and tools, including your own fundraising page and ongoing fundraising support from Two Daughters Foundation staff

Fundraising Minimums:


Marathon: $350

Half Marathon: $250

5k: $150


Once you've achieved your fundraising goal, Two Daughters Foundation will reach out to you with a registration link that will allow you to register at no additional cost to you.

Please note that you will be accountable for covering the remaining amount to meet the fundraising minimum if the fundraising minimum is not met by the fundraising deadline.


Contact info@twodaughtersfoundation.org if you have any questions! We are happy to help you get set up and provide fundraising tips. 


We look forward to running with you!

name: Run for Salem Free Clinics
description:
2025 Race Results are here 

Thank you for supporting Salem Free Clinics, a community non-profit dedicated to providing quality, compassionate healthcare at no cost to the uninsured as an expression of Christ's love. Last year’s race was a huge success with a record amount of participants. This year, we are excited to announce that we will have both an in-person and virtual race option again!

 

Register by July 31st to be guaranteed a free t-shirt (only adult sizes available)!
•    $30 for Early Bird Pricing | $35 starting August 1st
•    $15 registration fee for ages 6-12
•    Ages 5 and below register for free (no t-shirt included)

 

NOTE TO IN-PERSON PARTICIPANTS: At our event, we ask that you keep your furry friends at home. Thank you!

 

NOTE TO VIRTUAL PARTICIPANTS: Run or walk your distance between August 8th and August 15th and keep track of your time to send to Huber Timing if you want it posted. To post your time, follow the instructions in your Welcome Email sent at the race start time on August 8th.

name: RUN/WALK FOR THE RARE!
description:
Haley's Heroes Foundation presents 7th Annual RUN FOR THE RARE, a 10k, 5k and 1 mile run/walk to support International Batten Disease Awareness Day.  Did you know that Rare is everywhere? Join us as we run on Sunday, June 14, 2026. 1 in 10 people have a rare disease and 50% of those are children. There are more than 7000 known rare diseases and an estimated 350 million people globally diagnosed with a rare disease. YET, 95% of all rare diseases don't have a FDA approved treatment or cure. Let's run (or walk) to change the course of the lives for all those with rare disease. Post pictures at #RUNWALKFORTHERARE!  

The race will start and finish outside of the Pavilion in the North Meadow. Starting time is 10am and all participants should be finished by 1pm.

Cost is $45 for adults and $35 for children and includes the t-shirt.

Registration fee includes  a T-shirt, coupon for wings and fries, coupon for ice cream and a Photo Booth.

June 13 - Early packet pick up is 2pm-4pm at Gallagher's Fitness | 135 Commercial St NE, Salem, OR 97301
June 14 - Packet pick up beginning at 9am at the run

There are more than 7000 known rare diseases and an estimated 350 million people globally diagnosed with a rare disease. YET, 95% of all rare diseases don't have a FDA approved treatment or cure. Let's run (or walk) to change the course of the lives for all those with rare disease. Post pictures at #RUNWALKFORTHERARE!  

The race will start and finish outside of the Pavilion in the North Meadow. Starting time is 10am and all participants should be finished by 1pm.

Cost is $45 for adults and $35 for children and includes the t-shirt.

Registration fee includes  a T-shirt, coupon for wings and fries, coupon for ice cream and a Photo Booth.

June 13 - Early packet pick up is 2pm-4pm at Gallagher's Fitness | 135 Commercial St NE, Salem, OR 97301
June 14 - Packet pick up beginning at 9am at the run

name: Salem Run'ucopia Thanksgiving Day Turkey Trot 6k/10k/15k
description:
Answers to Frequently Asked Questions: 

Yes, strollers are okay.

No dogs please. Please leave them at home.

Yes, you can still register with this page up until Thanksgiving morning.

Yes, you can change races by going to your profile in RunSignUp and choosing "change event."

Walkers, please do not block the whole path. Stay right, so runners can pass on the left.

 

Music, cowbell, good times… Run’ucopia is a Salem tradition. The course will cross the new bridge through one of the largest interconnected urban park systems in the nation! Bring your family and friends and engage in some healthy activity before your feast.  Consider this your “appetite development.”  It is a tradition of friends, family and competitors. 

Distances:

1K kids run (6 & under) Free! Just sign the form on race day...
6K run/walk (4 mile)

10K run (6.2 mile)
15k run (9.3 mile)

Location: Riverfront Park, Salem, Oregon.  Start/Finish at the pavilion.

Date & Time:  Thanksgiving morning.  Thursday, November 27,2025.  Here is your schedule:

8:00 am   Check-in opens at the pavilion. Grab your bib
8:45         1k Kids race
9:10         Race start 15k
9:12         Race start for 10k

9:14        Race start for 6k

Post-race:  Check the raffle to see if you won

9:50         6k awards. Hot chocolate & coffee from Dutch Bros is enjoyed until supplies run out. Commemorative photos are taken.
10:15      10k awards and 15k soon thereafter.

The Course:  The course is a beautiful tour of the largest interconnected urban park system in the United States and starts at the pavilion on the south side of Salem Riverfront Park.  It passes around the Eco-Earth and onto the new bridge into Minto Brown Island Park.  

The 6k run/walk course is now a little more of a loop course. It is closer to 4 miles, and you get to tour a little more of beautiful Minto Brown Island Park.

The 10k and 15k go deeper into Minto Brown Island Park before heading back to the Pavilion start/finish area. Many signs & volunteers mark the way. Be sure to check out the route below.  The 10k is a very simple out-and-back with a turnaround near the 1930's Buick.

The 15k is also an out-and-back, but on the return, you have to turn right to do your 15k loop, which takes you off the pavement onto a nice dirt trail, directing you back towards the starting line. You go deep, then do the loop.  Signs and volunteers guide the way.

View the 6k course here: 6k/ 4 mile course
 
View the 10k course here:  Revised 10k course
 
View the 15k course here: Revised 15k course

Again this year: Express what you are grateful for this year on the giant chalkboard.

Timing: The Run’ucopia is always chip-timed. 

Pre-Registration:  There is a small online sign-up fee. Register early for the best price. Entry fees are non-refundable and non-transferable.

Early packet pickup: Wednesday 11/26 in downtown Salem at Gallagher’s Fitness Resources (135 Commercial St. NE) from 2:30pm to 5:45pm (Come down to the Basement). Do not arrive early unless you are shopping please. Pickup some new running gear, sports nutrition, or Christmas gifts while you are there.

Age Groups for the 6k, 10k, 15k runs:  14 & under, 15-19, 20-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65-69, 70-79, 80 & over.  Ribbons for top 3 age group placers. Special gifts for top 3 men’s and women’s winners in each distance.

The 1k kids run is free this year, and is for kids 6 and under. Just report to the registration desk to sign the waiver & get their bib. This one is just for fun and is self-timed. All kids run finishers get a ribbon.  5-6 is not too young to do the 6k with the group, but separate sign up is required for that event.

Walking Groups: Walkers are welcome and encouraged to join in the fun.  For safety reasons, we ask walkers to stay to the right side of the path to allow runners to pass on the left.  The paths are narrow, so please do not block the whole path.

Chart your progress:  One of the great things about running & walking is that the improvements are REAL.  They can be clearly seen by your time on the course. So we encourage everyone to write their time on their bibs to remember it for next year. 

Opportunities to contribute to your community: The registration form includes a place to donate to our charity partners. The race organization also makes annual contributions. Please join us to help make Salem awesome.  

Participating again this year is Outward Church and their annual Thanksgiving Meal Program.  They are back at it this year organizing a feast for families in need.  Each Thanksgiving, they cook and deliver full meals to over 200 families, many of them were at least partially sponsored by generous Run’ucopia runners.  To sponsor a family’s full meal, it is $35.  Or please consider just the turkey at $20, or just the sides for $10.  The on-line registration form lets you donate any level you feel able to give. You can read more about it here: http://www.THXSalem.com

As you can imagine, there are a lot of logistics involved in cooking, loading and delivering this many meals. They need your help on the delivery. If you would like to join in delivering Thanksgiving meals, all are welcome, and your help is greatly appreciated. Just check out http://www.THXSalem.com

Salem Harvest is back again as a charity partner, and they also help feed economically-challenged families in our community. These volunteers will be guiding runners around the course.

Family Discount: There is a discount for families of 4+ for the race. To get the discount, on-line registration is required.  We just extended this family discount deadline to November 26. Just register and come get your bibs. As always, you get the best deal by registering early.

Raffle: After you get your bib, be sure to check out the raffle items. There are always cool gear, food, some quirky items to keep it interesting, and some kid stuff. Put your raffle tab from your bib in the jar of your favorite raffle item. You only win the stuff you want to win here.

Sponsors:

Gallagher's Fitness Resources, Dutch Bros Coffee, FastSigns South Salem.

Dutch Bros will be providing coffee and hot chocolate.

More information, including the Frequently Asked Questions, can be found on our webpage at www.RuninSalem.com.

Questions? Please email the Race Director at info@runinsalem.com or call/text 503.750.9245.  Do not contact Gallagher's Fitness Resources regarding the race. GFR is a sponsor and early packet pickup location, but questions go to info@runinsalem.com.

This is a minimalist & green event, so please use all recycling bins, and keep Salem clean.

Come early, enjoy the music and get pumped up!

name: Sandy Community Action Center Annual Tickle Trot 5K
description:
The Tickle Trot is a 5K in Sandy, Oregon that benefits the Sandy Community Action Center held Thanksgiving morning each year.

This year we will have a virtual race option for those that can't attend but wish to support our mission of feeding families in our local community.

This is a fun and informal event available to all ages and is untimed.

Last year our Thanksgiving Boxes serving 707 people in our community were completely funded by this event.  We were able to provide 8,600 pounds of food!

name: Silverton Turkey Trot
description:
Join us for our annual 3k or 5k fun run/walk benefiting the Robert Frost Elementary PTC! The fun will begin and end at Robert Frost Elementary.

Each participant will receive a raffle ticket and can enter to win an incredible prize donated by one of Silverton’s many amazing local businesses! All proceeds go to the Robert Frost PTC to support the students and teachers at Robert Frost Elementary. This is an untimed event, just for fun!

This year will feature a junior course (3k) for the younger runners looking for a shorter challenge. Costumes are encouraged! Strollers and well-behaved, leashed dogs are welcome.

FAMILY REGISTRATION NOTE: If you are registering for a family of four, the registration will show up as one entry without giving an option to add individuals. During the sign in process on the day of the race, the other three members will be verified. If there are any issues with registration, please use the question option and you will be assisted asap. 

Same day registration will be available. 

♣♣♣

UPDATE 11/24/2025 - The Senior Center parking lot will not be available for parking this year, they have a Thanksgiving event that will need the space for their patrons! Please carpool if you can and park at the church next door, or Safeway or up the side streets. We will be closing the Robert Frost parking lot for safety. Please plan a little extra time to get parking. 

♣♣♣

New this year - if you are going to support your friend and family with a warm coffee in hand instead of running, please consider volunteering! Each volunteer can "sponsor" a runner and get a FREE single entry!! Sign up to volunteer and text 5038968185 and you'll receive a URL code for a FREE entry!

♣♣♣

You will NOT be able to purchase a t-shirt day of the race BUT you will be able to order one and have it mailed!!

♣♣♣

All race participants will receive a raffle ticket to enter for their favorite prize (bucket style raffle- you decide which prize/bucket to place your ticket in), with plenty of amazing options up for grabs. 

The raffle will take place after the start of the race (approximately 8:45 am) and winning ticket numbers will be posted for participants to view at the end of the race.  Make sure to have your ticket stub handy after the race in order to claim your prize!

2025 PRIZES!!

This year's PRIZE from - 

Chinook Winds

McMenamins

Oregon Gardens

Chipotle

Portland Japanese Gardens

Trader Joes

Burgerville

Al's Garden and Homes

and MORE!!

 

WE CAN'T WAIT TO SEE YOU ALL!!

name: Sole Sisters 13.1 / 10k / 5k
description:
Women walkers, joggers, and runners of all ages and abilities are welcome to join us in the Sole Sisters Half Marathon, 10k, and 5k! Join us as we celebrate the gift of sisterhood, and the satisfaction of achieving big goals!

Enjoy a beautiful out and back course that winds through the scenic trails along the Willamette River and beautiful side streets of Wilsonville. 

***This is a timing optional race, with special recognition given to the top three finishers in each age division.  

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

Each participant will receive...

  • Weekly Long-distance Routes in 1 of 15 Different Locations beginning March 2026

  • Optional in-person weekly training led by coaches (location dependent)

  • Special Events and Raffles at Road Runner Sports in Tualatin

  • Weekly Emails/Connection 

  • Race Day Breakfast Item 

  • Personalized Race Bib  

  • Finisher's Medal

  • Optional Race Tech T-Shirt or Tank Top available for purchase. 

 

ALL REGISTRATIONS RECEIVED AFTER MAY 10th WILL NOT INCLUDE A PERSONALIZED RACE BIB

 

No refunds.  Transfers are allowed.

Dogs are not allowed on the race course.

name: Southern Oregon Runners Turkey Trot Run
description:
Come to Talent, Oregon for our Thanksgiving run! We will be hosting a food drive for the SOU food bank and a portion of the proceeds will go to SOR Student Runners Programs which include Shoes for Kids (provides shoes to Jr. High and High School athletes who would like to participate in Cross Country and Track but cannot afford proper running shoes), KidsRunFree (provides free entry to all SOR races for kids 18 & under), and XC Project (provides timing support for schools during cross country season).

When - November 27, 2025

Free Turkey Dash Kids Run( 8 and Under)8:00AM| 8 Mile Run 8:15AM|5k Run/Walk 8:30AM|2 Mile Family Run/Walk 8:40AM $20 for members| $25 for non members| Youth 18 and Under are free. Family Pricing available for this event, this is for families and families with extended family in town for the holidays, only.  

Where - Cummins 300 W Valley View Rd, Talent, Oregon 97540

Packet Pick Up - November 26th from 3:30-8pm at Legend Cider Co. Talent Taphouse, 245 W Valley View, Talent, Oregon 97540. Packet pick up is also available from 7-8am on the day of the race. NO DAY OF REGISTRATION will be offered. 

Participants will receive a custom race bib and finishers medal. No age group awards.

NO DOGS, BIKES, SKATEBOARDS OR SKATES PERMITTED.

*Races are on public roads and trails that ARE NOT closed to cars, pedestrian or cyclist.  Please use caution while on public roadways and paths.

name: Support the Girls! Breast Friends 5K Run/Walk
description:
In-Person Registration is Closed!

Thank you for your interest in the Support the Girls 5K! We have reached our participant capacity, and in-person registration is now closed.

Virtual Participation: You can still join the race virtually! Sign up here to participate from home.

 

According to statistics, over 4000 women in Oregon are diagnosed with breast cancer each year and our mission is to ensure no one goes through breast cancer alone. Striving to be relevant, accessible, and inclusive of all who want to participate.  Breast Friends empowers those to thrive beyond their cancer diagnosis through education, community, and support.

 

The services and opportunities we provide would not be possible without the generosity of our greater community!  Please join us for this fun community event at Stickmen Brewery in Tualatin.  The course is paved and mostly flat - perfect for all abilities and ages!  Grab your friends, co-workers, and family, and enjoy this walk/jog/run together!  Afterward, you can rest and recover with pizza and a beverage at Stickmen Brewing.

 

**Registration is CLOSED. Thank you for supporting Breast Friends!.  We’re grateful for everyone who signed up and can’t wait to see you on race day!

Our packet pickup this year will be a big, exciting event! Happening in the parking lot of Fit Alliance (15965 SW 72nd Ave, Tigard, OR 97224) on September 27th from 2pm - 5pm. Learn more by clicking on the packet pickup page to the left and keep an eye on your email the week before the race for all the details!

name: Timberline Marathon and Half Marathon
description:
Get ready for the most picturesque marathon and half marathon trail running course in the Pacific Northwest! The course completely circles shimmering Timothy Lake on single track trails that are absolutely a runner's dream. This gem is nestled at 3,227 feet in the high Cascades and the views of Mt. Hood across the lake are extraordinary.

Finisher medals and gender specific technical shirts are included with your registration.

The journey begins at the Clackamas Lake Historic Ranger Station and takes runners on a magical course that traverses three rustic bridges over sparkling tributaries that feed the deep blue waters of the lake. The ever changing scenery and terrain create an experience that is unparalleled. The Timberline Marathon and Half Marathon is a must for any runner's calendar!

name: Turkey Trot
description:
Join Columbia Gorge Toyota and Honda for our 5th Annual Benefit Run And Walk. 

Our mission is to put on a family friendly event where EVERY dollar brought in will be donated to a local cause.

This year, all funds will be donated to the Columbia Gorge Food Bank. Columbia Gorge Toyota and Honda will MATCH the first $5,000!!!

5k AND 1 mile run/walk options. Kids 12 and under are FREE!

Have a business, group, or organization? Try our Medium or Large flock options to easily sign up the whole crew.

Not a runner, no problem! Bring the whole family (Fido included) for face painting, music, costume contests, photos, fire pits, and the ability to give back in a very simple way. 

The big Lady will also be on location dressed especially for the occasion.

See you there!

name: Ugly Sweater  Run or Walk  5k
description:
It's time for the 5th Annual UGLY SWEATER 5K RUN OR WALK!! Bring the whole family, come dressed in your favorite Ugly Christmas Sweater and kick off the Holiday Season right! Enjoy a beautiful chip-timed run through Sisters in your favorite Ugly Sweater all while giving back! A portion of the proceeds will go to Living Well With Dementia (New non profit in Sisters) AND Outlaws Downhill Ski Team! We love to always give-back right here in Sisters!!

Create a team of 6 or more and receive a discount! (Discount will be refunded back to you once you reach 6 team members)

What you need to know:

  • Early Check in available on Friday 12/5  from 5:00 p.m.-6:30 p.m. (Location TBD)
  • 12/6 Saturday, Check in: Starts at 8:45 a.m.- 9:50 a.m.
  • 9:50- Kids Dash
  • 10:00 a.m.- 5k Run and Walk
  • Where: Race Start/Finish at The Barn: 171 E. Main Ave. Sisters, OR 97759
  • Race will finish at : The Barn with the finisher party!
  • What: Run or Walk a 5k in your best Ugly Christmas Sweater! 
  • Online registration required
  • Food and drink will be available for purchase at "The Barn"

What's included with your registration:

  • Awesome way to kick off the Holiday season with the whole family!
  • Enjoy a complementary beverage: (Beer, Seltzer or non-alcoholic option) at  "The Barn"
  • New this year....Fun Christmas Scarf, complete with light up Christmas tree!
  • Ugly Christmas Sweater Hand-Crafted  Medal
  • Holiday Glasses to complete your outfit!
  • Jingle Bells for your running shoes!
  • Candy Cane Reindeer
  • Chip-Timed event!
  • Meet Santa on the Red Vespa!
  • Custom Race Bibs
  • Hot Chocolate and Coffee Station at Start line!
  • Ugly Christmas Sweater contest for all! With prizes for best couple, best family or team and best individual!
  • New this year.....UGLY SWEATER CONTEST PARADE...FOR THE TOP 15 UGLIEST!
  • Holiday goodies to snack on
  • New tradition with friends and Family

name: Ugly Sweater Fun Run 5k
description:
The Ugly Sweater Run is a one-of-a-kind event that brings together families, friends, and community members to celebrate the holiday season with a dash of humor and a lot of heart. Don your most outrageously festive holiday sweater and run or walk a designated 5k route, creating a joyous spectacle of holiday spirit. This snow or shine event is for all ages and abilities, and even pets are encouraged to dress for the occasion! Join us on Saturday, December 7th at 9:00am at Harbor Links.

All participants will receive a FREE race day gift!

name: United PDX 5K Fun Run
description:
United PDX 5K Fun Run
Location: Shelter #2, Cook Family Park, Tigard, OR
Date: June, 6, 2026
Start Time: 8:00am

United PDX Soccer Club, one of Oregon's largest youth soccer organizations, is excited to host its Second Annual 5K Run/Walk! By participating, you’ll help support nearly 3,000 youth soccer players, ages 4 to 19, as they pursue their passion for the game. This event promises a fun and active way to engage with your community while contributing to a great cause.

The Course:
Run or walk through Tigard’s scenic Cook Park, cross the beautiful Tualatin River, and enjoy the peaceful routes into Durham and Tualatin. The course is one flat, shaded 5K loop, making it perfect for participants of all ages and abilities.

Timing:
The race will be professionally timed by Eclectic Edge Racing.

Post-Race Activities:
After crossing the finish line, stick around for some post-race fun! Visit our amazing vendors, including:

Gotta Have Coffee
Carioca Bowls
Level Beer
It’s the perfect way to relax and refuel after your run!

Support Youth Soccer:
All proceeds from this event go toward supporting the United PDX Soccer Club’s programs, helping kids in our community stay active and connected through soccer.

name: White River Snow Shoe 8k, 4k
description:
UPDATE: Permit is still pending but we are collaborating towards a great result on a non-holiday weekend! You can still register on the lottery system and will not be charged until the permit is granted - no risk while reserving your spot. 

The White River 4k and 8k are both great events for the casual snow shoe enthusiast to the endorphin junkie racer.  Both events begin and end at the White River Sno-Park between Government Camp and Mt Hood Meadows on Hwy 35.  The 4k is a single loop traveling through the upper White River canyon.  The 8k is 2 loops on the same course.  Warm snacks and beverages post race with medals, awards and x-dog raffles of unknown hijinks.

Late registration and check-in beginning at 8:30 AM race morning.  Be sure to bring a change of clothes.  Weather and conditions permitting we will do an awards ceremony immediately following the event.

name: "Walk for Wags & Wishes" 30-Day Dog Walk Challenge
description:
How far can you and your four-legged sidekick wander in 30 chilly days? Slip into FULL-ON WALK MODE—one trot, ten trots, whatever—and log every mile. Watch them stack up like presents under the tree!

Here's our challenge to you:

-Walk every day in December.
-Track your miles with any GPS app (we ❤️ Wooftrax).
-Starting December 1st, log your miles and your progress for bragging rights + surprise prizes + special gifts and incentives. We use the honor system, so please be fair.
-Go fundraiser-mode: raise $100 and we’ll refund your $25 entry.

You don’t need a dog to join the Walk for Wags & Wishes—you can stroll solo, jog with your earbuds, or even strut your stuff on a treadmill! The goal is to move, have fun, and be a fundraising powerhouse for the pets who need us most! Every frosty step fuels Haven Pet Center’s no-kill adoption and medical programs. Ready to unleash the zoomies for a cause?

Sign up, leash up, and let’s turn winter walks into lifesaving magic. How far will you roam?

name: 10th Antioch Rotary Club Bunny Hop 5K a.k.a. Antioch Rotary BunnyHop "X"
description:
2025 Results!

Please join the Antioch Rotary Bunny Hop 5K on April 19, 2025 (The day before Easter).

Here we go Hopping again!!!

It's Summertime so the Easter Bunny is on vacation! Next year we invite participants to run like the Hare or pace yourself steady to victory like the Tortoise. Participants will get a Finisher's Medal and are guaranteed a Bunny Hop T-Shirt if you register before Saturday, March 14, 2026.  Registration will open in October, 2025. If you like to be part of community video please  email your picture to rdeloso@yahoo.com.  Like us and see up to date notices on Facebook @AntiochBunnyHop5K

Important Notes:

(1) Packet Pick up will be at Fleet Feet Sports in Brentwood on Friday, April 3rd from 3-7pm. There will also be same-day Packet Pick-up on Saturday, April 4th from 7:15 - 8:25 a.m. Beat the confusion & crowds on Saturday by passing by Fleet Feet Sports on Friday!

(2) This 5K Fun Run is a timed event. Accurate timing is provided by the E-Tag attached on the back of your Race Bib - your time starts when you cross the Start Line Sensor and you finish when you cross the Finish Line Sensor. Race Timing will be provided by Ford Timing. 

All Finishers will receive a BunnyHop 5K Medal. First Place Overall in Men's & Women's will receive a plaque, and a Gift Card. 

Age Group Medals will go to the Top 3 in each of these Age Groups: 9 and under,
10-14, 15-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, & 70 and up.

AWARDS CEREMONY will take place after the KIDS KWIK DASH & EASTER EGG HUNT approximately 11:10am

(3) The 5K Course is entirely within Corteva Wetlands Preserve and the surface is mostly gravel and grass paths. Because of this we do not recommend bringing strollers or wagons unless you are prepared to carry these over some barriers and over the uneven terrain.

(4) We love our furry friends too, but we do not advise that you bring dogs to this fun run for safety reasons.

(5) The Bunny Hop Start Line is about 3/4 mile from the Antioch Marina Festival/Parking Area - please plan on a 20–30-minute nature walk! Plan on arriving at the Antioch Marina by 8:00 a.m. - there will be plenty of Parking and Porta Potties. Start Time will be approximately 9:00am

(6) This Race will happen Rain or Shine! 

(7) For Runners of Antioch Unified School District - please arrive at the Antioch Marina by 7:30am to pick up your Race Bibs and GoodyBags - There will be a special area for AUSD-sponsored Runners.

(8) Because of the size of the Event, we will not have a "Bag Drop"

(9) The KIDS KWIK DASH will take place at the Antioch Marina Parking Lot at approximately 10:30am

(10) The Easter Egg Hunt will follow the Kids Kwik Dash

The Rotary Club of Antioch is a non-profit volunteer civic organization servicing the local community for over 75 years. Some of the projects include Girls Empowerment Project, Boys King Conference, Community Beautification, and Assisting Seniors in the Community with home repairs.  The Bunny Hop 5k proceeds will directly go toward scholarships at the local high schools. If you would like to learn more about the Rotary Club of Antioch please visit www.antiochrotary.net

name: 12th Annual Turkey Trot OC 5K
description:
2025 ONLINE REGISTRATION IS OPEN! 

Now in its 12th year, we invite you to join our annual Turkey Trot OC 5K on Thanksgiving morning at 8:00 am. Your participation will continue the work of ending homelessness one life at a time. 

Give a hand-up to OC families leaving homelessness behind! 

 

REGISTRATION

Every participant must be registered to take part in the race. 
Children aged three and under, including those in strollers, are welcome to join, but DO NOT need to register. However, they are not eligible to receive a T-shirt or a medal. 

 

PACKET PICK UP
Save time and pick up your packet on a day before the race. A person can pick up packets on behalf of other registrants. 
Packet pickup will be held on Monday, November 24th & Tuesday, November 25th from 3:30-6:00 pm at 1 Hope Drive, Tustin. 

**Packets can also be picked up the morning of the race from 6:30 am - 7:30 am. 

RACE-DAY SCHEDULE 
Pre-race refreshments -  6:30 am
5K Run/Walk starts -  8:00 am
Expo & awards -  following the race

**This event is rain or shine. 

AWARDS
Age Division awards will be given to the first and second place winner of each category:  9 & under, 10-14, 15-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70+.
Top Finisher prizes will also be given for both the top three male and female categories. 

 

GIVEAWAYS
T-shirts & medals will be distributed WHILE SUPPLIES LAST.

name: 13th Annual 5K Run & Walk for Kids' Growth - Los Angeles
description:
RAIN OR SHINE

Join the Human Growth Foundation (HGF) in collaboration with the Children's Hospital of Los Angeles and be part of a GROWing solution!

This community-friendly and leashed-dog-friendly event takes you through the beautiful Griffith Park. Designed for runners and non-runners alike, it encourages the highest level of community involvement. Participants can run or walk the 5K course—families and strollers are welcome!

By joining the 13th Annual 5K Run & Walk for Kids' Growth, you help raise awareness of childhood growth disorders and the importance of early diagnosis and treatment. 

This event also raises critical funds to provide underserved children with rare growth disorders access to care and treatment. All Ages & Walks of Life Encouraged to Participate!

Each registered participant receives: 

✅ Finisher Medal

✅ Event T-Shirt

✅ Food & Refreshments

 

Event Location

Griffith Park 
4800 Crystal Springs Drive (At the Corner of Fire Road & Crystal Springs Drive)
Los Angeles, CA US 90027
Directions/Map: https://maps.app.goo.gl/nGTE9aDcHTajf87K9

🏃‍♂️ RACE DAY SCHEDULE 🏃‍♀️

🕖 7:30 AM – Race Day Registration & Packet Pickup

🕢 8:00 AM – Pre-Race Warm-Up

🕗 8:15 AM – 5K Run/Walk Starts

🏅 Awards Ceremony to follow after all participants return

🎶 Live Entertainment, Food, and Refreshments will be available throughout the event.

🎟 Raffle Prizes, Display Booths, and Giveaways will be distributed during the event.

🕙 10:30 AM – Event Ends

⏱ TIMING This event will be officially timed using conventional timing methods, and the course is paved.

 

🔥 HEAT WARNING 

Los Angeles temperatures/humidity can be high. To stay safe, please:

✔ Drink plenty of fluids (non-alcoholic) for 48 hours before, during, and after the race.

✔ Watch for heat-injury symptoms: dizziness, no sweating, nausea, cramps, redness, incoherent speech or thoughts.

✔ Seek immediate assistance if symptoms occur. 

✔ Wear loose, light-colored clothing for comfort.

 

🚫 CANCELLATION POLICY

Race Management reserves the right to postpone or cancel the event due to circumstances beyond its control (e.g., natural disasters or emergencies). No refunds will be issued under these circumstances. Management may also alter the course and distances for safety reasons.

 

📸 PHOTOS & VIDEO 

Professional photographers and videographers will be capturing the event. By registering for the 5K Run & Walk for Kids' Growth, you consent to having your photo or video taken and used for HGF promotional purposes.

 
🏆 AWARDS 

Awards will be given to the fastest male and female in each age category: 

🔹 10 years and under

🔹 YOUTH

🔹 MEN - ADULT

🔹 WOMEN - ADULT

 

🌟 WHY PARTICIPATE? 

The 5K Run & Walk for Kids' Growth is more than a race—it's a mission. We aim to:

✔ Increase awareness of childhood growth disorders and the importance of early diagnosis and treatment.

✔ Raise essential funds so that underserved children with rare growth disorders can receive care and treatment to reach their full potential.

 

⏰ WALK START TIME 

📍 Event Schedule
The Walk site opens at 7:30 AM, and the route begins at 8:15 AM.

🔹 Arrival Time
We recommend arriving by 7:00 AM for check-in, meeting sponsors, and getting ready for the race.

📏 Route Details
The route is 3 miles long and fully wheelchair and stroller accessible.

🥤 Food & Refreshments

✔ Water

✔ Hydration Drinks

✔ Light Snacks

 

👟 FIRST-TIME PARTICIPANT?

Welcome! We’re excited to have you join us!

✔ Stop by the Registration Tent to pick up your bib & t-shirt.

✔ You can run or walk at your own pace.

 

🐕 CAN I BRING MY DOG? 

Yes! Leashed dogs who are comfortable in large crowds are welcome to join you on Walk Day!

💰 WHERE CAN I TURN IN CASH/CHECK DONATIONS?

✔ We encourage mailing check donations before the Walk!

✔ Make checks payable to: Human Growth Foundation

✔ Check Memo: LA 5K Run/Walk 

 

📬 Mail donations to: 

Human Growth Foundation 43 Glen Cove Avenue, Ste B #224 Greenvale, NY 11548 

 

📷 GETTING EVENT PHOTOS 

We have an amazing photographer capturing the event, but we’d also love to see your experience!

✔ Tag us in your social media posts!

📍 Facebook: Human Growth Foundation

📍 Instagram: @human_growth_foundation

 

❓ HAVE MORE QUESTIONS? Reach out to our Event Coordinator: 

📩 HAYDEN > hayden@hgfound.org

 

 

🚀 We can’t wait to see you and celebrate alongside the HGF Community!

Yes! Leashed dogs who are comfortable in large crowds are welcome to join you on Walk Day!

name: 13th Annual Luc's Run
description:
Luc's Run is held annually each spring in historic Tuolumne, California and Virtually Anywhere in the World. Luc's Run is known as one of the premier races in the county.  We are looking at welcoming our local 10K, 2-mile, and Kids Run (ages 10 & under) back to Tuolumne, CA in 2023! And of course welcoming our supporters around the globe through our virtual run where hundreds of enthusiasts from around the world walk and run in support of Luc’s legacy on their own turf with a virtual 1/2 marathon, 10K, 2-mile, and Kids Run (ages 10 & under). Sign up for two events and save 5%, sign up for all three and save 15%! 

On January 28, 2013, Luc, a United States Air Force pilot was on a training mission over the Adriatic Sea off the coast of Italy. During the sortie, Luc was forced to eject from his F-16 and did not survive the ejection.  Luc is survived by family and friends who continue his Legacy through the Major Lucas Gruenther Legacy Foundation.

Major Lucas Gruenther was an incredible human being.  He was an outstanding F-16 fighter pilot, community role model, and a true humanitarian.  He lived his life to the fullest and never took a single day for granted.  Luc is remembered for the way he treated people with wisdom and kindness and was a genuine human being who made a tremendous positive impact.

All proceeds from this race go to the Major Lucas Gruenther Legacy Foundation, an IRS-approved 501(c)(3) non-profit organization.  The purpose of the Major Lucas Gruenther Legacy Foundation is to bestow scholarships to Americans for the advancement of educational goals and self development.

name: 15th Annual Reindeer Run/Walk
description:
Save the Date: the 15th Annual Reindeer Run will be here December 6th!

Come one, come all! There is something for everyone at the Reindeer Run. We welcome runners and walkers of every level to American Canyon on December 6th, beginning with pre-race festivities at 8am, and a staggered race start (10K at 9am, 5K at 9:05am for runners and 9:10am for walkers).  

 

This is a fun event for the whole family: kids 13-17 are $30 and youth 12 and under are $5 and include a finisher's medal and souvenir antlers! Early bird registration begins July 1st, so be ready to register to join in the fun!

 

*This event is contingent upon the requirements of Napa County Health Guidelines. If deemed necessary by the county, all in-person registrations will be switched to a virtual race. 


*Registration fees are non-refundable. Unused race fees are considered a donation to ACParks.

 

Need a race before the Reindeer Run? Be sure to check out these fantastic races on Thanksgiving Morning, November 27th:

Solano Turkey Trot, by Fleet Feet Vacaville

Napa Valley Turkey Chase, by Athletic Feat

name: 16th Annual BEACHFRONT RUN
description:
Hello Runners & Walkers!

We’re excited to invite you to City Impact's 16th Annual Beachfront Run on Saturday, May 30, 2026, at the beautiful Ventura Promenade.

Enjoy a race course with stunning views of Ventura’s coastline while participating in one of our exciting race options: Half Marathon, 10K, 5K, or the Kids 1K Run. The event will also feature a variety of vendors, lively music, and a festive awards ceremony.

Each participant will receive a custom event shirt and a finisher’s medal. Please note that if you register after March 15th, 2026, we cannot guarantee your preferred shirt size.

Awards will be given to the top 3 finishers in each 10-year age category (10-19, 20-29, etc.), so everyone has a chance to shine!  Whether you’re racing or cheering, this is a perfect event for friends, family, and colleagues to come together and enjoy the day.

All proceeds from the event will benefit City Impact’s programs supporting at-promise youth and families. Your participation makes a difference, and we thank you for your support!        


If you should have any questions, please email info@cityimpact.com or call 805.983.3636 x105.    

Much appreciation,


Vickie Saipale
Development/Event Manager

name: 16th Annual Mardi Gras Madness 5K/10K!
description:
About the Event

Join us on Sunday, March 1, 2026, as the Junior Chamber International of Santa Clarita (JCI) and the Santa Clarita Track Club proudly present the 16th Annual Mardi Gras Madness 5K/10K and Mini Madness 1K — benefiting JCI Santa Clarita and Students Off And Running (SOAR).

SOAR provides local youth ages 14–18 with a fully supported Los Angeles Marathon training experience — completely free for participants and their families — and is an Official Featured Charity of the 2026 Los Angeles Marathon.

What to Expect

Mardi Gras Madness is Santa Clarita’s premier family-friendly run/walk event, offering fun and fitness for all ages! Participants will enjoy a scenic USATF-certified 5K/10K course, chip timing, custom finisher medals, marathon-quality tech shirts, and a vibrant Health & Fitness Expo.

The festivities continue with a beer garden, great food, costume contest, games and giveaways, silent auction, celebrity hosts, and live entertainment. Whether you’re a seasoned runner, a stroller-pusher, or bringing your furry friend, Mardi Gras Madness welcomes everyone!

 
🏃‍♀️ COURSE INFORMATION
The MGM course is a USATF-certified, rolling 5K/10K circuit featuring scenic paseos, bridge overpasses, and sections along the beautiful South Fork River Trail.

Note: The 10K route includes a dirt equestrian trail from Mile 3.25 to Mile 4.85.
 
🎟 EARLY PACKET PICKUP
Skip the lines and pick up your race materials early!

📍 Saturday, February 28 | 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM
Location: Canyon Club Courtyard (rear entrance near H&M), Valencia Town Center

Please bring a valid ID to receive your 2026 - 8 One 8 Beer Garden wristband. No exceptions.

Due to overwhelming demand, onsite registration cannot be guaranteed this year.
 
🕗 RACE DAY SCHEDULE

6:30 – 8:00 AM - Check-In and Pre-Registration
7:25 AM - 1K Warm-Up
7:30 AM - 1K Start
7:55 AM - 5K/10K Warm-Up
8:00 AM - 5K/10K Start
9:30 AM - Awards Ceremony & Prize Drawings
 
🏅 AWARDS
Top 3 Overall Men & Women (5K & 10K)
Top 3 per Age Group:

  • 10 & Under
  • 11–14
  • 15–18
  • 19–29
  • 30–39
  • 40–49
  • 50–59
  • 60+
  • Top 3 Team Finishes
  • All 5K/10K finishers receive a custom medal, t-shirt, and goodie bag!

 
📍 EVENT DETAILS
Date: Sunday, March 1, 2026
Time: 7:00 AM – 12:00 PM
Location: Valencia Town Center, Valencia, CA 91355

name: 2025 Brentwood Turkey Trot for Schools
description:
Welcome to the 12th annual Brentwood Turkey Trot for Schools.  This 5K event benefits both the Brentwood Union School District and Liberty Union High School District athletic programs. We are proud to host this community event to promote health, athletics, and education. 

 

In Person & Virtual Race Options

Participants can choose between an in-person or virtual run. For the in-person run,  the race will be at the Streets of Brentwood on Thanksgiving morning at 8:00 AM.  For the virtual run, you can run whenever and wherever you want starting on Monday, November 24 through Sunday, November 30.  All participants will receive a 2025 race t-shirt and medal.  

 

Race Fees*:

Children ages 3 and under are welcome to participate, no registration necessary.

August 9 - October 31, 2025

  • Ages 4-9 - $20
  • Ages 10-18 - $25
  • Ages 19 and up - $40

November 1 - November 26, 2025

  • Ages 4-9 - $20
  • Ages 10-18 - $30
  • Ages 19 and up - $45

Race Day Registration - November 27, 2025 (Only available if we have not sold out)

  • Ages 4-9 - $30
  • Ages 10-18 - $35
  • Ages 19 and up - $55

If you register on or after November 1st, you WILL NOT be asked to for a t-shirt size.  You will be able to select a t-shirt from a variety of sizes at packet pickup or on race day.  

*Processing fees will be added to your race fee.

Course Information:

For the safety of our trotters DOGS ARE NOT ALLOWED ON THE COURSE.
Strollers are allowed on the course if they are pushed by an adult.  Bikes, scooters, and skateboards are also NOT ALLOWED on the course.

 

Packet Pickup:

Participants can check-in and pick up their race bibs and t-shirt at packet pick up, scheduled for Wednesday, November 26th from 3:00 - 7:00 PM at Pioneer Elementary School located on Shady Willow Lane in Brentwood. *Please note virtual racers will need to pick up their shirt, bib, and medal at packet pickup or race day by 7:50 AM.  We are not able to ship out race swag.   In-person racers with guaranteed shirts sizes will need to pick up their shirts by 7:50 AM on race day or shirts will be released for shirt exchange.

name: 2025 Cayucos Turkey Trot
description:
Thanksgiving Day Family 5k Fun Run / Walk

Check-in and bib pick-up will start Wednesday, November 26th at the Cayucos Pier from 2-4pm.  Each registered participant will have an assigned bib number and Thanksgiving-themed running socks, while supplies last.

On race day, check-in will begin at 7:30am.  We are set to start at 8:30am so be sure to give yourself enough time.  Dogs, strollers, and kiddos on scooters are all welcome.  

All proceeds will equally benefit Cayucos Elementary School and the California Association of Highway Patrolman Widows & Orphans' Trust Fund.

name: 2025 Jingle Bell Run - Los Angeles, CA
description:
Get ready for this year’s Jingle Bell Run, the original festive race for charity brought to you by the Arthritis Foundation. Wear your favorite holiday gear, and let's jingle all the way toward a cure!

Whether you're running, walking, or strolling, bring your friends, family, and coworkers along for the ride. Together, we're spreading joy and making strides towards a brighter future — saying "YES" to life, despite arthritis.

Don't miss out on this special occasion to make a real difference while celebrating four decades of impact with the Jingle Bell Run. Let's lace up, hit the pavement, and jingle our way toward victory over arthritis!

name: 2025 Pacific Palisades Turkey Trot
description:
The annual Pacific Palisades Turkey Trot celebrates its 11th Year on Thanksgiving Day 2025! Please come be part of the family fun...

REGISTER TODAY and join us at The Palisades Village Green in downtown Pacific Palisades on Thanksgiving morning -- November 27th -- to get your holiday season off to a running start!

(NOTE: The 10K course is a second lap of the 5K course)

10 Things to Know for About The 11th Annual Pacific Palisades Turkey Trot…

  1. Parking is available in and around the Alphabet Streets. Be advised Palisades Village is closed and locked.
  2. If you live near downtown Pacific Palisades, please walk. Less cars makes a better experience for everyone involved
  3. Head directly to Sunset & Swarthmore and look for the Registration Area (US Bank Parking Lot)
  4. Festivities start at 7:00 AM -- the earlier you come, the more fun your day will be
  5. Both the 5K and 10K start at 8:15 AM. The race program will conclude by 11AM
  6. LA Leggers and Fast runners to the front. Slower runners, walkers and strollers please move to the back of the field
  7. Medals and Water will be available at the Finish Line
  8. Dogs allowed this year. Please lean up after your dog (bring bags) and be mindful of other runners.
  9. 5k runners ideally should finish by 9:30 AM. 10K runners by 10:30 AM
  10. Medical Staff will be on-site

name: 2025 SHAY 5K Run/Walk
description:
Spreading Help Around You is a 501(c)3 non-profit organization that was founded in 2014 in honor of Shaylyn Anela Pinoliar, who tragically passed away on November 14, 2012. Our mission is to help and support families who have lost a loved one, educate them on the importance of being prepared during such a time of loss, and provide active service to the community.  As well as promoting Pedestrian Safety Awareness. This year, we proudly launched the SHAY Scholarship Program, marking an exciting new chapter in our commitment to supporting education and empowering future leaders. 

Each year, since Shaylyn’s passing, family, friends, and community members gather to honor her memory with an Annual 5k Run/Walk on Thanksgiving morning. Last year, we moved the event to Saturday after Thanksgiving. It was a great success, and we look forward to continuing the tradition this year to honor her memory.

Hosted by Lost Sierra Circuit and Healthy Bodies Fitness Gym

***Online sign-ups end at 9:00 PM on Wednesday. There will be day of registration available. Please be sure to arrive early. The race starts at 9:00AM.**

This year’s proceeds will go to Kara Torrance DaVeiga of Quincy, CA.

Race Details: 

Who: Everyone is welcome! This is a family-friendly event: kids, dogs, bikes, and strollers included.

What: Three chances to win!

🥇 First Place Female

🥇First Place Male

🥇First Place Child

Plus, fun finisher giveaways for all participants!

When: 9:00 AM, Thanksgiving Morning

Where: FRC 5K Course

Why: To support our recipient, Kara, who will receive all proceeds from this year’s race.

name: 2026 Avenue of the Giants Marathon
description: The Avenue of the Giants is one of the most beautiful races in the world!  It runs through old growth redwoods and follows a natural creek in the middle of a state park.  Staged on "The Avenue of the Giants" in Humboldt Redwoods State Park, located in rural Northern California. Course is on a paved road that winds gently up hill but is mostly a flat, fast destination race.  With little to distract you, the tall trees inspire the athlete in each of us to be strong.  The course is certified and the marathon is a Boston Qualifying event.

name: 2026 Cal Tri Castaic Lake - 6.20.26
description:
2026 Cal Tri Castaic Lake - 6.20.25

18 EVENT OPTIONS. 6 Olympic distance events (Triathlon, RunBikeRun, SwimBike, SwimRun, 1640 Yard Swim & 10K Run), 6 Sprint distance events (Triathlon, RunBikeRun, SwimBike, SwimRun, 400 yard Swim & 5K Run) and 6 Youth Sprint distance events (Triathlon, RunBikeRun, SwimBike, SwimRun, 400 yard Swim & 5K Run). Triathlon = swim + bike + run. Typically, the swim and run distances are standard but the bike distance varies from race to race. Check out the course maps for more detailed information.

CASTAIC LAKE. 
The 35th annual Castaic Lake Triathlon takes place at scenic Castaic Lake just 20 miles north of Los Angeles. The Castaic Lake Recreation Area, located just north of Santa Clarita, is an 11,200-acre multi-use facility with two lakes, boating, world class fishing, hiking, walking, horseback riding, wake boarding, jet-skiing, camping, picnicking, kayaking, and sailing.  August is a great time to enjoy the water in the high 60s, and a staging area aptly named Paradise Cove. "Tri-cation" Friday night camping available through Castaic Lake.


THE COURSE. 
The swim course is a modified V shape in Paradise Cove at Castaic Lake, with 8 lifeguards in the water on paddleboards.  The bike course then goes out on back roads to limit your interaction with cars.  The bike course does include some U-turns on back roads to allow this, so athletes should slow down at the turn around points.  The run is primarily on the rolling trails overlooking Castaic Lake. 

WHO WE SUPPORT
All proceeds will benefit the Canyon High School Cross Country and Track Teams (we've been doing this for 33 years to support our programs).  

This is a great triathlon for new triathletes.  For years our coaches and athletes have encouraged new triathletes (young and old), and created a welcoming atmosphere of support.  We offer an enjoyable experience for triathletes of all experience levels.  


AIR TEMPERATURE (AVG).
Mid June temperatures are often cooler in the morning, with early morning fog burning off to reach the mid 80s.  Our event will possibly be around 60 degrees.

WATER TEMPERATURE (AVG). 

Water temps in June typically range in the mid to high 60s.  Email updates will be sent out closer to the race with updates. Use the 20% CALTRI2025 discount code at blueseventy. Note: Fusion wetsuits not eligible for discount.

12 EVENT OPTIONS. 6 Olympic distance events (Triathlon, RunBikeRun, SwimBike, SwimRun, 1640 Yard Swim & 10K Run) and 6 Sprint distance events (Triathlon, RunBikeRun, SwimBike, SwimRun, 400 yard Swim & 5K Run). TO DO. Ventura Harbor Village. Ventura Pier. Channels Islands National Park

AIRPORT. Los Angeles (LAX)

AIR TEMPERATURE (AVG). 55 F / 68 F

WATER TEMPERATURE (AVG). 59 F. Wetsuit recommended. Use the 20% CALTRI2025 discount code at blueseventy. Note: Fusion wetsuits not eligible for discount.

name: 2026 CHALLENGE
description:
🏁 2026 Challenge: Run, Walk & Bike 2,026 Miles in 2026! 🏁

 
Starts January 1, 2026 - Embark on an EPIC year-long fitness journey! Whether you choose to complete this SOLO or TEAM up with friends, the goal is to cover 2,026 miles between January 1 and December 31, 2026
 
🧍‍♀️ Solo Challenger
Take on the full 2,026 miles on your own. Every mile you run, walk, or bike counts toward your personal achievement.

 

👥 Team Challenger
Form a team of 2+ participants and divide the 2,026 miles in any way you choose. Each team member will receive their own Finisher's Medal and Race Shirt in the mail!

 

Registration Includes:
  • Finisher's Medal: Celebrate your achievement with a BADASS medal!
  • 2026 Challenge Shirt or Tank Top: Buttery-soft apparel to showcase your accomplishment.
  • Official "2,026 Miles" Sticker: Display your commitment proudly.
  • RaceJoy App: Sync your activities and track progress on the live leaderboard.
  • Live Leaderboard: Stay motivated by seeing how you and others are progressing.
  • Custom Finisher's Certificate: Personalized recognition of your success.
  • Milestone Achievement Awards: Earn accolades as you reach key milestones.
  • Free Shipping within the USA
  • Charitable Donation to "Direct Relief"- more info on our website

Running

name: 2026 Disneyland® Half Marathon Weekend presented by HONDA
description:
In 2026, runDisney® is going to “Celebrate Happy” during the Disneyland® Half Marathon Weekend presented by HONDA, January 29–February 1. Happening amid the 70th anniversary of the Disneyland® Resort, this race weekend will be centered around some of the different ways to celebrate what delights us most. So come enjoy miles of smiles during a 5K hosted by Joy from Disney and Pixar’s Inside Out. Join Sorcerer’s Apprentice Mickey in an imaginative 10K. Run together with a friend as part of an “it’s a small world®” attraction-themed half marathon. And, for the ultimate achievement, take on the Dumbo Double Dare challenge made up of both the 10K and the half marathon. There are even Kids’ Races hosted by Stitch and morning yoga with Miss Piggy. As always, magic and one-of-a-kind medals are included.

 

Participants must attend the runDisney Health & Fitness Expo at least one day prior to their first event to pick up their race bib, participant shirt and pre-purchased merchandise. The Expo takes place Thursday, January 29 – Saturday, January 31.

name: 2026 Humboldt Redwoods Marathon, Half Marathon, 5K
description:
We'll forgive you if you have trouble concentrating on the road ahead of you while running The Humboldt Redwoods Marathon, half or 5K. After all, you'll probably be looking up at the old-growth redwood trees which tower over the course! This race is in Humboldt Redwoods State Park and the Half Marathon follows the second half of the iconic Avenue of the Giants Marathon course.

All courses are USATF Certified. The Marathon is a Boston qualifier. The race starts and finishes at the Dyerville Bridge.

name: 2026 Lake Chabot Trail Challenge (Half Marathon & 5K)
description:
“Beginning July 1, 2024, the “Honest Pricing Law” or “Hidden Fees Statute,” SB 478, makes it illegal for businesses to advertise or list a price for a good or service that does not include all required fees or charges other than certain government taxes and shipping costs.”

RACE INFO: We are so excited to celebrate the 42nd annual Lake Chabot Trail Challenge Half Marathon and 5K. This race is well regarded amongst serious trail runners in the outlying areas. The race begins at 8am for the Half Marathon and 8:30am for the 5K. Please arrive early so that you may find parking, pick up your bibs, use restrooms facilities, and be properly prepared to race before the start. Race takes place rain or shine and there are no refunds.

RACE COURSE: The half marathon course is a scenic, hilly loop, mainly on dirt fire roads.  The ridge-line views look down upon scenic Lake Chabot, surrounding grassy slopes, and eucalyptus groves.  Mt. Diablo and San Francisco Bay are visible along the route. There are water stations with first aid and radio support; we recommend bringing your own hydration as well.  The half marathon has a time limit of 3.5 hours. The 5k (3.1 miles) course is an out and back that has gentle rolling hills and consists mostly of paved surfaces.  This route includes one water station with first aid and radio support.

RACE FEE: Pre-registered runners will be guaranteed a t-shirt if registered by Sunday, May 10th, 2026.  The price for the 5K is $40 and Half Marathon $65. You must register by Saturday, June 6th. We will accept race day registration; however, the price for the 5K is $45 and Half Marathon $70. If you register on race day, we can only accept cash, check or Venmo.

There is a nominal fee (~$5) for Chabot parking lot. Free parking on Lake Chabot Rd and nearby streets.

RACE PACKET & BIB PICK-UP:  We will have race packet and bib pick-up on Sunday, June 7th starting at 7am at the Willow picnic site which is also the finish line area. We will not be mailing out any race packets or bibs. Both races are chip-timed.

T-SHIRT: Entry fee includes short sleeve, high quality t-shirts for registrations by May 10th so sign-up early.  There are no guarantee of t-shirts for runners registered after that date and on race day. We ask for those who did not get a shirt to check in after the race. Please ensure that you select the appropriate t-shirt size. We will not be doing any size exchanges from your original request.

AWARDS: Finisher's medals to those who complete their race.  Age division medals given to the top 3 in each of 12 age divisions in the half marathon and 9 age divisions in the 5K.

Photos:  Race photos are being provided by Darrell Lavin of Darrell Lavin Photography. You will receive an email post-race for instructions on how to access and purchase official race photos.

QUESTIONS: If you have any questions, please contact Rachel Lunt at teamlunt07@gmail.com.

DIRECTIONS: The entrance closest to the event's parking lot is: 17404 Lake Chabot Road, Castro Valley, CA 94546.  On Google Maps, this will appear as "Entry of Lake Chabot Parking Space."  The registration area and start lines are just a few minutes walk from the lot ( just follow the signs).

name: 2026 Optimism Cal Tri Newport Dunes - 11.1.26
description:
2026 Optimism Cal Tri Newport Dunes - 11.1.26. Started in 1978 as the Human Race Triathlon, Cal Tri Newport Dunes is the longest running triathlon in the world operating from the same location. Also started in 1978 was the Ironman World Championship Triathlon Oahu but it moved to Kailua-Kona, Hawaii in 1981. This serves as the Cal Tri Events National Championship Race with registration in the 1500-2000 range.

12 EVENT OPTIONS. 6 Olympic distance events (Triathlon, RunBikeRun, SwimBike, SwimRun, 1640 Yard Swim & 10K Run) and 6 Sprint distance events (Triathlon,  RunBikeRun, SwimBike, SwimRun, 400 yard Swim & 5K Run). Triathlon = swim + bike + run. Typically, the swim and run distances are standard but the bike distance varies from race to race. Check out the course maps for more detailed information.

TO DO. Disneyland Park & California Adventure Park. Balboa Island Ferry. Newport Beach.

AIRPORT. John Wayne (SNA)

AIR TEMPERATURE (AVG). 60 F / 73 F

WATER TEMPERATURE (AVG). 65 F. Wetsuit legal. Use the 20% CALTRI2025 discount code at blueseventy. Note: Fusion wetsuits not eligible for discount.
