name: Badwater Presents 40/40 NOW: Creating Balance in an Ultra World
description:
40/40 NOW, presented by AdventureCORPS: May 13 - June 21, 2026

 

Creating Balance in an Ultra World

 

We invite you to join us for a very special, first of its kind, 40-Day Life Adventure!

 

40/40 NOW is a 40-day program which can serve many purposes:

-              Cross-Training for Sport, and for Life

-              Celebrate the Summer Solstice as your Best Self

-              For Ultra Athletes: Sharpen your Body and Mind for the Summer Racing Season

 

40 / 40 NOW is open to anyone and everyone! (While we are the people behind the world-wide series of BADWATER® Ultramarathons, this opportunity is for anybody looking to head into summer as their very best self.)

 

Duration: 40 Days, from Wednesday, May 13 through Sunday, June 21.  

(The 2026 summer solstice is on Sunday, June 21, 2026 at 1:24 AM.)

 

Why 40 Days? 30 Days Creates a Habit, but a 40 Day Effort is a Spiritual Odyssey.

 

What Is the 40/40 Path? How does it work? What's involved? 

 

The core of this challenge is completing 40 minutes of intentional movement activities in the AM, and 40 minutes in the PM.        

-              One must be strength and/or flexibility oriented. Think weightlifting, yoga, stretch class, dance class, or martial arts. (This can be done at a gym or fitness studio, but also on your own at home, following DVDs or YouTube classes.)

 

-              The other 40-minute activity will be cardio-oriented. Think running, walking, hiking, bicycling, skating, or swimming. (For participants who already run or bike well over 40 minutes per day, we recommend pursuing a different sport for this 40-minute cardio activity.)

 

Additionally, each participant will check-In daily in the Strava Club: Given that participants will be all over the world, each morning (Pacific Time) we will post a “Daily Check-In!” reminder in the Strava Club: Every participant will comment to tell us what they did – and perhaps learned – that day after their PM activity. Accountability makes it real! Teamwork makes the dream work!

 

40/40 participants will also pursue ten different four-day personal challenges, and take “brain breaks” every Sunday: 

-              10 Personal Challenges: One will be announced every Four Days

-              Screen-Free Sundays: No digital noise for 8 hours: You pick the timeframe, as long as it's during waking hours. (If work or childcare means you need your phone close, keep the ringer on for notifications, or have a family member or friend be in charge of your phone. Or if you must be on your phone, just don’t scroll any social media.)

-              Also every Sunday: Pause and Celebrate!  This is the opposite of a To Do List, this is a Done List: Write it and celebrate all you’ve achieved today, or in the past four days, or in the past week!

Every day each participant will receive an email which contains:

-              An inspiring quote

-              A simple but powerful nutrition tip and/or recipe

-              A link to an inspiring online or social media talk

-              Also, every four days, the email will announce the next of the ten 4-Day Challenges

 

The 40/40 participants will receive a printed interactive guidebook containing: 

-              “The Power and Meaning of 40”

-              “The Power and Meaning of the Summer Solstice”

-              Recommended Reading List: 40 Books that could Change Your Life

-              Hints at the ten Four-Day Challenges (actual Challenge details will come by email, so there’s no “planning ahead” – part of the challenge is the surprise!)

-              40-Day Calendar to track your progress: May 13-June 21, 2026

 

 

HOW WILL 40/40 NOW PARTICIPANTS INTERACT?

                  For camaraderie and to share insights and inspirations, a special, private Strava Club will bring everyone together on an ongoing, daily basis.

 

WHAT HAPPENS ON DAY 1?

• You will study the 40 / 40 NOW Guidebook

• You will write a note to yourself about what you hope to gain from this, how you feel your life is now (where are you happy or unhappy, how you want to become a better version of yourself.) You will put this is an envelope and set it aside for 40 days.

• You will begin! – Your AM and PM 40-minute activities, and the first of the four-day personal challenges.

 

WHAT HAPPENS ON DAY 40? THE END IS JUST THE BEGINNING > COMING TOGETHER ON THE SUMMER SOLSTICE

 

With the arrival of the Summer Solstice, we will celebrate and “seal” this experience in several ways:

 

• First, you will read your Day 1 Challenged note to yourself. Whether you share about this in the Strava Club is entirely up to you; no pressure to “over share”!

• We will send out a few simple Rituals to Celebrate the Summer Solstice; choose one or more!

• You will post your final AM and PM activities to the Strava Club and log them in your printed 40 / 40 NOW Guidebook.

• Zoom Call: We will all come together for a 40-minute video chat via  Zoom; this will take place at 900am, Pacific Time. (There will be participants all over the world, but this time works best for those in the Western Hemisphere and Europe.)

 

FINALLY, some  Mementos will be sent to each participant after  40/40 NOW concludes:

40/40 NOW Keychain (Very high quality, meant to last!)

40/40 NOW T-shirt

40/40 NOW Decal

Delivered in a Custom 40/40 NOW Box

name: Badwater Salton Sea, presented by Mount to Coast
description:
The BADWATER® ultra running experience returns to the Anza-Borrego Desert and Palomar Mountain when the twelfth BADWATER SALTON SEA - presented by Mount to Coast - race takes place on April 26-27, 2025.

 

This remarkable event challenges teams of two or three ultrarunners – running together as duos or trios for the duration, NOT in a relay – to tackle an unimaginable traverse of Southern California deserts and mountains. The  route covers 81 miles (130km) from Salton City (elevation 234 feet / 71m below sea level) to Palomar Mountain, the almost tallest mountain in San Diego County (elevation 5500 feet / 1676m.)* Eight of the 81 race miles pass through Anza-Borrego State Park on a single track trail from Borrego Springs to Ranchita, creating a race route which is a mix of road and trail. There is a total elevation gain of over 9000 feet (2740m).

The eleven previous editions were received with wide acclaim. The thirteenth edition – with a limit of 100 runners – is scheduled for April 18-19 (Saturday-Sunday), 2026.

RACE DIFFICULTY

This is an extremely difficult race held in extreme conditions: Veterans of this event routinely state that it is as hard as any of the toughest 100 milers they have done.

The extreme weather changes - from 100+F / 38+C during the day, often with a sand storm, to freezing temperates with very wet fog at night - along with the extreme challenge of the two major mountain ascents - combine to make this an extremely difficult race.

It is critical to train properly for the heat and to train effectively for very steep desert single-track trail section of the race which is done in maximum heat and without the support crew nearby. Additionally, the single track trail is VERY steep and surprises runners every year with both its steepness, rugged terrain, and intense heat. Knowledge of maintaining proper electrolyte balance is also critical. Study the relevant articles at Badwater University closely, as well as race reports from former competitors.

Team Format

Unique to Badwater® Salton Sea is a “Team Ultra Racing” format: All race entrants must enter and race as teams of two or three runners (all male, all female, or co-ed divisions), remaining together for the duration – NOT in a relay format – and sharing just one support vehicle with at least two crew members.

 

We encourage each runner to select teammates with compatible running style and pace, and with whom he or she would really like to share this experience!

 

Divisions are offered for All Male, All Female, and Mixed (for 3x teams, 2 men and 1 woman, or 1 man and 2 women, are considered equal).

 

Some teams have come together in the past through the wonders of the internet, for example through our Facebook Event Page for each year’s event, or just through personal social media (and real world!) connections!

 

It is very important to pick good teammates to have an ideal experience at this race, and to have the highest likelihood of the whole team finishing together, intact, which SHOULD BE the goal of every team in the race. Here’s what we suggest:

 

– Invite runners that you have run with a lot, and find you have compatible speeds, styles (pacing, how much time you spend getting aid, etc.), and temperament (sense of humour, how much you like to talk versus staying quiet or listening to music, etc.). Those could be runners in your club or with whom you train a lot. But that could also be runners who don’t live near you, but you only see at races.

 

– Think about all the races you do. Aren’t there others who consistently finish right near you in lots of races? Seems like a good place to start with picking a teammate, don’t you think?

 

– Taking that a step further, why not pick teammates with whom you actually compete directly? Again, you’re likely about the same speed, so why not work together instead of against each other, for a change? Why not “bury the hatchet,” so to speak?

 

– What about fellow runners that you are mentoring, whether “formally” or just in a friendly way? Why not help another runner have an amazing experience in your company, with you playing the role of “grizzled old veteran” or Jedi of ultra running? There is no Luke Skywalker without Obi-Wan Kenobi, after all.

 

Anyway, those are a few ideas for not only picking good teammates, but also for having an exemplary experience, something that will really be transcendent, and meaningful, and will resonate far and beyond after the race is over and you’ve – hopefully – gone home with your buckles.

 

QUALIFYING REQUIREMENTS: Entry may be denied to those without sufficient endurance credentials. All applicants must have completed at least one difficult 50-mile ultramarathon in the previous 12 months prior to entry. Proof of this qualification must be included within the entry application OR by email at least 60 days prior to the race. Completing one or more tough 100-milers before this event is highly recommended, as is experience in desert heat racing. Veterans of this event routinely state that it is as hard or harder than any of the toughest 100 milers they have done.

 

REFUND POLICY: Generally speaking, it is our expectation that registered teams will not withdraw from this event. Instead, if one runner has to withdraw from the race, he or she will be replaced with a new teammate, at the discretion of the remaining runner(s) on the team. There are no transfers of registration, nor roll-overs to the next year. Entry fee refunds, less 25%, will be offered until 60 days prior to the event. After that, there are no refunds, nor roll-overs or credits.

 

ALL TEAMMATES MUST ENTER ON THE SAME WEEK: Please submit all teammates’ registrations and payments on the same day or within a few days. No runner or team is considered fully registered until ALL runners on the team are registered and paid in full. Runners who register, but don’t have a full team registered within two weeks, may be dropped from the roster and issued a refund, less 25%.

 

EVENT CANCELLATION: If the event is canceled due to pandemic, hurricane, community disaster, or other force majeure, neither refunds nor credits will be given.

 

ROUTE APPROVALS: Although we anticipate using the same or nearly the same route each year, the final, exact route is subject to approval from various government agencies and is always subject to change due to various factors beyond our control.

 

Visit our Badwater.com website for more information!

name: Bayside Saved by the Bell 5K, 10K & Half Marathon
description:
September 19, 2026 · 7:00 a.m. PST · 6846 Owensmouth Ave, Canoga Park, CA

Get ready to dash through time in The Bayside Dash, a 90s high school sitcom-themed race packed with retro vibes, school spirit, and Slater-strength energy.

Presented by Jed & Ted’s Excellent Races

Whether you’re more Morris or Turtle, this race lets you channel your inner Bayside Tiger and crush your course with a smile.

  • Friends Forever 5K
    🎶 Named after Zack Attack’s legendary ballad—because you don’t leave your squad behind on race day.
  • Time Out 10K
    ✋ Inspired by Morris himself—freeze time, catch your breath, and own the course.
  • Hall Pass Half Marathon
    🎓 Go the distance like you’ve got a free pass to run the school (and the streets of Canoga Park).
  • The Multiverse Transfer Student Challenge (Virtual)
    🌀 “Transfer Students” from any timeline can choose any distance and still earn their medal.

Expect high school pep rally energy, ‘Saved by the Bell’ moments, throwback tunes, and surprise “pop quizzes” of encouragement along the course. Costumes encouraged—go full Bayside or show off your best 90s teen energy.

📦 Multiverse Option (Virtual Runners Welcome!)  
Can’t make it IRL? Run virtually anywhere between Sept 20–22 and we’ll mail you your finisher medal.

This is a Jed & Ted’s Excellent Race—fun, fast, and full of nostalgia.

Sign up now. No hall pass required.

---

**Parody Disclaimer**  
This race is a fan-made parody event inspired by 90s pop culture and is not affiliated with or endorsed by any official trademark holders.

name: Because of Sadie 5K
description: We lost our amazing, beautiful daughter on January 31, 2022. She was just 14 years old. After contracting COVID, we received the devastating news that she also was diagnosed with leukemia. The combination of both diagnoses was too much for her body to handle and we lost her just 33 days later. Help us turn grief into joy. We volunteered often through the National Charity League. Walk, jog, or run in Sadie's honor to support her favorite philanthropy, Retrievers and Friends of Southern CA. They are an all-volunteer, non-profit organization devoted to finding homes for dogs and cats. Sadie enjoyed spending time there socializing animals, doing laundry, and cleaning the kennels. A portion of every registration fee will be donated to them.

name: Bedrock Valley Gravel Ride
description:
BEDROCK VALLEY GRAVEL RIDE

A Gravel Ride experience you don't want to miss. Choose your ride experience around Diamond Valley Lake. This is truly a historic ride in an ancient place. This area's heritage begins during the Ice Age where the most concentrated amount of Mastodons once roam the earth. The remains of hundreds of Mastodons and other prehistoric dinosaurs were discovered in the bedrock of where the lake now rests.

NEW! GRAVEL ROCK BIKE RACE is the first Gravel Bike race that takes you around the Lake. Ride Gravel/Mountain/E-Bike

GRAVEL ROCK RIDE 36K takes you ONE LOOP around beautiful Diamond Valley Lake. Great for your first Gravel/Off-Road Ride

GRAVEL ROCK RIDE 72K takes you TWO LOOPS around beautiful Diamond Valley Lake. Test your skills and make it a double.

GRAVEL ROCK RIDE 108K takes you THREE LOOPS around beautiful Diamond Valley Lake. Find your limits and test your endurance.

GRAVEL KIDS 10K is a fun and flat fun ride for the spirited rider/beginner. An out and back course that gets you stoked!

TEAM CHALLENGE enjoy the ride with friends and complete laps as a team in the 72k and 108k.

name: Bedrock Valley Trail Runs
description:
BEDROCK VALLEY TRAIL RUNS

The Bedrock Valley Trail Runs is a NEW trail running experience you don't want to miss. We offer something for the whole family to enjoy. Choose from the beautiful  Bedrock Valley Trail Marathon, Trail Half Marathon, 15k, 5k, Stroller 5k and bring the kids for the the 1 Mile Kid's Fun Run around Diamond Valley Lake. This is truly a historic run in an ancient place. This area's heritage begins during the Ice Age where the most concentrated amount of Mastodons once roam the earth. The remains of hundreds of Mastodons and other prehistoric dinosaurs were discovered in the bedrock of where the lake now rests.

TRAIL MARATHON is a great introduction into trail marathons. A relatively flat loop around the lake ending with some beautiful single track with small climbs. Ideal for all running levels.

TRAIL HALF MARATHON is a beautiful out and back section along the lake bed and perfect for accomplishing your first half marathon.

15K course challenges the runner with a little of everything: flat, fast, climbing, descending on the famous Wildflower single track trail.

NEW! 10K is a fast out and back with views of the lake.

NEW! STAMPEDE 5K is a fast and flat out and back. Great for a fast run or hike. 

SOARING 5K is a great distance through the stunning Wildflower Trails. Great for a quick run or hike. This course does take you up and down the trails finishing along the shoreline.

STROLLER TRAIL 5k our first specific stroller only 5k is a beautiful flat 3.1 miles out and back. Enjoy with the little ones.

KID'S 1 MILE FUN RUN is open to children 10 and younger. This is a non-timed run. All kids receive a finisher’s medal and other goodies.

NEW! GRAVEL ROCK BIKE RACE is the first Gravel Bike race that takes you around the Lake. Ride Gravel/Mountain/E-Bike

We are a CUPLESS race series. Please make sure to bring some form of hydration vessel to carry hydration for your event. There will not be cups provided at aid stations.

Choose from the beautiful  Bedrock Valley Trail Marathon, Trail Half Marathon, 15k, 5k, Stroller 5k and bring the kids for the the 1 Mile Kid's Fun Run around Diamond Valley Lake. This is truly a historic run in an ancient place. This area's heritage begins during the Ice Age where the most concentrated amount of Mastodons once roam the earth. The remains of hundreds of Mastodons and other prehistoric dinosaurs were discovered in the bedrock of where the lake now rests.

TRAIL MARATHON is a great introduction into trail marathons. A relatively flat loop around the lake ending with some beautiful single track with small climbs. Ideal for all running levels.

TRAIL HALF MARATHON is a beautiful out and back section along the lake bed and perfect for accomplishing your first half marathon.

15K course challenges the runner with a little of everything: flat, fast, climbing, descending on the famous Wildflower single track trail.

NEW! 10K is a fast out and back with views of the lake.

NEW! STAMPEDE 5K is a fast and flat out and back. Great for a fast run or hike. 

SOARING 5K is a great distance through the stunning Wildflower Trails. Great for a quick run or hike. This course does take you up and down the trails finishing along the shoreline.

STROLLER TRAIL 5k our first specific stroller only 5k is a beautiful flat 3.1 miles out and back. Enjoy with the little ones.

KID'S 1 MILE FUN RUN is open to children 10 and younger. This is a non-timed run. All kids receive a finisher’s medal and other goodies.

NEW! GRAVEL ROCK BIKE RACE is the first Gravel Bike race that takes you around the Lake. Ride Gravel/Mountain/E-Bike

We are a CUPLESS race series. Please make sure to bring some form of hydration vessel to carry hydration for your event. There will not be cups provided at aid stations.

name: Bee Sweet Citrus Farm-K
description:
Join the Bee Sweet Citrus and Ag One teams on Saturday, February 7, 2026, for our inaugural Farm-K event! This run/walk is a family-friendly event that benefits the next generation of agriculturalists, and we'd love for you to join in on the fun. 

Register for our timed 5k or our 1 Mile Walk in support of the Fresno State Ag One Foundation!

The event takes place at Fresno State's O'Niell Park, and all participants earn an event shirt and a custom finisher's medallion.

name: Bell Gardens 5K
description: Bell Gardens 5K course is designed to provide fast times, and it’s ideal for spectators. This is a two-loop course that covers flat wide public streets of Bell Gardens. Participants will start at Veterans park at the corner of Perry and Suva, head east towards Scout Street, then back to complete the loop on Florence Place. Making a turn on Perry then onto lap 2. A water station will be available at the start of the second loop. The Kid's 1/2 mile is out and back on Suva Street. The road will be completely closed to traffic.

name: Besties Run 5K. 10K. Half Marathon
description:
📅 Sunday, February 8, 2026
📍 5400 E Ocean Blvd, Long Beach, CA 90803

  
✨Grab your bestie— and get ready to celebrate the women who lift you up and run beside you through life’s ups and downs. Or come out solo and make new friends who cheer you on every step of the way. 
This isn’t just a run — it’s a movement for connection, confidence, and community. ✨

 

✨WHAT’S INCLUDED WITH REGISTRATION:

CERTIFIED COURSE

CHIP TIMING

FINISHER MEDAL

RACE BIB

RACE PHOTOS

RACE T-SHIRT

LIVE DJ & FINISH LINE PARTY

VENDORS & GIVEAWAYS

FOOD & REFRESHMENTS

SCENIC COASTAL COURSE ALONG THE LONG BEACH, BEACH PATH

 

✨About the Besties Option- Running is better together!


Our Besties Run entries are specially designed for duos — two registrations bundled as one, so you and your bestie can finish lines side by side.- make this your Galentine’s tradition! 

 

✨Why We Run Together
This event is all about women supporting women — cheering each other on, and proving we can do hard things together. 

 

✨All Paces, All Abilities, All Welcome
Runners and walkers are welcome.Whether you’re chasing a PR or enjoying a stroll with your squad, you’re part of the movement. 


✨Run Club Girls is proud to bring this empowering event to life — a celebration of sisterhood, self-love, and shared strength.

 

Event Management by CaliFlow Runs — where heart, hustle, and high vibes power every mile.

name: Bidwell Classic 5K, 10k and Half Marathon March 7th, 2026
description:
Join us for the Bidwell Classic 5K, 10k and Half Marathon. 

 

Celebrating 50 years of running in Bidwell Park in Chico CA this race has become a chico tradition for so many! We with 3 distances offered we are pleased to host the Bidwell Classic again in 2026! 

We are excited to offer a cash purse again for the top male and female in each event! 

 

BENEFITS STUDENT ATHLETES

A substantial portion of the race entry fees go to the local high school cross country running programs. When you participate in the Bidwell Classic, you are supporting local student athletes. If you would like to make an additional donation to the schools, please do so on the donation portion of the registration. Thank you so much for supporting this race and our local youth runners!

 

Online registration closes at 8:00am on Friday March 6th, 2026.  
In person registration will be available during packet pickup.
No in person registration will be available on race day.
 
Packet pickup will be available Friday March 6th 10:00am-4:00pm
Race day packet pick up will be available Saturday March 7th from 6:45am - 7:45am
Any questions about registration or packet pick up please email shawna@fleetfeetchico.com
 

 

START DATE & TIMES
When: Saturday March 7th, 2026

Where: Lower Bidwell Park/ Sycamore Field 

5K, 10k and Half Marathon run and fun walk: Starting time is 8:00am for the 5k and 8:10 for the 10k and Half Marathon.
 
Entry fees are non-refundable and non-transferable.
For special school group rates contact shawna@fleetfeetchico.com
 
Every registered runner will receive a 2026 race shirt if registered before February 6th. To guarantee your shirt size please register on or before February 6th. All registrations after February 6th will be subject to availability and size at packet pickup. Any leftover shirts after packet pick up will be available after the race at the Fleet Feet booth starting at 9:00am. 
If still running, you may have someone pick up a shirt for you. Please provide them your name and or bib #.
If you do not pick up your packet before the race (at packet pickup or at the race), your shirt will NOT be saved for you. 
 
COURSE CERTIFICATION AND MAPS
 
The 5k and 10k are flat, paved, and free of traffic. The half marathon has a 1/4 mile on each of the loops that are a single-track trail. All events start and finish at One Mile Recreation Area in Lower Bidwell Park.
 
The maps to all the racecourses can be found by clicking the link below:
Race Maps - Fleet Feet Chico
 

 

Shake out run Event!

Join us on March 6th at 6:00pm at Fleet Feet Chico for an easy evening shakeout run. We will go for a short run 3-6 mile run/walk and enjoy a cold beverage and come delicious carbs before the race. More information to come as we get closer to the event!

Location: Fleet Feet Chico, 241 Main St., Chico CA

Time: Show up between 5:30-6:00pm. Groups will start running at 6:15pm

 
PACKET PICKUP
 
Packet pickup will be offered at Fleet Feet Chico (241 Main St in downtown Chico) We will also have a small window on race day to pick up your packet.
 
Packet Pickup days and hours: 
 
Friday March 6th at Fleet Feet Chico
10:00am - 4:00pm
 
Located at Fleet Feet Chico, 241 Main St., Chico CA
 
Race Day Packet Pick up at the Fleet Feet Tent
6:45am-7:45am ONLY

 

RACE SHIRTS:


Race shirts are a unisex cotton shirt printed by Arroyo (formally Upper Park Printing) To be guaranteed a shirt in your size, you need to register on or before February 6th, 2026. All registration entries received after 2/6/26 will have shirts based on limited availability on a first come first serve basis.

 
DIRECTIONS AND PARKING
 
To the course: Enter Chico via Highway 99 either from the north or from the south. If you are coming from the north on 99, take the Highway 32 offramp and turn right at the first intersection. If you are coming from the south on 99, take the 32 offramp and turn left at the second intersection. Now you're heading west on 32 (East 8th St). From here, take 8th St just under a half-mile, then turn right on Sycamore St.

Sycamore St runs a few blocks into Woodland Ave, which runs parallel to the park. The park itself will be closed to vehicle traffic on race day, so find a parking spot on or near Woodland Ave. Please be courteous and park legally. Do not park in a way that blocks local residents' entry to or exit from their homes. There are several entrances to the One Mile Recreation Area from Woodland Ave. 

To Fleet Feet packet pickup: As above, from Highway 99 head west on Highway 32 (East 8th St).
Take 8th St about a mile then turn right on Main St. Drive north on Main St. Fleet Feet is located between 2nd and 3rd Streets. Fleet Feet's phone number is 530 345-1000.
 
TIMING
Timing will be done by Bizz Johnson Racing. All races will be a gun start and a chip finish. If you are racing for an overall placement, you must toe the line! (Based on Gun time/first to cross the line)
 
Gun start for 5k will be at 8:00am
Gun start for 10k, and Half Marathon will be 8:10am
 

AID STATIONS AND RESTROOMS
There will be 6 aid stations for the half, 3 for the 10k and 2 for the 5k.
1.     Cedar Grove Bathrooms – Loop 1 Water / Loop 2 Water, nutrition gels and electrolytes 
2.     Peterson Drive Gate – Loop 1 Water / Loop 2 Water, nutrition gels and electrolytes 
3.     One Mile Parking Lot on Vallombrosa Side – Water and electrolytes 
Restroom on the course will be located at One Mile recreation on the North and South side of the pool, Cedar Grove Park, and Pettersen Dr. Park entrance as well as portable restrooms at the start and finish.
 
RULES
 
  • Please no dogs on the course during the race. Stollers are allowed, please be cautious of other runners. If wearing headphones, only in one ear please! Must be able to hear your surroundings.
  • Be courteous when overtaking slower runners or walkers in your elected race location. We want you to race hard and fast, but with safety of yourself and others in mind. (Please remember that this is a public park and there may be others on course that are not part of the race)
     
  • Where your Race number so it is visible on the participant's front
  • Run your race with pride!
  • You must cross the timing mat for your chip to be read. If you are planning of racing for top finisher, the race is based on gun time and first to cross the finish line.
  • Run, hard, run fast and have fun!
     
 
AWARDS FOR TOP FINISHERS
 
We will be offering a CASH PRIZE Top male and female for each race! (5k, 10k and Half) We will have an award ceremony at 8:45am for the 5k, 9:15am for the 10k and 10:00am for the Half Marathon races.
 
Age group awards can be found at the Fleet Feet tent following the award ceremony for each race. 
(Awards will also be offered to the top three in each age group category for each gender in each race)
 
All unclaimed prized will be available for pick up at Fleet Feet Chico on Sunday March 8th during regular business hours. (11:00am-4:00pm)
 
Ages groups will be as followed: 
14 and under / 15-19 / 20-29 / 30-39 / 40-49 / 50-59 / 60-69 / 70 and over
 
Finisher Medals will be provided to all Half Marathon runners who finish the race.
(Any remaining medals will be available for pick up at Fleet Feet Chico for 5k and 10k runners on Sunday March 8th)
 
 
Please visit www.fleetfeetchico.com for more information or email shawna@fleetfeetchico.com

START DATE & TIMES
When: Saturday March 7th, 2026

Where: Lower Bidwell Park/ Sycamore Field 

5K, 10k and Half Marathon run and fun walk: Starting time is 8:00am for the 5k and 8:10 for the 10k and Half Marathon.
 
Entry fees are non-refundable and non-transferable.
For special school group rates contact shawna@fleetfeetchico.com
 
Every registered runner will receive a 2026 race shirt if registered before February 6th. To guarantee your shirt size please register on or before February 6th. COURSE CERTIFICATION AND MAPS
 
The 5k and 10k are flat, paved, and free of traffic. The half marathon has a 1/4 mile on each of the loops that are a single-track trail. All events start and finish at One Mile Recreation Area in Lower Bidwell Park.
 
The maps to all the racecourses can be found by clicking the link below:
Race Maps - Fleet Feet Chico
 

 

Shake out run Event!

Join us on March 6th at 6:00pm at Fleet Feet Chico for an easy evening shakeout run. We will go for a short run 3-6 mile run/walk and enjoy a cold beverage and come delicious carbs before the race. More information to come as we get closer to the event!

Location: Fleet Feet Chico, 241 Main St., Chico CA

Time: Show up between 5:30-6:00pm. Groups will start running at 6:15pm

 
PACKET PICKUP
 
Packet pickup will be offered at Fleet Feet Chico (241 Main St in downtown Chico) We will also have a small window on race day to pick up your packet.
 
Packet Pickup days and hours: 
 
Friday March 6th at Fleet Feet Chico
10:00am - 4:00pm
 
Located at Fleet Feet Chico, 241 Main St., Chico CA
 
Race Day Packet Pick up at the Fleet Feet Tent
6:45am-7:45am ONLY

 

RACE SHIRTS:


Race shirts are a unisex cotton shirt printed by Arroyo (formally Upper Park Printing) To be guaranteed a shirt in your size, you need to register on or before February 6th, 2026. All registration entries received after 2/6/26 will have shirts based on limited availability on a first come first serve basis.

 
DIRECTIONS AND PARKING
 
To the course: Enter Chico via Highway 99 either from the north or from the south. If you are coming from the north on 99, take the Highway 32 offramp and turn right at the first intersection. If you are coming from the south on 99, take the 32 offramp and turn left at the second intersection. Now you're heading west on 32 (East 8th St). From here, take 8th St just under a half-mile, then turn right on Sycamore St.

Sycamore St runs a few blocks into Woodland Ave, which runs parallel to the park. The park itself will be closed to vehicle traffic on race day, so find a parking spot on or near Woodland Ave. Please be courteous and park legally. Do not park in a way that blocks local residents' entry to or exit from their homes. There are several entrances to the One Mile Recreation Area from Woodland Ave.

  • Where your Race number so it is visible on the participant's front

name: Big Bear Turkey Trot
description:
The 12th Annual Big Bear Turkey Trot
✨ What’s New This Year
📍 A new home in the Moonridge Corridor, starting and finishing at Dank Donuts.
🌲 A fresh route incluing the new Rathbun Creek Trail, and a memorable lap through the Moonridge Zoo 🦓🦙🦅.
🏃 A paved 3-mile run through the pines that’s approachable for everyone!
🎶 Danksgiving Celebration party at the finish line featuring live holiday music and adult beverages 🍹

 
🗓️ Event Schedule

8:00 AM - Registration & check-in opens
9:25 AM - Holiday Warmup Yoga 🧘 with Colin Schour
9:30 AM - 3-Mile Turkey Trot 🦃
10:00 AM - Danksgiving Party 🎶🍩🥂 with live music & adult beverages
10:30 AM - Awards 🏆 & Costume Contest 🎭
 
💸 Registration
Adults: $40
Youth (under 18): $25
Kids Run: Free
Locals: $5 discount with ID at packet pickup
No refunds (rain, shine, or snow—it’s all part of the fun).
 
🎁 Included with Entry:

🎄 A holiday finisher ornament
🧘 A lighthearted yoga warm-up
🎭 A lively costume contest
🥧 Race timing and awards eligibility (elite wave start available for those who's costume is considered worthy). 
🎶🍹 The Danksgiving party at the finish line
 
📦 Packet Pickup

🗓️ Monday, Nov 24 – Wednesday, Nov 26 (4–7 PM): The Yellow Post, 546 Pine Knot Blvd
🦃 Race Morning, Nov 27 (8–9 AM): Dank Donuts, 42612 Moonridge Rd Big Bear Lake, CA
 
 
🙋 FAQs

Strollers & kids? Strollers are welcome, and the kids under 5 are free.
Refunds? Nope. The Turkey Trot happens in any weather.
Local discount? Show ID for $5 off.
What’s included? Ornaments, yoga, pie, costumes, music, and memories.
 
🎤 Closing Note

The Big Bear Turkey Trot has always been about more than miles—it’s a morning of laughter, costumes, pie, and community. This year, we’ll gather in Moonridge, run the trail, visit the zoo, and then celebrate together at Danksgiving. We’ll see you out there. 🦃✨

name: Big River Adventure
description:
Welcome to the 25th annual Big River Adventure!

Join us for a unique race experience where you can choose your adventure to run, swim, walk, or paddle your way through the scenic beauty of Mendocino County's Big River.

For the past 25 years, Cancer Resource Centers of Mendocino County has been bringing our community together for this special fundraising event. While the activities may change from year to year, our mission remains steadfast: to honor and remember those impacted by cancer, and to raise vital funds to support free services for individuals facing cancer in Mendocino County.

Starting at the Big River boat launch, participants will embark on a journey filled with stunning views and the shared goal of making a difference in the lives of others.

Don't miss out on this unforgettable adventure! Register now and be part of something truly meaningful.

To keep this family-friendly event affordable and accessible to our community, we will not be providing t-shirts this year.

Here is a link to a trail map

•             5k runners will run east on the haul road to the 5k turn around.

•             10k runners dash east on the haul road to the 10K turn around (10K map).

•             5k "Fun" Walkers will follow the 5k runners route.

•             Kiddie run will begin at the boat launch

•             Swimmers will dive in at the boat lunch and swim east up Big River

•             Paddlers will begin at the boat launch and paddle east up Big River  *Please note you must bring your own vessel.

There are multiple race age divisions. Note: Participants between the ages of 6 and 17 may enter any race division at a discounted rate of $20 at signup.

Race Contact Info

Phone / Teléfono: (707) 937-3833

E-mail / Correo electrónico: info@crcmendocino.org

name: Bike The Coast
description:
Experience gorgeous riding along pristine beaches, historic Pacific Coast Highway, iconic beach landmarks and unique, Southern California weather with the annual Bike The Coast Bike Tour.   Select from distances of 25 mile, 50 mile, and 100 mile rides and then come out and ride along with 2000 other enthusiast along some of Southern California's best-known cities and roadways.  When you finish, meet us back at  the Oceanside pier to celebrate with your selection of food options, a lively beer garden, great music and new friends.

This is a truly bucket list event if you are an avid rider who enjoys getting some exercise, having fun, and experience great November weather.  This is a 'rules of the road' ride so come prepared to obey all traffic laws.

name: Bizz Johnson
description:
Set PRs and qualify for the Boston Marathon on this fast, downhill course! Total net downhill loss for the marathon is 929 feet making it the PERFECT course to qualify on! Per official B.A.A. confirmation, there will be no time penalties assessed for this course.

All races in 2026 will be Sunday, October 11. The marathon and 50K start at 8:00 AM at Mason Station Trailhead on McCoy Road with an out-and-back before jumping onto the Bizz Johnson Trail at Mason Station where the races travel through scenic Lassen National Forest. The first few miles of the course climb approximately 280 feet through the forest to Westwood Junction, then it’s downhill to the finish at Susanville, with a 1300-foot descent over the final 20 miles. The trail follows the route of the old Fernley and Lassen Branch Line of the Southern Pacific Railroad, built in 1914.

Roughly two-thirds of the way through the race, the trail enters the Susan River Canyon. Here, you’ll pass orange cliffs and cross the river ten times on picturesque wooden railroad bridges. About four miles from the finish, you’ll pass through two former railroad tunnels, 800 feet and 450 feet in length.

The Express Half Marathon starts at at 9:00 AM at Goumaz Campground which is Mile 14 of the full marathon route. After a short up-and-back, the Express Half Marathon flies down the Bizz Johnson to the finish.

Starting at Devil's Corral, the new Express 10K on Sunday does the last 6.2 miles of the full marathon. This course promises to be a fast, fun race. 

For all four events, you will be bused to a remote start.

PACKET PICKUP

  • Saturday Noon - 6 PM (50K, Marathon, Express Half Marathon, Express 10K): Susanville Historic Train Depot, 601 Richmond Road
  • Sunday Morning 6 AM - 7AM (Marathon and 50K), 7AM - 8 AM (Express Half Marathon and Express 10K): Susanville Historic Train Depot, 601 Richmond Road

PLEASE visit our website for maps, schedules, and all the important details!!

name: Bizz Johnson's Southside Scramble
description:
Are you ready to SCRAMBLE? This amazing new trail race showcases the best of the Susan River Canyon! Runners will head up the Bizz Johnson Trail from Hobo Camp for the first half and return via the beautiful and flowy singletrack on the Southside trail across the river. The Southside Scramble has 3 different distances to choose from, a 22K, a 14K, and a 7K. All races start and end at the Hobo Camp Day Use Area. On ODD years, we will run a reversed course! For 2025, all races go out the Southside Trail and back on the Bizz Johnson Trail. 

For the Dirty Devil's 22K, runners start on the Fire Road above the Hobo Camp Day Use Area and take the "outbound" portion of the Bizz Johnson Trail approximately 6 miles all the way to Devil's Corral.  From Devil's Corral, runners turn and drop down to the Susan River, crossing over a seasonal foot bridge, and enter the stunningly beautiful Southside trail with its rockslides, vista points, and flowy single track all the way back to Hobo Camp.

The Tunnel's Blast 14K starts on the Fire Road above the Hobo Camp Day Use Area and takes the "outbound" portion of the Bizz Johnson Trail approximately 4 miles to the entrance to the first railroad tunnel. Before heading into the darkness of the tunnel, runners will veer off onto singletrack, where they climb over the top of the tunnel to reach the Southside Trail. From there, they will enjoy the stunningly beautiful Southside trail with its rockslides, vista points, and flowy single track all the way back to Hobo Camp

The "Hobo's Special" 7K starts on the Fire Road above the Hobo Camp Day Use Area and heads approximately 2 miles up to the Twin Bridges Access connector to the Southside Trail. You'll get just enough of the Bizz Johnson's steady climb to excite your senses for the fast, flowy Southside's single-track return.

Finishers:

At Hobo Camp Day Use Area, participants can enjoy a fun finish line party with food and beverages.  All finishers will receive a custom medal and a custom beach towel just in time for a cool dip in the Susan River! Overall awards will be given to 1st through 3rd finishers (M/F/NB). Age group awards will be given to 1st-3rd AG in 10-year age groups.  

Start Times:

7:30 Dirty Devil's 22K

7:45 Tunnel's Blast 14K

8:00 Hobo Special 7K

Aid Stations:

Aid stations will serve fruit and salty snacks, Heed electrolyte, and water.  This is a cup-less race so runners should have their own hydration systems. Hydrapak is our cupless racing partner and runners will be provided with a collapsible cup at packet pickup.

Aid Station #1 is located on the Bizz Johnson Trail at the lower end of the lower tunnel at Mile 3.8. This aid station serves both the 22K and the 14K. 

Aid Station #2 is located on the Bizz Johnson Trail at the Devil's Corral at the Southside trail turnoff at mile 5.94. 22K 

Aid Station #3 is located on the Southside Trail just above the Twin Bridges access trail. This is approximately 2 miles from the finish. This aid station serves all three race distances.

For ODD years, with the reversed course, the Aid Station distances are slightly different. Additionally, the Twin Bridges Aid Station reverts to just hydration.

This race is Trail-Sisters Approved. There will be equal space on the start line for women and women's hygiene products at all aid stations and the finish line.

Event Parking:

Carpooling is HIGHLY encouraged as parking at Hobo Camp is very limited.  

Here are your options:

1. Hobo Camp - Most parking is on the middle and upper levels. There will be volunteers helping you park very tightly. There is also some parallel parking along the entrance road to Hobo Camp after the gate. This parking must only be on the uphill side of the road and you must be pointed in the direction to LEAVE Hobo Camp. There is NO parking on the Fire Roads.

2. There is some parking at Miller Road at the Bizz Johnson Trail (You must not park blocking the Bizz Johnson Trail). This is a short walk of about .25 mile from the start line.

3. There is a LOT of parking at the Bizz Johnson Trailhead across from the Susanville Historic Train Depot at 601 Richmond Road. This is about .75 mi from the start line. This is a flat, easy walk. One option would be to bring your bicycle and ride to the start. It is a flat, easy, short ride. There will be a place at the finish line to lock your bike and leave your keys with the Race Director.

Packet Pickup:

Packet Pickup will be at the Susanville Historic Train Depot at 601 Richmond Road on Friday, June 21st from 3 PM until 6 PM.  Late Registration will be available on Friday at packet pickup.

Race Day morning packet pickup will be available at the Hobo Camp Day Use Area (Finish Line Area) beginning at 6 AM. There will be limited race day registration from 6 - 6:45 AM (22K), 6 - 7:15 AM (14K), and 6 - 7:30 AM (7K).

Post-Race Activities

The Finish Line is approximately .1 mile from the Start Line. Feel free to bring a picnic lunch and EZ-up and hang out on the grass watching the other finishers. We will have hotdogs, watermelon, water, sodas, and non-alcoholic brews from Athletic Brewing Company for runners. If your family wants to join you, there are several newer charcoal BBQs in the day use area. The river has excellent access at the Day Use area so cooling off is a MUST!

This race is capped at  150 runners total for all 3 events!

description:

Benefiting Scouting America

Join us for a fun-filled run/walk in support of Scouting America! Whether you're walking, jogging, or racing to the finish line, every step you take helps fund life-changing programs for local youth.

name: Blossom Bike Ride
description:
The 36th Annual Blossom Bike Ride will take place on March 7, 2026. We are currently working on the routes for this year.  As the mileage gets longer, the route provides more of a challenge. Our 7 mile family ride takes you along the rails to trails pathway through Reedley. The 20 mile route offers more scenic landscapes north east of town for your viewing pleasure. If you are looking for a little more challenge, you might want to try our 40 mile route. This will get you started on the right course of mileage for the year. If you are looking for the longer ride, we offer the 60 mile route with some climbing. This route will take you into the foot hills east of Reedley.

Let's get ready to Ride!

 
These are ride times:
  • 60 Mile 7:00am
  • 40 Mile 8:30am
  • 20 Mile 9:30am
  • 7 Mile Family ride 10:30
 
Ride begins at:

     Reedley College
     995 N. Reed
     Reedley, 93654
 
Please allow yourself to arrive at least half an hour before ride so that you can check in at registration desk and receive your bib and T-shirt if you signed up for one. We will NOT be checking in riders more than 35 minutes before scheduled ride.  
 
Typical weather should be a beautiful low 70's that day. 
 
See you Saturday!

name: Blossom Bike Ride
description:
The 36th Annual Blossom Bike Ride will take place on March 7, 2026. We are currently working on the routes for this year.  As the mileage gets longer, the route provides more of a challenge. Our 7 mile family ride takes you along the rails to trails pathway through Reedley. The 20 mile route offers more scenic landscapes north east of town for your viewing pleasure. If you are looking for a little more challenge, you might want to try our 40 mile route. This will get you started on the right course of mileage for the year. If you are looking for the longer ride, we offer the 60 mile route with some climbing. This route will take you into the foot hills east of Reedley.

Let's get ready to Ride!

 
These are ride times:
  • 60 Mile 7:00am
  • 40 Mile 8:30am
  • 20 Mile 9:30am
  • 7 Mile Family ride 10:30
 
Ride begins at:

     Reedley College
     995 N. Reed
     Reedley, 93654
 
Please allow yourself to arrive at least half an hour before ride so that you can check in at registration desk and receive your bib and T-shirt if you signed up for one. We will NOT be checking in riders more than 35 minutes before scheduled ride.  
 
Typical weather should be a beautiful low 70's that day. 
 
See you Saturday!

name: Bowman Run with the Bulls
description:
Join us for the Annual Run with the Bulls 5K Run/Walk!
Lace up your shoes and be part of this fun community tradition that welcomes runners and walkers of all ages. The scenic course winds through the heart of Auburn — The Endurance Capital of the World — showcasing its beauty and spirit.

The race starts and finishes at Railhead Park, with all proceeds supporting continued improvements to Bowman Charter School’s large gymnasium — a space that brings our students and community together.

🏅 Registration Details

  • $40 for kids (13 and under)
  • $45 for general registration
  • $50 same-day registration (shirt not guaranteed)
  • Family Discount: Register 3 or more and receive $3 off each runner!
  • Register by March 22 to guarantee your cotton race shirt.

All finishers will receive a finisher’s medal, and age-group awards will be presented for both kids and adults.

🎉 Team Challenge: Join a Bowman class team and help your class earn a special reward for the most participants and fundraising!

❤️ Can't join in person? You can sign up to participate virtually or support the cause with a donation—every contribution helps Bowman students go the distance!

📸 Race Day Highlights

  • Chip timing provided by Singletrack Running
  • Professional race photos by Facchino Photography — included with your entry

Come out and celebrate fitness, community, and school spirit — Run with the Bulls!

name: Breezin’ Through Beaumont
description:
On Saturday, May 16, 2026, the City of Beaumont will celebrate the return of Breezin’ Through Beaumont. This event consists of a 5k road race. Everyone is encouraged to come out and watch this exciting event. 

The race will begin in front of the Beaumont Civic Center, located at: 550 E. Sixth St., Beaumont, CA 92223. and continue along the islands of Palm Avenue to 13th Street before returning southbound to 8th Street where the race will wind around Stewart Park before finishing back at the Civic Center. Whether you are an experienced runner or an avid walker, everyone who is interested is encouraged to participate.

Event Times

  • 6:30 a.m. - Registration and bag pickup 
  • 8:00 a.m. - Race starts 
    • Expected to maintain a 15-minute mile pace 
  • 9:00 a.m. - Awards Ceremony

The awards ceremony is expected to take place at 9am on the front steps of the Civic Center. The top three male and female finishers in each age division will be awarded medals. Overall male and female winners will receive trophies. 

Registration Information

  • Preregistration (Open until April 30) - $30
    • Pre-registration guaranteed a race shirt.
  • Race Day Registration - $50

  • All sales are final. No refunds.

Current Divisions by Age

  • 7 - 9 
  • 10 - 12 
  • 13 - 15
  • 16 - 19 
  • 20 - 24 
  • 25 - 29 
  • 30 - 34 
  • 35 - 39 
  • 40 - 44
  • 45 - 49 
  • 50 - 54 
  • 55 - 59 
  • 60 - 64 
  • 65 - 69 
  • 70 - 74 
  • 75 - 79 
  • 80+ 

Bib Pick-up Information

  • Pick-up on race day at the Beaumont Civic Center beginning at 6:30 a.m. 
  • Runners can pick up their race bibs and t-shirts ahead of race day on May 11 – 14 from 1pm to 5pm at the Albert A. Chatigny Sr. Community Recreation Center, located at 1310 Oak Valley Parkway. 

Road Closures
During the events, there will be rolling street closures and no-parking zones throughout the course. The areas most affected within the city will be along:

  • 6th Street 
  • Palm Ave
  • 8th Street
  • Orange Ave
  • Magnolia Ave

description:
Make room for your Thanksgiving dinner and join us for the Bret Harte Athletics & Booster Club's 2025 Run Turkey Run 5K/10K on Thursday, November 27, 2025! This fun, family-friendly event starts and ends at Leland High School in scenic Almaden Valley, San Jose. Both the 5K and 10K courses are run on level terrain on the paved trails along the Los Alamitos Creek and the open space area. Scroll down for race day schedule and parking information.

name: Brian Waterbury Memorial Rock to Pier Run
description:
The 2026 Brian Waterbury Memorial Rock to Pier Fun Run and Rock’n Around the Pier Half Marathon will take place on Saturday, July 18 with a 8:00 am start time. 2026 marks the 56th running of the Rock to Pier Run and the 12th running of the Half Marathon.

The Brian Waterbury Memorial Rock to Pier Fun Run is a 6 mile beach run from Morro Rock to the Cayucos Pier. The finish line is at the iconic Cayucos Pier. This event is open to participants of all ages and abilities.

The Rock’n Around the Pier Half Marathon event begins at Morro Rock, continues to the Cayucos Pier, turn around and head back towards Morro Rock. At 10.5 miles the course will veer off the beach (through soft sand) and will follow a 1 mile loop through a local park returning to the beach (through soft sand) and finish at Morro Rock. Please note that the course will be closed at 12:00pm for runners. 

Parking is limited in Cayucos and all participants for the Rock to Pier Run are encouraged to return to Morro Bay via provided Bus transportation. There is plenty of parking at Morro Rock and nearby. Arrive early.

Limited shirt sizes are still available while supplies last.   Some sizes are sold out.

Both Events will begin at 8:00am

Water/Aide stations are available - 3 for Rock to Pier 

Transportation is provided from the Cayucos Pier back to the start at Morro Rock where a post event breakfast will be held.  Awards will be at Morro Rock.

This event is held on the beach--you will get wet.   Dogs are not allowed on the course due to the Snowy Plover nesting season. 

Any other questions, contact  kzink@morrobayca.gov

name: Brooks West XC Championships
description:
Welcome to the Brooks West XC Championships!

  • Date:
    • Saturday December 6, 2025
  • Schedule:
    • 7:05AM -  Freshman Boys
    • 7:25AM - Freshman Girls
    • 7:45AM - Sophomore Boys
    • 8:05AM - Sophomore Girls
    • 8:25AM - Junior Boys
    • 8:45AM - Junior Girls
    • 9:05AM - Senior Boys
    • 9:25AM - Senior Girls
    • 9:45AM - OPEN RACE (non-high school runners)
    • 10:20AM - Championship Girls Race
      • Restricted to Grades 9-12
    • 10:50AM - Championship Boys Race
      • Restricted to Grades 9-12
    • 11:45AM - Awards presentation, top 24 from Girls Championship Race
    • 12:15AM - Awards presentation, top 24 from Boys Championship Race
  • Awards
    • First 3500 athletes to register will receive a Brooks XC Spike Bag
    • The top 10 boys and girls from the Championship Races will be awarded with a spot in the Brooks XC Championships in San Diego on December 13th (must attend a high school in the US or US territory)

  • Event Merch Presale:
    • Celebrate your XC season with exclusive gear from the Brooks West XC Championships. Purchase gear on-site at the Fleet Feet Merchandise tent.
  • For full details please visit our event website
  • For race specific questions please reach out to the RD at dtodd4882@gmail.com

name: Buzz Marathon #26
description:
WHAT'S THE BUZZ?

The Buzz Marathon is a Boston qualifying race, hosted at Camp Roberts California National Guard Installation. This annual event includes; A full marathon, half-marathon, 10K, 5k, and a kids 1-mile run. Proceeds of this event help fund the Morale, Welfare, and Recreation (MWR) program with their mission of soldier care. MWR provides services to support the wellbeing of military personnel, their families, retirees, and veterans. The goal of MWR is to create a "home away from home" environment, helping service members maintain morale during training and other high-stress duties.

Boston Qualifier: USATF #CA24001TEB 

 

CAMP ROBERTS ENTRY REQUIREMENTS:

All participants and visitors must comply with base access protocols

Drivers are required to provide:

  • Real ID (or valid government-issued ID)
  • Current vehicle registration and proof of insurance
  • ALL VEHICHLES ARE SUBJECT TO SEARCH AND SEIZURE

All other visitors or passengers (ages 16 and above) are also required to provide a Real ID or government-issued identification.

 

COURSE DESCRIPTION

Runners will start at the heart of the Camp Roberts instillation, heading northeast through diverse terrain and varying elevations. Along the way, participants will take in breathtaking scenic views, with chances to spot local wildlife such as elk, deer, and the elusive kit fox.

The course also offers a unique blend of natural beauty and history, featuring glimpses of California wildflowers and historic military landmarks that highlight the rich heritage of Camp Roberts.

 

AID STATIONS

Aid stations are positioned approximately every two miles, with additional placements at key turns to help guide runners along the correct route.

Stations are located at the following mile markers:

  • 1.6
  • 3.6
  • 5.1
  • 6.55 (Half Marathon Turnaround)
  • 8.0
  • 9.9
  • 12.0
  • 13.12 (Full Marathon Turnaround)


Each station is stocked with water, Powerade, bananas, oranges, energy gels, and latrines.


 

PARKING

Parking on Convoy Parking Lot on California Blvd and Montana Blvd. Short walk to the start/finish line.

 

AWARDS

All participants will receive a T-shirt and a finisher medal. Awards ceremony will be held at noon, where we’ll present a plaque to the overall first-place male and female in each race.

 

PACKET PICKUP

The Camp Roberts MWR will be hosting packet pickup at the Phoenix Recreation Center (Building 6083), located approximately 75 yards from the Start/Finish line at the corner of Arizona and California Blvd.

Packet pickup and security clearance will be available:

  • Tuesday to Friday, March 17th – 20th, 9:00 AM – 3:00 PM
  • Race Day – Saturday, March 21st, 6:00 AM - 8:00 AM

Participants are strongly encouraged to check in early during the Tuesday–Friday window to complete security clearance and avoid race-day delays.

On site reg available for $20 extra 3/17 - 3/2010AM-4PM

Join us in celebrating our 15th year when we host runners in our Half Marathon, 10k and 5k Run as half and 10k participants run through Sea Lion Cove, African Adventure and NEW KINGDOM OF ASIA at Fresno Chaffee Zoo, with a grand finish at Chukchansi Stadium. Or choose our Rock and Run 5k, it doesn't go through the Zoo, but has all of the other benefits of the Half Marathon.

The Half Marathon is a 20 point race in the CLASSIC Runner of the Year Series!

name: California December Distance Night
description:
Join us for an evening of distance racing under the lights at Occidental College this December. This event is designed for high school and college athletes looking to leverage their cross-country fitness, as well as community runners aiming to take one final swing at a fast time before the year comes to a close.

The program will consist of 800s, Miles, and Two Miles for runners of all ability levels, as well as a few faster 5k sections to close out the night. Races will be organized for all ability levels, with pacers in each heat to support runners in reaching their pacing targets. 

We hope to see you in December in Los Angeles.

name: Californian Dreamin 5K, 10K, & Half Marathon
description:
Californian Dreamin’ 5K, 10K & Half Marathon

🌴 Date: Sunday, August 24, 2025
🌊 Location: Long Beach, CA

Dream big, run free, and soak up the California sunshine at the Californian Dreamin’ Run in Long Beach! With ocean views, a laid-back vibe, and a scenic coastal course, this event captures the heart of the Golden State in every step.

 

Event Highlights
☀️ Iconic Coastal Views: Experience the beauty of Long Beach’s beaches, palm trees, and breezy ocean paths.
🏅 Finisher Medals: Finish strong and take home a medal inspired by the California lifestyle.
🎉 Positive Vibes: Run to the rhythm of good vibes, great music, and an encouraging community.
👟 Distances for All Levels: Choose from 5K, 10K, or Half Marathon—perfect for new runners and seasoned athletes alike.


📸 Photo Opportunities: Snap the perfect race-day pic with Cali-themed photo ops and share your #DreaminRun moments.

Why You’ll Love It
The Californian Dreamin’ Run isn’t just a race; it’s a celebration of the California dream. Whether you’re running for fun, fitness, or a personal best, you’ll love the friendly, inclusive atmosphere and unforgettable course.

Registration Includes
✅ Timed race with scenic course
✅  Finisher medal
✅ USATF Certified Course
✅ Post-race refreshments
✅ Professional  free race photos

Schedule:
📅 Race Day Check-In: 6:00 AM


🏁 Start Times:

Half Marathon - 7:00 AM
10K - 7:30AM
5K -  7:30AM
Join us for a day of sun, sand, and smiles as you run your California dream!

Register Now 👉

“California is not a place; it’s a feeling. And this race will make you feel unstoppable!”

name: Camp Heartbreak – Friday the 13th of February -After Dark  5K. 10K Half Marathon
description:
💔 Camp Heartbreak – Run If You Dare
🌙 Friday the 13th of February – Long Beach
5K | 10K | Half Marathon
📍 5400 E. Ocean Blvd, Long Beach, CA
📅 Friday, February 13, 2026
🕓 Check-in 4:00 PM
Start Times (Based on distance) | Half 5:00 PM | 10K & 5K 6:30 PM

 
💘 About the Event
Welcome to Camp Heartbreak, where love stories end in sprint finishes and Cupid’s arrows miss… on purpose. 💀


They say heartbreak hurts — but here, it burns calories.

Join us for Run If You Dare, a Friday-the-13th Valentine’s race that mixes romance and ruin under the moonlit shoreline of Long Beach. Whether you’re running from your ex, chasing closure, or just here for the medal and the music, this night’s for the fearless and the heart-strong.

 
🌊 What to Expect
USATF-Certified Course 🏁
Professional Chip Timing ⏱️
Free Race-Day Photos 📸
Finisher Medals for All Participants 🏅
Overall & Age Group Awards
3 On-Course Water Stations (one at each turnaround)
Finish-Line Festival & Camp Dance Party 🎶
Costume Contest — Best Heartbreaker & Most Tragic Love Story 👠💔
DJ, Lights & Glow Effects for that classic CaliFlow After-Dark vibe
Runners, Walkers & Lovelorn Souls of All Paces Welcome!
 
🩶 Course Info
Your journey begins beneath the glowing CaliFlow arch at 5400 E. Ocean Blvd, tracing a flat, paved path along the waves — scenic, fast, and a little bit sinister.

Each turnaround hides a “Camp Heartbreak” surprise — maybe a runaway Cupid, a rose-covered machete, or a love letter gone wrong.

Half Marathon: 3 × 4.36-mile loops
10K: 2 × 5K out-and-backs
5K: 1 loop

Every station features glowing course markers, cheering “counselors,” and enough good vibes to heal even the most tragic of love lives.

 
🔥 The Vibe – Totally Camp CaliFlow


Think Valentine’s Day Massacre meets Glow Run Rom-Com.
We’re talking camp signs, flickering lanterns, red lights, and finish-line slow jams.

Whether you come solo, with your sweetheart, or as a crew of heartbreak survivors, one thing’s for sure — you’ll leave with a full heart and maybe a few goosebumps.

Because at CaliFlow Runs, we don’t fear Friday the 13th.
We run right through it — in style, with heart, and with a whole lot of glow.

✨ Not just a race. Join the movement.

name: Camp Shamrocked: The  Friday the 13th  After Dark - 5K. 10K. Half Marathon
description:
☘️ Camp Shamrocked: The Unlucky Run
🌲 Friday the 13th – 5400 E Ocean Blvd, Long Beach
5K | 10K | Half Marathon
📍 5400 E Ocean Blvd, Long Beach, CA 90803
📅 Friday, March 13, 2026
🕓 Check-In: 4:00 PM
Start Times | Half: 5:00 PM | 10K & 5K: 6:30 PM

 
💀 About the Event
Welcome back, campers… and may the luck be ever in your disfavor. 🍀
They say strange things happen every Friday the 13th — but when it lands right before St. Patrick’s Day, you can bet the leprechauns are up to no good.

Join us for Camp Shamrocked: The Unlucky Run, a moonlit race where green fog meets grit, and superstition takes the scenic route down the Long Beach shoreline. Whether you’re chasing a PR or just chasing your luck, you’ll be part of something rare — a tribe that runs through the chaos with heart, humor, and a little mischief.

 
🌊 What to Expect
USATF-Certified Course
Chip Timing for accurate results ⏱️
Free Race-Day Photos by Nina & Dre 📸
Finisher Medals for All Participants 🏅
Overall & Age Group Awards
3 On-Course Water Stations (one at each turnaround)
Campfire Finish Line Festival 🔥
Costume Contest – Leprechauns, Lucky Charms & Creatures of the Night 👻
DJ, Lights & Green Glow Effects for that signature CaliFlow After-Dark magic
Runners, Walkers, and Shamrocked Souls of All Paces Welcome!
 
🌕 Course Info
The course begins under the glowing CaliFlow arch near Belmont Pier, winding along the oceanfront path under the light of the moon (and maybe a little mischief).

Expect glowing green markers, fog  and checkpoints straight out of Camp Shamrocked lore:
🍀 Cabin 13 — where luck runs thin
🪞 The Clover Crossing — every 13th step’s a gamble
🔥 The Campfire Finish — where legends light up the night

Half Marathon: 3 × 4.36-mile loops
10K: 2 × 5K out-and-backs
5K: 1 loop

Each station will be fully stocked with water, encouragement, and a few surprises to keep your spirits high and your luck questionable.

 
🧿 The Vibe – Welcome to Camp Shamrocked
At CaliFlow Runs, we don’t chase luck — we create it. This is your chance to laugh in the face of superstition, defy the odds, and dance your way across that finish line under a canopy of stars and green glow.

So grab your glow sticks, pull on something lucky (or not), and join us for the most unforgettable Friday the 13th run of the year.

✨ Not just a race. Join the movement.

name: Camp Turkey Terror: After Dark- Friday the 13th  Turkey Trot: 5K. 10K. Half Marathon
description:
This a 2026 Event

🦃 Camp Turkey Terror – Where the Turkeys Fight Back
🌲 Friday the 13th 
5K | 10K | Half Marathon
📍 5400 E Ocean Blvd, Long Beach, CA 90803
📅 Friday, November 13, 2026
🕓 Check-In begins : 4:00 PM to 6:30 PM
Start Times | Half: 5:00 PM | 10K & 5K: 6:30 PM

 
💀 About the Event
Welcome to Camp Turkey Terror — where the tables have turned and the turkeys are taking revenge. 🦃🔥
It’s Friday the 13th, and under the harvest moon, the woods come alive with feathers, fog, and just a hint of chaos.

Join us for the final chapter in the Camp CaliFlow Trilogy, a fall night of fun, fright, and fearless miles. Whether you’re running from guilt, running for the pie, or just running for the glow, this one’s for you.

Because at Camp Turkey Terror… the turkeys fight back.

 
🌊 What to Expect
USATF-Certified Course 🏁
Professional Chip Timing ⏱️
Free Race-Day Photos by Nina & Dre 📸
Finisher Medals for All Participants 🏅
Overall & Age Group Awards 🥇
3 On-Course Water Stations (one at each turnaround)
Finish-Line Feast & Campfire Festival 🔥
Costume Contest – Pilgrims, Pumpkins & Poultry Welcome 🦃🎃
DJ, Lights & Glow Effects for that signature CaliFlow After-Dark magic
All paces welcome — runners, walkers, and leftovers alike!
 
🌕 Course Info
The course begins beneath the glowing CaliFlow arch near Belmont Pier, tracing the flat, scenic Long Beach path under the light of the harvest moon.

As you make your way through the fog, you’ll pass a few iconic “Camp Turkey Terror” checkpoints:
🔥 The Final Feast Turnaround
🍂 Stuffing Station 13
🥧 Pie or Die Water Stop

Half Marathon: 3 × 4.36-mile loops
10K: 2 × 5K out-and-backs
5K: 1 loop

Each turnaround features a full water station, friendly “camp counselors,” and plenty of autumn spirit to keep you moving before the turkeys catch up.

 
🍁 The Vibe – Totally Camp CaliFlow
Think Thanksgiving meets slasher flick, but with way better lighting and medals you’ll actually want to show off.

Expect glowing campfires, pumpkin decor, moody fog, and more laughs than screams as you cross the finish line at our “Campfire Feast” celebration.

Because at CaliFlow Runs, we don’t fear the chaos — we run through it.
And this time… the turkeys are watching. 👀

✨ Not just a race. Join the movement.

name: Castle to Coast Fun Run - 2026
description:
Wake up with the sunrise for a unique Central Coast experience!

Castle to Coast starts at stunning William Randolph Hearst Memorial Beach, nestled beneath iconic Hearst Castle. Lace up for an invigorating 8.2-mile run along breathtaking Highway 1, making your way to the charming coastal town of Cambria, finishing at Shamel Park.

Enjoy spectacular early morning ocean views of the Pacific Ocean, making this run as visually stunning as it is energizing. This low-key, feel-good event is the perfect way to kick off your new year, whether you’re a seasoned runner or simply looking for a fun and rewarding challenge.

Along the route, you’ll be supported by enthusiastic Cuesta College Student-Athlete volunteers, ensuring a safe and enjoyable experience. At the finish line, participants can look forward to giveaways from Running Warehouse, FLUID Sports Nutrition and other local merchants. Plus, a convenient shuttle service will transport you back to the starting line. Stay and relax in quaint Cambria to celebrate your accomplishment.

name: Catalina Island Marathon, 10K, 5K
description: California's State Off-Road Marathon Championship is also the oldest trail marathon in the state and takes place on beautiful Catalina Island located off the coast of Los Angeles and surrounded by blue ocean, green hills and more beauty than you have ever run through.   Experience the Catalina Island Conservancy the way it was intended to be experienced, on foot, running, and noticing the history and beauty of the island.  This is a bucket list event that you will want to run year, after year, after year.

description:

Your tax deductible race fee will feed a horse for a week!
This event honors all life, remembers those we've lost, and embodies the resilience of the human spirit.

name: Cerro Gordo Silver Run
description:
Saturday. May 23, 2026 | Start Time: 8:00 AM | Check-in by 6:30 AM
(Camping & lodging info at the bottom of this description)

Check out the video recap from this past year for more context!

Are you tough enough to race up a mountain road built for mule trains and silver barons?

Join us for a legendary race in the Eastern Sierra - an 8-mile uphill battle climbing 4,600 vertical feet to the historic ghost town of Cerro Gordo, once the richest silver mine in California.

This is not your average run.
This is a gut-check. A pilgrimage. A challenge against time, gravity, and yourself.

The infamous Cerro Gordo Road was carved out in 1865 to shuttle silver down from the mountains. Now, once a year, runners race back up - chasing glory, chasing ghosts, and chasing history.

When you summit the town, the day’s just beginning. Cross the finish line and celebrate with:
– A giant mountaintop BBQ
– Live music and games
– Self-guided exploration of the abandoned town
– And a well-earned sense of triumph.

What’s included:
- Aid stations every mile stocked with fuel and encouragement
- A limited-edition Silver Run 2026 shirt and finishers medal
- Shuttle vans for the ride back down
- Eternal bragging rights: the winner’s name is engraved in silver and enshrined in Cerro Gordo’s history

Last year’s winning time: 1:14:04 by Jacob Banta
Think you’ve got what it takes to beat it?

There’s no time limit. Whether you finish in 1 hour or 5, this mountain has room for all. We’ve had teenagers run with their parents. We’ve had an 81-year-old cross the finish line. All are welcome - as long as you're willing to dig deep and climb.

Check out the 2025 race results:
https://my.raceresult.com/341872/results

Don’t miss the most epic footrace in California.
This is all happening: Saturday. May 23, 2026 
Come run for the silver.

Camping & Lodging

Our neighbor is providing camping spots available in Keeler, CA, less than 1/4 mile from the starting line, available for $20/spot. These will have restrooms available at the campground area. This is by far the cheapest and closest accommodation option. 

Otherwise, Lone Pine, CA is 15 miles from the starting line and has a wide variety of hotels, motels, RV parks, and more. 

Another option is BLM Land camping. There is a lot of BLM land around and you can camp there for free for up to 14 days. Google "BLM camping" for more information. 

There will be multiple parking lots available in Keeler, CA the day of the race to leave your cars. There will be volunteers on site to direct you to these day of the race. After the race, you will be brought down by shuttle bus, back to these parking lots.

name: Champion Mine Trail Race
description:
Challenge Yourself and Enjoy the Great Outdoors

Join the Sierra TrailBlazers Running Club and Bear Yuba Land Trust for the inaugural Champion Mine Trail Race!

Get ready to travel to a must-see destination race in Northern California. Explore some of Nevada City’s most exciting trails with this brand-new half-marathon (13.1 miles) event. The course winds through towering pines, crosses a historic swinging bridge, and challenges runners with a series of rewarding climbs. With multiple aid stations, historical landmarks, and a newly constructed trail section offering varied terrain, this course rivals some of the best trail races in Northern California.

Runners will enjoy breathtaking views along the Tribute Trail and Deer Creek, combined with a beautiful variety of landscapes throughout the race. Best of all, the adventure begins right on Nevada City’s historic Broad Street — a truly unforgettable starting line!

The Champion Mine Trail Run offers a dynamic mix of pavement, gravel, and single-track trails, making it a must-do event for any trail enthusiast.

name: Chasing Santa – 5K, 10K, 10-Miler, Half Marathon
description:
Santa’s on the move and it’s your turn to chase him down the Long Beach coast. Chasing Santa is all about festive miles, holiday spirit, and a little seasonal mischief by the sea. Whether you’re jogging, walking, or just soaking up the holiday cheer, this run is the perfect way to start the season with miles, smiles, and a touch of Santa magic.

Details

Start Location: 5400 E Ocean Ave, Long Beach, CA 90803
Parking: Parking in the lot is $2/hour and starts at 8am, if you are running the Half/10m you can use the Passport app to pay for parking. Street parking is free.

Event Schedule

Saturday
1:00-3:00pm – Early bib pick-up on the 2nd floor at Sports Basement Long Beach (store discount sent via email the week of the event & post-race)
2100 N Bellflower Blvd, Long Beach, CA 90815

Sunday
6:20am – Bib pick-up opens at the start
7:00am – Half marathon and 10-miler start
7:30am – 5k & 10k start
10:20am – Course closes (3 hours, 20 minutes for the Half)
Early start of 6:30am may be pre-arranged in advance for half marathoners, email your request to events@hightideruns.com. All early starters will not be eligible for awards.

Out & Back Course

5k & 10k: The 5k route is used for the 5k (one lap) and 10k (two laps) – 5k route
10m: The 5m route is used for the 10m (two laps) – 5m route
Half: The 5m route is run twice and the 5k route is run once for the Half – 5m route and 5k route

More About the Course

This is an out and back course, meaning you will begin and finish in the same location.

Our courses are not closed, which means that there are often runners, walkers, and others enjoying the day along with you. Safety is must and all runners must stay on the pedestrian side of the beach path. The course never goes off the beach path.

On-course support: Courses are well marked with two water stations and restrooms along the way. Turns will be clearly marked with chalk, a sign that says runner turn, and a flag.

Final Details

Bib: Please wear your race bib on the front of your shirt so we can track your time and send your pics!
Gear Check: You may leave personal items with staff at the registration tent. Please bring your own bag.
Medals: All runners receive a finishing medal. 1st place medals are given to the overall 1st male and female in each distance
Results & Photos: An email with race results and photos will be sent the day after the race and earlier on Instagram. Race photos are free!

Join Us Again: Did you have a blast running with us at our low-pressure, high vibes race? We have themed races throughout the year in Long Beach, the San Fernando Valley, San Diego, and Orange County. Register for multiple races at a time to earn a discount. Check our full schedule

Have Another Question? Check our FAQ page, it's probably answered there!

name: Chasing Santa – 5K, 10K, 10-Miler, Half Marathon
description:
Santa’s on the move and it’s your turn to chase him down the Long Beach coast. Chasing Santa is all about festive miles, holiday spirit, and a little seasonal mischief by the sea. Whether you’re jogging, walking, or just soaking up the holiday cheer, this run is the perfect way to start the season with miles, smiles, and a touch of Santa magic.

Details

Start Location: 5400 E Ocean Ave, Long Beach, CA 90803
Parking: Parking in the lot is $2/hour and starts at 8am, if you are running the Half/10m you can use the Passport app to pay for parking. Street parking is free.

Event Schedule

Saturday
1:00-3:00pm – Early bib pick-up on the 2nd floor at Sports Basement Long Beach (store discount sent via email the week of the event & post-race)
2100 N Bellflower Blvd, Long Beach, CA 90815

Sunday
6:20am – Bib pick-up opens at the start
7:00am – Half marathon and 10-miler start
7:30am – 5k & 10k start
10:20am – Course closes (3 hours, 20 minutes for the Half)
Early start of 6:30am may be pre-arranged in advance for half marathoners, email your request to events@hightideruns.com. All early starters will not be eligible for awards.

Out & Back Course

5k & 10k: The 5k route is used for the 5k (one lap) and 10k (two laps) – 5k route
10m: The 5m route is used for the 10m (two laps) – 5m route
Half: The 5m route is run twice and the 5k route is run once for the Half – 5m route and 5k route

More About the Course

This is an out and back course, meaning you will begin and finish in the same location.

Our courses are not closed, which means that there are often runners, walkers, and others enjoying the day along with you. Safety is must and all runners must stay on the pedestrian side of the beach path. The course never goes off the beach path.

On-course support: Courses are well marked with two water stations and restrooms along the way. Turns will be clearly marked with chalk, a sign that says runner turn, and a flag.

Final Details

Bib: Please wear your race bib on the front of your shirt so we can track your time and send your pics!

Medals: All runners receive a finishing medal. 1st place medals are given to the overall 1st male and female in each distance
Results & Photos: An email with race results and photos will be sent the day after the race and earlier on Instagram. Race photos are free!

name: Cherry Pickin 5k WAVE RACE
description:
Cherry Pickin’ 5K Wave Race                             

At Leona Valley Elementary

Saturday, May 23, 2026 

The 5K WAVE RACE! This is a handicapped race based on Age-Graded tables.
If you are a good runner for your age or gender, you could WIN this race! Your start time will depend on your age and gender per the table found in the link below.
Custom medals will be given to the top 150 overall finishers – not based on age divisions. There are no age group divisions since the start of the race is handicapped by age and gender.
Up and Down 5k Course - Uphill first half, super fun downhill coming back!
All entries get a t-shirt – while supplies last. 

There will also be a "Family Fun Run Wave."  If you would like to just come out and run, jog or walk and not worry about time or placing you may opt for the Family Fun Run Wave, starting at 8:00 am. You will not be timed and you will not earn a finish placing.

This event is a fundraiser for the West Antelope Valley Education Foundation - WAVE. They provide funding for extracurricular opportunities such as field trips, clubs, sports, etc for the students of the Westside Union School District.

CLICK HERE FOR RACE FLYER WITH FURTHER DETAILS! 
Including the Starting Wave Table!

name: Child Abuse / Foster Care Awareness 5k Run/Walk
description:
The Social Work Student organizations, Phi Alpha Honors Society, and Title IV-E program at California State University, Fresno are hosting a Child Abuse/Foster Care Awareness 5K Run/Walk, which will not only raise awareness about child abuse and Foster Care but also incorporate a wellness component for families. This dual-purpose event aims to both advocate for child safety and foster care, raising awareness of the need to support the well-being of families, caregivers, and foster youth. By promoting self-care and providing resources for mental and physical well-being, this event seeks to increase family and individual well-being. Proceeds will support next year's event to make this an annual event. 

Special pricing for children 9 and under of $25.00 - Discount applied during check-out.
