name: Chino Valley YMCA Reindeer Romp 5K
description:
Join us for the 14th Annual Chino Valley YMCA Reindeer Romp at Ayala Park in Chino, California. 

PLEASE READ: The run/walk starts at 8:15 AM. You are welcome to run with your friends or family.

  • Flat and fast USATF Certified course at Ayala Park in Chino - 5665 Edison Ave., Chino, Ca 91710
  • This 5k is the first leg of the Chino Triple Crown - participate in the Chino Valley YMCA Reindeer Romp, Run for Russ (February 7th, 2026) and the DairyAire (March 7th, 2026) and receive a special Triple Crown medal! 
  • All entrants in the 5k will receive a shirt and finisher medal. 
  • ALL PROCEEDS BENEFIT THE CHINO VALLEY YMCA

 

REGISTRATION FEE SCHEDULE: 

  • 8/1/25 - 11/30/25 $45
  • 12/1/25 - 12/6/25 $50
  • Group discount of $5.00 for groups of 5 or more entrants. Paper applications only. (Please email us for an application)

 

EMAIL: romp@weymca.org

 

*** COSTUME CONTEST!!  This year we will be awarding the best child and family costume.  Show your holiday spirit by decking yourself out in all your favorite holiday garb, donning your jingliest bells, twinkliest lights and tying on your tinsel! ***

 

PLEASE LEAVE YOUR PETS AT HOME.

 

Packet pickup and late registration will be Friday, December 5th from 4PM - 6PM at the Chino Valley YMCA. Also Saturday morning before the race STARTING AT 7:00AM.

 

SORRY, NO REFUNDS! THANK YOU FOR YOUR DONATION!

 

Consider supporting a new event in Chino - American Cancer Society MAKING STRIDES, a 5k walk event to support Breast Cancer awareness and fundraising! Saturday October 4, 2025 at the Chino City Hall. Making Strides of Inland Empire Presented by San Antonio Regional Hospital | (acsevents.org)

name: Chocolate Chase 5K for Craniofacial Awareness
description:
Join us for our Inaugural Chocolate Chase where fitness and Craniofacial awareness converge in the most delicious way! Whether you participate in the timed 5K race, one-mile walk, kids dash or just come out to celebrate and support, we will have something for everyone. Best of all--chocolate treats!   Post-race venue in Crocker Park will provide an opportunity for families and friends to connect.  Funds raised will be donated to FacesOfTomorrow.org.  

 

EVENT SWAG:

-Short-sleeved cotton t-shirt for race registrants

-Shirt or cape for superhero dash registrants 

-Commemorative medal for race and dash finishers

-See's chocolate bar at the finish line compliments of Elk Grove Orthodontics

-Referral bonus for referring 5 or more registrants: embroidered logo canvas shopper tote 

-Age group awards for 5K

 

PACKET PICK UP: 

-Saturday May 17: 10-6pm (Fleet Feet, 2311 J Street)

-Race Day Sunday May 18, 7:15am Crocker Park

 

RACE DAY SCHEDULE:

7:15am Packet pick up and event day registration

8:15am: Superhero Kids Dash start

8:30am: 5K and one mile run/walk start

 

5K COURSE INFORMATION:

Start in front of Crocker Art Museum, along Riverfront Promenade through Old Sacramento, along river to Robert Matsui Water Park and back.

 

AWARDS FOR 5K:

Top male and female finisher in each age category will be recognized.  (12 and under, 13-17, 18-21, 22-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70-79, 80+). Awards may be picked up at the awards tent at the post-race venue. If you are unable to pick up your award on race day, please email ChocolateChase916@gmail.com. Awards will not be mailed. 

 

STROLLERS & DOGS:
Strollers are permitted in the race. We just ask that you and your bundle of joy start the race in the back of the pack. No scooters, bikes, skates, skateboards on the course. 

We love dogs, but only service dogs are allowed on the course.  All other dogs are not allowed to participate, but stop by the Cleft Pup Brigade rescue for your four-legged fix!

 

GETTING HERE: 

Crocker Park is located at 211 O Street in downtown Sacramento, steps from the Capitol Mall and the Riverfront Promenade.

-By Car: Parking is conveniently located at City Lot X at 2nd and N Street for $5.  The lot is accessible via 3rd Street, turning right onto N Street. (Follow parking signs.) Two- and three-hour metered street parking is available around Crocker Park. Check parking signage for prices. Pay with card or download the ParkMobile app to find and pay for parking.  

-By Bicycle: Bike racks are located around the Crocker Art Museum's main entrance. 

-Public Transportation  Closest light rail stops are 7th Street & Capitol and 8th & K Street.  YoloBus 42B makes stops within walking distance at Capitol Mall & Front Street and Capitol Mall and 7th Street. Youth and students in grades TK-12 can ride Sac RT for free

name: Chocolate Chase 5K for Craniofacial Awareness
description:
Join us for our Inaugural Chocolate Chase where fitness and Craniofacial awareness converge in the most delicious way! Whether you participate in the timed 5K race, one-mile walk, kids dash or just come out to celebrate and support, we will have something for everyone. Best of all--chocolate treats!   Post-race venue in Crocker Park will provide an opportunity for families and friends to connect.  Funds raised will be donated to FacesOfTomorrow.org.  

 

EVENT SWAG:

-Short-sleeved cotton t-shirt for race registrants

-Shirt or cape for superhero dash registrants 

-Commemorative medal for race and dash finishers

-See's chocolate bar at the finish line compliments of Elk Grove Orthodontics

-Referral bonus for referring 5 or more registrants: embroidered logo canvas shopper tote 

-Age group awards for 5K

 

PACKET PICK UP: 

-Saturday May 17: 10-6pm (Fleet Feet, 2311 J Street)

-Race Day Sunday May 18, 7:15am Crocker Park

 

RACE DAY SCHEDULE:

7:15am Packet pick up and event day registration

8:15am: Superhero Kids Dash start

8:30am: 5K and one mile run/walk start

 

5K COURSE INFORMATION:

Start in front of Crocker Art Museum, along Riverfront Promenade through Old Sacramento, along river to Robert Matsui Water Park and back.

 

AWARDS FOR 5K:

Top male and female finisher in each age category will be recognized.  (12 and under, 13-17, 18-21, 22-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70-79, 80+). Awards may be picked up at the awards tent at the post-race venue. If you are unable to pick up your award on race day, please email ChocolateChase916@gmail.com. Awards will not be mailed. 

 

STROLLERS & DOGS:
Strollers are permitted in the race. We just ask that you and your bundle of joy start the race in the back of the pack. No scooters, bikes, skates, skateboards on the course. 

We love dogs, but only service dogs are allowed on the course.  All other dogs are not allowed to participate, but stop by the Cleft Pup Brigade rescue for your four-legged fix!

 

GETTING HERE: 

Crocker Park is located at 211 O Street in downtown Sacramento, steps from the Capitol Mall and the Riverfront Promenade.

-By Car: Parking is conveniently located at City Lot X at 2nd and N Street for $5.  The lot is accessible via 3rd Street, turning right onto N Street. (Follow parking signs.) -By Bicycle: Bike racks are located around the Crocker Art Museum's main entrance. 

-Public Transportation  Closest light rail stops are 7th Street & Capitol and 8th & K Street.  YoloBus 42B makes stops within walking distance at Capitol Mall & Front Street and Capitol Mall and 7th Street. Youth and students in grades TK-12 can ride Sac RT for free

name: Cinco De Mayo Run 5K/10K/13.1 LOS ANGELES
description:
🌶️🏃‍♂️ Run Against All Odds: Cinco de Mayo Run! 🌟

This Cinco de Mayo, challenge yourself and celebrate resilience, community, and culture with the Cinco de Mayo Run Against All Odds! Whether you’re running for fun or for fitness, this event is all about pushing limits and embracing the spirit of overcoming obstacles—just like the holiday itself! 

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)
Yes, but please note that it takes time for us to ship your shirt. Your shirt will likely arrive after the run. You can wear any shirt you find appropriate to run the race! 
 
Wave Times: (Email Us Your Desired Wave Time: info@thebestraces.com)
(Waves filled on a First Come, First Serve Basis)
Wave A: 7:30AM
Wave B: 8:00AM
Wave C: 8:30AM
Late runners can run upon arrival (Please note our coordinators stay 3 hours after the first wave)
Are there any other Questions we missed?
https://www.thebestraces.com/faq/
Virtual Run Option:
- Our Virtual Run uniquely offers a Training Pack with Digital Tools to support your run. 
Virtual runs can be done any time and place of your choosing using any tracking device (optional). After you finish, you can submit your results to info@thebestraces.com to receive your medal! 
Race Bundle:
Sign-up for more races and get a discount! 

Sponsorships & Promoting your Business:

If you're looking to become a sponsor, we'd love showcase your business!
https://www.thebestraces.com/events
 

Team Glo Volunteers:

Be part of the Journey!

Our Charity Initiatives. Find out more @ www.thebestracesjourney.com
Keep running. Every mile you log after the race, we'll donate $1 to one of the charities we work with! (Note that Fundraising is Optional)

name: CINCO DE MILE 5 QUE- FRESNO 5K
description:
Come and celebrate “5 de Mayo” at this UNIQUE EVENT! Join your fellow taco loving participants and run this SCENIC COURSE out and back along Woodward park. Course is on a bike paved trail and some dirt road/trail! As you cross the finish line, you will be greeted by a post-run FIESTA like none other!  MUSIC ENTERTAINMENT before, during, and after your run, followed by a FOLKLORICO DANCE demonstration. Whether running or supporting a runner, everyone is welcome to celebrate running, food, and community. For sure, a FUN event you don't want to miss! 

Our 5K is a 20-point CENTRAL VALLEY RUNNER OF THE YEAR event. 

All participants receive:

  • FREE TACOS for ALL participants!!
  • MEXICAN “AGUAS FRESCAS”
  • SHIRT  
  • UNIQUE MEDAL 
  • AGE GROUP UNIQUE AWARDS
  • EXTRA/ADDITIONAL MEDAL!!  Reyes Running Series! Collect all of them! 
  • 20 PT RUNNER OF THE YEAR SERIES EVENT (5 mile race)
  • DANCE ENTERTAINMENT (FOLKLORICO/ZUMBA)
  • ATHENA/CLYDESDALE AGE GROUP CATEGORIES
  • KIDS RACES INCLUDING A 10 METER "RUN" FOR KIDS UNDER 1 YEAR OLD
  • GREAT, RUNNING COURSE (WIDE OPEN, OUT AND BACK, DIRT TRAIL)
  • DJ, MUSIC, FUN!!

SPECIAL AWARDS FOR THE FOLLOWING: 

  • LATIN DANCE COMPETITION (Cumbia, salsa, merengue...)
  • BEST COSTUME COMPETITION  for 5 de Mayo!
  • CLYDESDALE (MEN- 225LBS)  AND ATHENA (WOMEN-185LBS) AGE GROUP CATEGORIES 

6:00PM    CINCO DE MILE 5 QUE RUN/WALK AND 2 MILE WALK 

5:45PM    KIDS RACES

                                        AWARDS

TOP 3 AGE GROUP CATEGORIES 5 QUE RUN AND ATHENA/CLYDESDALE GROUP CATEGORIES. NO AWARDS FOR 2 MILE WALK.   

                                        KIDS RACES!!!!

5:45PM- 400 meters (7–10-year-old)                   5:52PM-  50 meters (1–2-year-old) 

5:47PM- 200 meters (5-6 year-old)                       5:55PM-  10 meters (under 1 year-old)

5:49PM-  100 meters (3–4-year-old)

UNIQUE AWARDS FOR TOP 3  (BOYS/GIRS) ON EACH KIDS RACE!! ALL KIDS GET A SHIRT/MEDAL!!

Walking Registration & Packet Pickup:  THURSDAY, 04/30TH/25 (4:30-6:30 PM). FLEET FEET, Fresno. 

Race Day Registration & Packet Pickup:  FRIDAY, 05/01/25 (4:00-5:45 PM) GROUP ACTIVITY AREA

name: Citrus Heritage Run
description:
The Citrus Heritage Run is a Half Marathon, 10K, 5K, and 1-mile kids race on Saturday, January 10, 2026. This unique and “sweet-smelling” course winds through the historic orange groves of the California Citrus State Historic Park in Riverside, CA. As one of the most scenic course routes in Southern California, you will experience breathtaking views of surrounding mountain ranges and skyline as you inhale the smell of sweet citrus and orange blossoms beginning to bloom. This race is truly one-of-a-kind and all race distances sold out in 2025!

This event is a great tune-up race for 2026. We offer high-quality tech-fabric long-sleeve tees in men’s, women’s, and youth sizes, finisher medals, and age group awards. Along the course, you will find entertainment (live bands) and several hydration stops. At the finish line, you will be greeted with music by a live band and post-race refreshments which include freshly squeezed orange juice from a local orange grove, as well as warm food, a celebratory beer and hand-crafted mimosas! 

The Citrus Heritage Run is an experience you won’t want to miss!

name: City of Lincoln Huffin' for the Stuffin' Turkey Trot
description:
Welcome to the 8th annual Huffin' for the Stuffin' Turkey Trot presented by the City of Lincoln Recreation Department.

Our 5K run is LIVE with professional timers again this year as we continue our festive engagement with families and community. There is a .17 mile Donut Dash for children 4 to 7 years old to take part in as always. THE DONUT DASH HAS SOLD OUT as of 11/4/25

This event is a FUN RUN and meant for community engagement & family FUN! There will be 1st, 2nd & 3rd place finisher awards as well as general finisher award for participants who sign up before the deadline. The proceeds from our run helps to support the City of Lincoln Recreations Scholarship Fund which helps offer scholarships (financial aid) to cover fees for our recreation programs to families in need. 

Registration: Registration is now open thru November 24th 2025.  Please register by November 1st to receive a shirt and finisher award!

We do order extra shirts, they will be on a first come first served basis after the deadline. 

Race Schedule: Thursday, November 27th 7:45am arrival

RACE DAY
Plan to arrive no later than 7:45am in order to park and arrive at the starting area for announcements. The first announcements start promptly at 8:00am.

Refreshments provided for all registered participants following the race.

All 5K participants receive a unisex 50/50 cotton blend race shirt. Late registrants are not guaranteed choice of shirt or medal.

Register online by November 1, 2025 to guarantee your shirt size and finisher award!

                           Kids Donut Dash at 8:00am 

                           5K to start at 8:30am 

Route Information: Twelve Bridges Park and trail 5k route  Lincoln Turkey Trot 5K - 

https://www.mapmyrun.com/routes/view/6645991889/ 

Pre-Race Shirt Pick Up: Lincoln Community Center 2010 First Street Lincoln CA 95648

Tuesday, November 25th & Wednesday, November 26th 11am to 6pm.

Please plan to attend one of the Pickup days or have someone collect your shirt for you. Please register early to guarantee your shirt and finisher award! IF YOU ARE REGISTERED FOR THE DONUT DASH ONLY, YOU DO NOT NEED to COME TO THE PICK UP DATES. The pick up dates are mainly for the shirt/ bib pick up.

Refund Policy: All entries are non-refundable and non-transferable and are considered a donation to our recreation department (without purchase of race insurance)

name: Claremont Turkey Trot
description:
Welcome to the 18th annual Claremont Turkey Trot presented by Claremont Sunrise Rotary. With a new start/finish location at Claremont's Memorial Park, the scenic course winds its way through the tree-lined streets of the Claremont Colleges and the adjacent historic neighborhoods. A slight downhill grade on the last leg provides a welcome boost into the finish.

Approximate Start Times:
7:30AM    1K Kid's Fun Run
8:00AM    5K Run/Walk

Late registration and packet pickup will take place on Wednesday, November 26 from 4PM to 7PM at the Claremont Depot. Located at 200 W First Street, Claremont, CA 91711. Race day packet pickup begins at 6AM.

Everyone in the 1K Kids Fun Run receives a finishers medal and a race shirt. All participants in the 5K Run/Walk get a race shirt. Trophies are awarded to the top male and top female overall finishers. Gold, silver, and bronze medals are awarded to the top 3 male and top 3 female finishers in each age division. Age divisions are <10, 10-14, 15-19, 20-24, etc. Race shirt availability is not guaranteed for late registrations, so please register early!

name: Clueless & Breathless 5K, 10K & Half
description:
December 20, 2025 · 7:00 a.m. PST · 6846 Owensmouth Ave, Canoga Park, CA

Like, ugh, are you seriously going to miss this?
Step into your platform shoes and strut into the Clueless & Breathless 5K, 10K & Half—a 90s high school holiday run bursting with mall glam, holiday sparkle, and way too much lip gloss.

Presented by Jed & Ted’s Excellent Races

Whether you’re a Beverly Hills princess, a debate team queen, or just trying to burn off those holiday carbs, this race is your chance to be totally buggin’—in the best way.

  •  Clueless & Breathless 5K 🎀 This one's as quick as a shopping trip to The Galleria. Bonus if you run in plaid.
  • Totally Buggin’ 10K 💅 Longer than Cher's holiday gift list—and twice as fierce.
  • The Alaïa Half Marathon 👠 Because it's like, a totally important designer challenge. Don’t get mugged—stay hydrated.
  • The Multiverse Holiday Shopping Spree (Virtual) 🛍️ Run any distance, from anywhere—even the food court. Your medal ships post-haste.

Expect mallcore energy, glam cheer zones, 90s jams, and a sprinkle of holiday chaos.
Costumes strongly encouraged—extra credit for fur-trimmed Santa hats and feather pens.

 
📦 Multiverse Option (Virtual Runners Welcome!)
Run virtually anytime from Dec 20–22, and we’ll mail your medal faster than a boyfriend makeover montage.

This is a Jed & Ted’s Excellent Race—fun, fast, and full of nostalgia.

name: Coalinga Turkey Trot
description:
The inaugural Coalinga Turkey Trot is happening on Thanksgiving morning!
Trot your way through the 5K course or walk the 2K (1.2 miles) before you head home to feast. 
The event is family-friendly, so make sure to sign up your all of your kids, cousins, aunts and uncles! 
The event takes place rain or shine at the Coalinga-Huron Sports Complex on Cambridge Avenue.
Please NO PETS, but strollers are welcome. 
Each participant will receive a Turkey Trot t-shirt. 
Proceeds from the race will benefit the Coalinga Lions Club.

name: Coffee Lovers Run 5K/10K/13.1 LOS ANGELES
description:
☕️For all the Coffee Lovers, this run is for you!

You’ll love the shirt we send you. Set a goal, bring a friend, and join this super fun 5K/10K/13.1 Half-Marathon!

 

Overview:

Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.

This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:
We will email you a final update the Wednesday before the race with final details and course maps.
Do you accept last minute registrations? (For those signing up 2 weeks before the race)
Yes, but please note that it takes time for us to ship your shirt. Your shirt will likely arrive after the run. You can wear any shirt you find appropriate to run the race! 
 
Wave Times: (Email Us Your Desired Wave Time: info@thebestraces.com)
(Waves filled on a First Come, First Serve Basis)
Wave A: 7:30AM
Wave B: 8:00AM
Wave C: 8:30AM
Late runners can run upon arrival (Please note our coordinators stay 3 hours after the first wave)
Are there any other Questions we missed?
https://www.thebestraces.com/faq/
Virtual Run Option:
- Our Virtual Run uniquely offers a Training Pack with Digital Tools to support your run. 
Virtual runs can be done any time and place of your choosing using any tracking device (optional). After you finish, you can submit your results to info@thebestraces.com to receive your medal! 
Race Bundle:
Sign-up for more races and get a discount! 

Sponsorships & Promoting your Business:

If you're looking to become a sponsor, we'd love showcase your business!
https://www.thebestraces.com/events
 

Team Glo Volunteers:

If you're interested in helping put on runs for the Community and helping people achieve their goals, we invite you to join our team of volunteers, fill out the form here: https://www.thebestraces.com/volunteer-form/
 

Be part of the Journey!

Our Charity Initiatives. Find out more @ www.thebestracesjourney.com
Keep running. Every mile you log after the race, we'll donate $1 to one of the charities we work with! (Note that Fundraising is Optional)

name: College of the Canyons 17th Annual Turkey Trot
description:
A Santa Clarita annual tradition. Come join us for a calorie earning three-mile Turkey Trot. Beginning at College of the Canyons and winding through the campus and trails overlooking the Santa Clarita Valley. The course then has a fast downhill finish and onto the Cougar Stadium Track.

Live Results and scoreboard showing your finishing times completes the experience before you head off to get your fill of Turkey, fixins' and family to complete your day.

Your entry fee includes an original t-shirt design and finisher medals for the first 300 athletes crossing the finish line.

Free parking

name: Concord 5000
description: Concord High School Cross Country and Track & Field teams are excited to host this unique opportunity for our community. Have you been running 5k road races and are interested in running on the TRACK to get your true 5000 meter time with a professional timer? Then this race is for you. We will have a fun, festive atmosphere where you are cheered on by other runners. There will be music, a food truck, a custom shirt vendor and prizes for the top three finishers in each category, plus a special gift for the fastest couple of the night! (It is the day before Valentine's Day!) Proceeds will benefit Concord High School Cross Country and Track & Field programs. Concord High is a Title 1 school with over 50% low-income families, so profits will go toward race entry fees, team gear/uniforms, and individual shoes. Tell all your friends to join us under the lights on Friday, February 13th!

name: Concord California Turkey Trot 5K
description:
Diablo Valley Federal Credit Union (DVFCU) is pleased to welcome you to our information page about the Concord Turkey Trot, a 5K run/walk benefiting Loaves and Fishes of Contra Costa.

The event will take place at Newhall Park on Thanksgiving, Thursday, November 27, 2025, at 8 AM.  For the safety and enjoyment of all participants, registration for this event is capped at 1,850 participants.  Everyone participating in the 5K run/walk course must have a paid registration, with the exception of children 2 years old and under, who will be in a stroller for the duration of the event. 

The course includes varied terrain, including grass fields, park pathways, and city streets. Those participating with strollers or pets will be asked to enter at the back of the start area so as not to impede those wishing to race for time. All 5K Run/Walk Participants will receive a tech t-shirt and a medal!

The race will take place rain or shine.  Once your registration has been paid, there are no refunds. This includes inclement weather or any other reason, such as injuries or personal emergencies.

name: Conquer The Pier at Venice Beach 5K
description:
5K Venice Beach - Saturday, July 19th

Start and Finish in the same location

This is the only race that starts and finishes out over the water on the iconic Venice Beach Pier — with ocean views, salty air, and vibes for days.

name: Cookie Wonderland Decorating Day
description: Get ready to sprinkle, frost, and create delicious works of edible art at Cookie Wonderland Decorating Day. Kids will enjoy making festive masterpieces while the adults make a one of a kind holiday plate to display them on. Each family bundle includes 3 cookies to decorate and one plate to design.

name: Corona 5000
description:
From 1913-1916, the roar of engines and the thrill of speeds approaching 100 mph electrified Grand Boulevard in Corona, as up to 100,000 spectators cheered during the legendary Corona Road Races. This perfect circle in the heart of “Circle City” was the stage for automotive history. Now, 110 years later, Grand Boulevard is set to pulse with excitement once again!

Join us for the Inaugural Corona 5000, a vibrant 5K run and walk that revives the spirit of this historic course. Lace up your shoes and be part of a new legacy, racing or strolling the iconic loop of Grand Boulevard. 

This is a Race For the Ages, all ages. 

Don’t miss your chance to make history in Corona’s Circle City!

name: Coronado Turkey Trot presented by Rady Children’s Hospital Auxiliary
description:
MOVE YOUR FEET BEFORE THE FEAST!

Join us for the 12th Annual Turkey Trot presented by the Coronado Unit of the Rady Children’s Hospital Auxiliary on Thanksgiving, November 27, 2025, at Tidelands Park. This family-friendly 5K welcomes runners and walkers of all ages. Enjoy a beautiful course along the San Diego Bay and celebrate the holiday with a fun, festive atmosphere! For our 15 and under runners, your age-based pricing discount is already built in as soon as you enter your birth date.

All net proceeds benefit the Orthopedics and Scoliosis Center at Rady Children's Hospital-San Diego. Register early as this event sells out every year!

_________________________________________

We offer three ways to participate in the Coronado Turkey Trot, ensuring everyone—from seasoned runners to our tiniest trotters—can join the Thanksgiving fun:

5K Run/Walk: Our signature race welcomes runners and walkers of all ages. The 5K follows a scenic out-and-back route along the San Diego Bay and includes full race amenities, including an event shirt for paid 5K participants. Kids 15 and under automatically receive built-in age-based pricing at checkout.

Tiny Trotters Fun Run (Ages 5 & Under): A special option for our littlest runners! Tiny Trotters (ages 5 & under) run alongside the 5K with their families. It’s a simple, no-cost way to let young children be part of the excitement. Registration is free (no shirt included).

Virtual 5K: Not in Coronado on race day? You can still be part of the tradition from wherever you are! Virtual participants complete their 5K on their own time and course, and we’ll mail your race items directly to the address provided at registration. A great option for out-of-towners or anyone who prefers a flexible race experience.

 

Race Day Schedule


6:30am – Packet Pick-Up Opens

7:35am – Pre-Race Warm Up 

8:00am – 5K Start 

9:15am – Awards Ceremony (Overall Winners)

9:30am – Event Concludes

Subject to change

 

Packet Pick Up - Hours & Locations

 

Saturday November 22nd, 2025
Spreckels Park
601 Orange Ave, Coronado, CA 92118
10:00 AM – 2:00 PM

 

RACE DAY, November 27, 2025
Tidelands Park
2000 Mullinex Dr, Coronado, CA 92118
6:30 AM – 8:00 AM

 

Notes for Packet Pick-Up

Walk-up Registration is available at Packet Pick-Up if the event is not sold out. Photo IDs are required. You may pick up for a friend if you have a copy of their photo ID. NO EXCEPTIONS! Photos of ID shown on cell phones are accepted. Please plan on attending one of the pre-race packet pick-ups; out-of-towners may pick up on race morning beginning at 6:30am, but it is discouraged.

name: Corporal Javier Bejar Memorial Run     Reedley Police Department
description:
Join us as we honor the life and legacy of Corporal Javier Bejar, a Reedley Police Officer, Marine Corps veteran, and beloved member of our community who made the ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty.

This memorial run is more than a race—it’s a tribute to courage, service, and community. Every stride taken represents our gratitude for Corporal Bejar’s dedication and the enduring impact he left behind.

All participants will receive a commemorative race shirt and finisher’s medal, designed to celebrate his life and sacrifice. Whether you run, walk, or cheer from the sidelines, your presence helps keep his memory alive and supports the values he stood for: honor, commitment, and service.

Together, let’s run in remembrance and unity.

 

NOTE: Only the first 350 Runners are guaranteed a medal.

 

Packet Pickup & Schedule

Packet Pickup: Friday, February 20th from 3:00pm - 6:00pm

Reedley PD - Annex Building 843 G Street, Reedley, CA

Schedule:

Saturday, February 21st

6:00am Late Packet Pickup 

7:00am Ceremony

7:20am 6 Mile Walk Start

7:45am 2 Mile Walk & 10K Run Start

Event Schedule

Saturday
1:00-3:00pm – Early bib pick-up on the 2nd floor at Sports Basement Long Beach (store discount sent via email the week of the event)
2100 N Bellflower Blvd, Long Beach, CA 90815

Sunday
6:20am – Bib pick-up opens at the tables closest to Claremont Ave
7:00am – Half marathon & 10m start
7:30am – 5k & 10k start
7:35am – Registration & start line close

10m: The 5m route is used for the 10m (two laps) – 5m route

Bib: Please wear your race bib on the front of your shirt so we can track your time and send your pics!
Gear Check: You may leave personal items with staff at the registration tent. Please bring your own bag.

Results & Photos: An email with race results and photos will be sent the day after the race and earlier on Instagram. Race photos are free!

name: COVINA FUN RUN XXIX
description:
Join Us for the 2026 Covina Fun Run!
The Covina Rotary Club is proud to sponsor the 2026 Covina Fun Run at District Field Covina on April 25, 2026! In partnership with Covina-Valley Unified School District, Charter Oak Unified School District, and valued sponsors, our dedicated committee members are volunteering their time to create a fun, family-friendly, and health-conscious event that brings our community together.

How You Can Make a Difference
Since 1923, the Covina Rotary Club has been committed to serving and uplifting our community. Proceeds from this event directly support local youth programs, veterans, and other vital initiatives. Would you consider making a donation to help us achieve our mission? Every contribution—big or small—makes an impact, helping to fund teacher mini grants, youth programs, and other community-driven efforts.

Join Us!
Be part of something special—run, walk, sponsor, or donate to help make a lasting difference in Covina. Together, we can strengthen our schools, support our teachers, and promote health and wellness in our community.

Covina Rotary Charities is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.

name: Cycle Through the Vineyards 2025
description:
CYCLE THROUGH THE VINEYARDS 2025

 

Temecula Sunrise Rotary (a 501c3 nonprofit) is again celebrating Spring in the beautiful Temecula Valley Wine Country on Sunday April 27th with our annual CYCLE THROUGH THE VINEYARDS 2025! And for our past participants, 2025 brings exciting changes! For the first time AKASH Winery and Vineyards will be this year's host venue for the start/finish, post-ride celebration and raffle! And we are again excited to award a raffle grand prize drawing of an AVENTON E-BIKE from AVENTON BIKES! And our local AVENTON dealer Bicycle Warehouse of Temecula has upgraded the ebike and warranty coverage to bring the value of this ebike to over $2,500!  Secondly, this year we have added a shorter scenic guided tour route of 13 miles for our intermediate riders. While there is no way to totally avoid the challenges of the vineyards naturally hilly terrain, the shorter route is designed to better accomodate some of our intermediate level participants. 

 

AKASH Winery is a local family-owned winery nestled amongst the gentle vine covered rolling hills in the heart of Temecula Wine Country. They will be offering discounts on their wines (both flights and bottles), craft beer and food for our ride participants! We are confident that our riders and guests will find AKASH to be one of the most stunning vineyard settings in our Temecula Valley Wine Country to commence and conclude this year's guided scenic journeys and post-ride gathering. We are truly fortunate to have such a picturesque location for our Cycle Through the Vineyards this year.

name: DairyAire 5K and Fun Run
description:
Our 16th Annual DairyAire 5k is the last leg of the Chino Triple Crown! Flat and fast course around Ayala Park. Price includes shirt and finisher medal for all participants. Come and have a fun and healthy morning, all proceeds benefiting the Chino Youth Museum.

PLEASE READ: The 5K run/walk starts at 8:15 a.m. You are welcome to run with your friends or family.  Results will be posted as soon as you finish. The Kids' Run will precede the 5K at 8:00 a.m.

  • Flat and fast course at Ayala Park in Chino - 5575 Edison Ave., Chino, Ca 91710
  • The 5K is the last leg of the Chino Triple Crown - Triple Crown medals will be given out after the DairyAire 5K - FINISH the 2025 Reindeer Romp, the 2026 Run for Russ and the 2026 DairyAire 5k for your special medal!
  • All entrants in the 5k will receive an official event shirt and finisher medal.
  • Groups of 5 or more will receive a $5.00 discount per runner, paper applications only. (Please email us for an application)
  • Kids' Run is 1/2 mile long and every kid will receive a medal and shirt

ALL PROCEEDS BENEFIT THE CHINO YOUTH MUSEUM

5k Entry fee is $45 October 25 - March 2, $50 March 3 - March 7. 

Kids Fun Run Entry fee is $25 October 25 - March 2, $30 March 3 - March 7. 

Please contact the Carolyn Owens Community Center (COCC) at (909) 334-3258 for a paper application or questions. Group registration is available by paper application only. You may also email CYM@cityofchino.org for a paper application or group pricing. Groups of 5 or more receive a $5.00 discount per runner. ($40 per runner for the 5k through March 2nd, $45 March 3rd or after)

Packet pickup and late registration will be Friday, March 6, 4:00 p.m. - 6:00 p.m. at the park operations center, 5575 Edison Ave. Also Saturday morning before the race STARTING AT 7:00 a.m.

SORRY, NO REFUNDS! THANK YOU FOR YOUR DONATION!

 

** We love dogs, but please do not bring them to the DairyAire 5K! **

name: Davis Stampede
description:
The Davis Stampede takes place each year in February, and includes 5K, 10K and Half Marathon routes. We also offer a family friendly 2K (1.24 mile) fun run/walk division that is perfect for younger athletes, families, and pups. Starting and finishing at Davis’ Playfields Park, the Davis Stampede is a great way to kick off 2026 with a commitment to fitness. Courses are mostly flat and take runners and walkers through east and south Davis’s greenbelts and neighborhood streets. Race amenities include finisher’s medals, half marathon pace groups, t-shirts, a post-race expo, and course water stations stocked with water and electrolyte replacement along the course.

 

Registration will open on October 1, 2025

Please register early! The Half Marathon often sells out or comes close to it.

 

Start Times:

8:00 a.m. - Half Marathon and 10K
8:10 a.m. - 5K
9:00 a.m. - 2K 
last updated 9/2025; subject to change

Entry Includes:

Blend performance short sleeved t-shirt, finisher medal, chip timing, eligibility for division awards. Option to upgrade to a long sleeve technical (100% polyester) shirt for $8; available while supplies last. You also may opt out of the short sleeve t-shirt and save $5. 

Packet Pick Up:

You can pick up your packet (bib and shirt) on Saturday, February 21 from 1pm to 4pm at Playfields Park (race venue). We allow you to pick up for friends, and ID is not required.  You can also pick up on race day (Feb. 22) starting at 6:30 a.m. If picking up on race day, we suggest arriving at least one hour prior to your race start. We encourage all participants to have their QR code available on their phone for fast check-in. You can find this in your confirmation email. 

Safety pins will be available at registration. On race morning, please pin your race bib to the clothing on the FRONT of your body so that it is visible to timing officials, course monitors, and race photographers. 

Overall and Age Group Awards:

Overall awards will be presented to the top male, female and nonbinary finishers based on gun time. Age group awards will be determined by net time and will be awarded to the top three male, female, and nonbinary registrants per age group. Registrants may decline to state their gender and / or age, however, those entrants will not be eligible for age group or overall awards or results ranking in those categories.  Award pick up is available on race day; unclaimed awards are not mailed. Awards also presented to the top three finishers in each special division. See section below for more detailed information on age groups and special divisions. 

Participate Virtually:

Those who are unable to attend on event day or who would prefer to participate on their own schedule may register as a virtual participant. Virtual packets will be mailed on or about 2/25/26 and will include a bib, finisher medal for the division you designate upon entry, and t-shirt (if selected). Virtual participants are welcome to pick up their packets at the Saturday Packet Pick Up if preferred. The deadline to sign up as a Virtual Participant is Thursday, February 19. The last day to request a switch from an in-person division to the virtual division (in cases of injury, change of plans, illness, etc.) is February 21 at 11:59 pm and this may be done via email.  Virtual participants may upload their results online by following these steps: (1) search name in upper right-hand corner; (2) next to name, click 'edit time'; (3) input your finish time in the format of HH:MM:SS and provide other requested information. Times may be submitted from February 21 through March 22 (link will be available on Feb. 21), although you may complete your run/walk any time that works for you after time of registration. Submitting a time is optional and not required. There are no age group or overall awards for the virtual divisions.  

Half Marathon:


Half Marathon course cut-off time is 3.5 hours or 11:30 a.m. Those on a pace to finish after this time will be offered a ride back to the finish line.

Minimum age to participate in the Half Marathon is 15. Consideration will be made on a case by case basis for youth 14 and under to participate in the Half Marathon who are sufficiently trained; must be accompanied by an adult (who must be registered). Send your request to acopfoundation@gmail.com by February 12th.

Water/fluid stations will be located approximately every two miles and will offer water and electrolyte replacement. Please carry nutrition or salt with you should it be a part of your training/racing regimen. 

Strollers, Dogs, Wagons, and Wheels:

Wheelchair entrants may participate in all divisions. Racing wheelchairs should start at the front and coordinate with event official; pushed or casual wheelchair entrants should start toward the back. Pushed wheelchairs should start towards the back. Adaptive Divisions in the 5K, 10K, and Half Marathon.  Please note: half marathon has approximately 1/4 mile on crushed gravel by Barovetto Park plus about 1 mile on trail (service road around Wildhorse Golf Course). 5K or 10K entrants wishing to push a stroller MUST start toward the back of the pack at the starting line, no exceptions.  In the 2K, strollers, dogs, wagons (for children or dogs) and wheelchairs are permitted. Wagons must have seatbelts if children are inside them. Those with dogs or strollers should line up behind the runners who are participating without a dog/stroller. Dogs must be on a nonretractable leash, well behaved in crowds and around other dogs, and owners must clean up after their pet. It is not suggested that children under age 11 run unaccompanied in the 2K. 

Timing:

Because this even utilizes chip timing for all events, we remind participants that there is no need to crowd the start line when the race starts; your time does not start until you physically cross the mats at the starting line. All age group awards and results placements, except for the top overall finishers (i.e. first 3 per gender across the finish line), are determined by chip/net time.

Guides/Support Runners for Adaptive Entrants:

If you are a sighted guide for a visually impaired participant, or a support runner/walker for an entrant in an adaptive category, please do not enter the adaptive division. Support Runners (including sighted guides) must be registered for the event either as a standard paid entrant or as a support runner. To register for the support runner/walker category, select "Support Runner" choice at registration (end of list). Those registering as a support runner will not be eligible for age group awards nor be ranked by age.   In the case that support runners  wish to receive the full race experience (eligible for awards, ranked by age division, etc) in that case they should register for the distance they are going to run/walk (Half Marathon, 5K, etc) instead of as a Support Runner, but be sure to not enter an Adaptive Division. Email acopfoundation@gmail.com with any questions prior to registering.  

Notes:
- We suggest that support runners/walkers and guides wear high visibility clothing or a vest indicating that they are a guide or a support runner. However, it is not required. 
- Please do not register as a Support Runner if you do not already have an athlete you are paired with. At this time we do not have a matching program, but will post if there are adaptive entrants seeking support runners.
- Please email us at acopfoundation@gmail.com with any questions. 

Beneficiary 

The event will benefit Cancer Champions. Read more about their mission at https://cancerchampions.org.  

Volunteers

Volunteers are needed to help with a variety of tasks on race day, as well as at Packet Pick Up. Sign up on the volunteer tab. For more information about the opportunities we have available for interested volunteers, or to sign up as a group, please see the volunteer tab on our website here. 

Refund Policy & Race Rules:

Entries are non-refundable and non-transferable to other events in the case of illness, injury, or change of plans; event happens rain or shine. You must be registered for the distance for which you intend to participate.  We reserve the right to postpone, delay, reschedule, or cancel the event if unforeseen condition occur that would compromise the ability for the event to be held in a manner that is safe for athletes, volunteers, staff, law enforcement, and the community. Should the event be postponed, rescheduled, or canceled, refunds will NOT be offered. Read complete details here: https://runsignup.com/Race/28183/RefundPolicy

Strollers, Dogs, Wagons, and Wheels:

Wheelchair entrants may participate in all divisions. Racing wheelchairs should start at the front and coordinate with event official; pushed or casual wheelchair entrants should start toward the back. Pushed wheelchairs should start towards the back. Adaptive Divisions in the 5K, 10K, and Half Marathon.  Please note: half marathon has approximately 1/4 mile on crushed gravel by Barovetto Park plus about 1 mile on trail (service road around Wildhorse Golf Course). 5K or 10K entrants wishing to push a stroller MUST start toward the back of the pack at the starting line, no exceptions.  In the 2K, strollers, dogs, wagons (for children or dogs) and wheelchairs are permitted. Wagons must have seatbelts if children are inside them. Those with dogs or strollers should line up behind the runners who are participating without a dog/stroller. Dogs must be on a nonretractable leash, well behaved in crowds and around other dogs, and owners must clean up after their pet. It is not suggested that children under age 11 run unaccompanied in the 2K. 

Timing:

Because this even utilizes chip timing for all events, we remind participants that there is no need to crowd the start line when the race starts; your time does not start until you physically cross the mats at the starting line. All age group awards and results placements, except for the top overall finishers (i.e. first 3 per gender across the finish line), are determined by chip/net time.

Guides/Support Runners for Adaptive Entrants:

If you are a sighted guide for a visually impaired participant, or a support runner/walker for an entrant in an adaptive category, please do not enter the adaptive division. Support Runners (including sighted guides) must be registered for the event either as a standard paid entrant or as a support runner. To register for the support runner/walker category, select "Support Runner" choice at registration (end of list). Those registering as a support runner will not be eligible for age group awards nor be ranked by age.   In the case that support runners  wish to receive the full race experience (eligible for awards, ranked by age division, etc) in that case they should register for the distance they are going to run/walk (Half Marathon, 5K, etc) instead of as a Support Runner, but be sure to not enter an Adaptive Division. Email acopfoundation@gmail.com with any questions prior to registering.  

Notes:
- We suggest that support runners/walkers and guides wear high visibility clothing or a vest indicating that they are a guide or a support runner. However, it is not required. 
- Please do not register as a Support Runner if you do not already have an athlete you are paired with. At this time we do not have a matching program, but will post if there are adaptive entrants seeking support runners.
- Please email us at acopfoundation@gmail.com with any questions. 

Beneficiary 

The event will benefit Cancer Champions. Read more about their mission at https://cancerchampions.org.  

Volunteers

Volunteers are needed to help with a variety of tasks on race day, as well as at Packet Pick Up. Sign up on the volunteer tab. For more information about the opportunities we have available for interested volunteers, or to sign up as a group, please see the volunteer tab on our website here. 

Refund Policy & Race Rules:

Entries are non-refundable and non-transferable to other events in the case of illness, injury, or change of plans; event happens rain or shine. You must be registered for the distance for which you intend to participate.  We reserve the right to postpone, delay, reschedule, or cancel the event if unforeseen condition occur that would compromise the ability for the event to be held in a manner that is safe for athletes, volunteers, staff, law enforcement, and the community. Should the event be postponed, rescheduled, or canceled, refunds will NOT be offered. Read complete details here: https://runsignup.com/Race/28183/RefundPolicy

name: Day of The Dead 5K & 10k
description:
Event Location

  • Date & Time: Sunday, October 25, 2026
    Location: Wild Runners Fair Oaks, 10149 Fair Oaks Blvd, Fair Oaks, CA

Participant Packet Pick Up

  • Saturday, October 24, 2026, 10 am – 4 pm
  • Race Day, Sunday, October 25, 2026, 6:30am - 7:30 am
  • Location: Wild Runners Fair Oaks, 10149 Fair Oaks Blvd,  Fair Oaks Ca 95628

Race Day Schedule

  • 6:30 am - 7:30 am: Race day registration and packet pick up
  • 7:30 am: All final items dropped off for the La Ofrenda
  • 8:05 am - Kids Races begin
  • 8:20 am - Day of the Dead progression to starting line
  • 8:30 am - Day of the Dead 5k/10k race begins
  • 9:30 am - Awards ceremony and costume contest

Swag & Event

All participants receive:

  • Bib number, timing device and safety pins
  • Short-sleeved event shirt
  • Finisher medal
  • Coupon for one-free tamale for each participant*
  • Special offers from our sponsors

* Redeemable only at the post-event expo and festival on October 25, 2026. 

  • Family-Friendly Walk/Run Events: The Day of the Dead 5k has something for every generation to enjoy from a 5k for adults to our Kid Races. 
    Live Entertainment: Immerse yourself in Mexican tradition with live music and performances. With stilt walkers and live music, transport yourself to another time as we pay homage to the cultural heritage of our grandparents.
  • La Ofrenda: To honor loved ones who have passed, bring offerings, such as photographs, flowers, nostalgic items, and foods as we create a collective space of remembrance and gratitude.  All items should be placed on La Ofrenda by 7:30am in front of the Wild Runners store at 10149 Fair Oaks Blvd.
  • Antojitos Delights: Enjoy the flavors and culinary delights that our grandparents cherished. In addition to free home-made tamales for race participants, indulge in the food and delectable treats of Mexican heritage.
  • Post-Race Festival and Expo: Unwind and connect with fellow participants post race! Explore our Community Partner and vendor booths showcasing the latest in fitness, wellness, and recovery services.  

5k Course

The race kicks off with a 0.5-mile downhill through the charming Old Fair Oaks Village neighborhood and over the bridge. Following a 3.2-mile out-and-back path along the picturesque American River Trail towards Bannister Park, the course remains entirely on paved roads and trails, catering to participants of all abilities and those with strollers.  The race concludes with an approximate half-mile ascent back to the finish line.

Awards & Age Divisions

Awards ceremony to follow event at 9:30 a.m. for the 5k and costume contest. Prizes for overall male and female winners will be presented. Top three finishers in each age division will receive a special prize. Age-group winners pick up prizes at the Awards table.

Top boy and girl finishers in the 1/4 and 1/2 mile races will receive a special prize. All other kid finishers will receive medals.

Top 3 finishers in the male and female races will respectively receive: 

  • 1st Place: $100 gift card to Wild Runners
  • 2nd Place: $50 gift card to Wild Runners
  • 3rd Place: $25 gift card to Wild Runners

1st place finishers in each Age Group (5k Run) will receive a free pair of socks from our sponsor from OS1st:
12 & Under, 13-15, 16-18, 19-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65-69, 70-74, 75-79, 80+

Costume Contest:

  • 1st Place: $100 gift card to Wild Runners
  • 2nd Place: $50 gift card to Wild Runners
  • 3rd Place: $25 gift card to Wild Runners

Rules & Guidelines for all entrants*

  • Bib numbers must not be altered, should be worn on the front of the runner, and be visible.
  • No unregistered runners, walkers or pacers.
  • Wearing headphones is discouraged.
  • No bicycles.
  • Your pup is welcome to participate in the 5k race (always on leash and after signing a waiver).
  • Strollers are welcome.
  • Walkers/runners of all abilities and capabilities welcome. 
  • Shirts are not guaranteed for the late registration ( you can ask for previos year shirt)

* No refunds

name: DeadFish Endurance Swim 2025
description:
WELCOME MESSAGE

DeadFish is dedicated to inspiring joy through a healthy lifestyle, encouraging personal challenges, and building endurance.

We strive to create a global swimming community that unites diverse individuals — driven by compassion, connection, and a shared commitment to supporting children’s education and those in need.

Together, we swim not just for distance, but for purpose.

 

EVENT OVERVIEW

  1. Registration: Free to participate
  2. Categories:
    • 5KM Category: A motivating challenge for intermediate swimmers looking to test their stamina.
    • 10KM Category (DF Distance): The signature DeadFish distance — ideal for seasoned athletes seeking to push their endurance.
    • 15KM Category (Qualification Required): A demanding test of stamina for highly experienced swimmers.
    • 21.1KM Category (New for 2025): The ultimate endurance challenge — a true test of both body and spirit.
    •  
  3. Swim Dates: December 15 – 31, 2025
    Participants may choose any single day within this window to complete their swim.

     4. Location: Pool, lake, river, or ocean
         All swims must be completed in one continuous effort.

DONATION
Swim with purpose — every stroke makes a difference.

This year, our DeadFish community unites to raise funds for children in remote and flood-affected areas of Vietnam — those who need our love, care, and support the most.

We are still finalizing the distribution process, but one thing is certain:

100% of all funds raised will go directly toward helping children — providing essentials, education, and hope.
As the plan develops, updates will be shared on our official pages so everyone can see how your kindness is making an impact.

 

SPONSORS AND DONORS

We welcome sponsors and donors from around the world to join hands with us. Your support helps us create a more meaningful experience for swimmers and a brighter future for children in need. We are seeking sponsors and donors who can:

  1. Support us in providing finisher shirts or swim caps for participants.
  2. Contribute donations to help children in remote areas of Vietnam access better living conditions and education.

 

PARTICIPANTS WILL RECEIVE

  1. An E-Bib will display your name and Bib Number.
  2. E-certificates will be provided upon successful completion
  3. Keep an eye out for additional offerings from our sponsors!


GUIDELINES AND REGULATIONS FOR PARTICIPANTS

 

EVENT REGULATIONS 

  1. Each individual participant must complete the challenge in one uninterrupted attempt.
  2. Participants are allowed to register for only one category (5km, 10km, or 15km).
  3. Swim gear: Fins and paddles are optional but not advisable if you want to push your limits.
  4. Wetsuits are advised when the temperature is below 76 degrees, whether for pool swimming or open water swim.
  5. Use a bright buoy when swimming in open water swim.  
  6. All participants must sign a consent waiver and swim at their own risk.
  7. Young aquatic athletes (ages 14 and under) must submit consent waiver forms signed by their parents or guardians.
  8. Adhering to your category's designated distance promotes fairness and maintains a competitive spirit.
  9. For safety reasons, please check in via Runsignup or inform the organizer or your club leader to confirm the swimming schedule before starting.


CUT-OFFS, EVENT FINISH, TIMING, AND RESULT 

EVENT CUT-OFFS

The cut-off times will be based on elapsed time (the amount of time that has passed between the start and end). Results calculated based on moving time.

  • 5KM Category: Cut-off Time: 3.5 hours from the moment you enter the water.
  • 10KM Category (DF Distance): Cut-off Time: 7 hours from the moment you enter the water.
  • 15KM Category: Cut-off Time: 10.5 hours from the moment you enter the water.
  •  21.1KM Category: Cut-off Time: 15 hours from the moment you enter the water.

 

THE IMPORTANCE OF CUT-OFF TIMES IN SWIMMING EVENT

Cut-off times in swimming events serve several vital functions that enhance both the efficiency and safety of athletes.

  • Firstly, they ensure that all athletes can finish their races within a specified timeframe, facilitating a well-organized schedule.
  • Secondly, cut-off times are crucial for the safety of swimmers, especially in longer distances and Open Water Swims, as they help prevent exhaustion and potential risks in the water.
    Additionally, they enable club leaders to manage the event effectively, ensuring accurate timing and results without unnecessary delays.

EVENT FINISH, TIMING

  1. Did not start (“DNS”) – Register but fails to start;
  2. Did not finish (“DNF”) – Starts an Event but did not finish the swim
  3. Not classified (“NC”) – Starts to swim and finished the swim but  fails to meet cut-off time.
     

RESULT

  1. Results will be accepted from December 15, 2024, until January 2, 2025 (the challenge concludes on December 31, 2024).
  2. Ensure that your results are made public on Strava.
  3. Join the Strava DeadFish group (details to be provided).
  4. Your results will be verified by your team leaders before being submitted to RunSignUp.
  5. If you are not part of a team, please submit your results directly to RunSignUp, and the organizer will handle the approval.
  6. To submit your results: Go to your RunSignup profile by clicking the Profile Icon in the top right corner.
    Under Upcoming Events, select Submit Virtual Results, enter your time, and click Submit Time.

SOCIAL MEDIA LINKS

  1. RunSignup (signup) : https://runsignup.com/deadfish
  2. Strava (results) : To be updated
  3. WhatsApp (questions) : To be updated
  4. FacebookGroup : www.facebook.com/groups/882487679711867
  5. Twitter: https://x.com/DeadFishSwim
  6. Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/deadfish_swim/
  7. LinkedI: To be updated
  8. DeadFish Website: To be updated

TRAINING TIPS FOR EACH DISTANCE
This guide is designed to help you prepare for your chosen distance (5K, 10K, or 15K) and ensure you have a safe and successful swim. Whether you're a first-timer or an experienced athlete, these tips will help you maximize your performance and enjoy the event.

  1. 5KM Category:
    Focus on building a steady pace and mastering breathing techniques.
    Aim for 3-4 swim sessions a week, incorporating intervals and long-distance swims.
    Include strength training and flexibility exercises for balance and injury prevention.
  2. 10KM Category:
    Incorporate endurance-based workouts, focusing on consistency over long distances.
    Train in open water if possible to adapt to conditions.
    Focus on nutrition and hydration during long swims.
  3. 15K Category:
    Build up stamina gradually over months; plan for a mix of long, steady swims and interval training.
    Nutrition strategy becomes crucial—practice fueling during training to maintain energy
    Open-water acclimatization is key, so make sure to practice sighting and adjusting to conditions.
  4. 21.1K Category:The ultramarathon of swimming — symbolizing spirit, discipline, and compassion. Only for those ready to go beyond limits.

 

EVENT DAY CHECKLIST

What to Bring:

  1. Swim suit
  2. Wetsuit (if needed, depending on water temperature) 
  3. Goggles
  4. Anti-fog Spray
  5. Swim cap
  6. Garmin watch
  7. Gear: Paddle and fin
  8. Open Water Swimming: Buoy
  9. In the swimming pool: Abacus, stones, or paper and pen for tracking laps
  10. Nutrition: Gels and electrolyte drinks
  11. Vaseline
  12. Towel and dry clothing for after the race
  13. Sunscreen
  14. Any other essential personal items
  15. Emergency phone number

Pre-Swim Warm-Up:

  1. Arrive early to get comfortable with the venue.
  2. Perform a light dynamic warm-up and stretch to loosen muscles.
  3. Familiarize yourself with the course and any key markers.

 SAFETY GUIDELINES

  1. Carefully review the schedule and plan your swim accordingly.
  2. Adhere to the established safety protocols for the event.
  3. If participating in open water swims, make sure to check the tide table.
  4. Always swim with a partner; never swim alone, as having someone with you improves safety in emergencies.
  5. Stay aware of your surroundings and environmental factors, such as currents and water temperature.
  6. Swim in sync with the group.
  7. If you start to feel fatigued or unwell at any time, please signal a safety boat for help if you're in open water, or simply stop swimming if you're in the pool.
    Remember, safety always comes first.

MENTAL PREPARATION

  1. Divide the swim into manageable segments, particularly for the 10K and 15K distances.
  2. Visualize your swim and create a strategy to address potential challenges, such as pacing, rough waters, or fatigue.
  3. Maintain your focus and confidence—your training has equipped you for this!
  4. In the pool, practice sets like (100 x 100) or (150 x 100), taking a break after every 10 sets or so. 

POST-SWIM RECOVERY

  1. Gradually cool down with a gentle swim or stretching to aid muscle recovery.
  2. Rehydrate and replenish with a snack rich in carbohydrates and protein.
  3. Take time to rest and let your body recover from the intense effort.
  4. CELEBRATE - share pictures on social media. You’ve earned the right to brag because you are now a Deadfisher.

 

Q & A

  1. Can I switch my club?
  2. Can I switch my race event (for example, from 10KM to 15KM)?
  3. Is it possible to change my name?
  4. Am I allowed to forgo wearing a watch?
  5. Since I don't own a watch, what alternatives can I use?
  6. What is the process for submitting my results?
  7. If I haven't completed 10km, can I still register for the 15km event?
  8. Will I receive a finisher shirt after the event?
  9. Is it permissible to divide the swim into different segments?
  10. Where can I seek assistance if I experience difficulties during the open water swim?
  11. Am I required to make a donation?
  12. Can I change my bib number?

DONATION
Swim with purpose — every stroke makes a difference.

This year, our DeadFish community unites to raise funds for children in remote and flood-affected areas of Vietnam — those who need our love, care, and support the most.

We are still finalizing the distribution process, but one thing is certain:

100% of all funds raised will go directly toward helping children — providing essentials, education, and hope.
As the plan develops, updates will be shared on our official pages so everyone can see how your kindness is making an impact.

 

SPONSORS AND DONORS

We welcome sponsors and donors from around the world to join hands with us. Your support helps us create a more meaningful experience for swimmers and a brighter future for children in need. We are seeking sponsors and donors who can:

  1. Support us in providing finisher shirts or swim caps for participants.
  2. Contribute donations to help children in remote areas of Vietnam access better living conditions and education.

 

PARTICIPANTS WILL RECEIVE

  1. An E-Bib will display your name and Bib Number.
  2. E-certificates will be provided upon successful completion
  3. Keep an eye out for additional offerings from our sponsors!


GUIDELINES AND REGULATIONS FOR PARTICIPANTS

 

EVENT REGULATIONS 

  1. Each individual participant must complete the challenge in one uninterrupted attempt.
  2. Participants are allowed to register for only one category (5km, 10km, or 15km).
  3. Swim gear: Fins and paddles are optional but not advisable if you want to push your limits.
  4. Wetsuits are advised when the temperature is below 76 degrees, whether for pool swimming or open water swim.
  5. Use a bright buoy when swimming in open water swim.  
  6. All participants must sign a consent waiver and swim at their own risk.
  7. Young aquatic athletes (ages 14 and under) must submit consent waiver forms signed by their parents or guardians.
  8. Adhering to your category's designated distance promotes fairness and maintains a competitive spirit.
  9. For safety reasons, please check in via Runsignup or inform the organizer or your club leader to confirm the swimming schedule before starting.


CUT-OFFS, EVENT FINISH, TIMING, AND RESULT 

EVENT CUT-OFFS

The cut-off times will be based on elapsed time (the amount of time that has passed between the start and end). Results calculated based on moving time.

  • 5KM Category: Cut-off Time: 3.5 hours from the moment you enter the water.
  • 10KM Category (DF Distance): Cut-off Time: 7 hours from the moment you enter the water.

  •  21.1KM Category: Cut-off Time: 15 hours from the moment you enter the water.

 

THE IMPORTANCE OF CUT-OFF TIMES IN SWIMMING EVENT

Cut-off times in swimming events serve several vital functions that enhance both the efficiency and safety of athletes.

  • Firstly, they ensure that all athletes can finish their races within a specified timeframe, facilitating a well-organized schedule.
  • Secondly, cut-off times are crucial for the safety of swimmers, especially in longer distances and Open Water Swims, as they help prevent exhaustion and potential risks in the water.
    Additionally, they enable club leaders to manage the event effectively, ensuring accurate timing and results without unnecessary delays.

EVENT FINISH, TIMING

  1. Did not start (“DNS”) – Register but fails to start;
  2. Did not finish (“DNF”) – Starts an Event but did not finish the swim
  3. Not classified (“NC”) – Starts to swim and finished the swim but  fails to meet cut-off time.

TRAINING TIPS FOR EACH DISTANCE
This guide is designed to help you prepare for your chosen distance (5K, 10K, or 15K) and ensure you have a safe and successful swim. Whether you're a first-timer or an experienced athlete, these tips will help you maximize your performance and enjoy the event.

  1. 5KM Category:
    Focus on building a steady pace and mastering breathing techniques.
    Aim for 3-4 swim sessions a week, incorporating intervals and long-distance swims.
    Include strength training and flexibility exercises for balance and injury prevention.
  2. 10KM Category:
    Incorporate endurance-based workouts, focusing on consistency over long distances.
    Train in open water if possible to adapt to conditions.
    Focus on nutrition and hydration during long swims.
  3. 15K Category:
    Build up stamina gradually over months; plan for a mix of long, steady swims and interval training.
    Nutrition strategy becomes crucial—practice fueling during training to maintain energy
    Open-water acclimatization is key, so make sure to practice sighting and adjusting to conditions.
  4. 21.1K Category:The ultramarathon of swimming — symbolizing spirit, discipline, and compassion. Only for those ready to go beyond limits.

 

EVENT DAY CHECKLIST

What to Bring:

  1. Swim suit
  2. Wetsuit (if needed, depending on water temperature) 
  3. Goggles
  4. Anti-fog Spray
  5. Swim cap
  6. Garmin watch
  7. Gear: Paddle and fin
  8. Open Water Swimming: Buoy
  9. In the swimming pool: Abacus, stones, or paper and pen for tracking laps
  10. Nutrition: Gels and electrolyte drinks
  11. Vaseline
  12. Towel and dry clothing for after the race
  13. Sunscreen
  14. Any other essential personal items
  15. Emergency phone number

Pre-Swim Warm-Up:

  1. Arrive early to get comfortable with the venue.
  2. Perform a light dynamic warm-up and stretch to loosen muscles.
  3. Familiarize yourself with the course and any key markers.

 SAFETY GUIDELINES

  1. Carefully review the schedule and plan your swim accordingly.
  2. Adhere to the established safety protocols for the event.
  3. If participating in open water swims, make sure to check the tide table.
  4. Always swim with a partner; never swim alone, as having someone with you improves safety in emergencies.
  5. Stay aware of your surroundings and environmental factors, such as currents and water temperature.
  6. Swim in sync with the group.
  7. If you start to feel fatigued or unwell at any time, please signal a safety boat for help if you're in open water, or simply stop swimming if you're in the pool.
    Remember, safety always comes first.

MENTAL PREPARATION

  1. Divide the swim into manageable segments, particularly for the 10K and 15K distances.
  2. Visualize your swim and create a strategy to address potential challenges, such as pacing, rough waters, or fatigue.
  3. Maintain your focus and confidence—your training has equipped you for this!
  4. In the pool, practice sets like (100 x 100) or (150 x 100), taking a break after every 10 sets or so. 

POST-SWIM RECOVERY

  1. Gradually cool down with a gentle swim or stretching to aid muscle recovery.
  2. Rehydrate and replenish with a snack rich in carbohydrates and protein.
  3. Take time to rest and let your body recover from the intense effort.
  4. CELEBRATE - share pictures on social media. You’ve earned the right to brag because you are now a Deadfisher.

 

Q & A

  1. Can I switch my club?
  2. Can I switch my race event (for example, from 10KM to 15KM)?
  3. Is it possible to change my name?
  4. Am I allowed to forgo wearing a watch?
  5. Since I don't own a watch, what alternatives can I use?
  6. What is the process for submitting my results?
  7. If I haven't completed 10km, can I still register for the 15km event?
  8. Will I receive a finisher shirt after the event?
  9. Is it permissible to divide the swim into different segments?
  10. Where can I seek assistance if I experience difficulties during the open water swim?
  11. Am I required to make a donation?
  12. Can I change my bib number?
  13. How do I register?

Welcome to your incredible team!
The Deadfish team wishes you the best of luck! We encourage you to push your limits and achieve your personal goals in the 5K, 10K, or 15K, 21KM challenge. We believe you’ve got what it takes to accomplish something remarkable!

name: Desert Orienteering Festival
description:
Please consider volunteering. All volunteers will receive an email with a $50 coupon toward registration per slot. 

REMINDER: DOF26 will not be offering OUSA categories. Run any race you want! 

***************************************************************************************************************

Saturday, Jan 17th

The Adventure Trek

12pm Mass Start

The festival kicks off with a 2-hour score orienteering Adventure Trek, where both experienced and beginner participants can chart their own path through the desert.

This year’s challenge takes place in the vast flatlands northeast of Buttes Pass, where navigational precision and overland speed will be the keys to victory.

Course Setter: Chris Day

 

Sunday, Jan 18th

The Classic

Starts 10am-11:30am

Measure your fitness and navigation skills against the best in a traditional 7-course classic orienteering competition that will span both technical and fast terrain.

Beginners can stick to the basic White course or use their newly built skills to take on the Yellow or Orange competitions.

Course Setter:  Matej Sebo

 

The Night Goat

5pm Mass Start

Are you ready to take on the desert at night? ​

This modified format will extend our Goat (8-10km), Borrego (4-5km), and Beginner mass start tradition, but with a dusk start time. Following is encouraged, but as night settles and the group splinters, you might face the dark desert alone to complete this point-to-point course. Beginners who want just a taste of the night can opt for a lighted guide.

Course Setter:  Mark Prior

 

Monday, Jan 19th

The Maze Middle

Starts 9am-11am

Navigate the slot canyons and steep slopes of the iconic "Maze" in a middle distance 7-course point to point competition. The distances will be short, but the complexity high, with numerous route options and physical challenges between controls in this three-dimensional wonderland.

Beginners will thrill to exposed ridges and memorable vistas while following a more straight-forward route. 

Course Setter: Julien Ouellet

Navigate the slot canyons and steep slopes of the iconic "Maze" in a middle distance 7-course point to point competition. The distances will be short, but the complexity high, with numerous route options and physical challenges between controls in this three-dimensional wonderland.

Beginners will thrill to exposed ridges and memorable vistas while following a more straight-forward route. 

Course Setter: Julien Ouellet

description:

Saturday, Jan 17th

The Adventure Trek

12pm Mass Start

The festival kicks off with a 2-hour score orienteering Adventure Trek, where both experienced and beginner participants can chart their own path through the desert.

This year’s challenge takes place in the vast flatlands northeast of Buttes Pass, where navigational precision and overland speed will be the keys to victory.

Course Setter: Chris Day

 

Sunday, Jan 18th

The Classic

Starts 10am-11:30am

Measure your fitness and navigation skills against the best in a traditional 7-course classic orienteering competition that will span both technical and fast terrain.

Beginners can stick to the basic White course or use their newly built skills to take on the Yellow or Orange competitions.

Course Setter:  Matej Sebo

 

The Night Goat

Are you ready to take on the desert at night? ​

This modified format will extend our Goat (8-10km), Borrego (4-5km), and Beginner mass start tradition, but with a dusk start time. Following is encouraged, but as night settles and the group splinters, you might face the dark desert alone to complete this point-to-point course. Beginners who want just a taste of the night can opt for a lighted guide.

name: Desi Strong Run/Walk 4 Kids
description:
The Run/Walk 4 Kids is a fun filled, family and pet friendly event. Admission into the event is free with a minimal donation requested to participate in the 5K. The Family Bubble Run will kick off immediately after completion of the 5K.

Why We Walk - Until we achieve a cure, our efforts will ensure these families receive the comfort, relief, support and fun to help them in the ultimate fight against these diseases. Please join our foundations in the fight to CURE Pediatric Cancer and other serious illnesses.

The Desi Strong Foundation is geared to help children facing cancer feel that love & support that Desi was so graciously granted. Together we will fight this beast called Childhood Cancer & help fund for a cure.

We can’t all be doctors or cancer researchers or caregivers but walking with us can raise the money that makes their work possible. And in the meantime, help children and their families feel the love while they fight these horrible diseases.

There are various levels of sponsorship available for the 5K and Kids Fun Run. As you will see, each sponsor will be highly visible in many aspects of the event. We hope that you will consider sponsoring our race.

name: Dia De Los Reyes Magos Half Marathon & 5k - Bakersfield
description:
"Dia de los Reyes Magos" or 3 wise men day is a very important Mexican celebration! On January 6th, kids are expected to receive presents from the "Reyes Magos" and families get together to share the "Rosca de Reyes" or sweet bread and drink some hot chocolate! This "Rosca de Reyes" bread contains inside several baby Jesus. It's the tradition that whoever gets the baby Jesus is expected to bring tamales and hot chocolate on February 2nd! Join us at this celebration for a morning of family fun at the Dia De Los Reyes Magos Half Marathon and 5k.
