name: Dirty 30 XL - GRAVEL MEETS MTB
description:
Twice the Grit, Double the Glory – Tackle the Dirty 30 XL on a Drop Bar bike or Mountain Bike at Lake Hodges! Choose your challenge: one lap or two of scenic single-track, rugged fire roads, and relentless climbs — all packed into a thrilling figure-8 course layout built for both drop bar (gravel bike) and mountain bikes. Starting and finishing at Lake Hodge main parking lot offers easy access to trailheads and beautiful support areas and don’t  forget great community building! Riders will reconvene at a central aid station at the staging area after each lap — a great opportunity to refuel, regroup, and soak in the atmosphere before heading out again. The course design is configured as a figure 8, great spectating and easy to re-fuel. Hammer Nutrition Feed station is 1 and 2 at Sunset (just under the HWY 15) @mile 3.6 and 17.

WHEN:

  • December 6, 2025


WHERE:

  • Lake Hodges Boat Ramp20175 Lake Drive, Escondido
  • This address takes you to the gate of the parking lot. Proceed through the gate and follow the road to the boat ramp parking lot

SCHEDULE:

  • Registration/Check-In: 6:30am
  • Course Open for Pre-Riding: 6:30am
  • Race Start: 8:00am

COURSE:

  • Diverse trail types: Expect a seamless mix of hard-packed gravel, smooth and rolling fire roads, punchy climbs, and technical singletrack — all hugging the scenic north shore of Lake Hodges .
  • Flow and challenge: The route weaves through connecting areas like Raptor Ridge and Highland Valley Trail, offering both flowy descents and test-your-metals climbs. Lake view trails may also be incorporated for extra elevation and epic views.
  • Distance per lap: 30 miles
  • Elevation gain: Approx. 1,750 feet per lap (3,500 feet total for the 60-mile option)
  • Route style: Figure 8 loop — riders pass through the main venue at mile 21 just over the halfway point of each lap.
    30‑miles Lap - RideWithGPS

name: Dirty 30 XL - GRAVEL MEETS MTB
description:
Twice the Grit, Double the Glory – Tackle the Dirty 30 XL on a Drop Bar bike or Mountain Bike at Lake Hodges! Choose your challenge: one lap or two of scenic single-track, rugged fire roads, and relentless climbs — all packed into a thrilling figure-8 course layout built for both drop bar (gravel bike) and mountain bikes. Starting and finishing at Lake Hodge main parking lot offers easy access to trailheads and beautiful support areas and don’t  forget great community building! Riders will reconvene at a central aid station at the staging area after each lap — a great opportunity to refuel, regroup, and soak in the atmosphere before heading out again. The course design is configured as a figure 8, great spectating and easy to re-fuel. Hammer Nutrition Feed station is 1 and 2 at Sunset (just under the HWY 15) @mile 3.6 and 17.

name: Do It For Her 5K
description:
Run through Temecula’s Wine Country and enjoy the tranquil beauty of rolling vineyards and sun-drenched hills. As you run along the winding paths, the early morning light casts a golden hue over the landscape, highlighting the neat rows of grapevines and the rustic charm of the wineries scattered throughout the valley. Finish with a Vitagliano sangria made from some of the finest Super Tuscan-style wines produced in California.  Shop our local vendors carrying locally grown produce and handcrafted items, all under a beautiful covered patio.  Food Available for purchase.


All proceeds benefit the Heather Janikowski Foundation and the Make A Wish Foundation

name: Don Osborne Memorial Run
description:
Welcome to the 34th Annual Don Osborne Memorial Run hosted by the Oakdale Lions Club!

This event will happen rain or shine. Light snacks, fruit, juice, and water will be available for all participants.

  • What: 5k Run and 1 Mile Run/Walk on the flat, paved city streets with traffic control
  • Where: Williams Meyers Park (G Street and South Second Avenue) behind the Oakdale Library
  • When: Saturday, February 7th, 2026
    • 8:00am - 9:15am | Race day registration and packet pickup
    • 9:00am | 1 Mile Run/Walk start
    • 9:30am | 5k Run start
    • 10:15am | Awards Ceremony

    ***Please note that registration fees will need to called into Alan Graham after January 26th. Contact information is below.

    Mail your entry to the following address:
        Oakdale Lion's Club
        P.O. Box 550
        Oakdale, California 95361

 

Awards: Gift certificates will be awarded to overall male and female winners in 1 Mile and 5k races. Medals will be awarded for top 3 finishers in each division in the 1 Mile and 5k races.

name: Dream Big 5k
description:
Join us for a day of fun and fitness at the third annual Dream Big 5k, proudly presented by the Kiwanis Club of Victorville. Whether you’re a seasoned runner or just looking for a fun walk with friends and family, this event promises an enjoyable experience for participants of all levels.

The race takes you through the scenic paths of Victor Valley College, located at 18422 Bear Valley Rd, Victorville, CA, starting bright and early at 8:00 am on Saturday, August 22. But the fun doesn't end at the finish line! Stick around for a variety of race day activities, including local vendors, lively music, and more. Every stride you take helps us support students in the Victor Valley, driving the change we wish to see in our community. Grab your running shoes, and let’s make dreams come true together at the Dream Big 5k!

After the main Dream Big 5K, stick around for even more fun—our Dream Big Mini K for children ages 12 and under! Held at Victor Valley College, this in-person event is all about encouraging kids to get active, dream big, and feel proud of their accomplishments. It’s a joyful, high-energy experience where little ones can cross the finish line to the cheers of friends and family.

The first 50 registered participants of the Mini K will receive a special finisher medal—so don’t wait to sign up! Let’s make it a day to remember filled with smiles, movement, and celebration. Come cheer them on and help create a lasting memory at the Dream Big Mini K!

name: Elevate 5k & 12 Hour Race at First Baptist Church
description:
Please visit www.ElevateRace.com for the most up to date and detailed information.
Thank you for your interest in participating in our 8th annual Elevate race!

  • What: 5k & 12 hour race
  • Purpose: To support our Elevate missions project
  • When: 5k starts Sat, Feb 14, 2026 @ 9:30am / 12 hour race starts Fri, Feb 13, 2026 @ 8:45pm
  • Where: First Baptist Church campus in Santa Maria, CA
  • Cost:
    • 5k = $22
    • 12 Hour = $45 (This is a bargain! The average price for 12 hour races here in CA is $155.)


All the proceeds from this event will go to support the Elevate missions project. Your participation as either a runner or volunteer will help make it possible!

5k: For only $22 you can challenge yourself to complete the 5k (3.1 miles) race. Awards will be given to the winners in both distances for the different age groups at the 10:30am awards ceremony. While this is a competition, everyone is invited to participate regardless of age or physical ability. It will be a lively and encouraging environment which will be fun for both first timers and experienced runners. Runners must arrive by 8:45 on race morning to receive their race bib and all final instructions before the race begins at 9:30am.  The 5k awards ceremony will take place at 10:30am.

12 Hour race: I know we have some adventurous people out there! How far do you think you could run and walk in 12 hours? The race runs from Friday night at 8:45pm until Saturday morning at 8:45am. It will finish 45 minutes before the start of the 5k. This is a great time to test yourself physically and mentally. Would you like to complete your first marathon? In 12 hours you could even walk a marathon if you could finish each mile in just under 28 minutes.

Here's some good news. We'll have some food and drinks to fuel you through the night, and you can take breaks as often as you'd like. Each lap is 1 mile, and near the start/finish line we'll have an area set up specifically for the 12 hour participants. You're encouraged to bring a comfortable chair, footrest, change of clothes, blankets and anything else that can help make your experience more comfortable. Napping is permitted but not encouraged. Friends and family members are invited to spend the evening there with us supporting and encouraging the participants. There is no minimum number of miles you have to complete. Yes, the person that completes the most loops is the winner, but runners and walkers of all levels are encouraged to set an individual goal and see what they're capable of doing. Races like this are typically very relaxed. Very few people would run the entire time in a race of this distance. Going through the night also provides a unique experience. There will be a variety of awards for the 12 hour race & the 12 hour race awards ceremony will take place at 8:45am right when the race finishes.

As a bonus (or maybe more like a penalty), all 12 Hour participants can also participate in the 5k for free if desired! 12 Hour runners must arrive by 8:00pm Friday evening to receive their race bib and all final instructions before the race begins at 8:45pm.

Course info: Each loop is 1.036 miles for the 5k. The 5k is three loops. For the 12 Hour race there is a minor adjustment to make each loop 1 mile. The loop is entirely on the First Baptist / VCA campus, and during the 5k there will be volunteers throughout the course in order to provide a safe environment for young runners. 12 Hour runners will need to have either a headlamp or flashlight to use on the back portion of the loop where there are no lights.

For the 5k we will have water, Gatorade and bananas during the race and celebratory ice cream sandwiches at the end for all finishers. The 12 Hour participants will have a variety of hot and cold drinks and solid foods to choose from. We hope you have a great time training for and participating in this race!

Please visit www.ElevateRace.com for the most up to date and detailed information.

name: Ellevate Foundation 5K
description:
Beginning Thursday November 27th through Sunday November 30th, join us by completing 3.1 miles from wherever you are!
You can do this by running, jogging, walking, skipping, rolling!

Log your miles on an app like Strava or whatever tracking device you use. 
This is not necessary but fun to show your friends and family what you accomplished.

Ellevate Foundation is a 501c3 nonprofit formed in 2023 for the purpose of elevating women by providing tools and resources to grow personally and professionally, and provide grants to attend professional development events. Our goal for 2025-2026 is to raise enough money through our annual Women's Leadership Summit (WLS), donors and fundraising events like this, to not only fund our annual summit but to fulfill our mission of sending at least 2 women to a national professional development event.

Join us between November 27 - November 30 for second annual virtual 5k.

All profits go to Ellevate Foundation's mission.

name: Ely Mountain Trail Race
description:
Ely Mountain Trail Race – Shaver Lake, CA

14K (8.7mi) + 8K (4.9mi) | Balsam Forebay | Cooler temps. Hot trails.


We’re stoked to bring a brand new adventure to the San Joaquin Running Co lineup — and this one’s a beauty. Join us in the mountains above Shaver Lake for the first-ever Ely Mountain Trail Race, where crisp air, big climbs, and epic views are all on the menu.

 

The 14K course brings the heat with about 1,800 feet of climbing, including a 1,000’ ascent up Ely Mountain. You’ll earn sweeping views of the Sierra, Shaver Lake, and the valley below — then fly down some smooth and fast singletrack and dirt roads back to the finish.

 

The 8K hits a slightly easier route to the top but still climbs about 800 feet, with all the mountain vibes and finish line feels.

 

🏔️ Special Award for King & Queen of the Mountain – fastest segment times to the top of Ely!

🎽 Custom race shirts

🏅 Finisher medals + podium awards

🍕 Post-race food + refreshments

🌲 All the crisp mountain air you’ve been missing

We’re capping this one at 250 runners, so don’t sleep on it — grab your spot and come break in these trails with us.

name: End of the Trail Half Marathon, 10K & 5K
description:
PACKET PICK-UP:

February 27th (Friday). Sole 2 Soul Sports - Visalia at 4241 S. Mooney Blvd (Target Shopping Center). 

TIME: 3:00pm to 6:00pm

 

RACE DAY PACKET PICK-UP:

OPENS at 7:00am, Near the start line under the Visalia Runners Canopy

 

ALL RACES START TIME: 8:00 AM

 

START & FINISH: MOONEY GROVE PARK at the END OF THE TRAIL STATUE.

COURSE DETAILS: The half marathon, 10K, and 5K will Start & Finish at the End of the Trail Statue (road) and will run approximately 1 mile through scenic Mooney Grove Park before heading out the back gate.  The half and 10K continues out on country roads with lots of local cross country teams cheering you on. There will be  DJ Music at the 10k Turn-Around.

These routes are FLAT & FAST with closed roads, DJ’s, live bands, portable restrooms, aid stations, and more! 

At the Finish Line, you will be welcomed back with your EOTT Custom Finisher’s Medal, Hot Breakfast, Chocolate Milk, and a Post-Race Celebration in the Park! You’ll want to stay around and relax in the park with your running buddies!

Whether you Run or Walk, you'll want to join this memorable experience in the beautiful setting of Mooney Grove Park.

Race Proceeds & All Donations will benefit many local high school running programs in Tulare County, athlete scholarships and other community running events to promote health and wellness. You will see those high school runners cheering you on, working our Aid Stations, and keeping you moving!

Why End of the Trail?

  • Courses are Flat & Fast
  • It's a Post Race Party in the Park
  • Closed Running Streets
  • Perfect Cool Weather
  • Custom Finisher's Medal
  • FREE Race Tech Shirt to ALL 5K, 10K & Half Marathon participants

  • Post Race Celebration Venue for You, Family, Friends
  • And MORE

name: Endless Summer in the LBC 5K, 10K, & Half Marathon
description:
🌊☀️ Sun. Sand. Miles. Vibes. ☀️🌊

 

Join us on July 12th, 2025, for Endless Summer in the LBC, the ultimate mid-summer running experience along the beautiful Long Beach waterfront. Whether you're looking to set a new PR, enjoy a scenic run, or just soak in the summer vibes, this event has something for everyone!

🏝 Event Highlights:
✅ Scenic Course: Breathe in the fresh ocean air and enjoy stunning beach views along our fast, flat course.
✅ Frozen Treats at the Finish: Cool down with ice-cold frozen pops after you cross the finish line!
✅ Hydration Stations with ICE: Stay refreshed with Gatorade, water, and ice at two aid stations along the course.
✅ Volunteer Medic on Scooter: Keeping an eye on everyone and making sure we all stay safe in the summer heat!
✅ Beach-Themed Photo Ops: Snap your best summer vibes with our amazing beach-inspired backdrops!
✅ Shaded Family Viewing Area: Friends and family can chill in a shaded spectator zone while they cheer you on!
✅ Awards & Swag:
🏅 All finishers receive a custom medal.
📸 FREE race photos to capture the moment.
🥇 Top 3 male & female finishers in each distance win awards.

👟 Event Details:
📅 Date: Saturday, July 12, 2025
📍 Location: Long Beach Waterfront
🏃 Distances: 5K, 10K, and Half Marathon
⏰ Start Times:

7:00 AM – Half Marathon
7:30 AM – 5K & 10K
🎉 Fun Contest – Summer Vibes Edition!
Bring out your best summer-themed outfits! Show up in your most colorful, beachy, tropical attire, and you could win a special prize! Categories include:
🌴 Best Beach Bum Look
🌺 Most Tropical Vibes
😎 Coolest Sunglasses Style

📍 Race Logistics:
🎟 Bib Pick-Up: 6:15 AM – 7:35 AM at the Race Ready Athletics Tent.
🚗 Parking:

Free street parking on along Ocean Blvd.
Paid parking inside the lot $2.00 per hour.


🚻 Restrooms: Available at the start/finish area and along the course.
🍼 Stroller & Walker-Friendly: Everyone is welcome!
Why CaliFlow Runs?
We’re all about good vibes, community, and making running fun. Whether you’re a seasoned racer or just getting started, our events are designed to be inclusive, energetic, and unforgettable.

So grab your sunnies, lace up, and let’s chase Endless Summer in the LBC! 🌞🏃‍♂️🏖

name: Falcon 5K
description:
Hey Falcon 5k supporters - we've already locked down the date for next years run! 

Join us on Saturday, August 15th for the Second Annual Falcon 5k, a community event supporting the College Park High School Cross Country Team! This race is a great way to celebrate the start of the season, build our community, connect with local runners, and show your support for our student-athletes.

Whether you're a seasoned runner, a proud alumni, or a supportive community member, this event is open to all and promises a fun, energetic atmosphere. Proceeds will go directly to the CPHS cross country program to help with travel, gear, and meet expenses.

The race will start at 8AM at the College Park Track, be sure to register by August 2nd to guarantee your t-shirt size!

Come run, cheer, and be part of the College Park spirit!

name: Falconry Lessons: Hawk Walk
description:
Experience the ancient art of falconry — where humans and birds of prey work together in perfect harmony. In these hands-on lessons, you’ll learn how to handle, train, and fly magnificent raptors like hawks and falcons under the guidance of a master falconer. Discover the deep bond between falconer and bird, gain insight into centuries-old hunting traditions, and witness the power and grace of these incredible creatures up close. Perfect for nature lovers, adventurers, and anyone seeking a truly unforgettable wildlife experience. 

Transportation will be departing NAB Liberty Center at 0900.

Experience begins at 1030.  We will be finding a good spot for lunch after experience before returning to Coronado.

name: Finish The Ride and Finish The Run Griffith Park
description:
Full event details can be found at www.streetsareforeveryone.org/finish-the-ride-griffith-park

It’s not just an event; it’s a movement for the safety of all on the streets of California.


Join cyclists, runners, walkers, and many others to enjoy the beautiful scenery and back roads of Griffith Park. Our rides take you on a journey through the park and surrounding areas, and our runs/walks travel around the most tranquil areas of Griffith Park. Top it all off with our wonderful end-event venue at the Autry Museum. 

The event benefits:
Streets Are For Everyone – aims to improve the quality of life for pedestrians, bicyclists, and drivers alike by working to reduce traffic-caused fatalities to Zero.

SAFE addresses the problem in a holistic fashion through direct education, broad awareness campaigns, partnerships, community outreach, policy and legislation, support for those impacted and other proven strategies.


Check out FinishTheRide.org for videos and information about the amazing beginnings of the movement.


The event includes:


Finish The Ride -- Sunday, May 3rd, 2026
12 Mile Fun Ride/Roll
20 Mile Nice N' Easy
35 Mile Leg Burn
Bahati Foundation Metric Century

Andrew Jelmert Half Century

 

Finish The Run -- Saturday, May 2nd, 2026
Run = 1K Kids and Puppy Run, 5K, 10K and Half Marathon


Free t-shirt or athletic sleeves with registration
Chip timing (5K, 10K, and Half Marathon only) and NEW individual event medals awarded for all events!
Great live music and dancing, Beer Garden (2 beers included for 21+)
Free festival and safety expo with giveaways, raffles, prizes, and more. 

Feel free to bring the whole family, even the dog!


Join Finish The Ride and Finish The Run Griffith Park 2026, not only for yourself but for those who survived, those who didn't, and the safety of ALL!
#FinishTheRide #FinishTheRun #NeverGiveUp #PhoenixRising


For more information on the event itself or how you can help, e-mail us at Events@StreetsAreForEveryone.org or call (844) 884-7233 Ext. 801

name: Finish The Ride and Finish The Run Santa Clarita
description:
Finish The Ride & Finish The Run – Santa Clarita
Sunday, October 25, 2026 • 6:00 AM – 2:00 PM
West Creek Park • 24247 Village Circle Drive, Valencia, CA 91354

Join us for a memorable day of running, riding, walking, and rolling—all for a purpose. Finish The Ride & Finish The Run is more than an event; it’s a movement to make roads safer for cyclists, pedestrians, and drivers everywhere.

 
🌄 What to Expect


Multiple Ride Options (Routes are subject to change)
• 12‑Mile Family Fun Ride/Roll – ideal for beginners & families (mostly on bike paths). 
• 25‑Mile Tour de River Ride – advanced beginner/intermediate route. 
• 62‑Mile Metric Century – challenging ride with scenic canyons and elevation gain (~3,500 ft).


Run/Walk Options
• 5K Run/Walk
• 10K Run/Walk
• 1K Kids & Puppy Run – for little ones and canine companions. 
 
🕒 Schedule (October 25, 2026)


Time                                             Event


6:00 AM                                       Check‑in opens

name: Fleet Feet Fall Classic - Trail October 18th, 2026
description:
LOCATION

South Rim Trail Head/ Backside of Bidwell Golf Course
Chico, CA US 95928

 

DISCRIPTION 

Fleet Feet Chico is pleased to offer two trail races in our beautiful Upper Bidwell Park.  The two races will start on the south side of the park down Annies Trail for a fun adventure on the single-track trails. Toss in a creek crossing and a nice finish through Yahi and the golf course, you’re sure to enjoy your run! 

 

The two races include a half marathon and a 4-mile an hour backyard endurance challenge! 

 

The Half Marathon will start at 8:10am along the rock wall off Centennial/South Rim trail head. This race will be a challenging climb with 1600 ft of gain in the first half. Enjoy a party at the top of 10-mile house at Aid station #1 and enjoy an all downhill second half of the race!

 

4-mile endurance race will start at 8:00am. Runners will run a 4-mile loop. If you complete the loop in under 60 mins you will go back in the shoot for loop #2. At the top of each hour a new round will start. This will continue for 8 hours! Every other lap we will change the direction of the loop!  If there is more than one person going into the final hour the run will become a foot race to the finish! If you complete all 8 loops, you will have run approximately 32 Miles! Do you have what it takes? Do one loop, 3 loops or all 8! It’s sure to be a good time for the runners and the spectators!

 

After the race head up to Bidwell Golf Course Bar and grill for some delicious food and drinks! All runners get a breakfast burrito with your race registration plus and additional 15% off any other food or drink. 

 

By supporting this race, you are supporting two great causes! 

Chico Velo Trailworks. Launched in 2014, Chico Velo’s Trailworks supports and manages the creation and maintenance of sustainable and enjoyable trails in our region. They have established a strong partnership with the City of Chico to maintain the trails in Upper Bidwell Park. Trailworks have done additional work in the Oroville area and beyond. They are actively seeking new partnerships and opportunities within our community to promote sustainable trail design. Trailworks volunteers put in hundreds of hours every year improving trails for all users to enjoy. To see their latest project check out our Colby Mountain Recreation Project.  A portion of your race entry will go to this great local stewardship as they continue their work to help keep our local trails accessible for us all! If you would like more information on this program or would like to sign up for a park cleanup day, click the link below.

Chico Velo Trailworks - CHICO VELO

 

In addition to supporting Chico Velo Trailworks we are also donating a portion of the race proceeds to local fire academy cadets. Many of the current class are volunteer firefighters who have worked and volunteered in our community and are continuing their education to be able to make a lifelong career the Fire industry. With a fire prone environment that we live in throughout Butte County we rely on our local fire personnel, staff and volunteers to keep our community safe! Cadets will be volunteering on the racecourse to help ensure the safety of all our participants.  Cadets can be seen on our racecourse supporting our race as emergency EMTs and safety aids at the creek crossings. If you are interested in becoming a volunteer firefighter visit the links below for more information.

Become a Volunteer | Butte County, CA

 

RACE START TIMES


4-Mile Endurance Run            8:00am

Half Marathon                         8:10am

 

REGISTRATION

Registration for this race is available online.

  • Online registration closes October 16th at 9:00am.
  • In person registration on October 16th and 17th at Fleet Feet Chico from 10am-2pm.
  • Register by Friday September 29th to guarantee yourself race shirt.
  • If you register between September 18th – October 18th your shirt will NOT be guaranteed, they will be first come first serve at packet pickup.
  • All leftover shirts (if any) will be available for pickup or for sale (non-registered runners) AFTER the Half Marathon race on October 18th. The shirts will be available first come first serve starting at 10:00am.  

 

RACE FEE SCHEDULE

  • October 21st – December 31st - (online)        
    • Half Marathon   $80.00
    • 4-Mile Endurance Run     $80.00
  • January 1st – May  31st (online)         
    • Half Mar._______________$85.00
    • 4-Mile Endurance Run___$85.00
  • June 1st- September 30th (online)
    • Half Marathon__________$90.00
    • 4-Mile Endurance Run___$90.00
  • October 1st- October 16th (online, closes at 9:00am on 10.16)
    • Half Marathon__________$95.00
    • 4-Mile Endurance Run___$95.00

  • In person Registration at Packet Pickup (Oct. 16th and 17th) ONLY
    • Half Marathon__________$100.00
    • 4-Mile Endurance Run___$100.00

 

 

PRE-RACE SHAKE OUT RUN

Join us on Saturday October 17th at 7:30am at the Horseshoe Lake Parking Lot (Parking Lot E) in Upper Bidwell Park. We will head out on a beautiful 4 mile run before our race on Sunday! We will have coffee, muffins, and all the miles and smiles! All who attend will be entered in a drawing for a free race entry for 2026!

 

PACKET PICKUP

Packet pickup will be held at Fleet Feet Chico on the following days and times:

  • Friday and Saturday October 16th and 17th, 2026
  • 10:00am-2:00pm 

Race Day Packet Pick up (At Race Location)

  • Sunday October 18th
  • 6:45 - 7:45am

 

Fleet Feet - Chico
241 Main Street
Chico, CA 95928
(530) 345-1000

 

SWEAT CHECK

Sweat check will be available for all runners at this year’s race! If you have a jacket, extra shoes, a key or a phone that you don’t what to run with, you can check your bag at the sweat check tent. Clear poly bags will be provided for all runners who would like to use this service. At the tent we will tag your bag with your bib number and hold on to it while you run. Come back after the run to collect your items.

  • Sweat check will be available from 7:30am to 4:15pm on race day.

 

OFFICAL COURSE CERTIFICATION AND MAPS

Both the Half Marathon and the 4-Mile Endurance run will start on the south side of Upper Bidwell Park.

The 4-mile run will take Annies to J-Ford to cross over the creek to Yahi trail. On Yahi runners will continue up the trail to Day Bear Hole parking lot where there will be an Aid Station and restroom if needed before continuing down the Fire Road back to Lower Yahi to finish through the Golf Course. (Hopefully for your next loop) 

Click here for both course maps:

  • Half - Half Marathon Race Map
  • 4MPH Endurance Race Map

   

DIRECTIONS AND PARKING FOR OPTIONAL RACE LOCATION

To the course:

The race is located along the Centennial/South Rim rock wall, approximately a quarter mile past the gate at Centennial Ave and Chico Canyon Rd. 

 

Directions from HWY 99: 

Take exit at HWY 32 and head east on HWY 32/ Deer Creek HWY towards Bruce Rd. 

At the stoplight at Bruce Rd, you will turn left and continue to Chico Canyon Rd. 

Follow to the end where the road meets the gate. 

This is a drop off ONLY location! 

 

 

PARKING

Parking can be found at the following locations: 

  • 5 Mile Recreation - .5 mile from the start. The preferred parking area, gate will be open at 6am on race day.
  • Hooker Oak Park - .75 mile from the start
  • Observatory Parking Lot (limited) - .75 mile from the start
  • Horseshoe Lake Parking Lot – 1 mile from start
     

BIKE VALET

Bike valet will be available at the race this year! We encourage you to ride your bikes to the race and Chico Velo will have their bike valet services available to make sure your bike is safe while you run! This is a great way to warm up or cool down before and after your race. To encourage you to ride we are doing a raffle for everyone wo checks a bike in!

 

NO PARKING ALLOWED AT BIDWELL GOLF COURSE!
 

 
RACE RULES:

  • Be courteous when overtaking slower runners or walkers in your elected race location. We want you to race hard and fast, but with the safety of yourself and others in mind.
  • Use best trail educate. Calling out “runner back’ or ‘runner up” when on the trails
  • Follow all trail flagging and marking assigned to the race. Do not go off trails or cut the course. (Pink and Orange Flags)
  • Do NOT remove any course markings!
  • Where your race number on the front of your body so it is visible to the timers!
  • You must cross the timing mat for your chip to be read at the finish of the half marathon. If you are planning to race for top finisher, the race is based on gun time start and first to cross the finish line.
  • 4-Mile runners must complete the loop under the 60 min threshold to be able to start the next loop. If you choose not to start the next loop, you must drop by placing your race tag/bracelet in the drop box for your laps to be logged.
  • Please pack out all trash that you may have from your nutrition or hydration. Trash cans will be available at all aid stations. Leave no trace!
  • No crews or pacers will be allowed for either race on course. All crewing must happen at the start/finish area in the designated runner prep area.
  • All drop bags for the 4-mile race must be checked in by 7:45am on race day. They can be checked in and out between each lap as needed.
  • No pets will be allowed on the course during the race.
  • No strollers will be allowed on the course.
  • Run hard, run fast and have fun!
  • You must complete all 8 laps to be considered for top 3 male/female in the endurance race.

Thank you for understanding. 
 

AID STATIONS AND RESTROOMS
There will be 3 for the Half Marathon and 2 for the 4-Mile Challenge.

1.     10 Mile House (Green Gate) – Half Marathon
2.     End of Fire Road (U Ford/North side) – Half Marathon
3.     Bear Hole Parking Lot Mile 2/11.5 – Water, electrolytes, nutrition gels - 4-Mile and Half Marathon

4.      Start/Finish Area – Water, electrolytes, trail snacks, bars and gels, and more. This will also serve as a post-race fuel station for the Half Marathon and 4-Mile Endurance runners! 

 

Unnecessary waste and trash are something we are working to eliminate from our events. As an organization dedicated to maintaining a clean race and doing our part to keep our trails (roads) clean, starting this year, we will be making a push in our sustainability efforts. This means we are eliminating the use of disposable cups at our races. Runners will have the option of carrying their own hydration vessels or using a HydraPak reusable SpeedCup provided at packet pickup.

                                         

HydraPak is offering all race registrants a onetime use 20% sitewide discount. Use discount code: FF-sr25 to save on training and race day hydration. Visit HydraPak by clicking the link here

                                         

BATTLE OF THE AID STATIONS!                                                                                                                                    

This year we are having a battle of the aid stations!

This will be a fun competition for the aid stations to pump up of the spirit and have a good time on the course. Your job as a runner is to hit the aid stations and check out the energy, the refreshments and report back. We will have a voting box at the Fleet Feet tent for you to judge the aid stations! Winners of the Battle of the Aid Stations will be announced after each race.

Who has the "Best snacks, Best Energy, Best Overall aid station"

To sign up to be in the Battle of the Aid Stations or any other volunteer position please click the link below!

Fleet Feet Chico: Fleet Feet Fall Trail Classic 2025 Volunteers


Limited restrooms on the course will be located at the finish area of the race (South Rim Trail), Aid station one at the top of 10-Mile house road, and Bear Hole

 

POST RACE REFRESHMENTS

 


T-SHIRTS AND AWARDS

  • Guaranteed Tee-shirt cutoff is September 17th, 2026
  • Cotton blend shirts from Upper Park Clothing Co. will be provided to all participants who register for this event before the tee shirt cutoff. (9/17/26) Any participant who registers on or before September 17th will be guaranteed a race tee.
  • Any participant who registers after September 17th will be able to receive a race shirt based on limited size availability (very few extras will be ordered). Any shirts not picked up at packet pick up prior to the race will be available on a first come first serve basis to all paid runners for pick up, and available for sale to any unregistered spectators starting at 10:00am at the Fleet Feet booth.
  • All shirts come in adult male (unisex) sizes, so you may wish to choose a smaller size than normal for female and child runners.
  • No youth sizes will be available.

 

Awards will be presented to the top male and female finishers in the half marathon as well as the top 3 in each age group bracket. 

 Age group brackets will be as followed: 

  • 14 and under / 15-19 / 20-29 / 30-39 / 40-49 / 50-59 / 60-69 / 70 and over

 

The winner of the 4-Mile Endurance Challenge will be either the last person standing or the first to cross the finish line in the final hour foot race to the finish. 2nd and 3rd place will also receive an award for their efforts! (Male and Female)

 

SPECTATING

We would love to see everyone come out to support our local athletes in this new trail race! Because the trail is a single track there are limited locations that you can safely watch your favorite runners without interrupting the flow of the race. Here we have provided a few locations where you can safely watch your runners and help cheer them on to the finish.

 

  • Start/Finish area- in the meadow of the finish/ South Rim area. At this location you will not only see the runners start on the run, but this is also the location    of the finish. For the 4-Mile runners this will also serve as the location where they will hold until the start of the next loop.
  • Green Gate Parking Lot – This location will serve at Aid Station one for the half marathoners and will also be a great spot to cheer on your runners as they      will have just climbed the final hill of their run…. All downhill from here! Parking will be very limited. If you plan to cheer for your runners at this location, carpooling is highly recommended!
  • Bear Hole parking lot- This location is about one and a half miles past the Horseshoe Lake gate on Upper Park Rd. You will need to walk or bike to this location as the road will be closed to cars for the day. The Parking lot serves as aid station 3 for the half marathon as well as aid station 1 for the 4-mile runners. Runners will be coming in and out of this location from both directions, so this will be a fun and high energy place to spectate. 

 

VOLUNTEERING 

If you are interested in volunteering at the race, please check out all the available shifts! We cannot put on this event without great volunteers!

Fleet Feet Chico: Fleet Feet Fall Trail Classic 2025 Volunteers

 

For more information, please email shawna@feetfeetchico.com

 

            **No Refunds on race entries or merchandise purchased for this event**

 Age group brackets will be as followed: 

  • 14 and under / 15-19 / 20-29 / 30-39 / 40-49 / 50-59 / 60-69 / 70 and over

 

The winner of the 4-Mile Endurance Challenge will be either the last person standing or the first to cross the finish line in the final hour foot race to the finish. 2nd and 3rd place will also receive an award for their efforts! (Male and Female)

 

SPECTATING

We would love to see everyone come out to support our local athletes in this new trail race! Because the trail is a single track there are limited locations that you can safely watch your favorite runners without interrupting the flow of the race. Here we have provided a few locations where you can safely watch your runners and help cheer them on to the finish.

 

  • Start/Finish area- in the meadow of the finish/ South Rim area. At this location you will not only see the runners start on the run, but this is also the location    of the finish. For the 4-Mile runners this will also serve as the location where they will hold until the start of the next loop.
  • Green Gate Parking Lot – This location will serve at Aid Station one for the half marathoners and will also be a great spot to cheer on your runners as they      will have just climbed the final hill of their run…. All downhill from here! Parking will be very limited. If you plan to cheer for your runners at this location, carpooling is highly recommended!
  • Bear Hole parking lot- This location is about one and a half miles past the Horseshoe Lake gate on Upper Park Rd. You will need to walk or bike to this location as the road will be closed to cars for the day. The Parking lot serves as aid station 3 for the half marathon as well as aid station 1 for the 4-mile runners. Runners will be coming in and out of this location from both directions, so this will be a fun and high energy place to spectate. 

 

VOLUNTEERING 

If you are interested in volunteering at the race, please check out all the available shifts! We cannot put on this event without great volunteers!

Fleet Feet Chico: Fleet Feet Fall Trail Classic 2025 Volunteers

 

For more information, please email shawna@feetfeetchico.com

name: Fleet Feet Free Thanksgiving Day 5k Fun Run
description:
Join Fleet Feet San Diego for a family-friendly morning of running, walking, and giving thanks! Get up and get moving before all the food and football on Thanksgiving Day. The first 175 registrants will receive a limited edition 2025 Fleet Feet Thanksgiving Day 5k t-shirt! Stick around after the run for morning refreshments and early access to Black Friday shopping deals.

 

Missed out on the first 175 free t-shirts? No worries! Extra t-shirts can be purchased in the Online Race Store or as you register! T-shirts will be available to order through Wednesday, 11/12.

 

We will start our informal 5k at 8am, and t-shirts will be available for pickup on Wednesday 11/26 from 11am-6pm, or Thanksgiving morning 11/27 starting at 7:15am. Please note, t-shirts will not be available for purchase at the event and must be ordered online before 11/13.

 

Our route will be entirely on sidewalk and start and end at our store. Strollers will be able to traverse the course, so bring everyone! There will be a marked turnaround for a 1 mile option, too. Please note that this run follows a "fun run" format, which means that the route will be marked, but roads will not be closed. All runners, walkers and participants will be required to follow all pedestrian traffic laws for safety.

 

This event is FREE! As in years past, we are asking for donations of canned food for the San Diego Food Bank to benefit those in need. This year we are incredibly proud to be supporting our very own Kevin Hopp and the Molly's Angels Foundation. Over the course of Thanksgiving week, Kevin Hopp will be running 350 miles to raise funds for Molly’s Angels Foundation and to support Monarch Schools, a lifeline for homeless youth, and Vista Hill, which provides crucial mental health, education, and social services. Join Kevin Hopp and his friends on this journey and help them reach their goal to make a lasting impact. Support his week of fundraising by joining the RunGiving Supporting Molly's Angels Foundation Strava Group, where each mile run earns $1 donated with a goal of reaching $25,000! Donations can also be made directly through HoppCantStopp.com!

 

Email community@fleetfeetsandiego.com with any questions. Free t-shirts are reserved in order of registration and are available while supplies last!

 

 

**Please note that t-shirts will not be available to purchase the morning of the run or in-store!

name: Fleet Feet x Brooks Santa Run 5k
description:
Kick off the holiday season with a jolly good time at the Santa Run 5K! This festive fun run starts and finishes at Naughty Pines Brewery, where the holiday cheer flows as freely as the beer.

Every registered participant will receive their very own Santa suit — beard and all — so get ready to turn the streets into a sea of red and white! We also highly encourage all elves, reindeer, snowmen, and holiday enthusiasts to show up in your most festive gear. The more holiday spirit…the better!

This year, we’re excited to partner with Brooks, who will be onsite demoing the new Glycerin for participants to try out. Want to run like Santa on clouds? Here’s your chance!

Choose your holiday pace:

✨ The “Naughty” Pace – for our speedy runners ready to dash like Dasher.

✨ The “Nice” Pace – for our walkers and joggers who want to sip cocoa, smile, and enjoy the magic.

This 5K is all about fun, community, and holiday vibes. Whether you're chasing a PR or just enjoying the winter wonderland, you're in for a merry good time.

So grab your suit, rally your holiday crew, test out some fresh Brooks Glycerins, and meet us at Naughty Pines Brewery for the most spirited run of the season! Ho ho go! 🎄🎅🍻

name: Fog Run
description:
The Probation Auxiliary County of Kern presents their 36th Annual 5K-10K Fog Run at Lake Ming in Bakersfield. This is a fun and family friendly 5K-10K race to support at-risk individuals in Kern County.

Proceeds will also benefit the Kern County Probation Department's Helping Hands program. Helping Hands is a nonprofit organization, and their goal is to guide at risk youth towards success by removing barriers and equipping them with the basic needs. Together the two organizations provide scholarships, vocational training, mentoring, clothing, hygiene products, and other necessities.  We believe our programs leave a lasting impact on youth by removing barriers and increasing self-esteem, confidence, and drive to go to school. It is our hope to set up individuals for success and make our community a safer place. The race takes place on a beautiful scenic course overlooking beautiful mountains and lake views.

Packet Pickup

Thursday, January 8, 2026, from 4:30PM – 6:30PM at Kern County Probation Department, 2005 Ridge Rd., Bakersfield, CA 93305
Friday, January 9, 2026, from 4:00PM – 6:00PM at Orangetheory Fitness, 12838 Stockdale Hwy Suites 4A-1 & 4A-2, Bakersfield, CA 93314
Race Day Check-in/Packet Pickup: January 10, 2026, 6:30am – 7:30am at Lake Ming 

 
Event will occur rain or shine.

name: For The Bay 5K Run 2026
description:
Lace Up for a Cause, Support Bay Area Youth

Shoreline Park, Mountain View, CA US 94043

 

"For The Bay 5K" is a fundraiser for Mobilize Love, a Menlo Church ministry partner, providing academic support, mentorship, and life skills training to under-resourced youth in the Bay Area. Mobilize Love's mobile after-school programs and human services address physical needs, develop life skills, and build community, fostering flourishing lives for children and families.

Each increment of $32,000 covers the cost of providing after school services to kids in resource-challenged public schools for the year. These after-school services are characterized by:

  • Serving over 300 kids per week during our after school programs
  • Developing literacy and numeracy skills
  • Providing Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) 
  • Introducing and sharing the Gospel
  • Providing nutritious and delicious meals-You can't learn if you're hungry
  • Establishing a consistent presence and trust

 

Visit Mobilize Love to learn more about their incredible impact on our community.

name: Fort Bragg Whale Run and Walk
description:
The 38th Annual Whale Run & Walk for 2026!
Fort Bragg, Ca is a small, picturesque city on the Pacific Ocean, nestled between sandy beaches and the redwood forest. Every year there is a huge Whale Festival on the 2nd weekend of March, and the morning Whale Run kicks it off! After the Whale Run there are events all over town, including a craft fair, guided whale viewing, beer and wine tasting, and a live symphony concert in the evening.

The local Fort Bragg Soroptimists have been holding this race for 38 years, with as many as 800 runners participating on a beautiful day on the Mendocino Coast. The ocean and trails are as magnificent as ever and we know you will love the views and all the festivities in town on race day. All runners, walkers, and spectators will enjoy breathtaking whitewater ocean views (including whales) along this year’s new course starting at the Noyo Headlands Park (Cypress Street) on the Coastal Trail in Fort Bragg, CA

Here are the events you can sign up for:

  • 5k-- runners will run north and turn around at or near Compass Rose.
  • 5k-- "Fun" Walkers will follow the 5k runners route. 
  • 10k-- runners dash north past Glass Beach then cross the beautiful Pudding Creek Trestle to the 10K turn around (10K map).
  • 1/2 Marathon--same route as 10k but the turnaround is at MacKerricher State Park.
  • Kiddie run -- 300 meter run in 2 age groups (U6 and U10)

There are multiple race age divisions. Note: under 16 run/walkers may enter any race division for a discounted rate at signup.

Early signups are encouraged!! The entry fee will increase starting March 1, 2025. We also have some inventory of last year's tshirts for sale for $10 plus shipping: go to https://runsignup.com/Race/Store/CA/FortBragg/FortBraggWhaleRunandWalk 

DOGS: We may actually have a dog entry option!!  Details soon.

name: Foster the Future Run
description:
The 9th Annual Foster The Future 5/10K Run/Walk Beyond Foster Care Wellness Fest is coming to Pasadena, California just north of the world famous Rose Bowl! Join us for this is a wonderful wellness opportunity to help support Journey House, Pasadena; providing services for former foster youth since 1983.

Journey House's Mission is to support former foster and probation youth to live fully independent, successful lives.
Founded in 1983, Journey House provides emotional support and guidance, as well as financial aid to help them with the cost of attending college and vocational schools.
Our goal is to create opportunities for advancement in education, economic stability, and a better quality of life for former foster youth.

For more information visit: journeyhouseyouth.org

name: Foster5K + Kids Dash
description:
The 9th Annual Foster5K + Kids Dash

Sunday, April 27, 2025

The Foster5k is a cornerstone event in Silicon Valley dedicated to championing the cause of foster children in Santa Clara County. All proceeds support Child Advocates of Silicon Valley (CASV) and its Court Appointed Special Advocate (CASA) Program, dedicated to providing everlasting impact on our community's most vulnerable youth.
The Foster5K features a chip-timed race and a Kids Dash, making the event enjoyable for walkers, joggers, and runners of all ages. The Kids Dash is a fun-filled event designed just for kids! This untimed fun run features a 700 meter Big Kids Dash for youth ages 6 to 10 and a 250 meter Little Kids Dash for children ages 5 and under. The Kids Dash focuses on fun, movement, and participation.
Whether sprinting, jogging, or skipping to the finish line, everyone can have a good time and support our community's foster youth along the way. See you there!

 

All proceeds benefit Child Advocates of Silicon Valley, an independent nonprofit serving our community's most vulnerable youth - foster children aged birth to 21 years old who have experienced abuse, neglect and/or abandonment. Together we can help LIFT UP our foster children. Learn more about how to help a child in foster care at childadvocatessv.org.

name: Freedom Run
description: Welcome to the Fresno Freedom Run! Start off your 4th of July celebrations with a bang and beautiful 4-mile run! The event will take place at Woodward Park with hundreds of acres of trees, geese, and beautiful wildlife. We are sure it will be an adventure! You will enjoy our American flag lined course. We hope to inspire you to race, run or walk at the best of your ability. Motivate your friends, family and fellow competitors to join in. What a way to start one of the most important days of the year for our great country.

name: FRESNO 5,000M
description:
Experience the thrill of a true track event! The 5,000M run, often referred to as a "5K on the track," challenges athletes to complete 12.5 laps on a standard track. This event is perfect for both seasoned runners and those looking to try a track race for the first time—or for the first time in a long time!

 

This isn’t just a race—it’s a chance to support the Fresno High School Track Team, with 100% of proceeds going directly to the program. And the fun doesn’t stop with the 5,000M! We also offer an Open Mile Run and a 100-Meter Kids Race, plus a spirited 4x400M Relay to close out the event.

 

Whether you're chasing a personal best or simply enjoying the camaraderie of the running community, this event has something for everyone!

name: Fresno Turkey Trot
description:
Sierra Challenge Express

Presents:

the 26th annual

Fresno Turkey Trot @ Woodward Park

 

For over a quarter of a century, the Fresno running community has come together on Thanksgiving morning to make a difference — supporting the hungry in our city through generous donations and race registrations. The Fresno Turkey Trot isn’t just a run; it’s a tradition of gratitude, generosity, and good times. This year, your participation not only benefits the Central California Food Bank, but also supports the Coach Ray Knight Youth and Scholarship Programs, helping student-athletes across the Central Valley pursue their academic and athletic dreams.

Kick off your Thanksgiving with purpose! Whether you run the chip-timed 5K or enjoy the untimed 2-Mile Walk, you’ll be part of a festive and meaningful morning. Every participant will receive a long-sleeve Thanksgiving shirt, a commemorative finisher’s medal, and a tasty post-race treat.

Registering your family? If you register 4 to 10 people, you’ll automatically receive 10% off. Register 10 or more, and you’ll save 20%! Simply select "Multi-Person Pricing" during registration.

name: Fresno Urban Run
description:
Starting inside of Chukchansi Park, you will be put to the challenge of climbing every step from the bottom to the top of the stadium, followed by a run up a 6-story circular garage and then down an adjacent 6-story circular garage, proceeded by a half-mile run down Fulton Street to the Tuolumne Overpass (Urban Hill), before the final challenge, climbing 220 stairs to the top of a 10-story building, The Grand Tower, where your timing sensor will stop your clock!
Overall length of the Urban Run is approx 3 Miles.  
All donations support The Alisa Ann Ruch Burn Foundation!

The Fresno Urban Run is a 20 point race in the California Classic Runner of the Year Series!

name: From Fields To Finish Line 5 K
description:
Race will be hosted by the Farmworker Advocacy Club from Fresno State whose mission is to create an environment where students can come and share their stories to uplift the voices of those who provide for us. Farmworkers are essential and deserve to be appreciated as such. In efforts to bring awareness to the needs of farmworkers, as a club we hold fundraisers to help purchase essential items, hold lunches, and hold events on campus and in the community as a form of outreach. The race will begin and finish at ONeil Park located on Fresno State Campus and will continue around a 3 miles parameter down Cedar, Bullard, and Chestnut. Participants will receive a t-shirt and food voucher upon registering. Water stations will be available throughout the parameters along the grapevines for participants. As this is a fundraiser, we will not have official timers, if you wish to know your time feel free to download Strava (a running app that tracks your time) and join our group.

https://www.strava.com/clubs/farmworkeradvocacy5k

name: FTD Walk for Hope 5K
description:
Raising Awareness and Funds for Frontotemporal Degeneration

We are excited to announce the FTD Walk for Hope 5K, a community event dedicated to raising awareness and funds for Frontotemporal Degeneration (FTD), a devastating brain disorder that affects behavior, language, and personality. Unlike Alzheimer’s disease, FTD often strikes people in their 40's to 60's, leading to profound changes in relationships, work, and independence. There is currently no cure, and increased awareness and research funding are crucial.

The FTD Walk for Hope 5K supports AFTD (Association for Frontotemporal Degeneration), a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization. All donations and sponsorships are tax-deductible to the extent allowed by law. Your generous support helps advance AFTD’s mission to raise awareness, improve the quality of life for those affected by FTD, and drive vital research toward a cure. Together, we bring hope to families and move one step closer to a future free of FTD.

The FTD Walk for Hope 5K will take place on Saturday, April 11 at 10:00 a.m. at Maidu Park in Roseville, California. We hope to bring together families, friends, and supporters for a fun casual walk in honor of those affected by FTD and to raise awareness throughout our community.

Thank you for considering this opportunity to make a difference. Together we can #EndFTD.

name: Fullerton Fit 5K Trail Run
description:
Fullerton Fit 5K Trail Run and Health & Wellness Fair
Saturday, June 6th, 2026
8:00 - 11:00 AM
 

Join us for the City of Fullerton’s inaugural 5K Trail Run, a community celebration of fitness, wellness, and fun! Lace up your running shoes and experience a scenic dirt trail course that winds through the natural beauty of the Brea Dam area and alongside the Fullerton Tennis Center & Golf Course. This trail run is not stroller friendly and encouraged for children ages 10 and up. 

This event isn’t just about the race—it’s a full day of community connection. Enjoy the Health & Wellness Fair, featuring local vendors, fitness demonstrations, and resources to support your healthy lifestyle from 8:00 - 11:00 AM.

Come hungry and enjoy a variety of delicious healthy food trucks & vendors offering fresh bites and post-race treats. Whether you’re a seasoned runner, a weekend walker, or simply want to cheer on friends and family, this event has something for everyone. Be part of history and join us as we kick off a new Fullerton tradition!

Race Entry Includes:

  • Free Finisher's Photos & Video
  • Race T-shirt
  • Finisher Medal
  • Reusable Water Bottles

name: G.O.L.O.W. Turkey Trot
description:
Join us for the G.O.L.O.W. Turkey Trot 5K, a fun community run/walk to kick off your Thanksgiving morning with energy, gratitude, and local pride! This event supports all Live Oak Wrestling teams — from youth through high school — helping fund uniforms, tournament fees, and training opportunities for our student-athletes.

 


Whether you’re a competitive runner or just want to walk with family and friends, everyone is welcome! The race begins at 8:00 AM, and participants are encouraged to show their Live Oak spirit — wear your purple, gold, or GOLOW gear!

 


Registration Includes: $50

 • Official Turkey Trot tee shirt

 • Finisher’s medal for top 6.

Use hashtag #GOLOWTurkeyTrot when sharing your photos to show your support and community spirit! 

 


Help us make a difference for Live Oak Wrestling — run, walk, or trot for the cause!

description:

name: GRANITE BAY TURKEY TROT 3K/6K
description:
THE GRANITE BAY TURKEY TROT IS CURRENTLY SOLD OUT FOR 2025. I WOULD LOVE TO HAVE HAD MORE PEOPLE, BUT I HAD TO CAP IT OFF AT 100 PEOPLE BECAUSE I ONLY ORDERED 100 BIBS, 100 SHIRTS, AND 100 MEDALS. I DID NOT EXPECT THE DEMAND TO BE SO HIGH, AND THE DEMAND DID NOT RISE UNTIL THE FINAL 2 WEEKS OF REGISTRATION, AND THERE WOULD NOT HAVE BEEN ENOUGH TIME TO ORDER MORE SHIRTS, BIBS, AND MEDALS AND FOR ALL PRODUCTS TO ARRIVE ON TIME BEFORE THE RACE AND PACKET PICKUP. LASTLY, I WAS NOT ABLE TO SECURE CHIP TIMING SO WE ARE ONLY DOING GUN TIMING FOR THIS RACE AND SO I HAD TO CAP IT OFF AT 100 PEOPLE. FOR 2026, I HOPE TO SECURE CHIP TIMING GOING FORWARD SO WE CAN ACCOMMODATE MORE PEOPLE, AND IN FUTURE YEARS, WOULD LOVE TO HAVE UP TO 300 PEOPLE.

THOSE WISHING TO STILL PARTICIPATE MAY DO SO UNOFFICIALLY AND FOR FREE BUT WILL NOT BE ABLE TO TAKE A BIB OR A MEDAL. I WILL HAVE EXTRA SHIRTS ON HAND FOR PURCHASE FOR THE UNOFFICIAL FOLKS IF THERE IS A SURPLUS IN SHIRTS ONCE THE EVENT HAS STARTED. AGAIN SPOTS WILL BE GIVEN ON A FIRST COME FIRST SERVE BASIS AND ONLY BASED OFF OF THE NUMBER OF NO-SHOWS OF OFFICIAL PARTICIPANTS AND ONLY ONCE THE RACE HAS STARTED.

THANKS!!!

 

DESCRIPTION:

 

A FAMILY-FRIENDLY, ALL-COMERS 3-KILOMETER (1.86 MILE) FUN RUN AND WALK THAT STARTS ON WELLINGTON WAY NEAR THE GRANITE BAY HIGH SCHOOL PARKING LOT, AND VENTURES ALONG EAST ROSEVILLE PARKWAY, TRAVELS DOWN HILLSBOROUGH DRIVE, AND VENTURES BACK ALONG THE PEDESTRIAN SIDEWALKS OF EUREKA ROAD AND FINISHES IN FRONT OF GRANITE BAY HIGH SCHOOL ON WELLINGTON WAY. 

6k course does 2 loops of the 3k course -- reversing course and doing it backwards!!!

3k: Clockwise

6k: Clockwise, then Counter-Clockwise

 

Date: 

Thursday, November 27th, 2025

 

Time:

7:30am

  

Location: 

Wellington Way, in front of

Granite Bay High School,

#1 Grizzly Way,

Granite Bay, CA 95746


Parking:
GBHS Parking lot, or on the street along Wellington Way

Cost:
$25 + 2.50 online processing fee which includes a bib, t-shirt, medal, GUN timing, post-race snacks, and water


Course: 

Starts on Wellington Way in front of Granite Bay High School, and follows a 1.86 mile, 3 kilometer clock-wise loop traveling along the pedestrian sidewalks only along East Roseville Parkway, Hillsborough Drive, Eureka Road, and back to Wellington Way. Course will be lightly traffic controlled by CHP and/or PCSO.

6k course does 2 loops of the 3k course -- reversing course and doing it backwards!!!

3k: Clockwise

6k: Clockwise, then Counter-Clockwise

 

Packet Pick-Up: 

Granite Bay Public Library,

Wednesday, November 26th, 2025,

11am-5pm

 

Beneficiary: 

Fieldhaven Feline Center, Lincoln  

 

To Volunteer:  

e-mail   GraniteBayTurkeyTrot@gmail.com

name: Great Donut Run / Walk 5k
description:
Great Donut Run

Sunday, May 19, 2024

Irvine Valley College                                

Welcome back Donuteers!  We are so excited to bring the Great Donut Run back in person with more donuts then ever before!  If you haven't registered yet then donut hesitate and sign up today!   We've got an easy breezy 1 miler at 7:30 the 5k run/walk at 8:00am. Both races are open to all ages and abilities. Take all the time you need to finish. This is not a timed event. We've got yummy donut holes at the halfway point on the 5k to keep you carbed up along the way.  We also have the Donut Double Dare if you want to run the 1 mile and 5k back to back!  Double the fun Double the donuts!  For all the kiddies looking to earn their own race bling we start their races at 9:15.  We have several distances from 50 yards to half a mile, based on ages from zero (yes, under 1 year old! ) to 12 yrs old.  It's never too early to start dashing for donuts!  Whatever race you choose, you're donuts will be safely waiting for you!  We've also got gorgeous big bling finishers medals that you'll love!

The race starts and finishes in the same location at Irvine Valley College. The course is walker and stroller friendly.  It's all flat and fast and this is a non timed, family fun run.  This is a great way for first timers to get out and enjoy a race without any pressure or timelines!  Get your donut friendly gear on and win one of many costume awards!  We can't wait to see you! 

Online Registration closes on May 16th.  If you miss the deadline you can register at Packet Pick up at Road Runner Sports in Laguna Hills on Saturday, May 18th.  We'll be there from 12-4pm or you can register on race day but please come early! 

More info on www.GreatDonutRun.com

name: Green Valley Lake 5k/10k/& Half Marathon
description:
🌲 GREEN VALLEY LAKE 5K / 10K / HALF MARATHON
Saturday, August 2, 2025
Green Valley Lake, CA (Between Running Springs & Big Bear in the San Bernardino Mountains)

 
🕖 START TIMES
7:00 AM: Early Start Half Marathon (for those expecting to take 3.75+ hours)
7:30 AM: Standard Half Marathon Start
8:30 AM: Mass Start for 5K & 10K
 
🏞 COURSE HIGHLIGHTS
This is a breathtaking mountain race in the heart of the San Bernardino National Forest!

Start with a scenic ¾-mile out-and-back along the lake
Climb gradually up Green Valley Lake Rd and onto a forest service road
Enjoy a 400 ft elevation gain to an overlook at the 5K turnaround
10K and Half Marathon continue along rolling terrain on FS Road 2N13, through pine forests and rocky vistas
Course is part paved (1.5 miles), then transitions to dirt roads and trail
Water & aid stations every 1.5 miles
Get ready for that fresh air, mountain-made, above-the-clouds experience!

 
📍 LOCATION
Green Valley Lake – Just 40 minutes from Redlands, located off Hwy 18 between Lake Arrowhead and Big Bear.

Post-race activities take place in the Downtown Community Garden on Main Street.
Race HQ / Packet Pickup: Black Dog Social Club, 33231 Green Valley Lake Rd.

 
🥇 WHAT YOU GET
Custom, high-quality event t-shirt
Unique, huge finisher medal
Top 3 overall awards per race distance
Age group medals (3 deep in 5-year spans up to 80+)
Chip timing by Itz About Time
🏆 Age Groups:
10 & under, 11–14, 15–19, 20–24, 25–29, 30–34, 35–39, 40–44, 45–49, 50–54, 55–59, 60–64, 65–69, 70–74, 75–79, 80+
(Separate overall awards for each race distance.)

 
🏁 AWARDS CEREMONY – COMMUNITY GARDEN
9:15 AM – 5K Awards
9:30 AM – 10K Awards
9:45 AM – Half Marathon Awards
 
🧁 FOOD & FUN
Coffee ,pastries , street tacos, and more available for purchase packet pickup and race morning
Food available for purchase post-race
Live music at the Community Garden post-race
Hang out in a welcoming mountain community with big hometown vibes
 
🎽 PACKET PICKUP
Friday, July 31 3:00 PM – 6:30PM @ Black Dog Social Club
Saturday (Race Day): 6:30 AM – 8:30 AM @ Race Site
 
🏕 STAY THE WEEKEND
Make it a full mountain getaway!

Airbnbs in Green Valley Lake
Green Valley Lake Campground (0.5 miles from race) 
Giant Oaks Lodge, Running Springs (5 miles)
Rentals available at: green-valley-lake.com
 
🌅 FRIDAY NIGHT SUNSET RUN (Optional Add-On)
Friday, August 1 at 7:00 PM – Sunset Trail 5K
A fun, scenic, single-track 3.1-mile warm-up trail run.
💌 Email: carenfasttrack@aol.com to sign up.

 
🚴‍♀️ WANT TO RENT MOUNTAIN OR E-BIKES?
Visit Mountain Life Supply Co.
32855 Hilltop Blvd, Running Springs (past Valero Gas Station on right)

 
🌲 GIVING BACK
Proceeds benefit The Children’s Forest via the Southern California Mountains Foundation, empowering youth to become leaders in environmental stewardship.

Your support helps:

Train young Forest Rangers, Firefighters & Scientists
Maintain trails like The Exploration Trail
Support the Camacho family in memory of their daughter
We also proudly support:

The Green Valley Lake Community Garden (host of our awards)
The Local Museum, providing water support on the course
🙏 Donations welcome – Hit the "DONATE" button at registration!

 
FINAL NOTES
This is a scenic mountain course – come for the run, stay for the views!
A perfect escape from the summer heat and city smog
Come experience the camaraderie and community like no other!

name: Grievances & Gratitude Run – Let Go, Run Free, Embrace the Positive! 5K, 10K, and Half Marathon
description:
All participants will receive a medal, and you have the option to take part in the "Let Go and Affirmation" activity, or simply enjoy the run—it's entirely up to you. We believe this is a fun and positive way to kick off 2025, setting the tone for a great year ahead!

How it Works:

Let Go Before You Go: Before the run, write down anything you want to release—your grievances, frustrations, or things weighing you down. Drop them into our burn containers or "goodbye" containers, leaving the negative energy behind.


Run Free: Take off on a scenic race, clearing your mind and body as you move forward, step by step.
Affirmations Await: Cross the finish line and head to our New Year Mantra Board, where you'll collect a positive affirmation to inspire your journey ahead. Start the new year with fresh energy, purpose, and gratitude!


This race isn’t just about physical fitness—it's a chance to embrace emotional wellness and set a positive tone for the year ahead.

 

 
Why Calilflow Runs?

CaliFlow Runs is dedicated to creating inclusive, energetic, and community-driven running events that celebrate you. We bring people together to promote health, wellness, and positive vibes through races that are accessible, fun, and infused with the unique culture of the Golden State.

Who Can Participate? Everyone - Runners, Walkers, Strollers - All are welcome

About Our Courses: Our courses are open, which means you'll be sharing the path with other runners, walkers, and beachgoers. Safety is our top priority, so please stay on the pedestrian side of the beach path. The courses are well-marked, with water stations and restrooms available along the way.


Course Information: Course Information

Bib Pick-Up and Start Times:

Bib Pick-Up: 6:00 AM End 7:35 AM at the Race Ready Athletics Tent
Half Marathon Start Time: 7:00 am
5K, 10K, 15K & 10 Miler Start Time: 7:30 am

Start Location:5400 E Ocean Blvd
Long Beach, CA US 90803

Parking Information:
Street parking is free. Parking machines are $2.00 per hour.


Awards: 

The top 3 men and women in each distance will receive a medal.

Podium awards ceremony  at 8:45 AM

name: Griffith Park Resolution Run
description:
Celebrate The New Year With Us! Join us for 2026 and help us make it even better! We're giving out some goodies to the first couple registrations so don't miss out and register now!

 

Our Half Marathon course is roughly 90% on a trail with the remaining 10% on asphalt. Below is a quick overview of the course.

The start of the course is at Shane's Inspiration in Griffith Park.
Mile 1: Upper Old Zoo Trail
Mile 2: Bill Eckert Trail (Hills with beautiful views!)
Miles 3-5: Mainly downhill on asphalt
Miles 6-8: Rolling Hills (Tetris)
Mile 9: All downhill
Miles 10-13: Quick flat trail to the finish!

Our 12K shares the same start line as the Half Marathon.
Miles 1-3: You will pass through the old Griffith Park Zoo and zoom through some hills
Mile 4: All downhill
Miles 5-7+: Quick flat trail to the finish!

Our 5K is a nice and quick route around the golf course.

15K Relay - New for 2026!
Create a team of 3 and each run a 5K loop. Compete in any of our 3 divisions for the relay!
Coed, Male, Female

name: Griffith Park Trail Marathon Relay & 8K
description:
Join us for the Griffith Park Trail Marathon Relay & 8K, an unforgettable race experience celebrated as one of Runner’s World magazine’s 10 Best Races You’ve Never Heard Of in 2024! This iconic event is the perfect opportunity to push yourself, bond with friends, and take in the breathtaking beauty of Griffith Park. With a combination of scenic trails and challenging terrain, you’ll be in for the ride of your life. Whether you’re a seasoned runner or just starting out, join us for a solo run or bring a team for a relay. And with fully-stocked aid stations and an energetic volunteer crew, you’ll have everything you need to crush it. So come on, grab your running shoes, and let’s make this a moment to remember! Register now for a day of adventure, camaraderie, and lasting memories.
One of the largest urban parks in the country, Griffith Park is a 4,300-plus acre slice of runner heaven. The grounds include famous sites like the Abandoned Los Angeles Zoo, the Observatory, and the Hollywood Sign. There’s more than 30 trails totaling around 50 miles for runners and hikers. Join us for the Griffith Park Trail Relay Marathon and get a taste of what the second largest city park has to offer.
  • All participants will receive a premium short sleeve women's or men's cut t-shirt. (Guaranteed shirt size if you register by May 13!)
  • Relay run is chip timed for fast & accurate results.
  • $1500 in Cash prizes for the Open division
  • Trophy/Plaque for the top 3 teams in each recreational division
  • Finisher’s medal for all participants
  • 3 well supported aid stations with medical staff (2 on course, 1 at start/finish)
  • Food and refreshments at the start/finish area.
  • Music from multiple live DJs
  • Food Trucks
  • Access to the exclusive GPTMR packet pickup sale and raffle at Fleet Feet Burbank

name: Hanukkah 8 Krazy Kilometers and 2K Latke Loop Fun Run
description:
IN-PERSON EVENTS

Runners, joggers and walkers of ALL ages and abilities are invited to the eighth annual Hanukkah 8 Krazy Kilometers, an 8K run organized by TEMPLE BETH EL of Bakersfield, California, in celebration of the eight-day Jewish holiday of Hanukkah.  This family-friendly community event also includes the 2K Latke Loop Fun Run.

The 8K and 2K runs will take place on Sunday, December 14 , at the beautiful PANORAMA VISTA PRESERVE (panoramavista.org).  The race starts at 8:30 AM.  The 8K and 2K courses will take participants through scenic natural preserve land situated along the Kern River in northeast Bakersfield.  This riparian woodland area is home to many native plants and animals and includes hiking, biking and equestrian trails.

Registration includes a custom finisher medal, Hanukkah swag, water and refreshments, and entry into the race raffle.  PLUS those who register by 6 PM on November 30 will be guaranteed an event T-shirt.  In addition . . .·      

        Teams of 3 or more will receive a registration discount

·       Awards will be given to top finishers of the 8K

·       Race day festivities will include music and giveaways

VIRTUAL EVENT

Run or walk (or skip, skate, swim, bike, treadmill, etc.) ANYWHERE and ANYTIME during the eight days of Hanukkah . . . Monday, December 15 through Monday, December 22. 

Participants will be able to download a custom race bib, run or walk an 8K or 2K distance at a location of their choosing (e.g., neighborhood, running trail, stairwell, etc.), post their results on the "RESULTS" page, and download a finisher's certificate.  PLUS teams with three or more virtual event members will receive a registration discount.  And back this year is a RACE RAFFLE for registrants of the virtual event.  The drawing will take place on Facebook Live (check back for date and time).

Registrants will receive a race shirt, finisher medal and Hanukkah swag.  Race items will be mailed on December 11 to those who register by 12 noon on December 10.  A second mailing will be made the week of December 22 to those who register after 12 noon on December 10.  A small shipping fee will be applied during registration.  Unfortunately, packet pickup is not available for the virtual event.

PROCEEDS

Race proceeds will benefit TEMPLE BETH EL (templebethelbakersfield.org), a Reform Jewish synagogue and tax-exempt charitable organization under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code, and the KERN RIVER PARKWAY FOUNDATION (kernriverparkway.org), a local nonprofit that works to protect, preserve and restore the natural riparian and wildlife habitat of the Kern River.

Race proceeds will benefit TEMPLE BETH EL (templebethelbakersfield.org), a Reform Jewish synagogue and tax-exempt charitable organization under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code, and the KERN RIVER PARKWAY FOUNDATION (kernriverparkway.org), a local nonprofit that works to protect, preserve and restore the natural riparian and wildlife habitat of the Kern River.

name: Have a Heart for Kids 5K Run/Walk
description:
The Have a Heart for Kids 5K Run/Walk is a fundraiser for the Yuba City Education Foundation.  The proceeds benefit students and their families within the YCUSD community. 

Start and Finish will be on the River Valley High School track with an 8:45am warm-up and announcements and a 9:00am start.  Breakfast will be served at 9:30am and awards at 10:00am.

Registrations are open until the day of the run, however T-Shirts are not guaranteed if registrations are after Friday, February 21, 2025.

name: HDR Miles Mania
description:
Here is a chance for runners of all ages to race the MILE -- FOR FREE!! 

  • This is a FREE EVENT!  There will be no race shirts, but there will be participation ribbons and age group 1-3 place ribbons. 
  • The races will be held by age and grade level beginning at 8 am and Noon!

The West Antelope Valley Education Foundation (WAVE) and the High Desert Runners are hosting these races on the track at Joe Walker Middle School as part of the Empowering Youth Festival.

  • The festival runs from 9am to 1pm. 
  • This is a fun event for families to bring their children and participate in the day’s activities! This year's vendors and demonstrators are still being lined up, but some of the vendors at our last festival included Robotics Teams from AV High School District, free bike repair by Lancaster Sunrise Rotary and Lakay’s Cycling Club, and activities provided by Lancaster and Palmdale City Parks and Recreation. We also enjoyed Quartz Hill Karate demonstrations, dance, and cheerleading performances throughout the event. The outdoor activities included the Go Green BMX Show, Excel Tennis, WAVE Kindness Rock Painting, 4-H Club, and local food trucks. Two of the favorite community service vehicles were the Waste Management Trash Truck, and the AMR Ambulance.

name: Heart and Sole Valentine's Run 5K, 10K, and Half Marathon
description:
Celebrate love, fitness, and fun at the Heart & Sole run along the beautiful Santa Monica coast! Whether you're running solo, with a partner, or with friends, this Valentine 's-themed event offers a scenic 5K, 10K, and Half Marathon course that promises breathtaking ocean views and a vibrant race day atmosphere.

 

 Every runner will receive a unique heart and sole-themed finisher medal

Start your Valentine's celebration early with a fun-filled day at Heart & Sole! Share the love and register today for a race that will leave your heart racing and your soul inspired.

Why Calilflow Runs?
CaliFlow Runs is dedicated to creating inclusive, energetic, and community-driven running events that celebrate you. We bring people together to promote health, wellness, and positive vibes through races that are accessible, fun, and infused with the unique culture of the Golden State.


Who Can Participate? Everyone - Runners, Walkers, Strollers - All are welcome


About Our Courses: Our courses are open, which means you'll be sharing the path with other runners, walkers, and beachgoers. Safety is our top priority, so please stay on the pedestrian side of the beach path. The courses are well-marked, with water stations and restrooms available along the way.

 

Course Information: https://www.caliviberuns.com/w/CaliVibeRuns/Page/SantaMonicaCourse


Bib Pick-Up and Start Times:
Bib Pick-Up: 6:00 AM End 7:35 AM at the Race Ready Athletics Tent
Half Marathon Start Time: 7:00 am
5K, 10K, 15K & 10 Miler Start Time: 7:30 am
Start Location: 5100 E Ocean Blvd 
Long Beach, CA 90803
 
Parking Information: Street parking is available, but be sure to read the signs carefully as street sweeping occurs daily. We recommend parking in the paid lot near the start line, which ranges from $10 to $12. If you arrive before the lot attendant, you can pay at the machine near the entrance.


Awards: 
The top 3 men and women in each distance will receive a medal.
Podium awards ceremony for 5K/10K at 8:45 AM
Podium awards ceremony for half marathoners at 9:30 AM

description:

name: Heart of Cool Trail Run
description:
Are you looking for a fun run for a great cause? If so, HoC 5k, 10k and half marathon is just what you are looking for!  Proceeds from this race go directly back to youth of BOMUSD (Black Oak Mines Unified School District) to inspire their future success through agriculture, engineering and VAPA (Visual and Performing Arts).  In addition, a percentage of the funds will also be used to scholarship a child to attend Camp Taylor, a camp specifically designed for youth with heart disease. 

Register by September 30 to receive a HoC cotton t-shirt with registration.  All half marathon participants receive something new for 2025 (TBD).  Check out our Instagram or Facebook page for a photo of the design.

This is a family friendly event and we highly encourage you to bring the whole family!  We offer a family discount package for immediate family members for the 5k and 10k distance!  If you want to participate in the event without your child, take advantage of our $8 per child - child care for children ages 3 and up!  We will have a post race pancake breakfast. 

The Heart of Cool Trail Run traverses some of the best trails Cool, CA and the Sierra Foothills have to offer.  Run on the same trails as many of the famous local (and world renowned) events such as Western States 100 Mile, Way too Cool 50k, Rio Del Lago 100 Mile, and many more!

To reduce waste and the possibility of littering our trails, this will be a cup free event.  Be sure to bring a cup or water bottle that can be refilled at aid stations.

Packet and bib pick up will be on Race Day.

Registration will be available online until the start of each event!

We can always use volunteers for this event. If you are able to lend a hand during the race, or the day before, please click on the Volunteer tab.

name: Hell Of A Half Marathon & 2 Person Relay
description:
IF IT DOESN’T CHALLENGE YOU…IT WON’T CHANGE YOU

YES, THE COURSE IS CHALLENGING, THE WEATHER IS HOT, BUT WHAT ELSE WOULD YOU EXPECT AT THE HELL OF A HALF MARATHON?!! OH, AND DON'T WORRY, THERE WILL BE A LOT OF OTHER CRAZIES WHO WILL JOIN YOU DURING YOUR 13.1 JOURNEY, ON THE ROAD LESS TRAVELED....

IT'S ONE THING TO FINISH A HALF MARATHON, BUT TO SAY YOU COMPLETED THE HELL OF A HALF MARATHON, IS BIG TIME BRAGGING RIGHTS!

WHAT MAKES THIS RACE STAND OUT:

2nd Race - Run The Valley Half Marathon Series

  • FREE Race Photos
  • FREE Race Tracking with RACEJOY

  • Top Relay Awards (3 Divisions)

  • PRO~PT at the Finish Line for your Post Race 
  • Awesome Finishers Medal
